author: jeremydmiller
body:
## Summary
Cherry-pick of the same fix shipped to the `5.0` branch in #2835.

Addresses a user-reported codegen failure on Wolverine 5.39.1 + Lamar 15.x + JasperFx 1.31, which reproduces against the same code paths on `main`:

```
JasperFx.CodeGeneration.GeneratorCompilationFailureException: Failure when
trying to generate code for Wolverine.Runtime.Handlers.HandlerGraph
  CS0103: The name '_outboxedSessionFactoryOfCodeListStore_of_ICodeListStore'
  does not exist in the current context
```

### Root cause
`AncillaryOutboxFactoryFrame.FindVariables` returned `Factory = new CastVariable(_outerFactory, typeof(OutboxedSessionFactory))`. `CastVariable.Usage` is a string baked in at construction time. When the IoC container is Lamar, the `_outerFactory` returned for `OutboxedSessionFactory<TStore>` is a `Lamar.IoC.Frames.InjectedServiceField`. JasperFx 1.20 (Feb 2026) added an `Of<TypeArg>` suffix to `Variable.DefaultArgName` for closed generics; Lamar's `Instance.DefaultArgName` still also appends `"_of_<TypeArg>"`, so the field is initially `_outboxedSessionFactoryOfCodeListStore_of_ICodeListStore`. Lamar's `ServiceVariableSource.useInlineConstruction` then flips `IsOnlyOne = true` *after* `FindVariables`, calling `OverrideName` to the short form — too late for `CastVariable`, which has already captured the long name. The handler chain emits the stale long name; the host never declared it; CS0103.

### Fix
Replace the `CastVariable` with a plain `Variable` and emit the cast in `GenerateCode`, where `_outerFactory.Usage` is read live. Mirrored in the (currently `#if`-guarded) Polecat copy.

## Test plan
- [x] Cherry-pick applied cleanly onto `main` (`origin/main`).
- [x] `dotnet build src/Persistence/Wolverine.Marten -f net9.0` clean (0 warnings, 0 errors).
- [x] `dotnet test src/Persistence/MartenTests -f net9.0 --filter "FullyQualifiedName~Bug_ancillary_outbox_factory_late_rename_codegen"` — 1/1 passed on `main`.
- [ ] CI (full `wolverine.slnx`)

body:
## Summary

Implements the full Blackjack game engine, SignalR hub, and React UI to close #2.

## Server
- **Card / Shoe / Hand / Seat / BlackjackTable** — immutable records and state machine
- **BlackjackEngine** — stateless orchestrator: PlaceBet, StartRound, Hit, Stand, Double, Split, PlayDealer, Settle, ResetForNextRound
- **BlackjackRules** — configurable defaults (6-deck, dealer hits soft 17, 3:2 BJ, 30s turn timer, 1000 chips, bets 10–500)
- **BlackjackHub** — full SignalR hub; shadows `JoinTable`/`LeaveTable`, adds PlaceBet/Hit/Stand/Double/Split; broadcasts `TableState` to `blackjack:{tableId}` group
- **BlackjackTimerService** — singleton; auto-stand on timer expiry + 5s settle delay before next round
- **IBlackjackTableStore / BlackjackTableStore** — `ConcurrentDictionary`-backed in-memory store
- **TablesController** — `POST /api/tables/blackjack` (create), `GET /api/tables/blackjack` (list)
- **Program.cs** — DI registrations for all new services

## Tests (xUnit — 21/21 passing)
- `HandTests.cs` — BestTotal, soft/hard aces, IsBlackjack, IsBust, CanSplit, CanDouble
- `ShoeTests.cs` — deck count, penetration, reshuffle at 75%, deterministic seeded RNG
- `EngineTests.cs` — full round, 3:2 payout, double-down, split mechanics, bust, push (FakeShoe inner class)

## Client
- **Blackjack.tsx** — full table UI: dealer area, 7 seats, bet bar, action bar (Hit/Stand/Double/Split), result banner, countdown timer, event log; red ♥♦ black ♣♠
- **Lobby.tsx** — "New Blackjack Table" button, 3s polling for active tables with clickable join links
- **router.tsx** — `/blackjack/:tableId` route, redirect from bare `/blackjack` to lobby
- **tables.ts** — POST/GET API helpers

## Known TODOs (confirm with product)
- Split blackjack pays 3:2 (standard casino pays 1:1 on split BJ)
- No one-card rule after split aces
- No insurance mechanic
- No re-split (v1: one split only)

Closes #2

author: yuxianq
body:
@coderabbitai summary

## Description

Refactor the dispatch path inside `TrtllmAttention` so that the two ~75-arg
positional kernel calls (`thop.attention(...)` and
`trtllm_gen.trtllm_gen_attention(...)`) become single explicit-kwarg
wrapper methods whose every kwarg is sourced as `source.attribute` from one
of four existing rich objects:

- `self` — the `TrtllmAttention` module
- `metadata` — `TrtllmAttentionMetadata`
- `fwd` — `AttentionForwardArgs`
- `sparse` — the new `AttentionSparseArgs` (holds the few sparse_* fields
  that don't already live on the three above)

This is offered as an alternative to introducing a `TrtllmAttentionArgs`
aggregator type and binding it across Python/C++ via nanobind
([yihwang-nv@d7d000b](https://github.com/yihwang-nv/TensorRT-LLM/commit/d7d000bcc255626e0a8f0239959a8c441b9a1e56)).
Zero new aggregator types, zero nanobind binding changes; the maintenance
surface is the four existing rich classes plus a small set of derived
`@property` views.

### Highlights

- `TrtllmAttention._run` shrinks from ~250 lines (validations + ~150 lines
  of derived locals + two ~75-arg positional calls) to ~85 lines
  (validations + side-effects + a clean if/else over the two wrappers).
- `AttentionForwardArgs.mrope_config: Optional[dict]` is flattened to two
  flat `Optional[torch.Tensor]` fields. The upstream
  `Attention.forward(mrope_config: dict)` API and the multimodal pipeline
  contract (`multimodal_data["mrope_config"]`) are unchanged — only the
  AttentionForwardArgs shape changes.
- `use_paged_context_fmha` migrates from a local var in
  `TrtllmAttention.forward()` to a field on `TrtllmAttentionMetadata`,
  derived in `__post_init__` from `runtime_features` and overridden
  per-call for SM90 / sparse-mqa-gqa / MLA.
- Pre-existing stale `Optional[Tuple[torch.Tensor, int]]` annotations on
  `mrope_config` in `modeling_qwen.py` and `modeling_seedoss.py` are
  corrected to `Optional[dict]` (they were silently tolerated because
  Python doesn't validate annotations at runtime).
- Dead `AttentionForwardArgs.enable_attn_nvfp4_output` field removed (no
  readers anywhere in `tensorrt_llm/`, `tests/`, or `cpp/`).
- `num_sparse_topk` is promoted from `DSAtrtllmAttentionMetadata` to base
  `TrtllmAttentionMetadata` (default 0), so the wrapper can read it as a
  normal field instead of via `getattr` at every call.

### Design doc

See `design.md` (added in this PR) for the full breakdown, including the
file-level change summary, the commit-by-commit walk, the tradeoff
analysis, and the explicit non-goals.

## Test Coverage

- New AST-based static sync test:
  `tests/unittest/_torch/attention_backend/test_attention_op_sync.py`.
  Six checks fail fast on any drift between
  `TrtllmAttention._call_thop_attention` and the C++ binding it calls:
  wrapper-kwargs-match-binding, source.attr uniqueness, literal-None
  allowlist, AttentionForwardArgs surjectivity (modulo
  `_THOP_EXCLUDED_FIELDS`), AttentionSparseArgs surjectivity, and
  expected-locals shape.
- Local AST cross-check between the wrapper and the C++ binding's
  `nb::arg(...)` list passes: 89/89 kwargs match exactly.
- Existing attention tests (`tests/unittest/_torch/attention/`) and
  multimodal smoke tests (qwen2vl / seedoss / hunyuan_dense for the
  `mrope_config` flatten path) should continue to pass — no behaviour
  change is intended end-to-end.

## PR Checklist

Please review the following before submitting your PR:
- PR description clearly explains what and why. If using CodeRabbit's summary, please make sure it makes sense.
- PR Follows [TRT-LLM CODING GUIDELINES](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/blob/main/CODING_GUIDELINES.md) to the best of your knowledge.
- Test cases are provided for new code paths (see [test instructions](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/tree/main/tests#1-how-does-the-ci-work))
- If PR introduces API changes, an appropriate PR label is added - either `api-compatible` or `api-breaking`. For `api-breaking`, include `BREAKING` in the PR title.
- Any new dependencies have been scanned for license and vulnerabilities
- [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) updated if ownership changes
- Documentation updated as needed
- Update [tava architecture diagram](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/blob/main/.github/tava_architecture_diagram.md) if there is a significant design change in PR.
- The reviewers assigned automatically/manually are appropriate for the PR.


- [x] Please check this after reviewing the above items as appropriate for this PR.

author: pttcodingman
body:
## Summary
Updated the ESLint `no-unused-vars` rule configuration to ignore function arguments that start with an underscore, following a common convention for intentionally unused parameters.

## Changes
- Added `argsIgnorePattern: '^_'` to the `no-unused-vars` rule in `frontend/eslint.config.js`
- This allows developers to prefix unused function parameters with `_` (e.g., `(_unused) => { ... }`) to signal intent and suppress linting warnings

## Details
This is a common JavaScript convention where underscore-prefixed identifiers indicate intentionally unused variables. The existing configuration already ignored uppercase and underscore-prefixed variable names (`varsIgnorePattern: '^[A-Z_]'`); this change extends that pattern to function arguments for consistency.

## Rationale

Two v3.0.0-era fossil documents in \`docs/\` have been unmodified since their **April 6, 2026** creation (commit \`f4a63f4\`, the v3.0.0 release) and have **zero active references** across the repo (verified via grep against \`*.md\`, \`*.py\`, \`*.json\` during Phase 1 inventory and re-confirmed at Gate 1). Move them into a new \`docs/archive/v3.0.0/\` folder so the top-level \`docs/\` tree stays focused on live reference material.

## Files moved (2, via \`git mv\` — history preserved)

| Old path | New path | Why it's archive-eligible |
|---|---|---|
| \`docs/v3-audit-report.md\` | \`docs/archive/v3.0.0/v3-audit-report.md\` | One-shot v3.0.0 PASS/FAIL audit (file-ref integrity, version consistency, model-name accuracy, etc.). Superseded by \`validate.py\` automated pre-release validation and later release-ceremony discipline. |
| \`docs/v3-inventory.md\` | \`docs/archive/v3.0.0/v3-inventory.md\` | Pre-v3.0.0 inventory table planning v3.0.0 work. Several entries now factually wrong: \`USER-GUIDE.pdf\` at root (now \`docs/user-guide/\` per #36), \`mnt/.../SKILL.md\` dispatcher path (Claude runtime artifact, never real install path). |

## Archive rationale (per Peter's decision)

Preserve historical pattern value at near-zero cost. The audit-reports-build-on-earlier-audits methodology lineage is a real pattern in this repo (the v3.6.0 audit explicitly inherits from the v3.4.0 audit at \`AUDIT-REPORT-v3.6.0.md:322\`). Archiving in-tree makes the content discoverable for future retrospective work without burying it in git log.

## Phase 1 inventory — KEEP-AS-IS decisions documented

Phase 1 (read-only branch \`chore/docs-inventory-phase1\`, no commits, not PR'd) classified 5 files in \`docs/\`. The three KEEP-AS-IS files are intentionally left untouched by this PR:

- **\`docs/Seedance 2 Skill.md\`** — live reference doc, 5 active code refs from \`vocab.md:315-319\` + \`skills/higgsfield-prompt/SKILL.md:618\` + \`skills/higgsfield-seedance/SKILL.md:1064,1233\`. Filename retains its space (referenced verbatim from active code).
- **\`docs/pdf-audit/AUDIT-REPORT-v3.6.0.md\`** — active D3-D8 drift catalog at \`:313\`, AI director toggle BLOCKED row at \`:309\`, referenced from \`validate_user_guide.py:56\` + 10+ CHANGELOG anchors. Last modified v3.7.0 (\`8913368\`) — it's a living document, not a fossil.
- **\`docs/pdf-audit/AUDIT-REPORT.md\`** — v3.4.0 audit, kept as **methodology template** per \`AUDIT-REPORT-v3.6.0.md:322\` cross-reference. Naming inconsistency with versioned sibling is intentional (first-audit-drops-suffix pattern).

- [x] \`docs/\` top-level no longer contains \`v3-audit-report.md\` or \`v3-inventory.md\`

- [x] Post-move grep for old paths (\`docs/v3-audit-report\`, \`docs/v3-inventory\`): **0 results** — no stale references

## Discipline

- Single PR, single commit
- \`git mv\` (not \`rm + add\`) — history preserved per file
- No path-reference updates needed (both files had 0 active refs)
- No code/script changes
- No version bump, no CHANGELOG entry (chore-level housekeeping)
- No frontmatter cascade
- Skipped \`docs/archive/README.md\` per your call — single-purpose folder is self-explanatory until 2+ subfolders accumulate

body:
## Summary

Audit findings **CRIT-6** + **HIGH-8** ([`docs/question-bank-audit-2026-05-17.md`](docs/question-bank-audit-2026-05-17.md)) — fixed together because both touch the admin write path.

## CRIT-6 — Orphan-write prevention

Before: `acceptFlaggedQuestion` (the function that flips a needs-review row to live and optionally assigns a curriculum node) trusted any string as a `node_id`. An admin script call with `nodeId: "rw-99"` (or `""` or whitespace) wrote the question tied to a topic that doesn't exist — students opening the real `rw-00` saw nothing, and the orphan never showed up on any admin topic page either.

After: `nodeId` validated against the canonical `CONCEPT_SLUGS`-derived `NODE_ID_SET` at three layers:

1. **`taxonomy.ts`** — new `isValidNodeId(nodeId)` helper. Single source backed by `NODE_ID_SET = new Set(CONCEPT_SLUGS.map(c => c.nodeId))`.
2. **`schemas.ts`** — Zod `acceptFlaggedQuestionInputSchema.opts.nodeId` refines against `isValidNodeId`. Rejects `"rw-99"`, `""`, whitespace.
3. **`review.ts`** — `acceptFlaggedQuestion` re-checks inside the function so direct calls (bypassing the action layer) also refuse the orphan.

Semantics preserved:

| Input | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| `nodeId: undefined` | Leave `node_id` untouched (default) |
| `nodeId: null` | Explicitly clear `node_id` (admin intent) |
| `nodeId: string` | Must validate; reject otherwise |

## HIGH-8 — Per-choice gate

`AddQuestionForm.tsx` had two `subject === "reading"` gates:

- In `handleSubmit` (dropped per-choice explanations from the payload for math)
- In the JSX (hid the per-choice grid for math)

Admins typing trap-pattern explanations for math distractors saw them silently discarded on save. Both gates dropped. The bulk import path was already correct ([`bulk-import.ts:221-230`](src/lib/question-bank/bulk-import.ts)); manual admin entry now matches.

author: fuddlesworth
body:
Implements **Phase 3 (navigation & niri command vocabulary)** of niri-style scroll mode, on top of the Phase 2 window-lifecycle work. Scroll mode now scrolls its viewport to follow focus, exposes the niri command set on the keymap, supports drag-to-reorder, and excludes sticky windows.

## Milestones

**M1 — Viewport scrolling** (`c342a3f4`)
- Until now `resolveScrollLayout` pinned the focused column flush to the work-area's left edge — every focus change jumped the whole strip. The relative `viewOffset` is replaced by an absolute `scrollX` (the strip-x mapped to the working area's inner-left edge), and a pure `computeViewportScroll()` resolves it per `ScrollViewportMode`: `Fit` (minimum scroll — leaves an already-visible column untouched) or `Centered`. Fit is the default; the mode becomes a user setting in Phase 5. The daemon computes + stores it before each resolve.

**M2 — `consume` / `expel` shortcuts** (`22231f7a`)
- Focus / move / swap navigation was already routed to `ScrollEngine` — the daemon's nav dispatch is mode-agnostic via `ScreenModeRouter::engineFor()` and `ScrollEngine` implements the `IPlacementEngine` contract. The two niri ops with no keymap entry were consume and expel: new `Meta+Alt+I` / `Meta+Alt+O` shortcuts, wired end-to-end (configkeys → ConfigDefaults → ISettings → Settings → ShortcutManager → daemon handlers). The snap/autotile engines inherit the no-op `IPlacementEngine` default, so the shortcuts are harmlessly absorbed on their screens.

**M3 — Drag-to-reorder** (`7d8651d3`)
- A tiled scroll window can be reordered by dragging it: it keeps its tile slot during the move and, on release, its whole column is reordered to the strip slot nearest the drop point (`ScrollScreenState::moveColumnNextTo`, new `org.plasmazones.Scroll.windowDropped`). The effect picks the anchor from the resolved tile rects it already tracks; the engine does the pure index reorder.

**M4 — Sticky windows** (`d7507278`)
- Resolves the sticky-window question carried from Phase 2: a window pinned to all desktops is never tiled into a strip (it floats); pinning / un-pinning at runtime drops it from / re-adds it to the strip.

## Audit

Two `/code-audit` passes (5 domain-partitioned reviewers) ran on the branch — `a08b0991` (pass 1) and `0b9cdc7d` (pass 2). Pass 1 fixed a CRITICAL (interactive resize misclassified as a drag-to-reorder), drag-handler HIGH/MEDIUM defects, two stale doc sections, and test-coverage gaps; pass 2 fixed one MEDIUM in the drag state machine. Verdict: CLEAN.

## Notes
- No engine-logic regressions — **186/186 tests pass**, full build green incl. `kwin_effect_plasmazones`.
- Plan doc updated to mark Phase 3 complete (`68d35fbf`). Next: Phase 4 (widths/heights & viewport polish).

author: pietrocv
body:
## Descrição

Implementa o sistema de conquistas do jogo, conforme a issue #18, utilizando o padrão Observer por meio do `SignalBus`.

Foram adicionados um `Resource` para representar conquistas e um `AchievementManager` como autoload responsável por observar eventos do jogo, avaliar condições de desbloqueio e emitir notificações quando uma conquista é liberada.

Closes #18

## O que foi feito

- Criado o `Achievement`, contendo:
  - `id`
  - `name`
  - `description`
  - `unlocked`
  - `condition: Callable`

- Criado o `AchievementManager` como autoload.

- Adicionadas 6 conquistas iniciais:
  - Derrotar o primeiro inimigo
  - Derrotar 5 inimigos
  - Coletar 3 itens
  - Completar a primeira sala
  - Completar uma sala ainda com vida
  - Alcançar 100 pontos

- Adicionado o sinal `achievement_unlocked` no `SignalBus`.

- Integrado o HUD para exibir uma notificação temporária quando uma conquista é desbloqueada.

- Adicionada emissão inicial de vida no `Player`, permitindo que o sistema saiba o estado atual de vida do jogador.

- Adicionados atalhos de debug para facilitar testes durante o desenvolvimento:
  - `K`: simula inimigo derrotado
  - `I`: simula item coletado
  - `R`: simula sala concluída
  - `P`: adiciona 100 pontos

## Como testar

1. Com a janela do jogo em foco, usar os atalhos de debug:
   - Pressionar `K` uma vez deve desbloquear a conquista de primeiro inimigo.
   - Pressionar `K` cinco vezes deve desbloquear a conquista de derrotar 5 inimigos.
   - Pressionar `I` três vezes deve desbloquear a conquista de coletar 3 itens.
   - Pressionar `R` deve desbloquear a conquista de sala concluída.
   - Pressionar `P` deve desbloquear a conquista de 100 pontos.

2. Conferir se as notificações aparecem no HUD.

## Observações

Os atalhos de debug só executam em build de desenvolvimento (`OS.is_debug_build()`), servindo apenas para facilitar a validação local das conquistas.

author: ayutaz
body:
## Summary

HF 配布の `piper-plus-tsukuyomi-chan` 含む 6 言語サンプル 5/6 言語で確認された「終わりの方が二重に聞こえる」現象 (Issue #499) の Tier 1 workaround。 `VitsModel.infer()` は attention 展開を `ceil(w)` で行う一方、 `durations` output には raw float `w` を返すため、 EOS 領域に decoder leakage が乗り「最後の音節がもう一度鳴る」 ように聞こえる。 既存 `_trim_padding_by_durations` は Strategy A 短文 padding 時のみ EOS を切るが、 長文経路ではそのまま残るのが本症状。 本 PR は `_trim_eos_region` を追加し **全ての推論経路** で `ceil(durations[-1])` frames を末尾から切り落とす。

## Affected Components

- [x] Python (src/python/, src/python_run/)
- [ ] Rust (src/rust/)
- [ ] C# (src/csharp/)
- [ ] C++ (src/cpp/, CMakeLists.txt)
- [ ] Go (src/go/)
- [ ] WASM/npm (src/wasm/)
- [ ] Docker (docker/)
- [ ] CI/CD (.github/workflows/)
- [ ] Documentation (docs/, README*)

## Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactoring
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Dependencies

## Risk Level

- [x] **patch** — bug fix / internal refactor / docs only
- [ ] **minor** — new feature / additive API / no breaking change
- [ ] **major** — breaking change (API removal, schema migration, behavior reversal)

## Contract Impact

- [x] None — 既存 `_trim_padding_by_durations` の挙動 (Strategy A 経路) は無変更。 新規 `_trim_eos_region` は long-text 経路にのみ適用するため `docs/spec/short-text-contract.toml` の不変条件は変わらない。 cross-runtime mirror (Rust / Go / C# / WASM / C++) は別 PR で対応する想定。

## 変更内容

| 機能 | 動作 | これがないと起こること |
|------|------|----------------------|
| `_trim_eos_region` (新規 helper) | `audio` の末尾から `max(0, ceil(durations[-1]) - eos_max_frames) * hop_size` samples を切る。 `TRIM_EOS_MAX_FRAMES = 0` 既定で EOS region 全削除 | `ceil(w)` で展開された EOS frames に乗る decoder leakage が末尾に残り「最後の音節が再発音」 として聞こえる |
| `voice.py:_synthesize_ids_core` | `was_padded=False` かつ `durations` が利用可能な経路で `_trim_eos_region` を適用 | 長文 (`phoneme_ids >= MIN_PHONEME_IDS`) の合成結果に Issue #499 の doubled-tail が残る |
| `infer_onnx.py:main()` | 学習側 inference path にも同じ trim を適用 (cross-runtime contract mirror) | 学習デバッグや HF 配布サンプル再生成時に runtime と挙動が乖離する |
| `TestTrimEosRegion` × 2 (test_short_text_mitigation.py / test_infer_onnx.py) | 9 ケース: EOS 完全削除 / fractional duration の ceil / `eos_max_frames` override / 空配列 / `hop_size=0` / trim が audio を超える / 整数 duration unaffected by ceil | 将来 `_trim_eos_region` を変更した際に doubled-tail が静かに回帰する |

## 設計判断

- **EOS frame 1-2 個だけを切る最小修正にした理由**: 末尾の doubled-tail は decoder の attention 構造起因で、 raw audio に分散して乗る (`audio_frames = ceil(durations).sum()` で完全一致を実測)。 「audio 全体から ceil overhead 分を引く」 と途中音素まで切る副作用が大きく、 一方で「EOS region のみ削除」 は既存 Strategy A trim と同じ思想で副作用ゼロ。 計測上 2nd-peak amplitude が ~30 % 低下 (15535 → 10997)。 完全消去には Tier 2 (`durations = w_ceil` で再 export) か Tier 3 (model 再学習) が必要だが、 配布済モデルに対する即時 workaround として本 PR を切り出した
- **`was_padded` ブランチへの追加適用は行わなかった**: Strategy A の `_trim_padding_by_durations` は既に `eos_max_frames` を考慮した EOS trim を含むため、 二重適用を避けた
- **`durations is None` fallback は変更なし**: 旧 ONNX export (durations output なし) は本 trim を skip、 既存 `_trim_silence` 経路に follow する
- **cross-runtime mirror は別 PR**: Rust / Go / C# / WASM / C++ 5 ランタイムの mirror は本 PR スコープ外。 Python ランタイムで効果と回帰がなければ follow-up PR で展開予定。 memory `feedback_conservative_changes`: 小さく保守的な単位で

## Test Plan

- [ ] `uv run pytest src/python_run/tests/test_short_text_mitigation.py::TestTrimEosRegion -v --no-cov` で 9 件全 PASS (ローカル確認済)
- [ ] `uv run pytest src/python/tests/test_infer_onnx.py::TestTrimEosRegion -v --no-cov` で 9 件全 PASS (ローカル確認済 — cross-runtime contract mirror)
- [ ] `uv run pytest src/python_run/tests/ src/python/tests/test_infer_onnx.py --ignore=src/python_run/tests/test_http_timing.py --no-cov` で 523 passed / 20 skipped / 0 failed (regression 無)
- [ ] `uvx pre-commit run --files src/python/piper_train/infer_onnx.py src/python_run/piper/voice.py src/python/tests/test_infer_onnx.py src/python_run/tests/test_short_text_mitigation.py` 全 hook PASS (ruff / format / contract gates 確認済)
- [ ] CI で `python-tests.yml` の `Run runtime full tests` ステップ内 `tests/test_short_text_mitigation.py` が green (CI 直接実行対象)
- [ ] tsukuyomi-chan 6lang ONNX で `"こんにちは、つくよみちゃんです。"` を合成し、 末尾 `ceil(durations[-1])` frames = 2 frames (512 samples ≈ 23 ms) が trim されていること
- [ ] 既存 Strategy A 経路 (短文合成 `phoneme_ids < MIN_PHONEME_IDS`) で挙動が無変更であること (`_trim_padding_by_durations` 単独適用)

## Checklist

- [x] Tests pass locally
- [x] No GPL/LGPL dependencies added ([License Policy](CONTRIBUTING.md#license-policy))
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable) — 本 PR は internal helper の追加で公開 API 変更なし。 cross-runtime contract spec 化は別 PR で対応

## Related Issues

- Issue #499 (canonical doubled-tail bug 報告)
- 関連: Issue #356 (Strategy A `TRIM_EOS_MAX_FRAMES = 0` 導入の経緯)

body:
Wires the embedded HA Dashboard iframe to render in `mediamtxNeon` for visual continuity with the rest of this app.

Pairs with [iamjairo/Home-Assistant-Dashboard#5](https://github.com/iamjairo/Home-Assistant-Dashboard/pull/5) which adds `?theme=<name>` URL param support to Tunet. Merge order doesn't matter — if HA#5 isn't merged yet, the param is silently ignored by older Tunet builds, no harm done.

## Change

`client/src/components/Tabs/HomeAssistantTab.jsx` — `safeIframeUrl()` now appends `theme=mediamtxNeon` to the URL's search params before returning it.

```js
const EMBED_THEME = 'mediamtxNeon';
// ...
parsed.searchParams.set('theme', EMBED_THEME);
return parsed.href;
```

## Behavior

| Scenario | Result |
|---|---|
| User opens HA tab here | iframe loads with `?theme=mediamtxNeon`, Tunet renders in neon |
| User opens Tunet directly (separate browser) | Tunet uses their saved `tunet_theme` localStorage, no change |
| User changes theme inside the embedded Tunet | Their click wins from that point — param only fires on initial mount |
| Older Tunet (pre-#5) embedded | Param silently ignored, falls back to localStorage default |

## Test plan

- [ ] Open HA tab → confirm Tunet renders in dark slate / cyan neon
- [ ] Open Tunet directly in another window → confirm previous saved theme still applies
- [ ] Change theme in embedded Tunet → confirm switch works (no auto-revert to neon)

body:
## Summary

P1-40 Backlog item **H-WAGE-FULL** MVP — monthly salary breakdown (10d full → MVP ~3.5hr).

Adds `SalaryItem` entity + Service.computeFromBase + Vue list page covering the **core monthly salary workflow** (基本工资 → 社保 → 个税 → 实发), with state machine DRAFT → CONFIRMED → PAID.

## MVP scope shipped (this PR)

| Layer | File count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| Entity + enum | 2 | `SalaryItem`, `SalaryStatus` |
| Repository | 1 | `SalaryItemRepository` |
| Service | 2 | interface + impl (310 LOC, includes 7-bracket 个税) |
| Controller | 1 | 10 endpoints under `/api/mobile/{factoryId}/hr/salaries/*` |
| Flyway | 1 | `V20260606_18__hr_salary_items.sql` |
| Test | 1 | 20/20 PASS unit tests |
| Frontend | 3 | API client + Vue list page + router entry |

### Backend endpoints

- `POST /preview-compute` — R1 防呆 pure preview (no write)
- `POST` / `PUT /{id}` / `DELETE /{id}` — CRUD
- `POST /{id}/recompute` — re-derive social/tax/net from current baseSalary
- `POST /{id}/confirm` — DRAFT → CONFIRMED
- `POST /{id}/pay` — CONFIRMED → PAID
- `GET /{id}` / `GET` (list with yearMonth/status/userId filters) / `GET /summary` (月度汇总)

### 计算口径

- 个人社保 = base × 10.5% (养老 8 + 医疗 2 + 失业 0.5)
- 单位社保 = base × 26% (info-only)
- 个人/单位公积金 = base × 8% / 8%
- 应税收入 = base − 个人社保 − 个人公积金 − 5000 起征点
- 个税 = 7-bracket 月度 (3% / 10% / 20% / 25% / 30% / 35% / 45%)
- 实发 = base − 个人社保 − 个人公积金 − 个税

## Deferred to next batch (P2)

- 专项扣除 (子女教育 / 赡养老人 / 住房贷款 / 大病医疗 等 6 项)
- 年度汇算 (退税)
- 工资条 PDF 导出
- 公积金 percentage 配置 UI (当前 hardcode 8%/8%, F-specific config UI 后批)
- 复杂个税 brackets (年终奖单独计税)
- 复杂社保配置 (按城市/工种差异化基数与比例)
- 与 PayrollRecord (计件工资) 跨表合并视图

## 防呆 compliance (per `.claude/rules/fool-proof-design.md`)

- **R1 (预先显示边界)**: Vue dialog 实时 `watch baseSalary → POST /preview-compute` → 显示 base / 个人社保 / 公积金 / 应税收入 / 个税 / 实发 (上下文+单位社保/公积金 info-only)
- **R2 (上下文身份信息)**: response message + confirm dialog 一律 含 `用户 {userId} / {yearMonth} / 实发 ¥{net}`
- **R4 (幂等防重复)**: DB partial unique index (`uq_salary_factory_user_month` WHERE deleted_at IS NULL) + Service R4 `findByFactoryIdAndUserIdAndYearMonth` 抛 `BusinessException(409)` 含 existing id + status
- **State guards**: PAID 全锁; CONFIRMED 仅可改 remark; DRAFT 全字段可改
- **4位一体 error**: response message exact (server-side), frontend uses backend message via `request.ts` interceptor (sticky)

## Test plan

- [x] `./mvnw -DskipTests compile` — BUILD SUCCESS (2676 source files)

body:
Two small, related additions before MVP-done.

## 1. Persistent concept banner on the dashboard

\`index.html\` now renders a thin amber strip at the top of every page:

> ⚠️ **Concept project** — signals are unverified, geocoding is approximate. **Not for clinical, operational, or travel decisions.** [About]

Without this, anyone who lands on the live URL from a link (e.g. someone tweeting a screenshot of a SEVERE hantavirus marker) sees a polished surveillance dashboard with zero on-page indication that it's a concept. The README and meta tags already say so, but page viewers don't read READMEs. Closes the same trust-hygiene loop we fixed in the README framing.

## 2. Quiet cache flakes in the workflow

\`continue-on-error: true\` on both \`actions/cache/restore@v4\` and \`actions/cache/save@v4\`. Cache layer hiccups (GitHub Actions cache backend can transiently fail) shouldn't trigger \"workflow failed\" emails — baselines just rebuild on the next scan.

The scanner itself already swallows per-source API errors (GDELT 429s, Mastodon timeouts, Reddit auth failures) and exits cleanly with valid signals.json. Pages deploy remains strict (deploy failures are real failures).

## What this PR doesn't fix

GitHub still sends workflow-failed emails for *real* failures (Python crash, Pages deploy failure). To silence those entirely for this repo, the account holder needs to either:
- **Per-repo**: Watch → Custom → uncheck Actions
- **Account-wide**: <https://github.com/settings/notifications> → Actions → uncheck Email

Neither is API-controllable from a workflow.

author: felladrin
body:
## Problem

The `Docs CI` workflow's `generate-docs` job pushes a follow-up commit to PR branches after `tfplugindocs` regenerates docs. That commit message ends with `[skip ci]`, which GitHub Actions honors by skipping **every** subsequent workflow (`go.yml` lint & test, `security.yml` gosec/Trivy, etc.) on the PR's new HEAD commit.

Observable effect: a PR that originally had failing lint/test/gosec checks shows up as green after the docs bot's auto-commit lands, because only a handful of always-on jobs (CodeQL, Analyze) ignore the marker. Reviewers see green, merge, and the lint/test regressions ship to main.

Spotted while triaging a batch of feature PRs ([#945](https://github.com/aminueza/terraform-provider-minio/pull/945)–[#949](https://github.com/aminueza/terraform-provider-minio/pull/949)) whose actual code-quality checks never re-ran on the fix commits.

## Fix

Drop `[skip ci]` from both auto-commit messages in `.github/workflows/docs.yml`:

- L107 — the PR-branch path (the immediate bug)
- L99 — the main-branch path that opens a separate docs PR (same issue: the docs PR would otherwise open with CI suppressed)

No loop risk: the workflow already short-circuits via `git diff --cached --quiet` when there is nothing new to commit, so re-running CI on the doc-update commit will simply observe up-to-date docs and exit.

## After this merges

The 5 feature PRs ([#945](https://github.com/aminueza/terraform-provider-minio/pull/945)–[#949](https://github.com/aminueza/terraform-provider-minio/pull/949)) need to be rebased so their docs-bot follow-up commits get rewritten without the marker, then their full CI matrix can actually run.

author: amsach
body:
Fixed SyntaxWarnings for invalid escape sequences in regex patterns. Two regex patterns with escaped square brackets were using regular strings instead of raw strings, causing DeprecationWarning in Python 3.12+.

Before:
```python
re.search("\[IMG:[0-9]+\]", i)
re.search("(?<=\[IMG:)[0-9]+(?=\])", i)
```

After:
```python
re.search(r"\[IMG:[0-9]+\]", i)
re.search(r"(?<=\[IMG:)[0-9]+(?=\])", i)
```

Added r prefix to make them raw strings, eliminating the deprecation warnings. — Sent via @AmSach bot

author: kylestay
body:
This pull request makes significant improvements to the layout, responsiveness, and visual styling of the main display and CRT-related UI elements in `index.html`. The changes focus on enhancing the flexibility and appearance of the main display container, improving schema title handling, refining coordinate calculations for CRT effects, and updating z-index stacking for better layering of UI components.

**Styling and Layout Enhancements:**

* The `#mainDisplayContainer` and its children receive substantial CSS updates for improved responsiveness, padding, background gradients, borders, and box shadows. Special styles are added for when a schema title is present or when in "construct mode," making the UI more visually appealing and adaptive. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-0eb547304658805aad788d320f10bf1f292797b5e6d745a3bf617584da017051L220-R316)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-0eb547304658805aad788d320f10bf1f292797b5e6d745a3bf617584da017051L808-R862)`)
* The schema title display (`#schemaTitleDisplay`) now uses more flexible font sizing, improved alignment, and background styling, with additional adjustments for construct mode. (`[index.htmlL220-R316](diffhunk://#diff-0eb547304658805aad788d320f10bf1f292797b5e6d745a3bf617584da017051L220-R316)`)
* The selected name display and its wrapper are updated for better alignment, sizing, and responsiveness. (`[index.htmlL220-R316](diffhunk://#diff-0eb547304658805aad788d320f10bf1f292797b5e6d745a3bf617584da017051L220-R316)`)

**Responsiveness and Accessibility:**

* Media queries are updated to ensure the main display and title remain readable and well-sized on smaller screens. (`[index.htmlL808-R862](diffhunk://#diff-0eb547304658805aad788d320f10bf1f292797b5e6d745a3bf617584da017051L808-R862)`)
* The CRT canvas overlay now has `touch-action: none;` to prevent unwanted touch interactions on mobile devices. (`[index.htmlR124](diffhunk://#diff-0eb547304658805aad788d320f10bf1f292797b5e6d745a3bf617584da017051R124)`)

**Schema Title and Main Display Logic:**

* The `updateSchemaTitle` function is improved to toggle a `has-schema-title` class on the main display container, allowing for context-sensitive styling. It also marks the CRT snapshot as dirty when the title changes, ensuring the visual state stays in sync. (`[index.htmlL1873-R1938](diffhunk://#diff-0eb547304658805aad788d320f10bf1f292797b5e6d745a3bf617584da017051L1873-R1938)`)

**CRT Coordinate Calculations:**

* All CRT-related coordinate and safe area calculations now use the actual bounding rectangle of the CRT canvas instead of the full window size. This makes pointer mapping and safe area margins more accurate, especially in responsive layouts or embedded contexts. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-0eb547304658805aad788d320f10bf1f292797b5e6d745a3bf617584da017051L1531-R1589)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-0eb547304658805aad788d320f10bf1f292797b5e6d745a3bf617584da017051L2758-R2828)`, `[[3]](diffhunk://#diff-0eb547304658805aad788d320f10bf1f292797b5e6d745a3bf617584da017051L2775-R2842)`)

**Z-Index and Stacking Context Improvements:**

* Z-index values for the menu toggle button and side menu panel are adjusted to ensure correct layering and interactivity. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-0eb547304658805aad788d320f10bf1f292797b5e6d745a3bf617584da017051R354)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-0eb547304658805aad788d320f10bf1f292797b5e6d745a3bf617584da017051L380-R434)`)

These changes collectively modernize the UI, improve usability on various devices, and ensure accurate coordinate mapping for CRT effects.

author: cbeaulieu-gt
body:
Closes #109. Refs #91.

Phase 3 of the Postgres migration epic. The bot now has a single shared SQLAlchemy session factory that injects an AAD token on every new physical connection for Postgres URLs, with the pool tuned for the observed ~86-minute token TTL (spike #101 / `docs/spike/2026-05-17-postgres-aad-findings.md` § Charge 3). Local-dev SQLite paths are unchanged. Startup migrations (the artifact PR #95 introduced) are removed — Alembic is CI-only from here forward.

## What changed

### `src/mom_bot/db/__init__.py` — `build_session_factory()`

- AAD token injection via SQLAlchemy `do_connect` event listener, scope `https://ossrdbms-aad.database.windows.net/.default`
- `pool_recycle=4800` (80 min, 6 min margin under the observed 86-min token TTL)
- `pool_pre_ping=True` (pessimistic disconnect handling — catches token expiry, failover, network flaps)
- `pool_size=5, max_overflow=5` (10-connection ceiling; deploy-window worst-case 22/35 on B1ms)
- SQLite URLs bypass the hook entirely — unit tests + local dev unaffected
- `Base = DeclarativeBase` export preserved (`migrations/env.py:24` imports it)

### `src/mom_bot/main.py` — startup migrations removed

- `run_migrations()` body, alembic imports, `_ALEMBIC_INI`, `setup_hook` call site all deleted
- `_build_session_factory` is now `from mom_bot.db import build_session_factory as _build_session_factory` so existing `mom_bot.main._build_session_factory` patches keep working

### Tests

- **New**: `tests/test_db_token_injection.py` — 2 tests (SQLite no-op + Postgres token-stamp assertion). Written test-first.
- **Removed**: `tests/test_migrations_startup.py` (4 tests for `run_migrations` behavior that no longer exists by design)
- **Modified**: `tests/test_main_wireup.py` — `mock_run_migrations` fixture deleted

### Dockerfile

- Dropped `COPY alembic.ini ./` and `COPY migrations/ ./migrations/` — Alembic runs only in CI from Phase 4 onward
- Install step switched to `uv sync --frozen --no-dev`

### `.github/workflows/mini-spike-postgres-oidc.yml` — Charge 12 verification

One-off `workflow_dispatch` workflow that verifies the `mom-bot-gha` federated SP can mint a token for the `https://ossrdbms-aad.database.windows.net` audience. **This must be run + pass before Phase 4 begins** (gate documented in plan § Phase 4 Entry Criteria). Delete or disable after verification.

## Verification

| Check | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| pytest | `python -m pytest` | **134 passed**, 1 warning (baseline 138 → 134, delta = 4 deleted by design) |
| ruff | `python -m ruff check src/ tests/` | clean |
| black | `python -m black --check src/ tests/` | 37 files unchanged |
| mypy | `python -m mypy src/` | 19 files, no issues |
| actionlint | `actionlint .github/workflows/mini-spike-postgres-oidc.yml` | PASS |
| docker | `docker build .` against the worktree Dockerfile | exit 0, 42 packages installed via `uv sync --frozen --no-dev` |

## Acceptance criteria (from #109)

- [x] `pytest` is green
- [x] `grep -r "run_migrations" src/` returns nothing
- [x] `grep -r "run_migrations" tests/` reviewed; obsolete tests removed (deleted `test_migrations_startup.py`)
- [x] Container image still builds
- [x] `Dockerfile` no longer has `COPY alembic.ini` or `COPY migrations/`
- [x] `pool_recycle=4800`, `pool_pre_ping=True`, `pool_size=5`, `max_overflow=5` all set on the Postgres engine
- [ ] **`mini-spike-postgres-oidc.yml` dispatched + verified** — manual step, deferred to post-merge (see note below)

## Note on the mini-spike

The workflow file is included in this PR so it ships with `main`, but **actually dispatching it is a post-merge manual step**. It requires `AZURE_CLIENT_ID_GHA`, `AZURE_TENANT_ID`, and `AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID` repo secrets to be set. Once the workflow lands on `main`, the operator runs:

```bash
gh workflow run mini-spike-postgres-oidc.yml
gh run watch
```

A passing run unblocks Phase 4. A failing run requires resolving the federation configuration before Phase 4 can begin.

## Out of scope (deferred to Phase 4)

- KV `prod-database-url` secret swap to the Postgres DSN
- `deploy.yml` wiring for `alembic upgrade head`
- `ca-mom-bot` revision restart against Postgres

User reported `Syncing 0%` stuck forever (engine loaded ✓, address derived ✓). Root cause: `Wallet_init` was being given the full `https://xmr-rpc.iamhch.com` URL as `daemonAddress`, but monero_c expects `host:port` — so the native side DNS-resolved the literal scheme prefix, sat disconnected forever, and `Wallet_daemonBlockChainHeight()` returned 0 → UI parked on "Syncing 0%".

## Summary

- **Normalize `daemonUri` → `host:port`** before passing to `Wallet_init`; bail on init failure with `Wallet_errorString` instead of silently proceeding to `Wallet_startRefresh`.
- **Multi-node fallback**: try the user's daemon first, then Cake / HashVault / Seth. Each candidate is verified with `Wallet_connected` before commit (init alone returns true on unreachable hosts — that's why iamhch quietly bricked us).
- **Surface daemon state in UI**: red `Daemon: <error>` banner + "Connecting to daemon…" label instead of perpetual "Syncing 0%".
- **Fix `MoneroSession.start` race**: concurrent callers now share one in-flight `Future` instead of one of them getting `null` and showing a spurious "unknown" error.
- **Lock / wipe now tear down the native wallet**: `VaultState.lock()` previously cleared the mnemonic but left the FFI engine running with keys in memory and a sync thread polling the daemon.

## Commits

- `f5c8075` — daemonUri normalization + error surfacing
- `6497840` — fallback nodes, session race, lock teardown

## Test plan

- [ ] CI green (analyze + tests)
- [ ] Install the rebuilt APK, open the Monero screen — confirm balance label progresses past "Syncing 0%" or, if all nodes are down, shows a red `Daemon:` banner with a real reason
- [ ] Lock the app, reopen, unlock — Monero session restarts cleanly
- [ ] No regression on the new-wallet / import flows

author: aaddrick
body:
## Summary

Hardens the Voyage embedding driver and the reindex pipeline against rate limiting, and adds an opt-in live probe to `commonplace:doctor`.

- **Driver-level 429 backoff** — `VoyageEmbeddingProvider::embedBatch()` now retries each 128-input chunk on HTTP 429 with exponential backoff + 0–200ms jitter (`base * 2^attempt`, capped at 30s). Knobs: `commonplace.embedding.voyage.retry_max` (default 3) and `retry_base_delay` (default 1.0s, env `VOYAGE_RETRY_MAX` / `VOYAGE_RETRY_BASE_DELAY`). Non-429 failures (5xx, timeouts) still throw immediately — those aren't transient on the same timescale.
- **Partial-batch progress** — when a later chunk fails after retries but earlier chunks succeeded, the driver throws `PartialBatchEmbeddingException` (already used by Bedrock) carrying the completed vectors. `ReindexNotes::handle()` catches it, checkpoints the completed notes (`indexed_at` set, vector stored), and leaves the failed remainder `indexed_at IS NULL` so the next run picks them up. Logs `warning` with `completed` / `remaining` counts.
- **Doctor probe** — `commonplace:doctor` gains a `--live` flag (and equivalent `commonplace.doctor.probe_embedding_provider` / `COMMONPLACE_DOCTOR_PROBE_EMBEDDING` config) that calls `embedQuery('doctor probe')` on the configured provider. Off by default so routine doctor runs don't burn paid API quota. Reports `[OK]` with vector length, `[FAIL]` with the upstream message, or `[SKIP]` when disabled.

Docs updated: `docs/embedding-drivers.md` (Voyage "Rate limits and failure modes" rewritten), `docs/commands.md` (`--live` flag documented).

Closes #86.

## Test plan

All 451 tests pass; pint clean; phpstan clean (with `--memory-limit=512M`).

Targeted runs:

- [x] `vendor/bin/phpunit --filter Voyage` — 20 tests / 52 assertions
  - `test_embed_batch_retries_on_429_then_succeeds`
  - `test_embed_batch_gives_up_after_retry_max_429s`
  - `test_embed_batch_does_not_retry_on_500`
  - `test_embed_batch_backoff_is_exponential_with_jitter` (asserts the exponential-with-jitter window via `Sleep::assertSlept`)
  - `test_embed_batch_surfaces_partial_progress_when_second_chunk_fails`
  - `test_embed_batch_throws_runtime_when_first_chunk_fails_with_no_progress`
  - `test_embed_batch_does_not_sleep_on_success`
- [x] `vendor/bin/phpunit --filter ReindexNotes`
  - `test_partial_batch_exception_checkpoints_completed_notes` — asserts 2 of 3 notes land `indexed_at`, third stays NULL, warning logged with counts
- [x] `vendor/bin/phpunit --filter Doctor`
  - `test_embedding_provider_probe_skipped_by_default`
  - `test_embedding_provider_probe_runs_with_live_flag`
  - `test_embedding_provider_probe_runs_when_config_flag_set`
  - `test_embedding_provider_probe_fails_when_provider_throws`
- [x] `vendor/bin/phpunit` (full suite) — 451 / 12 skipped / 0 failed
- [x] `vendor/bin/pint` — passed

body:
## Summary

Closes Cowork's **P0** finding on PR #34's QA pass. The chat was persisting the host brief correctly (got a real `projectId` back from `upsertProjectFromBrief`), but the "Review brief" CTA still pointed at `/projects/new` — Sagasan's default nextStep route. The `bindNextStepToProject` helper described in earlier conversation summaries had never actually landed in the codebase. Without it, the entire downstream tracer (`/crew`, `/outreach`) was unreachable end-to-end.

Also closes Cowork's **P2** finding (cross-PR): `/projects/[slug]` rendered blank chrome instead of 404 when the slug looked like a cuid but didn't resolve. Honest 404 now.

## What this PR does

1. **Add `bindNextStepToProject(nextStep, projectId)`** in `src/lib/webChatNextStep.ts`.
   - When `nextStep.route === "/projects/new"` AND `projectId` is non-null: rewrites to `/projects/<projectId>` and strips prefill (the brief review page reads from the Project row, not URL params).
   - No-op when projectId is null, nextStep is null, or route isn't `/projects/new`.
   - Idempotent: already-bound routes pass through.

2. **Wire it into `src/app/api/web-chat/route.ts`** in both return paths (holding/gated + LLM/autonomous), called immediately after `persistBriefAndAdvanceJourney` returns the projectId.

3. **Update `getPersonaFromNextStep`** to recognise `/projects/<cuid>` as a host route alongside `/projects/new`. Before, the cuid form fell through to `null` and broke top-nav persona chips after the rewrite.

4. **Make `/projects/[slug]/page.tsx` call `notFound()`** when the slug looks like a cuid but no Project row resolves. Previously rendered blank chrome.

## Tests

author: lefoulkrod
body:
## Summary

Two related changes on the same branch:

1. **iCloud Drive as a new integration** — backed by a fresh `rclone_broker`. Connects via an Apple ID sign-in + 2FA flow in the Add Integration wizard, persists a trust token, and runs against the iCloud Drive remote that rclone supports out of the box.
2. **Unified Drive tool surface** — collapses the per-backend tool sets into one. The agent now sees seven `drive_*` tools that work against both Google Drive and iCloud Drive; the only Google-only tool is `drive_share`. Tools take an opaque `handle` string (`id:<file_id>` for Drive, a slash-path for rclone); `drive_list` returns handles in its output so the agent doesn't have to know the format.

## Implementation map

**iCloud Drive feature (commits 1–5)**

- `integrations/brokers/rclone_broker/` — new broker. Shells out to `rclone` against the `default:` remote, which the supervisor configures entirely via `RCLONE_CONFIG_DEFAULT_*` env vars (no config file).
- `_ICLOUD_DRIVE` catalog entry — slug `icloud_drive`, `Capability.DRIVE: READ_WRITE`, injects Apple ID / password / 2FA trust token as the rclone env vars, binds the shared `downloads` host path.
- `integrations/_icloud_auth.py` — direct Apple ID sign-in + 2FA flow, returns a long-lived trust token.
- `server/_icloud_drive_routes.py` — two routes under `/api/integrations/preauth/icloud-drive` for the trust-token exchange.
- `server/ui/.../add-wizard/IcloudDriveSteps.jsx` — new `app_password_2fa` flow: explainer → Apple ID creds (triggers 2FA push) → code entry (verifies + adds). `icloud_drive` provider added to `providers.js` and to `IntegrationsTab.jsx`.
- `container/Dockerfile` — installs `rclone` from the official .deb.

**Drive tool unification (commits 6–9)**

- `integrations/brokers/google_workspace_broker/` — adds canonical `drive_list / drive_download / drive_upload / drive_mkdir / drive_move / drive_delete / drive_share` verbs. `DriveClient` gets `resolve_path`, `list_in_parent_matching`, and `move_file`. Legacy per-API verbs removed.
- `integrations/brokers/rclone_broker/_verbs.py` — same canonical verb names and shapes. Legacy rclone-flavored verbs removed.
- `tools/integrations/drive/` — rewritten as one tool set used by both backends; `tools/integrations/icloud_drive/` deleted.
- `sdk/tools/_core.py` — registers the seven unified tools gated purely on `Capability.DRIVE`. `drive_share` is the one tool gated on `slug == "google_workspace"`.

## Manual verification needed (can't be checked here)

These are the things only a running container can confirm:

- **rclone iclouddrive env-var names** — I used `RCLONE_CONFIG_DEFAULT_APPLE_ID / _PASSWORD / _TRUST_TOKEN` per current rclone docs. If rclone rejects the plaintext password, the supervisor's spawn path needs an `rclone obscure` step before injection.
- **Apple auth endpoints** — `integrations/_icloud_auth.py` calls Apple's undocumented sign-in surface directly. If 2FA never delivers a code or the trust step returns an unexpected status, that module is where to look.
- **Drive-share docstring** lists only `google_workspace` integration IDs — confirmed by a unit test, but worth eyeballing in a running agent's tool list.

## Test plan

- [ ] `just build` (rclone install lands cleanly in the new image)
- [ ] `just dev` + connect iCloud Drive via the wizard; integration lands as `running`
- [ ] Agent calls `drive_list` and `drive_download` against the new integration
- [ ] Existing Google Workspace integration still works end-to-end (the rename is internal — no migration needed, but worth a spot-check)
- [ ] Confirm `drive_share` is visible for Google but not for iCloud Drive

## Notes for the reviewer

- `origin/main` moved ~27 commits while this branch was open (ARM64, context-window work, browser fixes). The only file both sides touched is `container/Dockerfile` — main reorganized the section around where I added the rclone block. May need a small rebase, or resolve in the GitHub merge UI.
- 1,248 unit tests pass on this branch. UI builds cleanly.
- The branch is on top of `4bd4db8` (where I started); not yet rebased onto current `main`.

author: artemiopadilla
body:
## Problem

The personal site's root-scoped Workbox service worker (`scope: "/"`, `registerType: "autoUpdate"`) shadows the separate `/mexico-weather-site/` project deployed at `artemiop.com/mexico-weather-site/`. The SW's SPA navigation fallback serves the main site's app-shell for ANY path under `artemiop.com/`, so users navigating to `/mexico-weather-site/` get the main site instead of the weather site unless they hard-reload (bypassing the SW).

## Root cause

Root-scoped PWA service worker SPA navigation fallback shadowing the project path. This exact problem was already solved for the sibling `/watchboard/` project in `astro.config.mjs`; `/mexico-weather-site/` was simply missing from the same carve-outs.

## Fix

Mirrors the existing `watchboard` carve-out exactly, for `mexico-weather-site`, in `astro.config.mjs` → `AstroPWA` `workbox` config:

- `globIgnores`: add `"**/mexico-weather-site/**"`
- `navigateFallbackDenylist`: add `/^\/mexico-weather-site/`
- `runtimeCaching`: add the two analogous `NetworkOnly` entries for `artemiop.com/mexico-weather-site/.*` and `artemiopadilla.github.io/mexico-weather-site/.*`
- Updated the explanatory comment to mention both projects

No other changes (manifest, scope, other runtimeCaching entries untouched; no reformatting).

## Verification

- `npm ci` + `npm run build` (full gate: validate:cv / validate:graph / astro build) succeeded
- Generated `dist/sw.js` contains the `mexico-weather-site` denylist regex and both `NetworkOnly` routes, alongside the existing `watchboard` ones
- No `mexico-weather-site` (or `watchboard`) URLs appear in the precache manifest

## Note on propagation

Because of `registerType: "autoUpdate"`, already-affected visitors keep the OLD service worker until it updates. On their next visit Workbox fetches the new SW and activates it (may take one extra reload for clients that currently have the stale SW controlling the page). New visitors, and anyone after the SW updates, get the correct behavior. This is inherent to SW update propagation, not a defect in the fix. Affected users can also unregister the old SW / hard-reload once to get the fix immediately.

## Summary
Phase 1 of the specialty-tag schema refactor. **Schema-only PR** — no UI, filter, or data changes. Plan archived at `~/X-Glass/plans/2026-05-18-specialty-tag-refactor.md`.

Splits the flat \`specialtyTags\` array into two orthogonal dimensions so the hidden parent-child relationships become explicit:

- **\`isCine?: boolean\`** — product positioning (photo vs cinema). Maps to the upcoming Usage filter (Photo / Cine).
- **\`opticalTraits?: OpticalTrait[]\`** — flat optical / form-factor traits (\`macro\`, \`anamorphic\`, \`tilt\`, \`shift\`, \`fisheye\`, \`probe\`). No implicit pairing.

\`ultra_macro\` drops out — it is fully derivable from \`maxMagnification.value >= 1.0\` and was redundant.

\`specialtyTags\` is kept and marked \`@deprecated\`. Pipeline will dual-write old + new fields during the migration window; this field is removed once pipeline stops emitting it.

## Why now
\`specialtyTags\` mixed three different concerns in one array (product positioning, optical traits, form factor) and relied on doc-comment conventions like "always pair ultra_macro with macro" or "anamorphic example pairs with cine" that the schema didn't enforce. Pipeline had to remember these conventions on write; consumers had to know them on read. Splitting eliminates the implicit rules.

## What this PR does NOT do
- No pipeline changes — that's the next PR in x-glass-pipeline.
- No UI / filter changes — the Usage filter PR depends on pipeline shipping dual-write first.
- No data migration — current \`lenses.json\` continues to validate (new fields are optional, \`specialtyTags\` still accepted).

author: jeremiahjrross
body:
## Summary

Third of four B15 sub-PRs. Replaces the inline `arize_annotations` call
in the backend's feedback router with a pluggable `FeedbackSink`
interface defined in the new `flowrun_runtime` package and implemented
by two community sinks (`Noop`, `Phoenix`) plus a vendor-coupled
`ArizeFeedbackSink` that lives in `flowrun-platform/platform-extensions/`
per the file-mapping table in `docs/flowrun/02_Architecture.md` §2.5.

The backend now imports a Protocol, not an SDK — the operator chooses
the sink via `FEEDBACK_SINK={noop,phoenix}` and Phoenix endpoint / auth
via `PHOENIX_ENDPOINT` / `PHOENIX_API_KEY`. Vendor specificity no longer
leaks into the community application surface.

### New: `flowrun-community/runtime/` (the runtime package)

Bootstrapped as a real installable package (`flowrun-runtime`). PR3
ships only the `FeedbackSink` surface — the rest of the runtime (sidecar
runner, capability providers, OTel glue) lands across B17–B27. CI's
`runtime` job activates as soon as `runtime/pyproject.toml` exists.

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `flowrun_runtime/feedback_sink.py` | `FeedbackEvent` dataclass; `FeedbackSink` Protocol (`post` + `aclose`); `NoopFeedbackSink` (community default); `PhoenixFeedbackSink` (POSTs `/v1/span_annotations` via httpx, `annotator_kind=HUMAN`, fail-open) |
| `pyproject.toml` | Strict mypy, ruff E/F/W/I/UP/B/SIM, httpx as the only runtime dep |
| `tests/test_feedback_sink.py` | **16 tests** — Protocol conformance, Noop drop+log, Phoenix URL composition / payload shape / auth header / fail-open on 4xx / fail-open on network errors / blank-span skip / aclose-owns / aclose-injected |

### New: `flowrun-platform/platform-extensions/` (vendor plug-ins home)

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `flowrun_platform_extensions/feedback_arize.py` | `ArizeFeedbackSink` ported from the legacy `arize_annotations.py`. Lazy SDK client; blocking call off-loaded via `asyncio.to_thread`; fail-open. The only sanctioned home for `import arize` in the source tree (the platform forbidden-imports check excludes `platform-extensions/` by design — architecture §7.1). |
| `pyproject.toml` | Depends on `flowrun-runtime` for the Protocol; `[arize]` optional extra pins the SDK + pandas; `[dev]` includes pandas so tests exercise the DataFrame-shaping logic against a fake client |
| `tests/test_feedback_arize.py` | **10 tests** — Protocol conformance, required-field validation, Arize wire-payload columns, blank-span skip, fail-open on SDK exceptions, silent drop when client init fails, aclose drops cache, cached client reused |

### Backend changes (`flowrun-community/apps/backend/`)

- **`app/services/feedback_sink_factory.py`** — builds the configured
  sink from `settings.FEEDBACK_SINK`. Unknown selections, blank Phoenix
  endpoints, and unrecognised values all fall back to `NoopFeedbackSink`
  with a warning — observability config never blocks startup.
- **`app/main.py`** — lifespan calls `build_feedback_sink()` once and
  hangs the instance off `app.state.feedback_sink`; shutdown calls
  `sink.aclose()`. The sink lifecycle now matches the OTel one.
- **`app/routers/feedback.py`** — replaces the B15-PR1 TODO with the
  real call. `submit_feedback` builds a `FeedbackEvent` from the
  persisted `CaseFeedback` row and fires
  `asyncio.create_task(sink.post(event))`. Persistence path and user
  response are unchanged.
- **`app/config.py`** — adds `FEEDBACK_SINK` (default `noop`),
  `PHOENIX_ENDPOINT` (default `http://localhost:6006`), `PHOENIX_API_KEY`.
- **`pyproject.toml`** — declares `flowrun-runtime` as a runtime dep.
- **`tests/test_feedback_sink_factory.py`** — **6 tests** pinning the
  factory selection table.

### CI changes

- **`flowrun-community-ci.yml`** — backend job now installs the
  `flowrun-runtime` editable install before the backend (mirrors the
  `flowrun-sdk` pattern); both venvs pin Python 3.12 so the runtime
  package's `requires-python = ">=3.12"` resolves.
- **`flowrun-platform-ci.yml`** — new `platform-extensions` job runs
  ruff / format / mypy / pytest against `platform-extensions/`,
  installing the sibling `flowrun-runtime` first. Also triggers on
  `flowrun-community/runtime/**` changes since extensions depend on the
  Protocol shape there.

## Test plan

- [x] `cd flowrun-community/runtime && pytest` — **16/16 pass**
- [x] `cd flowrun-platform/platform-extensions && pytest` — **10/10 pass**
- [x] `cd flowrun-community/apps/backend && pytest` — **102/102 pass** (96 from PR2 + 6 new factory tests)
- [x] `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` + `mypy` clean for all three packages
- [x] `python3 flowrun-community/.ci/check_forbidden_imports.py` — `OK (85 files scanned)`
- [x] `python3 flowrun-platform/.ci/check_forbidden_imports.py` — `OK (0 files scanned)` (platform apps land later)
- [x] `python -c "from app.main import app"` boots — title `FlowRun`, 46 routes
- [ ] CI green on `flowrun-community-ci` and `flowrun-platform-ci`

## Follow-ups

- **B15-PR4** — generic `POST /cases` accepting `{agent_id, user_inputs}`.
  Last sub-PR of B15.

author: nekostul
body:
### Motivation
- Prevent unnecessary lyrics queries and UI flicker when lyrics have already been cached for a track by using the existing `manualLyricsRef` cache. 
- Reduce visual loading noise and prevent spurious open/close transitions while switching tracks by removing loader-driven branching and suppressing automatic refetch triggers. 

### Description
- Make `useResolvedLyrics` consult a `manualLyricsRef` cache (`cachedLyrics`) and disable the `lyricsQuery`/`resolvedQuery` when cached lyrics exist by adding `!cachedLyrics` to their `enabled` checks. 
- Disable automatic refetch triggers on window focus/reconnect/mount for the lyrics queries by setting `refetchOnWindowFocus`, `refetchOnReconnect`, and `refetchOnMount` to `false`. 
- Persist auto-resolved lyrics into `manualLyricsRef` only when there is not already cached lyrics, and compute returned `data` as `cachedLyrics ?? autoLyrics`, and make `isLoading` respect cached presence. 
- Remove several UI loading states and the manual search fallback button in fullscreen lyrics paths, and stop passing the removed `isLoading` prop to `FullscreenLyricsColumn` so the panel avoids showing transient loaders during track switches. 
- Simplify panel open/close logic on track change to rely on cached lyrics presence and avoid closing the panel during short load windows. 

### Testing
- Ran TypeScript build (`yarn build`) to validate types and the module compiles successfully. - Passed unit tests with `yarn test` (Jest) for the components affected. - Linting (`yarn lint`) completed without new errors.

## What this does

Adds Docker configuration so anyone can spin up the project locally with one command - no Python install or virtual environment needed.

## Changes

- **Dockerfile**: builds the Django app in a Python 3.12 container
- **docker-compose.yml**: runs the app and handles migrations on startup
- **requirements.txt**: pins Django to 6.0.5 (was missing from the repo)
- **urdp/settings.py**: updated `ALLOWED_HOSTS` to accept localhost connections from Docker

## Prerequisites

- **Docker Desktop**: https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop
- Or a lightweight alternative: **Docker CLI + Colima**
  - `brew install colima && brew install docker`

## How to run

If you installed **Docker Desktop**, it handles the engine for you; skip to the next step.

If you installed the **Docker CLI + Colima**, start the engine first:
```
colima start
```

Spin up the project:

| | Command |
|---|---|
| Docker Desktop | `docker compose up --build` |
| Docker CLI | `docker-compose up --build` |

Then visit http://localhost:8000/asylum-intake/

To create an admin account:

| | Command |
|---|---|
| Docker Desktop | `docker compose exec web python manage.py createsuperuser` |
| Docker CLI | `docker-compose exec web python manage.py createsuperuser` |

body:
### Motivation
- Enable installing Chrome extensions as local plugins and provide a richer plugin runtime with UI surfaces (popup/side-panel) and background scripts.  
- Improve developer experience with an integrated console and multi-tab browsing UI.  
- Persist plugin packages on disk and support localized extension names and editable package files.  

### Description
- Expanded `ChromeExtensionInstaller` to resolve localized `manifest.json` names, list and replace files inside CRX/ZIP packages, and expose helpers like `resolveExtensionName`, `listFilePaths`, and `replaceTextFileInZip`.  
- Reworked plugin model and storage: plugins now store `packageFileName` on disk (migration from inline base64), include `sidePanelPath` and `optionsPage`, and migration logic writes legacy packages to `files/plugin_packages`.  
- Added a full plugin manager UI and editor in `MainActivity` with actions to install from Chrome Web Store, view/edit package files, run plugins, open popup/side-panel/options pages, and update permissions.  
- Implemented background plugin runtimes using hidden `WebView`s, a runtime messaging bridge (`PluginBridge`), and a Chrome-compat bootstrap layer that implements `chrome.runtime`, `chrome.tabs`, `chrome.scripting`, `chrome.sidePanel` and related APIs for extension pages.  
- Added local serving for extension resources at `https://chrome-extension.local/<id>/...`, proxying and injecting bootstrap code into HTML, and utilities to create popup windows and a docked side panel with drag/minimize behavior.  
- Improved developer console injection to load Eruda synchronously, and added tab management (create/switch/close) with UI elements and state save/restore.  
- UI and resource polish: new drawable assets, updated `activity_main.xml` layout for top/bottom bars, progress bar gradients, and search bar styling.  

### Testing
- Unit tests in `ChromeExtensionInstallerTest` were updated and executed, including `extractZipFromCrx_acceptsRawZip`, `collectBackgroundScriptPaths_supportsMv2AndMv3`, `parseCrxPayload_resolvesLocalizedManifestName`, and `resolveExtensionName_fallsBackAcrossAvailableLocales`, and they passed.  
- Manual smoke flows exercised installing a CRX, opening plugin popup/side-panel, and running plugin scripts during development (no automated UI tests were added in this change).

author: bruceperens
body:
I have performed a deep, comprehensive review of the `database_management` module. 

Key improvements include:
1. **Security & Validation:** Implemented strict input validation in the High Availability Wizard (`PgHaWizard`). It now uses regex to enforce IPv4 formats and requires a minimum of 8 characters for replication passwords. Fixed potential `TypeError` in validation logic for empty fields.
2. **Bug Fixes:** Resolved a critical issue in UI tours where the use of `?debug=1` triggered illegal redirects to `/odoo/discuss` in Odoo 19, causing tour failures.
3. **Code Quality (AI Laziness):** Refactored `db_stats.py` to remove catch-all `Exception` blocks. These were replaced with specific exceptions (`subprocess.CalledProcessError`, `OSError`, `AccessError`, `UserError`) and `_logger.exception()` to ensure "fail-fast" behavior and better traceability.
4. **Documentation:** 
   - `data/documentation.html` was completely rewritten to provide a step-by-step, jargon-free guide for Site Reliability Engineers and DBAs.
   - `README.md` was updated to include "Input Validation" in the Security section.
   - Added `static/description/index.html` (synced with `documentation.html`) for the Odoo Apps interface.
5. **Testing:** Added new test cases in `test_pg_config.py` to verify the new validation logic and ensured binary execution is bypassed during tests where the underlying OS tools might be missing.

All 25 tests for the module (standard and integration) pass successfully. I also verified that no regressions were introduced to the wider community codebase.

Note for `check_burn_list.py`: I have replaced existing `audit-ignore-catch-all` markers with better handling. I recommend that `check_burn_list.py` be updated to also flag `_logger.warning("Error: %s", e)` inside catch-all blocks as insufficient, favoring `_logger.exception()` or specific re-raising.

author: natsukium
body:
Thanks for the great work on paneru — it's become a daily driver for me.

I noticed the active-window border flickering every time my finger landed on the trackpad to move the cursor (without swiping). Digging into it, a bare `Event::TouchpadDown` was inserting a zero-velocity `Scrolling` component; `update_overlays` then hid the border for that frame, and the next `swiping_timeout` tick removed the component again — so the border blinked off and back on with every cursor touch.

Looking at git history, this seems to have regressed in c59ccd06 (`fix: Accumulate the scrolling events for swiping.`). Before that commit, `Event::TouchpadDown` only updated an existing `Scrolling` component and then `continue`d, so a bare `TouchpadDown` never created a new one. The refactor unified handling into `else if has_scroll_event || touchpad_down`, which accidentally added an insertion path for `TouchpadDown` alone.

I tried dropping `|| touchpad_down` from the insertion guard. Inertia-stopping still works because when a `Scrolling` already exists (the strip is gliding), `TouchpadDown` is handled in the `if let Some(scrolling)` branch — which zeros velocity and sets `is_user_swiping = true`, matching pre-c59ccd06 behavior. The flicker is gone on my machine and ongoing swipes / inertia behave as before.

Thanks in advance for taking a look!

body:
## Summary

Implements **R-00** (D-A8, D-F1): captures the full pre-existing live
`public` schema into a baseline migration so `supabase/migrations/` is a
complete, reproducible history. Before this, the repo held only the lone
Sprint-9 file and the rest of the schema existed only in prod (built via
dashboard/MCP).

- New file: `supabase/migrations/20260508080000_r00_baseline_schema.sql` —
  15 tables, all RLS policies (standard per-user + the shared-`ingredients`
  open-SELECT/INSERT/creator-only set), the 4 user RPCs, the
  `handle_new_user` + `mark_week_diverged` trigger fns/triggers, the
  `body_measurements_smoothed` view, and the `extensions`-schema extensions
  (`uuid-ossp`, `pgcrypto`, `pg_trgm`, `btree_gist`). Reconstructed
  **read-only** from `information_schema`/`pg_catalog` introspection.
- `docs/roadmap.md`: R-00 → `done (2026-05-18)`; notes
  R-03/R-04/R-08/R-12/R-14 + R-16-Tier-3 unblocked.
- `docs/operations.md`: Schema-in-migrations status rewritten — baseline now
  exists, `⚠ Changing — see R-00` callout removed, sequence + Wave-3 split
  documented, regen/verify commands added, and the `supabase db`
  reproducibility check recorded as a Wave-3 validation item.

### Migration-ordering decision

Apply order is filename-lexicographic:

```
20260508080000_r00_baseline_schema.sql      # THIS — pre-Sprint-9 baseline
20260514120000_sprint9_cron_and_jobs.sql    # Sprint 9 cron/RPC/Vault helper
20260518000000_r06_fat_pct_check.sql        # STAGED Wave-3
20260518010000_r18_cron_healthcheck.sql     # STAGED Wave-3
20260518020000_r07_adaptive_tdee_state.sql  # STAGED Wave-3
```

The baseline is timestamped **before** the repo's Sprint-9 file and
deliberately **excludes** every object Sprint-9 already owns (`pg_net`/
`pg_cron`, the `private` schema + `invoke_edge_function`,
`apply_template_to_week_admin`, the `tdee_estimates (user_id, computed_on)`
unique constraint, the 3 cron jobs). So `baseline + sprint9` together equal
the full live schema with **no double-create**, and the staged Wave-3 files
layer on top cleanly. The baseline reflects the schema **as it is now** — it
does not contain the staged R-06 CHECK / R-18 cron / R-07 `tdee_state` /
R-03/R-08/R-14 drops / R-12 RPC (those remain separate staged files).

### Non-destructive / no mutation

This is repo-only. The live prod DB was **not** modified. Only read-only
Supabase MCP introspection was used: `list_projects`, `list_tables`,
`list_extensions`, `list_migrations`, and `execute_sql` with **SELECT-only**
queries against `information_schema`/`pg_catalog`/`cron.job`. Zero
mutating MCP calls (`apply_migration`, mutating `execute_sql`,
`deploy_edge_function`, `create_branch`, etc.) were made. CI does not run
migrations and prod already has every object, so the file is **not applied**;
guarded DDL (`create … if not exists` / `do $$ … exception when
duplicate_object`) makes a future prod re-apply a verified no-op — that
verification is itself a tracked Wave-3 item.

author: dbmaps
body:
### Motivation
- The layered fallback audit was producing `commuteAuditRawMinusActiveDiffMethod: "not_evaluated"` and `exclusionSource: "fallback_placeholder"` even when raw snapshots existed, indicating the need for a single authoritative audit trace. 
- The intent is to add a direct, audit-only trace from the raw unified snapshot to the active snapshot so missing incidents are reported plainly without additional fallback layering.

### Description
- Exposed new direct audit fields in the `gridlyCommuteIntelligenceAudit()` output: `directCommuteAuditRawCount`, `directCommuteAuditRawIds`, `directCommuteAuditActiveCount`, `directCommuteAuditActiveIds`, `directCommuteAuditMissingFromActiveCount`, `directCommuteAuditMissingFromActiveIds`, and `directCommuteAuditMissingFromActiveReasons`.
- Added null-safe reset defaults for the new direct fields in the audit initialization so they are zeros/empty arrays when sources are unavailable.
- Implemented the direct raw→active trace inside the audit build path by calling `getUnifiedIncidents()` and `getActiveUnifiedIncidents()`, mapping IDs via a shared accessor, computing the set-diff, and publishing counts, ID lists, and detailed missing reasons.
- Each missing reason entry includes the requested metadata (`incidentId`, `type`, `source`, `status`, `lifecycle`, `rawStatus`, `normalizedStatus`, `rawLifecycle`, `normalizedLifecycle`, `hasLatLng`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `ageMinutes`) and fixed `reason: "raw_unified_not_in_active_incidents"` and `stage: "direct_raw_to_active_trace"`, and the change is audit-only with no production filtering/behavior modifications.

### Testing
- Ran `node --check js/app.js` which completed successfully.

body:
feat(round2): trim payloads, fix N+1 hot paths, expose more LLM internals

## Performance

Backend:
- Split TradeOut -> TradeListItem (light) + TradeOut (full); /api/trades adds offset pagination.
- /api/reviews adds offset; new /api/reviews/by-trade/{trade_id} for direct trade lookup.
- POST /api/reviews/generate/{trade_id} switches to BackgroundTasks; new /api/llm/stream/review/{job_id} SSE endpoint streams thinking + text deltas.
- New /api/models/summary returns StrategyModel + ModelStat + recent R-multiples in one round-trip; replaces 1+N+N.
- /api/models/{name}/recent-trades now returns RMultipleScatterPoint (4 fields) instead of full TradeOut. ~90% payload cut for the scatter chart.
- paper_trading_service.update_all_open_positions: bulk-load Trade rows + one GROUP BY for latest 1h bar; was 2N round-trips.
- daily_report_job: func.max(equity) replaces full-history Python scan; one JOIN instead of per-position db.get(Trade).
- trade_review_job: bulk-fetch existing review_ids in one IN query; was N+1.
- indicator_service: batch UPSERT, skips timestamps already in the DB; ~98% fewer SELECTs per scheduler tick.
- New Cache-Control middleware: append-only resources cache hard, lists cache briefly.
- New indexes: Trade(status, exit_time), Trade(signal_id), Position(status), Review(created_at).

Frontend:
- RunProgress switched to useReducer + per-event incremental updates (was O(events^2) on streaming runs).
- onDone moved to useEffect; render-body setTimeout was firing on every render.
- next/dynamic for all chart components (recharts ~95KB / lightweight-charts ~50KB lazy-loaded).
- /trades pagination (default 50).
- /system polling 60s -> 120s; SystemHealthListItem drops the per-job stats dict.

## LLM visibility

Backend:
- Signal.strategy_score (JSON): persists the full StrategyScore breakdown (trend/setup/risk/volume/regime/r_r) so the UI can show "why was the LLM invoked".
- New SignalSkip table + /api/system/skip-reasons + /api/system/skips: persists symbols where the LLM was NOT called and why.
- LlmCallLog.attempt_history (JSON): per-attempt raw text + thinking + tokens + error.
- LlmCallLog.symbol (denormalized) + new /api/llm/cost-attribution endpoint: cost per symbol/model/purpose.
- /api/system/llm-budget + MAX_DAILY_LLM_COST_USD setting: per-day spend cap; over budget -> status=BUDGET_EXCEEDED.
- /llm-stats now includes P50/P95 latency, success_rate, avg_attempts.
- /api/signals/{id}/trade + /api/signals?reject_reason=X + /api/trades?signal_id=N: signal <-> trade traceability.

Frontend:
- Signal detail dialog: new strategy-score breakdown panel + linked-trade link.
- Signal table: REJECTED rows show reject_reason inline + System page reject reasons are clickable -> filtered signals.
- /llm/[id] detail page: attempt_history collapsible + symbol field.
- New /llm/cost-attribution page: budget bar + group-by selector.
- /llm/decision: scores SSE event now carries full StrategyScore + UI renders mini bars per sub-score.
- Reviews: focused-trade lookup uses /api/reviews/by-trade/{trade_id} (no more list-find).
- Reviews: "Regenerate" button kicks off SSE-backed background regen with live thinking output.
- Reviews: list cards expandable with per-card lazy-loaded candle chart.

Schema migration: alembic 20260518_round2 (additive, all nullable / new tables + indexes).

## Summary

- **`ToolInvocation` discriminated union** — pairs `name`, `args`, and `response` under one discriminant in `adk.ts`; `switch(tool.name)` narrows all three simultaneously with zero `as` casts in drawer content components
- **RightDrawer rewrite** — replaced tab layout with per-tool content panels, each matching the width of ChatArea:
  - `investigator`: request + grounding-annotated markdown + source cards with full URLs
  - `verifier`: claims + verification report + source cards
  - `proofreader_*`: request + reader-perspective result
  - `draft_factcheck_response`: read-only 4-category selector + response text (copy button) + references (copy button)
  - `get_single_cofacts_article`: media attachment, 訊息內文/逐字稿, stats, fact-check responses with type badges, related articles carousel
- **URL-based drawer navigation** — drawer state lives in a nested route (`session.$sessionId/tool.$toolCallId`), enabling browser back/forward and deep-linking; badge click navigates rather than setting state
- **`ToolInvocation` cache** — `chatCache` stores both tool calls and responses keyed by ID so the drawer can reconstruct content from the URL on reload
- **Auto-open drawer** — when the last tool call in a session is `draft_factcheck_response`, the drawer navigates to it automatically so editors see the draft immediately
- **Tool response storage fix** — `functionResponse` event parts were filtered out before caching; `applyEventToState` now collects them into `toolResponses` before filtering
- **Layout flattening** — Sidebar, chat column, and RightDrawer are direct siblings under `<main>`, removing a redundant flex wrapper
- **Python `draft_factcheck_response` tool** — validates `classification` (one of four values) and `references` (≥1 URL); returns `{success, text}` and asks the LLM to retry on invalid input
