author: patient-zero-0
body:
## What

Third ops endpoint. The set so far:

| Endpoint | PR | The question it answers |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /v1/ops/token-cost` | A-42 (#110) | how much is user X spending on LLM tokens? |
| `GET /v1/ops/moderation-events` | A-43 (#113) | what red-line decisions did user X (or the tenant) trigger? |
| **`GET /v1/ops/moderation-stats`** | **this PR** | **what % of turns went redirect last 24h? which category fires most? are we still falling through to the local dict?** |

```
GET /v1/ops/moderation-stats
  ?user_id=<id>       optional drill-down to one user
  ?since=<iso8601>    inclusive lower bound on created_at
  ?until=<iso8601>    exclusive upper bound (half-open [since, until))
  -> 200 ModerationStatsResponse
  -> 401 OPS_AUTH_REQUIRED         (gate from A-41)
  -> 503 OPS_DISABLED              (OPS_API_TOKEN unset)
  -> 422 VALIDATION_ERROR          (empty user_id)
```

## Response shape

```python
class ModerationStatsTotals(BaseModel):
    event_count: int              # = allow + warn + redirect + block
    allow_count: int
    warn_count: int
    redirect_count: int
    block_count: int

class ModerationStatsBreakdownEntry(BaseModel):
    key: str
    count: int

class ModerationStatsResponse(BaseModel):
    since: datetime | None        # echoed
    until: datetime | None        # echoed
    user_id: str | None           # echoed (null when unfiltered)
    totals: ModerationStatsTotals
    by_verdict:  list[ModerationStatsBreakdownEntry]  # ALWAYS 4 in canonical order
    by_context:  list[ModerationStatsBreakdownEntry]  # count desc
    by_category: list[ModerationStatsBreakdownEntry]  # count desc, double-counted
    by_backend:  list[ModerationStatsBreakdownEntry]  # count desc
    generated_at: datetime
```

## Two pinned invariants

### 1. `event_count == allow_count + warn_count + redirect_count + block_count`

Headline invariant. Dashboards lose trust the moment these disagree. Pinned at:
- Repo level: `test_aggregate_totals_match_sum_of_verdicts`
- Route level: `test_totals_sum_equals_event_count`
- Route level cross-check: `test_by_verdict_counts_match_totals`

### 2. `by_verdict` is ALWAYS 4 entries in (allow, warn, redirect, block) order

Even when a verdict has zero events in the window, it appears in the breakdown with `count: 0`. This gives the dashboard a stable 4-column layout from day one — zero counts surface honestly instead of going missing. Pinned by `_VERDICT_ORDER` in the repo and pinned end-to-end by `test_by_verdict_canonical_order_pinned_end_to_end` (seeds only block events; asserts the response still lists all 4 keys).

## Category double-counting (intentional)

A row tagged `(self_harm, violence)` contributes **once to each** category bucket. The reading is "how often did category X fire", not "how many rows had exactly category X".

Without this, a dashboard showing `self_harm: 10` could hide that 8 of those rows were *also* violence — and ops needs to see both. Pinned by `test_aggregate_by_category_counts_each_tag_per_row` so a future refactor that switches to first-category-wins surfaces in review.

## Why aggregate in Python, not SQL GROUP BY

`categories` is a JSON list column on `moderation_events`. Bucketing it natively needs `jsonb_array_elements_text` (Postgres-only) and divergent code paths for the sqlite-backed unit tests the model intentionally stays portable for.

At v0 volume (~hundreds of events/day per ops query) the haul-and-group cost is negligible. When per-tenant volume crosses ~100k rows/query the `by_verdict` / `by_context` / `by_backend` GROUP BYs should move to SQL while category aggregation stays in Python. Tracked in the repo's `aggregate` docstring — **out of scope for this PR**.

## Shared `_aggregate_records` helper

Both InMemory and Postgres impls fetch their record set, then call the same helper. A future fix to the aggregation semantics (sort order, ties, counting policy) lands in both backends at once instead of drifting between them. The InMemory path filters its list; the Postgres path runs one SELECT with WHERE clauses, then converts rows → records and hands them to the same helper.

## Reuses existing ops infra

| Mechanism | First used in | Reused here |
|---|---|---|
| `X-Ops-Token` Depends + 503 fail-closed | A-41 | same Depends — `test_disabled_deployment_returns_503` mirrors A-42/A-43 |
| Half-open `[since, until)` window | A-42 | same semantics across all 3 ops endpoints |
| `_get_events_repo` dependency_overrides seam | A-43 | reused for in-memory test isolation |
| Filter-echo pattern | A-42 | `user_id` / `since` / `until` echo back |

## Tests (24 new across 2 files)

### `tests/test_moderation_events_repository.py` (+11 aggregate tests)

| Test | What it pins |
|---|---|
| `test_aggregate_empty_repo_returns_zero_totals` | empty → zeros + 4-row by_verdict + empty breakdowns |
| `test_aggregate_counts_verdicts_correctly` | totals fields populate from records |
| `test_aggregate_by_verdict_always_includes_all_four_in_canonical_order` | stable layout invariant |
| `test_aggregate_by_context_counts_each_context` | by-context grouping |
| `test_aggregate_by_context_sorted_by_count_desc` | most-frequent first |
| `test_aggregate_by_category_counts_each_tag_per_row` | **double-counting policy** |
| `test_aggregate_by_backend_counts_each_backend` | cloud-mod fallthrough visibility |
| `test_aggregate_filters_by_user_id` | cross-tenant isolation |
| `test_aggregate_filters_by_time_window` | `[since, until)` math |
| `test_aggregate_totals_match_sum_of_verdicts` | **headline invariant** |
| `test_aggregate_echoes_filters_back` | bounds + user_id echo |

### `tests/test_ops_moderation_stats_route.py` (+13 end-to-end tests)

| Test | What it pins |
|---|---|
| `test_returns_totals_and_all_breakdowns` | happy path (realistic 6-event seed exercises every field) |
| `test_empty_repo_returns_zero_totals_and_full_verdict_breakdown` | empty state 200, not 404 |
| `test_by_verdict_canonical_order_pinned_end_to_end` | layout invariant through wire layer |
| `test_totals_sum_equals_event_count` | headline invariant through wire layer |
| `test_by_verdict_counts_match_totals` | two views of the same data agree |
| `test_by_category_counts_each_tag_per_row` | double-counting policy through wire layer |
| `test_user_id_filter_drills_down` | cross-tenant isolation end-to-end |
| `test_since_until_window_applied` | window math at route boundary |
| `test_empty_user_id_returns_422` | `min_length=1` (no accidental tenant-wide aggregate) |
| `test_missing_ops_token_returns_401` | auth dep fires BEFORE validation |
| `test_wrong_ops_token_returns_401` | A-41 gate active |
| `test_disabled_deployment_returns_503` | `OPS_API_TOKEN` unset → 503 |
| `test_stats_response_never_exposes_raw_content` | privacy invariant (defensive — stats is row-agnostic, but pinned in case a future refactor inlines sample rows) |

## Files changed (8 files, +1118 / -0)

| File | Δ | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `app/services/moderation_events/repository.py` | +184 | aggregate types + `aggregate(...)` on Protocol + 2 impls + shared helper |
| `app/services/moderation_events/__init__.py` | +6 | re-export new types |
| `app/schemas/ops.py` | +76 | `ModerationStats*` wire schemas |
| `app/routes/v1/ops.py` | +90 | `_build_stats_response` + handler |
| `tests/test_openapi_contract.py` | +2 | path → `REQUIRED_ENDPOINTS` |
| `apps/api/openapi.yaml` | +219 | regenerated |
| `tests/test_moderation_events_repository.py` | +188 | 11 new aggregate tests |
| `tests/test_ops_moderation_stats_route.py` | +353 (new) | 13 end-to-end tests |

## Gates

- [x] `uv run pytest tests/` → 783 passed, 2 skipped (+24 net new)

author: bebecue
body:
while playing with lua scripting with the gb core, i found sometimes emu:readRegister() returns 16 bits value for 8 bit registers.

assuming cpu.b = 0x12, emu:readRegister("b") might return 0x12, 0x7F12 or any others.

the issue is in _GBCoreReadRegister(), param `void* out` is casted to `uint8_t*`, and `*value = cpu->b` will only write to the lowest byte, leave whatever garbage in high bytes untouched.

body:
Tiny harness fix prompted by PR #261 sitting with all-green CI but unmerged for hours.

**Gap**: Step 5 of the review cycle said `when threads resolved + CI green, auto-merge fires` but didn't tell the agent how to *detect* unresolved threads. With `required_review_thread_resolution: true` in the ruleset, status checks can be fully green and the merge silently waits.

**Fix**: Update the merge-watch step to make checking `reviewThreads.isResolved` explicit when a PR with green CI hasn't merged.

One-line change. No code touched.

<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>


## Problem

In `.github/workflows/emu-build-all-win.yml`, the `builds-matrix-win` job spawns up to 48 parallel matrix jobs (12 projects × 2 archs × 2 configs). Every single one of them:
1. Independently restores the same cache key `emu-deps-win-all-vs2026`
2. Runs `premake5 --genproto` which calls `protoc.exe` from the cache

Under heavy concurrency, GitHub Actions throttles or fails some of these cache restores. Because the restore step has `continue-on-error: true`, jobs that fail to get the cache silently carry on — then hit:
```
Error: premake5.lua:178: protoc not found! build/deps/win/vs2026/protobuf/install64/bin/protoc.exe
```

## Solution

Apply **Option 2**: run `--genproto` exactly **once** in a new `gen-proto` job, upload the `proto_gen/win` directory as an artifact, and have all matrix jobs download it instead of regenerating.

### Changes to `.github/workflows/emu-build-all-win.yml`

1. **Add a `gen-proto` job** between `deps` and `builds-matrix-win`:
   - `needs: ["deps"]`
   - runs on `windows-2025-vs2026`
   - Restore the deps cache (with `fail-on-cache-miss: true` so failures are visible)
   - Checkout the branch
   - Clone `third-party/common/win`
   - Set build date, capture commit SHA
   - Run premake with `--genproto` only (no `--emubuild`, `--emubuilddate`, `--dosstub`, `--winrsrc`, `--winsign` needed — just proto generation)
   - Upload `proto_gen/win` as artifact named `proto-gen-win-vs2026-${{ steps.build_ref.outputs.sha }}` with `retention-days: 1`

2. **Update `builds-matrix-win`**:
   - Change `needs` from `["deps"]` to `["deps", "gen-proto"]`
   - **Remove** the `"Restore combined deps cache"` step (no longer needed for proto gen — the matrix jobs only need deps for MSBuild linking, which is handled separately)
   - **Remove** the `--genproto` flag from the "Generate project files" premake command
   - **Add** a step before "Generate project files" that downloads the artifact:
     ```yaml
     - name: "Download proto_gen artifact"
       uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
       with:
         name: "proto-gen-win-vs2026-${{ steps.build_ref.outputs.sha }}"
         path: "proto_gen/win"
     ```

   > Note: the matrix jobs still need the deps cache for the MSBuild link step. Keep the cache restore step in `builds-matrix-win` but change it to `fail-on-cache-miss: true` and remove `continue-on-error: true`.

### Key constraints to preserve
- The existing `--emubuild=${{ steps.build_ref.outputs.sha }} --emubuilddate=${{ env.EMU_BUILD_DATE }} --dosstub --winrsrc --winsign --os=windows vs2026` flags must remain on the "Generate project files" step in the matrix job (just without `--genproto`)
- All other steps in `builds-matrix-win` (MSBuild, artifact upload) remain unchanged
- The `gen-proto` job should also capture commit SHA with the same pattern (`git rev-parse HEAD`) and use it in the artifact name so it matches what the matrix jobs will look up
- Use `actions/download-artifact@v4` (not v8, which doesn't exist) for the download step in the matrix

Assistant: ## Root Cause

The job fails at `premake5.lua:178` because `protoc.exe` is not found at the expected path:

```
build/deps/win/vs2026/protobuf/install64/bin/protoc.exe
```

The logs show the deps were restored from cache (`emu-deps-win-all-vs2026`), but the cached protobuf installation is either missing `protoc.exe` or the cache is stale/corrupt.

## Solution

### Option 1: Force-rebuild protobuf (quickest fix)

Re-trigger the workflow manually via `workflow_dispatch` with `rebuild_protobuf` set to `true`. This bypasses the cache and rebuilds protobuf from scratch, ensuring `protoc.exe` ends up at the correct install path.

### Option 2: Ensure `protoc` is installed during the protobuf build

Check the protobuf CMake build script (likely under `third-party/` or a build helper script). Make sure the `INSTALL` target includes the `protoc` binary. The CMake flag to enable this is:

```cmake
-DPROTOBUF_BUILD_PROTOC_BINARIES=ON
```

If you're calling CMake in a build script, ensure it looks something like:

```bash
cmake .. \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX="install64" \
  -Dprotobuf_BUILD_PROTOC_BINARIES=ON \   # <-- ensure this is ON
  -Dprotobuf_BUILD_TESTS=OFF
cmake --build . --config Release
cmake --install . --config Release
```

Without `protobuf_BUILD_PROTOC_BINARIES=ON`, CMake will skip installing `protoc.exe` even if it builds successfully.

author: billduke13
body:
## Summary
Hardens the mobile and keyboard UX of the floating dock, the editorial hero, and the chapter layout; adds a branded `+error.svelte` so 404 / 5xx routes stay inside the world layer.

## Related
- Not applicable

## Updates
| Item | From | To | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Dock touch targets | 28-32 px chips | >=44 px hit-area via `::before` extenders | Visual chip size unchanged; meets iOS HIG and MD a11y. |
| Keyboard tab order | First focusable was inside `<main>` content | Skip-link → `FloatingDock` → `<main>` | New `.l-skip-link` styled in `layout.css`. |
| Legal route active state | `/privacy`, `/terms`, `/disclaimer` had no active dock entry | New "Legal" entry highlights on any of the three | Driven by an optional `NavLink.match[]` field. |
| 320 px horizontal scroll | `<main>` scrollWidth 338 (overflow 18 px) | Contained via `flex-wrap` on hero top, `overflow-x: clip` on `.c-chapter` and `html/body` | `clip` (not `hidden`) keeps `position: sticky` intact. |
| Error page | Default SvelteKit error page broke the brand shell | `src/routes/+error.svelte` reuses `EditorialHero` + `ArtifactCta` | `noindex` on errors. |

## Details
### Updates dock touch targets
- Design/Spec: iOS HIG (44 pt) and Material Design (48 dp) minimum. Pre-fix Playwright measurements at 320 px showed `.c-dock__item` 29 px tall, `.c-theme-switch` and `.c-dock__brand` only 28-32 px square.
- Implementation notes: `position: relative` on each interactive child plus an absolutely positioned `::before` extender (`inset: -0.5rem` for square chips, `inset-block: -0.5rem; inset-inline: -0.125rem` for the wider label chips). Adjacent dividers are `aria-hidden` and non-interactive, so the small hit-area overlap is acceptable. The pseudo-element has no background and inherits no styling, so the visual chip size is unchanged.
- Reviewer focus: confirm the extender does not visually leak any color, does not break hover/active styling, and does not block dock divider rendering.

### Updates keyboard tab order and skip-link
- Design/Spec: WCAG 2.4.1 (Bypass Blocks).
- Implementation notes: the skip-link is hidden off-canvas and slides into the top-left corner on `:focus-visible`. `FloatingDock` was moved before `<main>` in `AppShell.svelte`; `<main>` carries `tabindex="-1"` so the skip-link anchor focuses it without rendering a focus outline on the content region itself.
- Reviewer focus: tab the page from a cold load — first stop should be the skip-link, second the dock brand, then dock items, then `<main>` contents.

### Updates Legal route active state
- Design/Spec: one dock entry should represent a route group.
- Implementation notes: `NavLink` gains an optional `match: string[]` field; `FloatingDock.isCurrent()` reduces over it (or falls back to `[href]`). The home item is now exported as `homeLink` from `navigation.ts` so the dock no longer hard-codes `"/"`.
- Reviewer focus: confirm `/products/yinyang` still highlights Products (the existing `startsWith` semantics are preserved).

### Updates horizontal overflow containment
- Design/Spec: root cause was the two `<span>` elements in `.c-editorial-hero__top` not wrapping on narrow viewports.
- Implementation notes: hero top is now `flex-wrap: wrap` with `gap: var(--spacing-2) var(--spacing-6)` so the eyebrow copy collapses to two rows on narrow viewports. `.c-chapter` and `html/body` get `overflow-x: clip` as defense-in-depth — `clip` (not `hidden`) so `position: sticky` and scroll anchoring still work in the split-layout chapters.
- Reviewer focus: at 320 px, `document.documentElement.scrollWidth === window.innerWidth` should hold across `/`, `/products`, `/products/yinyang`, `/products/quant`, `/privacy`.

### Adds +error.svelte
- Design/Spec: keep the world-layer fog, brand mark, and Tai Chi underlay on error states.
- Implementation notes: reads `page.status` and `page.error`; renders `EditorialHero` for the message and an `ArtifactCta` back to `/`. `noindex` meta tag keeps the error page out of search indexes.
- Reviewer focus: `pnpm dev`, visit `/no-such-page`.

## Testing
- `pnpm lint` -- passed (Prettier + ESLint clean)
- `pnpm check` -- passed (svelte-check, 392 files, 0 errors / 0 warnings)
- `pnpm test` -- passed (Vitest, 5 files / 29 tests)
- Manual steps reviewers should run:
  - At 320 x 720 viewport, confirm `<main>` no longer has a horizontal scrollbar.
  - Keyboard-tab from a cold load: skip-link → dock → main.
  - Visit `/privacy`, `/terms`, `/disclaimer`: dock should highlight "Legal".
  - Visit `/no-such-page`: branded 404 with "Back to home" CTA.

## Screenshots / Notes
- Pre-fix audit screenshots at 320 px were captured locally (not committed) to drive the priority decisions; please re-shoot after pulling to confirm parity.

## Breaking changes
- Not applicable. `NavLink.match` is optional; the previous `primaryNav` entries are unchanged.

## Risks and rollout
- `overflow-x: clip` requires modern browsers (Safari 16+, Chrome 90+, Firefox 81+). The site already targets evergreen browsers; older fallbacks simply re-expose the original 18 px overflow rather than breaking layout.
- Hit-area `::before` extenders may overlap adjacent dock items at the 2 px boundary. Source order resolves the overlap toward the later sibling, which matches left-to-right reading.

## Checklist
- [x] Tests added/updated if needed (existing tests pass; new browser-mode a11y tests are deferred to a follow-up pass)
- [ ] Docs updated if needed (contributor docs unchanged; the `NavLink.match[]` pattern can be mentioned in a future docs pass)
- [x] Backward compatibility considered
- [x] Rollout/monitoring considerations noted

Description:
This PR introduces significant enhancements to the OIChainAnalyser and related modules, focusing on both positional and intraday analysis. The changes aim to improve the accuracy, granularity, and interpretability of OI-based signals.

Key Changes:
New OI Analysis Features:

OI Positional Trend: Added a method to detect trends in OI changes over multiple days.
OI Acceleration: Tracks the rate of change in OI to identify rapid buildups or unwinding.
OI Capitulation: Detects significant unwinding of positions near the money, signaling potential market reversals.
OI Wall Migration: Identifies shifts in dominant OI levels (walls) across strikes.
Enhanced Constants:

Introduced new constants for positional analysis, such as OI_CAPITULATION_MIN_CHANGE_PCT, OI_POSITIONAL_TREND_DAYS, and OI_ACCEL_MIN_RATIO.
Adjusted thresholds for intraday and positional modes to improve signal quality.
Improved Debug Logging:

Added detailed debug logs for each analysis step, including input data, conditions, and results.
Enhanced traceability of signals with structured logging.
Refactored Code:

Consolidated shared logic for OI analysis.
Improved readability and maintainability of the OIChainAnalyser class.
Message Formatter Updates:

Added new message formats for the newly introduced OI signals, including emojis and detailed breakdowns.
Files Modified:
MessageFormatter.py:
Added new message formats for OI signals.
OIChainAnalyser.py:
Implemented new analysis methods and constants.
Enhanced existing methods with additional checks and logging.
Testing:
Unit tests were updated to cover new methods and constants.
Verified signal generation for various market scenarios using historical data.
Impact:
These enhancements provide traders with deeper insights into market dynamics, enabling better decision-making based on OI trends and anomalies.

## Related Issues
Fixes #2651

## Summary of Changes
- Keep local `walk_dir` timeout errors local to scanner/listing work so a slow directory walk does not mark the drive as faulty.
- Apply the same scoped behavior to remote `walk_dir`, including stream timeout-like errors, so remote scanner walks do not evict the connection or mark the drive offline.
- Preserve timeout and network-like failure marking for normal disk operations by keeping the default health tracking behavior unchanged.
- Treat `Duration::ZERO` as no operation timeout for remote disk health tracking, matching the existing local disk wrapper behavior.
- Add regression coverage for ignored scanner timeouts, default timeout failure marking, ignored remote network-like scanner errors, zero-duration remote operations, and writer backpressure during scanner walks.

## Verification
- `cargo test -p rustfs-ecstore execute_with_timeout`
- `cargo test -p rustfs-ecstore walk_dir_writer_backpressure_timeout_does_not_mark_drive_failure`
- `cargo test -p rustfs-ecstore timeout`
- `cargo fmt --all --check`
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `make pre-commit` with `en_US.UTF-8` locale

## Impact
Scanner walks can still return timeout errors, but those timeouts no longer move local or remote drives to suspect/offline state. Other disk operation timeouts and network-like remote operation failures still update drive health as before.

author: nagayoshi0923
body:
## 問題

マジックリンク（OTPセッション）で新規登録しようとすると、パスワード設定 (`updateUser({ password })`) が 422 を返した後に `customers` INSERT が 42501 (RLS) で失敗し「登録に失敗しました」が表示される。

## 原因の連鎖

1. **`updateUser({ password })` → 422** OTPセッションはパスワード直接変更を制限する場合がある
2. **既存の catch が 422 をスロー** → セッション状態が壊れた状態で後続処理へ（または直接エラー表示）
3. **`customers` INSERT が 42501** → `auth.uid()` が null 扱いになり RLS ブロック

## 修正

`updateUser` の 422 エラーを「パスワード設定スキップ・続行」として扱うよう変更。
OTPセッションではセッション自体は有効なので、パスワードをスキップしてプロフィール保存は完了できる。

```typescript
// Before
if (msg.includes('different from the old password')) { skip }
else { throw }  // ← 422 もここに来てスロー

// After
if (msg.includes('different from the old password') || updateError.status === 422) {
  logger.log('スキップ')  // 422 も安全にスキップ
}
```

author: omgitsguppey
body:
🚨 **Severity**: CRITICAL
💡 **Vulnerability**: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) via client-provided `projectId` in the admin role endpoint, and unhandled promise rejections on invalid tokens.
🎯 **Impact**: Attackers could potentially route sensitive administrative database operations to unexpected or attacker-controlled Firestore projects by tampering with the `projectId`. Additionally, invalid tokens bubbled up as 500 internal server errors.
🔧 **Fix**: Replaced the vulnerable REST `fetch` proxy with the native Firebase Admin SDK (`db.collection().update()`), eliminated the `projectId` parameter requirement (preventing the SSRF), and securely wrapped `verifyIdToken` to handle authentication failures gracefully.
✅ **Verification**: Verified the correct behavior and code stability using `pnpm run lint` and `pnpm run test`.

author: duongve13112002
body:
Hi @kohya-ss 

Problem: after encoding each batch on GPU, the process synchronously called
np.savez / save_latents_to_disk, leaving the GPU idle for the full duration of
the disk write before starting the next encode. With multiple GPUs each writing
N/num_processes files simultaneously, total disk throughput was saturated, so
adding more GPUs did not reduce wall time.

Fix: add a background ThreadPoolExecutor (write_executor) in both
new_cache_latents and new_cache_text_encoder_outputs. Disk writes are submitted
to this pool immediately after encoding, allowing the GPU to begin the next
batch encode concurrently. All writes are flushed before the function returns.

strategy_base.py:
- LatentsCachingStrategy: add set_async_write_executor / wait_for_async_writes;
  split save_latents_to_disk into async dispatch + _save_latents_to_disk_impl;
  tensors are cloned on CPU before handoff to prevent races
- TextEncoderOutputsCachingStrategy: same helpers plus save_outputs_npz()
  which copies numpy arrays and dispatches to the write pool
- Module-level _write_npz helper (avoids lambda/closure issues)

train_util.py (new_cache_latents):
- Create write_executor sized to cpu_count//num_processes capped at batch_size
- Log [Process X/N] device=... will encode M/total images at start
- Warn when num_processes=1 but multiple GPUs are visible

train_util.py (new_cache_text_encoder_outputs):
- Same write_executor pattern as VAE caching

strategy_flux/sd3/sdxl/lumina/hunyuan_image/anima:
- Replace np.savez(...) with self.save_outputs_npz(...)

body:
## Summary

Add an explicit `basename = "..."` argument to `#[viewset]` so projects do not need to understand the `extract_basename` token walker to predict their URL prefix. The legacy walker remains as a fallback but now emits a `deprecated` lint at the call site, giving users one release cycle to migrate before the fallback becomes an error in v0.2.0.

- `parse_optional_basename_arg`: parses the new attribute argument; absence preserves the legacy walker fallback
- `emit_deprecation_marker`: injects a `#[deprecated]` const that rustc surfaces as a lint at the call site, uniquely named per fn so multiple `#[viewset]` invocations do not collide with E0428
- `tests/ui/viewset/pass/viewset_basename_explicit.rs`: new trybuild fixture proving the explicit form compiles cleanly under `#[deny(deprecated)]`
- `viewset_macro.rs::tests`: unit tests cover the parser branches and the fn-form deprecation marker emission path (the fn-form trybuild route would require pulling `reinhardt-core` into the macros dev-dep tree — see `tests/ui.rs` header for the circular-dep constraint)
- `CHANGELOG.md`: Deprecated section announces the basename fallback timeline

## Type of Change

- Refactor (non-breaking; deprecation flow)

## Motivation and Context

The current `extract_basename` token walker requires understanding the macro internals to predict the URL prefix (Design Philosophy principle #2 violation: "CoC must be predictable without domain knowledge"). An explicit attribute is trivially predictable.

## How Was This Tested?

- `viewset_basename_explicit.rs` trybuild fixture compiles under `#[deny(deprecated)]`
- Unit tests in `viewset_macro.rs::tests` cover `parse_optional_basename_arg` and `emit_deprecation_marker`
- CI runs `cargo nextest run -p reinhardt-macros --test ui` on this branch

- [x] My code follows the project's style guidelines
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings (except the intentional deprecation marker)
- [x] I have updated CHANGELOG.md
- [x] My commit messages follow Conventional Commits

body:
### Motivation
- Ensure the unified Tasks workspace defaults to showing only the current active sprint across List, Board, and Timeline while still allowing users to view all tasks via explicit filters.
- Provide sprint context in timeline payloads and visually de-emphasize previous/completed sprint items, and add a compact sprint timer/controls strip with minimal icon buttons.

### Description
- Added a `scope` filter and `sprint_id` support (allowed values: `current_sprint`, `all`, `unsprinted`, `completed_sprints`, `sprint`) and defaulted missing scope to `current_sprint` in `TaskWorkspaceController`; resolved active sprints and exposed `currentSprint`, `activeSprints`, `currentSprintIds`, `currentSprintStats`, `selectedScope`, and `selectedSprintId` to the view.
- Applied sprint-scope constraints to the List query and paginated results in `TaskWorkspaceController` so `scope=current_sprint` limits tickets via `whereHas('sprints', ...)`; added safe fallback when no active sprint exists.
- Extended `KanbanService::queryFor()` and `groupedTickets()` to accept filter input and enforce the same sprint scoping for board rendering (supports `current_sprint`, `all`, `unsprinted`, `completed_sprints`, `sprint`).
- Extended `TimelineService::visibleQuery()` to support `scope` + `current_sprint_ids` and to restrict timeline tickets to tasks/bugs/generated tasks; updated `taskPayload()` to include sprint metadata (`sprint_id`, `sprint_name`, `sprint_status`, `is_previous_sprint`) and to emit a single-token `custom_class` of `timeline-previous-sprint` for previous/completed-sprint tasks (preserves the no-whitespace `custom_class` requirement).
- TimelineController now validates and defaults scope, resolves `current_sprint_ids` and passes them into `TimelineService::ganttPayload()`.
- UI updates: added `scope` + `sprint` selectors to the Tasks filter panel and made the Reset link revert to `scope=current_sprint`; replaced sprint control glyphs with compact SVG icon buttons on Tasks and Sprints panels; added gray styling for previous-sprint bars in the timeline partial; refined list column labels/config in `resources/js/app.js` to match grouped list UX.
- Updated `docs/IMPLEMENTATION_TRACKER.md` to record the change set and delivery notes.

### Testing
- Ran PHP lint checks with `php -l` on modified PHP files (`TaskWorkspaceController`, `KanbanService`, `TimelineService`, `TimelineController`) and they reported no syntax errors.
- Attempted Laravel automated commands `php artisan test`, `php artisan route:list`, `php artisan view:clear`, and `php artisan optimize:clear` but they could not run in this environment due to a missing Composer `vendor/autoload.php` (so the full PHPUnit/feature test suite could not be executed here).
- Frontend/visual changes were updated in Blade and JS assets and verified by code inspection; a full frontend build / browser validation was not run in this environment.

author: lilhawkeye2002-ux
body:
## Overview

This pull request is the result of a **structured, non-overlapping 4-pass code audit** (Semantic Analysis → Observability Analysis → Security SAST → Code Quality) applied to the `frontend-game-mockup` branch, followed by two rounds of iterative plan review that surfaced 6 additional findings (AF-001–AF-006). Every one of the **37 total findings** is resolved in this single commit.

**Audit scope:** Pass 1 and 2 were restricted to files modified in the last 7 days (recent-file set). Pass 3 and 4 applied to all tracked source files.

**Verified baseline (post-fix):**
- `616 passed, 17 skipped` — no test regressions
- Bandit security scan: `High: 0, Medium: 0, Low: 11` (was `High: 1`)
- No `C/D/E/F` grade cyclomatic-complexity functions anywhere
- No `TODO/FIXME` remaining in `gameworks/` source
- `pyflakes`: zero warnings on all modified files

---

## Technical Description

### PASS 1 — Semantic Analysis (`SEM`) · 8 findings

**SEM-ENG-001 · HIGH** — `gameworks/tests/unit/test_engine.py`
`class TestFirstClickSafety` was defined twice (lines 102 and 634). Python's module-level namespace silently replaces the first binding with the second; pytest discovers only the second class. The two behavioural tests for the first-click safety invariant (`test_first_click_never_hits_mine`, `test_second_click_can_hit_mine`) were permanently dead — never executed in CI. Fixed by renaming the line-634 class to `TestFirstClickSafetyTinyBoard`.

**SEM-MAIN-002 · HIGH** — `gameworks/main.py`
`_retry_game()` used two separate `if self._engine:` and `if self._renderer:` guards. When `_engine` is non-None but `_renderer` is None (possible during engine-initialisation races), the first block mutates `self._engine` and attempts `self._renderer.board = …` on a `None` reference. Collapsed to a single `if self._engine and self._renderer:` guard.

**SEM-REN-003 · MEDIUM** — `gameworks/renderer.py`
`anim_arr.fill(False)` and `win_anim_arr.fill(False)` were called every frame unconditionally. At 300×370 and 30 FPS with no active animation: ~3.3 million wasted writes/second. Both fills are now guarded by animation-active checks.

**SEM-REN-004 · MEDIUM** — `gameworks/renderer.py`
FA-022 was intended to replace a Python `set` of `(x,y)` tuples with a numpy `bool` array. The implementation built both simultaneously, defeating the optimisation. `win_anim_set` removed; `_draw_win_animation_fx` rewritten to accept the array and iterate via `zip(*np.where(win_anim_arr))`.

**SEM-ITER9-005 · MEDIUM** — `run_iter9.py`
`runs_attempted` metric excluded `batch_index == 0` warmup failures. Added a comment documenting this intentional semantic boundary.

**SEM-SA-006 · LOW** — `sa.py`
`prange(H)` with `fastmath=True` in the Numba kernel makes initial-loss summation order non-deterministic. Non-determinism notes added to `run_sa()` and `default_config()` docstrings.

**SEM-PIPE-007 · LOW** — `pipeline.py`
`run_last100_repair(grid, target, target, …)` passes `target` for both `target` and `target_eval`. An existing comment correctly documented this as intentional. Confirmed false positive; no code change.

**SEM-MAIN-008 · LOW** — `gameworks/main.py`
`raise exc` → `raise exc from exc` to preserve exception chain linkage.

---

### PASS 2 — Observability Analysis (`OBS`) · 6 findings

**OBS-ENG-001 · HIGH** — `gameworks/engine.py`
Pipeline fallback handler used `print(…)` and `traceback.print_exc()`. Invisible in headless CI and log aggregators. Replaced with `_log.warning("…", exc_info=True)`.

**OBS-MAIN-002 · MEDIUM** — `gameworks/main.py`
No observable signal if win animation stalls in RESULT state. Added `_result_enter_time` timestamp and `_log.warning(…)` if animation exceeds 15 seconds.

**OBS-ITER9-003 · MEDIUM** — `run_iter9.py`
Render daemon logged exception strings without `exc_info`. No liveness check after `join()`. Initial fix introduced a deferred `import logging as _logging` inside `finally` (D-08 regression). All fixed: module-level `_log`, `exc_info=_render_errors[0]`, `_render_thread.is_alive()` check.

**OBS-REPAIR-004 · MEDIUM** — `repair.py`
Added unconditional `_log.info("Repair start/done …")` to `run_phase1_repair()` — fires regardless of `verbose` flag.

**OBS-SA-005 · MEDIUM** — `sa_parallel.py`
Added `exc_info=True` to SA worker failure warning.

**OBS-BENCH-006 · LOW** — `run_benchmark.py`
Added `allow_pickle=False` to regression baseline `np.load`.

---

### PASS 3 — Security SAST (`SEC`) · 7 findings

**SEC-CORE-001 · HIGH** — `core.py`
Both `load_image_smart()` and `load_image_smart_v2()` opened caller-supplied paths without canonicalisation. Added `path = str(Path(path).resolve())` as first line of each.

**SEC-ENG-002 · HIGH** — `gameworks/engine.py`
`load_board_from_npy()` had identical path-traversal exposure. Added `path = str(Path(path).resolve())` before `np.load`.

**SEC-BENCH-003 · MEDIUM** — `run_benchmark.py`
`np.load` default allows pickle deserialisation. Added `allow_pickle=False`.

**SEC-ITER9-004 · MEDIUM** — `run_iter9.py`
`sanitize_run_tag()` docstring added; empty-string output for all-separator inputs documented. Downstream guards confirmed adequate.

**SEC-MAIN-005 · MEDIUM** — `gameworks/main.py`
`sys.stdout = _Capture()` from daemon thread replaced with `contextlib.redirect_stdout(capture)` scoped to the `with` block — eliminates thread-global side-effect.

**SEC-IMG-006 · LOW** — `assets/image_guard.py`
Added `path = path.resolve()` at start of `_compute_stats()` for defence-in-depth.

**SEC-REPAIR-007 · LOW** — `repair.py`
`checkpoint_dir` resolve moved from inside the per-round loop to function entry.

---

### PASS 4 — Code Quality (`QUA`) · 10 findings

**QUA-ITER9-001 · HIGH** — `run_iter9.py`
`run_iter9_single()`: 676 lines, CC~30 → **190 lines, CC=4 grade A** via 4 helpers:
- `_run_sa_phases(…)` → `(grid, histories, sr_post_sa)` — CC=3 A
- `_run_repair_phases(…)` → 9-tuple — CC=4 A
- `_build_run_metrics_document(**kwargs)` → `dict` — pure, no I/O — CC=9 B
- `_launch_background_renders(…)` → `(thread, errors_list)` — CC=1 A

**QUA-PIPE-002 · HIGH** — `pipeline.py`
`route_late_stage_failure()`: 298 lines, CC~28 → **~55 lines, CC=7 grade B** via `_run_phase2_route` and `_run_last100_route`.

**QUA-ENG-003 · MEDIUM** — `gameworks/engine.py`
`warnings: List[str] = None # type: ignore` → `field(default_factory=list)`; `__post_init__` removed.

**QUA-ENG-004 · MEDIUM** — `gameworks/engine.py`
`_pipeline_default_params()` and `_execute_pipeline()` extracted from `load_board_from_pipeline()`.

**QUA-SA-005 · MEDIUM** — `core.py`, `run_iter9.py`, `run_benchmark.py`
`downsample_target(target, w, h)` extracted to `core.py`; verbatim BILINEAR-downsample duplication eliminated.

**QUA-CI-006 · MEDIUM** — `.github/workflows/ci.yml`
`pip install -r requirements.txt` replaces hard-coded 7-package list; redundant `pip install bandit` removed.

**QUA-REN-007 · MEDIUM** — `gameworks/tests/renderer/test_animations.py`
4 clock-injection tests added using mutable-list fake clock — deterministic, zero wall-clock time.

**QUA-SOLVER-008 · LOW** — `solver.py`
`@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=16)` replaces unbounded `_NB_CACHE` dict (prevents ~480 MB growth in image-sweep mode).

**QUA-MAIN-009 · LOW** — `gameworks/main.py`
Production TODO comment removed from `_start_game()`.

**QUA-BOARD-010 · LOW** — `board_sizing.py`
`#min_width: int = 300` dead comment removed; docstring explains 300→50 rationale.

---

### Additional Findings (`AF`) · 6 post-execution audit findings

**AF-001 · HIGH** — `assets/image_guard.py:360`
`hashlib.md5(raw)` — Bandit B324 HIGH (CWE-327). Fixed: `hashlib.md5(raw, usedforsecurity=False)`. Bandit HIGH: 1 → 0.

**AF-002 · MEDIUM** — `run_iter9.py:836, 1711`
Two commented-out `min_width=300` lines removed.

**AF-003 · MEDIUM** — `run_iter9.py`
Module-level `_log = logging.getLogger(__name__)` added; deferred `import logging as _logging` inside `finally` block removed.

**AF-004 · MEDIUM** — `board_sizing.py:29`

author: charliek
body:
## Summary

- **Root cause** (different from the original #59 framing): when the Mac UI quits via ⌘Q without first `exit`-ing its shells, the daemon's `stream_pty` future is dropped without reaching the Exit branch that closes the tab. The PTY and tab row become orphans, persisting until daemon restart.
- On the next session the UI bootstraps a new tab in the same project (cross-client tabs aren't surfaced, per `App.swift:672`); when that new tab's shell exits, the daemon's `project_now_empty` check sees the orphan and returns `false`, so the M5 cascade never fires — leaving the sidebar row + blank window state from #59.
- **Fix**: add a `CleanupOnDrop` guard around the `stream_pty` outbound generator. On drop, it calls `close_tab(tab_id)` and tolerates `TabNotFound` (Exit branch already cleaned up). The cascade then deletes any project that ends up empty, matching the M5 design intent.

## Behavior change worth flagging

⌘Q now reaps tabs whose shells were still alive and cascade-deletes any project that ends up empty. Pre-fix those tabs and projects lingered as orphans, which is what was breaking the M5 cascade in the first place. This matches the "one terminal per tab, no detach/attach" design from the spec — nothing previously working is now broken.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo build -p roost-core` — passes
- [x] Live repro: with the fix, ⌘Q while a shell is alive emits the new `stream_pty drop: cleaned up orphan tab tab_id=N` debug log, then cascades to `delete_project` when the project ends up empty. CLI `tab list` / `project list` both empty after the cleanup. Daemon DB also empty.
- [x] Pre-fix repro (the original #59 stuck-blank-window scenario) is no longer reachable because the orphan tabs that prevented the cascade are now cleaned up on client disconnect.
- [ ] No automated test added — exercising the drop guard requires a tonic in-process server harness that doesn't exist in the repo yet (`mac/Tests` is XCTest for Swift utilities only; `roost-core/src/service.rs:714` `mod tests` is just OSC parsing). Underlying `Workspace::close_tab` correctness is covered by `state.rs::open_close_tab_cascades_to_empty_project`.

Closes #59.

## Summary

Implements the standalone consumer-side sync skill per `ai/skill-management-v1.md` §7.2.

**Stacked on PR #11.** Final PR in the v1 implementation sequence (PR 9 spec → PR 10 bootstrap → PR 11 skill-registry → this).

### What's in the skill

`SKILL.md` with progressive disclosure for the agent. Lives under `.claude/skills/skill-sync/`.

**Scripts (4):**
- `canonical_json.py` — duplicated from skill-registry per spec §10 so the skill is standalone in consumer repos.
- `validate.py` — schema validator for `skill-sync-config`.
- `regen_agents_md.py` — agents-md parser + `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` renderers; deterministic.
- `skill_sync.py` — main entry point. Clones the registry, walks subscriptions, fetches missing/upgraded artifacts via `git show` / `git archive`, prints a structured report.

**Resources:**
- `skill-sync-config.json` (user config, hash-excluded).
- `skill-sync-config-template-claude.json` and `skill-sync-config-template-codex.json` (templates).
- `agents-md-header.md` — `AGENTS.md` banner with `__AGENTS_MD_DIR__` placeholder.
- `claude-md-template.md` — `CLAUDE.md` body (banner + pointer to `AGENTS.md`).
- `schemas/skill-sync-config.schema.json` — strict (additionalProperties: false; semver/kebab/repo-slug patterns; `"latest"`-or-semver discriminator on `version`).

**Tests (23, all passing locally):**
- agents-md parser: metadata-line stripping, section boundary at next H1, alphabetical render order, subscription filtering, ledger/extracted-file exclusion, banner presence, determinism, case-insensitive heading match.
- Config schema: valid + invalid semver, prerelease, "latest", kebab + repo-slug pattern enforcement, required keys, no-extras.

### Key behaviors

- **Empty `subscriptions.agents_md` disables both AGENTS.md AND CLAUDE.md regeneration entirely** (per spec §7.2.1 step 5).
- **AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md inline edits are extracted** into timestamped candidate files in the agents-md directory before overwrite. No silent loss.
- **Deprecated items at "latest"** emit warnings carrying the ledger `description`. Pinned subscriptions stay silent.
- **Merged / implemented items** install the last published version under the original name AND emit a warning naming the artifact they were folded into.
- **Name clashes** (local file with no `ai-skills` origin metadata at a subscribed kebab) are surfaced as structured report items — the agent drives resolution with AskUserQuestion.
- **No LLM calls in any script.** Determinism preserved for testing.

### Test-infra changes that affect skill-registry

To make `pytest .claude/skills/` work when both suites are collected in one process:
- Removed `tests/__init__.py` from both skills (rootless dirs).
- Renamed `test_validate.py` → `test_registry_validate.py` / `test_sync_validate.py`.
- Updated both `conftest.py` files to clear shared-name modules from `sys.modules` before re-prepending the local `scripts/` path.

CI runs each skill's tests in its own subprocess so this doesn't change CI behavior — purely local-dev quality of life.

### Smoke-tested end-to-end

`skill_sync.py --registry-clone /home/user/ai-skills` loaded config, validated, found the subscribed `self-retrospective` skill in the ledger, and attempted to fetch at the recorded commit. Fetch logic verified separately at `HEAD` (returns a usable materialized skill dir). The bootstrap-recorded commit placeholder (`"commit": "bootstrap"`) is by design — real commit hashes are written on real ingestions.

## Summary

Two follow-up steps from `.claude/modernization-followup-plan.md`, both within `SPConnectionController.m`.

### Phase D3 — Pre-connection validation extracted to SAConnectionDetailsValidator
- `-[SPConnectionController initiateConnection:]` opened with ~60 lines of inline form validation: empty-host check, empty-ssh-host check, and four file-existence checks (SSH key + SSL key/cert/CA) with bespoke localized alerts. Pull the pure validation rules into `SAConnectionDetailsValidator` (Swift, no AppKit) so the "is this form ready to connect?" contract can be pinned in tests.
- `SAConnectionValidationFailure` bundles the kind + alert title/message — the controller pattern-matches the kind for per-failure side effects (clearing toggles, resetting paths) and presents the alert.
- AWS-directory authorization stays inline (depends on Security framework bookmark state the validator can't represent).
- **29 unit tests** cover happy paths for all four connection types, each individual failure trigger, skip-when-disabled / skip-when-wrong-type, failure ordering (host → ssh host → ssh key → ssl key → cert → CA), and `fileExistsExpandingTilde`.

### Connection-form helpers extracted to SAConnectionFormHelpers
- Three small pure helpers that were private methods on `SPConnectionController` move into `SAConnectionFormHelpers` (Swift):
  - `newFavoriteID()` — hash-of-`%f`-timestamp ID factory. The stringify-then-hash shape is preserved verbatim because new IDs are persisted in the favorites plist and changing the shape would risk collision with existing IDs on upgrade.
  - `stripInvalidCharacters(_:)` — trim outer whitespace + strip embedded newlines from user input.
  - `generateName(type:host:database:)` — auto-name (socket → "localhost", others require host, optional db suffix).
- The three controller methods become thin trampolines.
- **18 unit tests** cover ID non-zero + monotonic, strip semantics (no-op clean, leading/trailing whitespace+newlines, embedded newlines, embedded whitespace preserved, empty/whitespace-only), and `generateName` for all four connection types.

### Scope notes
- The plan's full D2 (favorites management actions — `addFavorite:`, `addGroup:`, `duplicateFavorite:`, `sortFavorites:`, `importFavorites:`, `exportFavorites:`) is bigger work — those IBActions are tightly coupled to `SPTreeNode` / `SPFavoritesController` and benefit from the test-target plumbing called out in [#2409](https://github.com/Sequel-Ace/Sequel-Ace/pull/2409)'s B2b note. Out of scope here.
- D1 (`updateFavoriteSelection:` — 170-line favorite-dict → form-fields mapping) also waits on richer Swift access to `SAConnectionInfo` and the favorite-key constants, deferred.

Stage 2 (registry expansion to 9 ops + ADR-004 + chain rewire), Stage 3 partial (act-op adapter + dispatcher + --dag opt-in for cortex code/repl), real-LLM cost recalibration for both LLM-backed and act ops, plus a principle-violation fix that surfaced from the Stage 3 partial landing.

### What landed (19 commits)

**Stage 2 — registry expansion** (`docs/dag-build-plan.md` Stage 2)
- 9 new ops under `pkg/cognition/dag/ops/`: `represent.embed`, `remember.vector_search`, `attend.rerank`, `value.score`, `value.detect_contradiction`, `decide.inject`, `decide.should_capture`, `model.predict_next`, `maintain.extract_insight`
- Versioned prompt templates under `pkg/cognition/prompts/*.tmpl`, bundled via `embed.FS`
- `pkg/cognition/dag/ops/template.go` loader enforces Stage-2 invariant `max_output_tokens ≤ 100`
- Every LLM op has a deterministic mechanical fallback (budget < 200ms, no provider, LLM error, JSON parse failure all fall back)
- `ops.RegisterDefaults` centralizes registration; `cmd/cortex/commands/run.go` walks an 8-node real-op chain
- [`docs/adrs/0004-prompt-templates.md`](docs/adrs/0004-prompt-templates.md) documents the format

**Stage 2 follow-up — legacy runner rewire**
- `internal/eval/legacy/runner.go` dispatches reflect + resolve modes through the new DAG ops (`attend.rerank`, `value.detect_contradiction`, `decide.inject`)
- legacy-cognition suite: 23/29 PASS pre → 27-28/29 PASS post (real-LLM measured)
- `decide.inject` fallback rebaselined to match `cognition.Resolve` thresholds (avg-based, not max-based)

**Cost recalibration — LLM ops** (`pkg/cognition/dag/ops/calibrate_test.go` build-tag-guarded probe)
- All 7 LLM-backed Stage 2 ops were 10-24× under-calibrated vs OpenRouter Haiku 4.5
- Updated hints based on real measurements
- `DefaultTurnBudget` 2000ms → 150000ms (the v0-era budget was implicitly stub-only)

**Reflect prompt iteration** (`pkg/cognition/prompts/attend_rerank.tmpl` v1→v3)
- Real bug: `formatCandidatesForPrompt` hid `category` from the model — scenarios encoded category preference but model couldn't see the field
- Fix + sharper v3 prompt eliminated `boost-decisions-over-patterns` FAIL entirely
- Steady state: 27-28/29 PASS (vs 24/29 pre-iteration)

**Stage 3 partial — act-op dispatcher** (`docs/dag-build-plan.md` Stage 3)
- Deliverable A: `internal/harness/dagnode/act_ops.go` adapts any `ToolHandler` as a `dag.NodeSpec` with axis-5 enforcement; `DefaultActOpContracts` + `DefaultActOpCosts` for the 5 canonical tools
- Deliverable B: `Loop.Dispatcher` hook + `NodeIDFromContext` on executor + `coding_turn` installs a dispatcher that routes tool calls through act ops with synthetic per-tool trace rows
- Deliverables C+D: `--dag` flag on `cortex code` + REPL opts into per-tool trace emission
- Deferred to Stage 3.5 (next session): full thin-wrapper rewrite of code.go + repl.go

**Principle violation fix** (the important one)
- The original `--dag` landing built a parallel `ToolRegistry`, silently zeroing `HarnessResult.FilesChanged` + `ShellNonZeroExits` when `--dag` was on — violated principles 5 (Reproducible) and 7 (Structured)
- Fix: `ToolDispatcher` signature now carries the registry; `NewActDispatcher` delegates execution to `reg.Dispatch` so harness accounting flows through unchanged
- `cortex_search` now included in the `--dag` path (was skipped before)
- Regression test pins the fix

**Stage 3.5 #1+#2 — real-LLM verification + act-op recalibration**
- Two `cortex code --dag` sessions ($0.014) verify trace shape end-to-end + accounting preservation
- Sample saved to `docs/dag-traces-stage-3-sample.jsonl`
- Recalibrated act-op costs from observed p50: read-class ops were 50-250× over-hinted

- legacy-cognition suite: 27-28/29 PASS steady state (vs 23/29 baseline)
- Real-LLM `cortex code --dag` verified: 5 act-op rows correctly shaped, `FilesChanged` accounting preserved end-to-end

author: philliphoff
body:
Surfaces per-spec validation findings in the viewer's dataset properties panel via a new **Validation** tab alongside Dataset / Layers.

## What you see

- **Tab header** carries a small count badge when findings exist:
  - red on errors, amber on warnings, accent on info-only
  - tooltip summarises counts
  - badge is hidden when there are zero findings
- **Tab body** shows a counts summary line and one row per finding with
  - severity icon (`ErrorCircle` / `Warning` / `Info` from FluentIcons),
  - rule id in monospace,
  - wrapped message,
  - optional `Feature: <gml:id>` line when `RelatedFeatureId` is set.
- **Empty states** distinguish:
  - "No findings." — rule pack ran clean.
  - "Validation rules not yet defined for *spec*." — spec has no pack.

Specs with a rule pack today: **S-122, S-124, S-125, S-127, S-128, S-129, S-131, S-411, S-421**.
Specs without one (S-101, S-102, S-104, S-111, S-201, S-57) keep the tab but show the "not yet defined" empty state.

## How it's wired

- `IDatasetProcessor.Validate()` returns `ValidationReport?` — default `null` means "no rule pack for this spec".
- Each of the 9 GML processors overrides it. They project the parsed raw dataset to the typed model and run `ValidationRuleSet<TTyped>.Default` via a new internal `ValidationRunner` helper that catches projection exceptions (e.g. empty datasets) and returns `ValidationReport.Empty`. Result is cached on the processor.
- `DatasetLoaderService.LoadAsync` invokes `processor.Validate()` once on the work thread after rendering succeeds and assigns the result to `DatasetEntry.SetValidationReport(...)`. Validation is **not** re-run on opacity / palette / time-step changes — it's a pure function of the parsed model.
- `DatasetEntry` exposes `Validation`, `Findings`, count properties (`ValidationFindingCount`, `ValidationErrorCount`, ...), `HasValidationFindings`, `BadgeIsError`/`Warning`/`Info`, tooltip / summary / empty-state strings.
- `ValidationFindingViewModel` wraps a single finding for display (severity → icon + class).

All UI strings live in `Resources/Strings.resx` per the viewer's localisation convention.

## Out of scope (kickoff said so)

- Click-to-zoom on findings (`Point` / `BoundingBox` are plumbed but not bound).
- Severity / rule filters.
- Findings map layer.
- Rule packs for S-101 / S-102 / S-104 / S-111 / S-201 / S-57.
- Persistence / export of findings.
- Background re-validation on settings changes.

## Tests

- `DatasetEntryValidationTests` (11 tests) covers count properties, empty-state selection, badge severity flags, and the `ValidationFindingViewModel` icon/class mapping.
- `DatasetProcessorValidationTests` adds an end-to-end smoke test that `S125DatasetProcessor.Validate()` returns a non-null report against an existing GML fixture and caches the result across calls.

`dotnet test --configuration Release` — **1714 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped** across all 24 test assemblies.

## Demo

1. Open a synthetic S-125 dataset that the rule pack flags.
2. Select the dataset row → Validation tab header shows a red badge with the finding count.
3. Switch to the Validation tab → see the error icon, rule id (monospace), message, and "Feature: …" line.
4. Switch to an S-101 ENC dataset → Validation tab still present, shows "Validation rules not yet defined for S-101".

author: agzieba
body:
## Summary

Standardizes the `predict_uncertainty()` return schema across all MotherML model backends and the pipeline abstraction layer, and adds comprehensive tests to lock in the expected contract.

## Problem

The `predict_uncertainty()` method had inconsistent return schemas depending on the model backend (CatBoost, RandomForest, TabPFN, LASSO) and the task type (regression, classification, multi-target):

- **Multi-target regressors** (`CatboostRegressorMother` with `target_type="multi_target"`) did not produce per-target output columns, leading to ambiguous downstream column handling in `pipeline_utils.py`.
- **`AbstractMotherPipeline` fallback** did not handle 2D multi-output predictions — it either raised an error or returned a malformed DataFrame.
- **`PipelineWithHyperparameterRooting.predict_uncertainty`** lacked parameter routing validation: unsupported kwargs (without the `step__param` convention) were silently ignored instead of raising a clear error.
- **`uncertainty_for_opt=True`** for multi-target CatBoost regression had no defined behavior and produced inconsistent output.
- **Classification fallback path** did not populate the `total_uncertainty` column, which is required by downstream CV and optimization logic.

## Changes

### core.py — `AbstractMotherPipeline.predict_uncertainty`
- Extended the fallback to handle **2D multi-output predictions**: produces a flat DataFrame with columns named `target_{i}_{field}` (e.g. `target_0_pred`, `target_1_knowledge_uncertainty`), consistent with the specialized CatBoost multi-target schema.
- Added a **classifier fallback path** using `predict_proba` and Shannon entropy as `total_uncertainty` when no dedicated uncertainty method is available.

### core.py — `PipelineWithHyperparameterRooting.predict_uncertainty`
- Added **strict kwargs validation** using sklearn's `step__param` naming convention. Parameters that do not match any pipeline step now raise a `ValueError` with a clear message instead of being silently dropped.
- Added **step-specific parameter routing** so that kwargs like `ml_model__n_ensembles=5` are forwarded only to the matching step.

### m_catboost.py — `CatboostRegressorMother.predict_uncertainty`
- Fixed the **`uncertainty_for_opt=True` path for multi-target regression**: now logs an explicit warning and returns a single `total_uncertainty` column (max across targets).
- Hardened multi-target output to always use `target_{i}_*` column naming, regardless of the original target column names in `y`.
- Preserved the **input DataFrame index** in the output for all code paths.

### m_catboost.py — `CatboostClassifierMother.predict_uncertainty`
- Ensured `pred` (standard model prediction) is always included as the first column.
- Added `predict_proba` output as `proba_{i}` columns in a stable position between `pred` and the uncertainty columns.
- Added explicit shape validation for the `predict_proba` output.

## Standardized Output Schema

**Single-target:**

| Column | Description |
|---|---|
| `pred` | Standard model prediction |
| `mean_predictions` | Ensemble mean (or `None` for fallback) |
| `knowledge_uncertainty` | Epistemic uncertainty |
| `data_uncertainty` | Aleatoric uncertainty |
| `total_uncertainty` | Total uncertainty |

**Multi-target:** Same fields, prefixed as `target_{i}_{field}`.

## Tests Added

### test_ml.py

| Test | Coverage |
|---|---|
| `test_predict_uncertainty_classification` | All classification algorithms return a DataFrame with the 4 required uncertainty columns |
| `test_predict_uncertainty_regression` | All regression algorithms return a DataFrame with all 5 required columns including `pred` |
| `test_predict_uncertainty_multitarget_with_dataframe` | Multi-target CatBoost always uses `target_{i}_*` column names regardless of original `y` column names |
| `test_predict_uncertainty_multitarget_preserves_index` | Multi-target output preserves the input DataFrame index |
| `test_predict_uncertainty_fallback_multitarget_schema` | `AbstractMotherPipeline` fallback produces correct per-target columns for multi-output `predict()` |
| `test_predict_uncertainty_fallback_multitarget_preserves_index` | Fallback preserves input index for multi-output |
| `test_catboost_regressor_uncertainty_for_opt_multitarget_warns` | `uncertainty_for_opt=True` with multi-target logs a warning and returns a single `total_uncertainty` column |

### test_pipeline.py — `TestPipelineWithHyperparameterRootingPredictUncertainty`

| Test | Coverage |
|---|---|
| `test_predict_uncertainty_without_parameters` | Basic call with no kwargs works and returns a DataFrame |
| `test_predict_uncertainty_with_valid_parameters` | `step__param` kwargs are forwarded correctly |
| `test_predict_uncertainty_with_invalid_parameter_no_separator` | Bare kwargs (no `__`) raise `ValueError` |

author: vampik33
body:
## Summary

Three independent bugs in the DeepSeek remediation reusables (`codex-{security,semver}-fix.yml`, `dependency-review.yml`) surfaced once the tier-0/1 fan-out wave actually hit real workload. All three previously latent because the pilot repo (`greentic-i18n`) had no violations.

## Bugs fixed

### 1. Wrong Goose model ID prefix

`GOOSE_MODEL=openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-v4-{pro,flash}` was rejected by OpenRouter via Goose:

> Bad request (400): openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash is not a valid model ID. Available models for this provider: …, deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash, deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro, …

Fix: drop the `openrouter/` segment in all 3 reusable defaults.

### 2. App-token mint fails in greentic-biz private repos

Both orgs are on **GitHub Free**, which does **not** propagate org secrets to private repositories (same limitation documented in \`project_branch_protection_limitation\` memory). Every nightly run on greentic-biz/{customers-tools,greentic-tenant-manager} crashed with:

\`\`\`
Error: [@octokit/auth-app] appId option is required
\`\`\`

\`tag-on-version-bump.yml\` already documents and works around this with \`continue-on-error: true\` + \`\${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}\` fallback. Applied the same pattern to all 3 deepseek reusables.

Trade-off: \`github.token\` fallback loses cross-workflow-triggering on the push event. That's acceptable here — the remediation PR's own CI fires via push event regardless. Long-term fix is upgrading greentic-biz to Team plan.

### 3. Empty \`BRANCH\` on scheduled runs

\`git push origin "HEAD:\${BRANCH}"\` resolved to \`HEAD:\` and died with \`fatal: invalid refspec\` because neither \`github.event.pull_request.head.ref\` nor \`inputs.branch\` is set under cron. Even defaulting BRANCH to a value would violate the never-push-to-main rule (\`feedback_branch_and_pr\` memory).

Fix: split the commit/push step:

- **PR-triggered** (\`BRANCH\` non-empty): keep the existing \`HEAD:BRANCH\` push so the PR's CI re-runs with the remediation patch.
- **Scheduled** (\`BRANCH\` empty): push to \`chore/deepseek-{security,semver}-\${GITHUB_RUN_ID}\` and \`gh pr create\` against the default branch.

Note: \`RUN_ID\` in the branch name means each nightly produces a new PR if alerts persist. Bounded accumulation, easy to close manually. Stale-PR cleanup can be a follow-up if it becomes painful.

## Scope

| File | Bugs addressed |
|---|---|
| \`.github/workflows/codex-security-fix.yml\` | 1 + 2 + 3 |
| \`.github/workflows/codex-semver-fix.yml\` | 1 + 2 + 3 |
| \`.github/workflows/dependency-review.yml\` | 1 + 2 (PR-only, no bug 3) |

No caller workflow edits — all 14 enrolled callers already use \`secrets: inherit\`.

## Verification

- [x] All 3 files pass \`yaml.safe_load\`.
- [x] Each \`steps.app-token.outputs.token\` reference now reads \`steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token\`.
- [x] Both \`Mint GitHub App token\` steps have \`continue-on-error: true\`.
- [x] \`grep -n "openrouter/deepseek"\` returns nothing in the 3 reusables.

## Test plan

After merge:

- [ ] Tonight (~03:00–03:53 UTC window): re-check failing runs cited in the bug report:
  - greentic-biz/greentic-tenant-manager codex-{security,semver}-fix — should now \`detect-work=success\`, gate \`should-fix=true\` for any real semver/security findings, then either push to a new \`chore/deepseek-…-…\` branch + open PR, or report no changes.
  - greenticai/greentic-start codex-security-fix — Goose should now accept the model and either remediate (PR opened) or no-op.
- [ ] Spot-check the App-token fallback path by looking at job logs: \`Mint GitHub App token\` step should show as failing-but-continued in greentic-biz repos; downstream steps should still succeed using \`github.token\`.

## Related

- Migration plan: \`plans/migrate-codex-deepseek.md\`
- Pilot tracking: greenticai/.github#188 (tier-0/1 fan-out), greenticai/.github#189 (sync script bugfix)

author: shantoislam242
body:
# Phase 8a — Admission CMS Part 1 (Notices + Prospectus)

**Part 1 of 3-part Admission CMS migration.** Phase 8b and 8c follow.

This PR migrates two of the six `/admission/*` pages — `/admission/notice` and `/admission/prospectus` — from hardcoded React to fully DB-driven CMS surfaces. Both pages are now editable end-to-end from `/admin` with the same admin UX as Phase 6/7 (multi-row tables, drag-reorder, ImageUploader for image + PDF).

After this PR merges, the remaining four `/admission/*` pages are in Phase 8b/8c scope:
- **Phase 8b** — `/admission/requirements` + `/admission/tuition-fees` (Program-linked)
- **Phase 8c** — `/admission/transfer-credits` + `/admission/waiver-scholarship` (policy singletons + Scholarship multi-row)

## Scope summary

| Surface | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `/admission/notice` | Single hardcoded Summer-2026 letterhead (141 LOC) | Server component reading the latest `isActive=true` `AdmissionNotice` row; empty state when no active row |
| `/admission/prospectus` | Client component with 1 hardcoded program PDF (179 LOC) | Server fetches `ProspectusEntry[]`, passes to `ProspectusClient.tsx` (same search + UG/PG filter UX) |
| Admin | — | `/admin/admission-notices` (CRUD + reorder + PDF/image upload) and `/admin/prospectus-entries` (CRUD + reorder + cover/PDF upload) |
| Sidebar | 5 collapsible groups | 6 collapsible groups (new "Admission" group, will host Phase 8b/8c) |
| Dashboard | 16 stat cards | 18 stat cards (+ AdmissionNotice count, + ProspectusEntry count) + 2 new action cards |
| Search index | 15 entity sources | 17 entity sources (+ AdmissionNotice latest-active, + ProspectusEntry full list) |

## Decisions A–E (+ B1) — surfaced before execution, chair-approved

The master prompt for Phase 8a proposed two table shapes that **did not match what the discovered pages actually rendered**. Surface-before-execute discipline caught both before any code was written.

### Decision A — Phase 6 Notice table reuse vs separate `AdmissionNotice`
**Resolution: separate table.** The Phase 6 `Notice` table is a flat notice-board card (title + description + file). `/admission/notice` is a formal Registrar letter with 6 additional structured fields (`refNo`, `subject`, `signatoryPreamble`, `signatoryName`, `signatoryDesignation`, `ccList`). Reusing the `Notice` table would have forced 6 nullable columns onto rows that never use them, or stored letterhead semantics in a Json blob (losing admin UX clarity). Cleaner separation.

### Decision B — Singleton-style vs multi-row with archive
**Resolution: multi-row + `isActive` flag.** The current page renders one notice, but the admin "publish a new notice" UX needs replacement-by-publish semantics. Multi-row with `isActive` toggle lets the admin queue/swap notices and (later) opens an archive route without schema changes.

### Decision B1 — Archive detail page `/admission/notice/[slug]` in 8a?
**Resolution: skip in 8a.** Older notices stay in the DB but have no public route. Admin toggles `isActive` to swap visibility. Defer the archive page to Phase 9 if archive demand surfaces.

### Decision C — Prospectus singleton (master prompt) vs multi-row (discovery)
**Resolution: multi-row `ProspectusEntry` table.** The master prompt proposed `AdmissionProspectus (singleton)` with hero/intro/program-highlights/brochure-PDF/CTAs. **Discovery contradicted:** the current `/admission/prospectus` page has no hero copy, no intro paragraphs, no CTAs — it's purely a multi-row program PDF grid with client-side search + UG/PG filter (1 row currently, UI built for many). A singleton with marketing copy would have broken visual parity (constraint #7). YAGNI — defer landing chrome to Phase 8b/9 when there's actual copy demand.

### Decision D — Reuse Phase 7 `Syllabus` table?
**Resolution: separate `ProspectusEntry`.** Same field shape (slug/title/shortTitle/department/level/cover/pdf/IDs), but semantically distinct documents. A program may have both a syllabus and a prospectus → slug collision risk. Slight duplication is cheaper than adding a `documentType` discriminator and breaking Phase 7 admin UX.

### Decision E — Cloudinary kind naming
**Resolution: revised 4 kinds.** Master prompt assumed prospectus singleton with hero/brochure. With multi-row Prospectus, the kinds become:
- `admission-notice-hero` / `admission-notice-file` → `admission/notices`
- `prospectus-cover` / `prospectus-pdf` → `admission/prospectus/{covers,pdfs}`

## Schema additions

One migration: `20260518045941_add_admission_8a_notice_prospectus`. Two new tables, no foreign keys, no touches to Phase 0–7 tables.

```prisma
model AdmissionNotice {
  id                    String   @id @default(cuid())
  slug                  String   @unique
  title                 String
  refNo                 String
  subject               String
  publishedAt           DateTime
  displayDate           String?

  headerOverline        String   @default("Office of the Registrar")
  bodyParagraphs        Json     // string[] — HTML-allowed paragraphs
  signatoryPreamble     String?
  signatoryName         String
  signatoryDesignation  String
  ccLabel               String   @default("Copy for Kind Information (not according to seniority)")
  ccList                Json     // string[] — plain text recipients

  heroImageUrl          String?
  heroImagePublicId     String?
  fileUrl               String?
  filePublicId          String?
  fileName              String?

  isActive              Boolean  @default(true)
  displayOrder          Int
  createdAt             DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt             DateTime @updatedAt

  @@index([publishedAt])
  @@index([isActive, publishedAt])
  @@map("admission_notice")
}

model ProspectusEntry {
  id            String   @id @default(cuid())
  slug          String   @unique
  title         String
  shortTitle    String
  department    String
  level         String   // 'Undergraduate' | 'Postgraduate'
  coverUrl      String
  coverPublicId String?
  pdfUrl        String?
  pdfPublicId   String?
  pdfFileName   String?
  displayOrder  Int
  createdAt     DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt     DateTime @updatedAt

  @@index([displayOrder])
  @@index([level])
  @@map("prospectus_entry")
}
```

### Seeded rows
- `AdmissionNotice` — 1 (Summer-2026 Inauguration Ceremony, extracted verbatim from the previous hardcoded page including all 4 body paragraphs with inline `<strong>` / `<em>` and the 5-entry Cc list)
- `ProspectusEntry` — 1 (B.Sc. in Mechanical Engineering, Undergraduate, with the same cover + PDF assets)

## File inventory (33 files, +1850 / −275)

### CP8a.1 — schema + seed (commit `8f1a85b`)
- `prisma/schema.prisma` — 2 new models
- `prisma/migrations/20260518045941_add_admission_8a_notice_prospectus/migration.sql`
- `scripts/seed.ts` — `seedAdmissionNotice` + `seedProspectusEntries` (idempotent upserts)
- `src/lib/cloudinary.ts` — 4 new kinds in `KIND_TO_SUBFOLDER`
- `src/components/admin/ImageUploader.tsx` — 4 new kinds on the `Kind` union

### CP8a.2 — admin layer (commit `5a41138`)
- `src/lib/validation.ts` — `admissionNoticeCreate/UpdateSchema`, `prospectusEntryCreate/UpdateSchema`, `prospectusLevelEnum`, `ccListSchema`; `uploadKindSchema` extended
- `src/lib/admin-actions/admission-notices.ts` — `create/update/delete/reorder`
- `src/lib/admin-actions/prospectus-entries.ts` — same
- `src/app/api/admin/admission-notices/{route,[id]/route,reorder/route}.ts`
- `src/app/api/admin/prospectus-entries/{route,[id]/route,reorder/route}.ts`
- `src/app/admin/(authed)/admission-notices/{page,AdmissionNoticeList,AdmissionNoticeForm,new/page,[id]/page}.tsx`
- `src/app/admin/(authed)/prospectus-entries/{page,ProspectusList,ProspectusForm,new/page,[id]/page}.tsx`
- `src/components/admin/Sidebar.tsx` — new `ADMISSION_NAV` group + collapsible state
- `src/app/admin/(authed)/page.tsx` — 2 stat cards + 2 action cards

### CP8a.3 — public wiring + search-index (commit `bc2ddd7`)
- `src/lib/identity.ts

## Why
EPAC-1918 moves eligible iOS cached reads off backend API routes and onto CloudFront artifacts now that the artifact publisher is available. The app keeps the same service/view-model surfaces while `ArtifactService` and `ArtifactIngestActor` handle fetch + SwiftData ingestion.

## What changed
- Added shared artifact keys for members, sittings, bills, member speeches, On This Day `all.json`, riding boundaries, and calendar export.
- Swapped `MemberSpeechService`, `OnThisDayService`, `RidingBoundaryService`, `CalendarExportService`, `BillsService`, and the `Fetch` members/sittings/Hansard loaders to artifact-backed reads.
- Extended `ArtifactIngestActor` to decode current artifact payload shapes and ingest member, sitting calendar, bill DTO, and sitting-speech data into the existing app models.
- Added artifact-path tests and updated adjacent service/view-model tests, including the calendar date-component assertion to match the app's Y/M/D comparison behavior.
- Updated the Clean Architecture use-case catalog to document the adapter swap.

## Backend URL call sites
Verified with `rg -n "BackendConfig\\.shared\\.baseURL" ios/epac ios/epacTests -g '*.swift'`.

| Call site | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ios/epac/Util/MemberSpeechService.swift` | Built `/api/v1/members/{id}/speeches` from `BackendConfig.shared.baseURL`. | Removed; fetches `.memberSpeeches(memberID:)` through `ArtifactService`, then filters/paginates locally. |
| `ios/epac/Util/OnThisDayService.swift` | Built `/api/v1/on-this-day/{MM-dd}` from `BackendConfig.shared.baseURL`. | Removed; fetches `on-this-day/v1/all.json` through `ArtifactService`, then filters by month/day, past date, and limit locally. |
| `ios/epac/Util/RidingBoundaryService.swift` | Built `/api/v1/ridings/{slug}/boundary` from `BackendConfig.shared.baseURL`. | Removed; fetches `.ridingBoundary(slug:)` through `ArtifactService`. |
| `ios/epac/Util/CalendarExportService.swift` | Returned `BackendConfig.shared.baseURL/api/v1/calendar/house.ics`. | Returns `ArtifactConfig.shared.baseURL/calendar/v1/house.ics`. |
| `ios/epac/Util/ReviewRequestManager.swift` | Uses `BackendConfig.shared.baseURL` for remote config. | Kept with an inline comment because no published config artifact exists yet. |
| `ios/epac/Util/NetworkService.swift` | Uses `BackendConfig.shared.baseURL` to detect backend-host requests. | Kept; this is shared transport/telemetry logic, not a migrated data fetch. |
| `ios/epac/Util/BackendConfig.swift` | Defines/comments the backend base URL. | Unchanged. |
| `ios/epacTests/NetworkServiceTests.swift` | Builds `/api/v1/live` for live-endpoint transport coverage. | Unchanged; live endpoint is explicitly out of scope. |

## Trade-offs not taken
- Constituency XML, single-member detail/contact, vote history, and written questions stay on their authoritative sources with inline comments because no compatible CloudFront artifact exists yet, or the current SwiftData schema does not match the artifact shape.
- Bills are read from the S3 artifact for list rendering, but SwiftData bill persistence remains unsupported until the app has a durable bill model.
- This PR is larger than the usual preferred size because EPAC-1918 intentionally spans the service group plus shared artifact decoding and tests.

## Test plan

- [x] Targeted artifact/service test pass:

author: lundog
body:
### Problem

OpenClaw's gateway (Node.js) cannot establish HTTPS connections to other StartOS services (e.g., LLM proxies like Maple) because:

1. **Node.js ignores the system trust store** — it uses its own bundled CA bundle and requires `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` to trust additional CAs
2. **`installRootCA` runs too late** — it executes in a `oneshot` that depends on the `primary` daemon, so the CA is installed *after* the gateway has already started
3. **The existing CA installation only updates the system store** (`update-ca-certificates`) which Node.js doesn't read

This results in certificate validation errors when OpenClaw tries to reach any StartOS-signed HTTPS endpoint from tool calls or model proxy configurations.

### Solution

1. **Move `installRootCA` to a prerequisite `oneshot`** — runs before the `primary` daemon starts, ensuring the StartOS root CA is in `/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt` before the gateway boots
2. **Add `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`** environment variable to the `primary` daemon's `env` block, pointing to the CA bundle path

### Changes

- `startos/main.ts`:
  - New `install-root-ca` oneshot that runs `installRootCA()` before any other daemon
  - `chown` oneshot now `requires: ['install-root-ca']`
  - `primary` daemon now `requires: ['install-root-ca', 'chown']`
  - Added `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS: '/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt'` to daemon `env`

- `Dockerfile`:
  - Added `ENV NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt` for consistency

### Testing

- [x] Built `.s9pk` with `make`
- [x] Sideloaded onto StartOS 0.4.0
- [x] Confirmed OpenClaw gateway starts without errors
- [x] Verified HTTPS connection to `maple/kimi-k2-6` (StartOS-hosted LLM proxy) succeeds
- [x] Chat completion requests via `https://<startos-host>:<maple-port>/v1` work correctly

### Impact

This fix enables OpenClaw to communicate securely with any other StartOS service over HTTPS, including but not limited to:
- LLM proxies (Maple, etc.)
- Other AI services
- Any StartOS-hosted API that uses the StartOS internal CA

No breaking changes — existing installations will simply gain working HTTPS after the next service restart.

author: valerielinc-ops
body:
GH Pages cannot do server-side 301s, and the SPA router's
window.location.replace from PR #200 only runs after JS hydration. That
left Google still seeing HTTP 404 on every GSC-discovered orphan URL
like /cerca-lavoro-basilea/offerte-di-lavoro-ticino-oggi/ — the SPA
fallback returns the 404.html page with HTTP 404 status, and the
crawler indexes the status before the redirect ever fires.

Add cantonOrphanRedirectsPlugin (apply:'build', enforce:'post',
closeBundle) that emits a real HTTP-200 HTML file at every
/{prefix}/cerca-lavoro-{canton}/{foreign-editorial-slug}/ combination.
Each file carries `<link rel="canonical">` pointing to that canton's
canonical equivalent, `noindex,follow`, and a `<meta http-equiv="refresh">`
so real users land on the right URL within ~500ms even before the SPA
boots. Plugin is collision-safe: skips when a higher-priority plugin
already wrote a real page at the path.

Scope: 24 cantons × 4 locales × 7 editorial slots (today / nurses /
part-time / 4 care-cluster) × the foreign slug variants from other
cantons = 2,016 redirect files (~4 MB to dist/). Gated by
SKIP_CANTON_ORPHAN_REDIRECTS=1 for fast local builds.

Test enumerates 7 representative orphan combinations including the
originally reported BASILEA URL, all 4 locales, and care-cluster slugs.
