body:
## Summary

Adds a bundled `copilot` plugin that registers an opt-in **agent runtime**
backed by [`@github/copilot-sdk`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@github/copilot-sdk)
and the GitHub Copilot CLI. Selection is fully **config-driven**. The runtime registers via
  `api.registerAgentHarness({ id: "copilot", ... })` and is selected by
  setting `agentRuntime.id: "copilot"` on a model or provider entry.
  
- What changed:
  - New bundled plugin `extensions/copilot/` (harness + 13 bridges +
    doctor probes + tests).
  - Docs: new `docs/plugins/copilot.md`; additions to
    `docs/concepts/agent-runtimes.md` and `docs/concepts/models.md` so
    the selection rules are discoverable.
  - QA capability inventory `qa/copilot-capabilities.md` pinning the
    runtime against `@github/copilot-sdk@1.0.0-beta.4`.
  - `.github/labeler.yml` entry for `extensions: copilot`.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary):
  - **No source-tree changes outside `extensions/copilot/` and docs/QA.**
  - 
## Motivation

OpenClaw users currently can't run any OpenClaw agent
using the Github Copilot SDK as the agent runtime. This
change adds the copilot agent runtime as a peer to `pi` / `codex` so the same agent
definition can be flipped between runtimes via one config field, while
PI remains the safe default for everyone else.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Feature
- [x] Docs

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [] Skills / tool execution
- [] Integrations

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #
- Related #
- [ ] This PR fixes a bug or regression

> Tracking issue will be opened on `openclaw/openclaw` before review.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior or issue addressed: route an agent attempt through the GitHub
  Copilot SDK runtime instead of PI, opt-in per model or per provider.
- Real environment tested: WSL Ubuntu, OpenClaw built from this branch,
  gateway running locally against a real GitHub Copilot subscription
  token.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

  ```jsonc
  // ~/.openclaw-copilot-play/openclaw.json
  {
    "agents": {
      "defaults": {
        "model": { "primary": "github-copilot/gpt-4.1" },
        "models": {
          "github-copilot/gpt-4.1": { "agentRuntime": { "id": "copilot" } }
        }
      }
    },
    "plugins": { "entries": { "copilot": { "enabled": true } } },
    "gateway": {
      "mode": "local",
      "http": {
        "endpoints": {
          "chatCompletions": { "enabled": true },
          "responses":       { "enabled": true }
        }
      }
    }
  }
  ```

  ```bash
  corepack pnpm install
  corepack pnpm build
  OPENCLAW_GITHUB_TOKEN=<redacted> \
    node openclaw.mjs --profile copilot-play gateway run \
      --port 18789 --bind loopback \
      --auth token --token <redacted>

  curl -sS -X POST \
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    http://127.0.0.1:18789/v1/chat/completions \
    --data '{"model":"openclaw/main","stream":false,
             "messages":[{"role":"user",
               "content":"reply with only POST-RUNSIDE-DELETE-OK"}]}'
  ```

- Evidence after fix (gateway log + HTTP response, redacted):

  ```
  [gateway] auto-enabled plugins for this runtime without writing config:
    - github-copilot/gpt-4.1 model configured, enabled automatically.
  [gateway] agent model: github-copilot/gpt-4.1 (thinking=medium, fast=off)
  [gateway] http server listening
    (9 plugins: acpx, browser, canvas, copilot, device-pair,
     file-transfer, memory-core, phone-control, talk-voice; 2.6s)
  [gateway] ready
  ```

  ```json
  {
    "id": "chatcmpl_c89dbe21-b073-4ba6-b6b0-44153655e756",
    "object": "chat.completion",
    "model": "openclaw/main",
    "choices": [{
      "index": 0,
      "message": { "role": "assistant",
                   "content": "POST-RUNSIDE-DELETE-OK" },
      "finish_reason": "stop"
    }],
    "usage": { "prompt_tokens": 21908,
               "completion_tokens": 9,
               "total_tokens": 21917 }
  }
  ```

- Observed result after fix: the gateway loads the `copilot` plugin
  alongside the other bundled plugins; the agent attempt is dispatched
  through the `copilot` runtime; the reply comes back through the
  Copilot SDK transport. Removing `agentRuntime.id` falls back to PI
  with no other change.
- What was not tested: TUI surfaces (the runtime is non-TUI; PI remains
  the TUI path); BYOK adapters (explicitly out of scope — the runtime is
  hard-bound to the canonical `github-copilot` provider).
- Before evidence: with `plugins.entries.copilot.enabled` false (or
  absent), the `agentRuntime.id: "copilot"` selector resolves to
  nothing and the attempt falls back to PI via the existing
  `selectAgentHarness` path — no other behaviour change for hosts that
  don't opt in.

## Root Cause (if applicable)

N/A — feature add.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

N/A — no bug.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- New opt-in agent runtime id `copilot`, selectable via
  `agentRuntime.id` on a model entry or `runtime.id` on a provider
  entry.
- New bundled plugin entry `plugins.entries.copilot.enabled`. When the
  entry is disabled or absent, the runtime id is unknown to the
  registry and the resolver falls back to PI with no behaviour change
  for existing users.
- `auto` selection never picks `copilot` — selection is always
  explicit.
- `/btw` for a `github-copilot/*`-model agent under the `copilot`
  runtime uses the same in-tree PI fallback path
  (`src/agents/btw.ts` → `streamSimple` via the `github-copilot`
  provider) that any other runtime would. The runtime does not
  implement `runSideQuestion`, so there is no SDK-specific `/btw`

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
[agent attempt] -> [PI runtime] -> [Copilot HTTP via the
                                    github-copilot provider]

After (only when agentRuntime.id === "copilot"):
[agent attempt] -> [copilot runtime] -> [@github/copilot-sdk +

Otherwise unchanged:
[agent attempt] -> [PI runtime] -> [unchanged path]
```

- New permissions/capabilities? `No`.
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? `No` — the runtime reads tokens the
  same way the rest of OpenClaw does (`GITHUB_TOKEN` /
  `OPENCLAW_GITHUB_TOKEN` / the existing `github-copilot:` auth-profile
  prefix / the logged-in Copilot CLI user). No new env vars are read
  and no new auth-profile namespace is added.
- New/changed network calls? `Yes (additive)` — outbound HTTPS to the
  Copilot endpoints the bundled SDK targets (same surface that
  subscription Copilot users already hit via
  `extensions/github-copilot/`). No new third-party hosts.
- Command/tool execution surface changed? `Yes (additive)` — the

- Data access scope changed? `No`. Per-agent `copilotHome` keeps
  Copilot CLI state isolated under
  `~/.openclaw/agents/<agentId>/copilot` by default.

author: bensepanski
body:
## Summary

- **`ws.py`**: Added `broadcast_to_session(session_id, event)` — a process-safe, async helper that delivers JSON events to all connected WebSocket clients for a session. Dead connections are pruned silently; the function is a no-op when no clients are connected, so it's safe to call unconditionally from every HTTP endpoint.
- **`sessions.py`**: After the AI response is committed, broadcasts `chat_message` (with role + content) and, when present, `proposal_ready` (with proposal_id + type).
- **`combat.py`**: Every state-mutating endpoint (`start_combat`, `submit_combat_action`, `next_turn`, `end_combat`) broadcasts a `combat_update` carrying the full `CombatStateRead` payload. Broadcast failures are swallowed with `logger.exception` so the HTTP response is never broken by a WS issue.
- **`ai.py`**: `accept_proposal` broadcasts `proposal_ready` (with `status=accepted`) and, when an entity is created, `entity_update` (with `entity_type` + `entity_id`). `reject_proposal` broadcasts `proposal_ready` with `status=rejected`.
- **`test_ws_broadcast.py`** (new, 8 tests): unit tests for `broadcast_to_session` (no-op, delivery, multi-client, dead-connection cleanup, session isolation) + 2 integration tests via Starlette `TestClient` + threading that verify a WS client receives `combat_update` and `chat_message` events triggered by HTTP endpoints.
- **`docs/architecture.md`**: Updated WebSocket section to document implemented vs. planned events and add a multi-process (Redis pub/sub) note.

## Why this matters

Before this PR, the WebSocket endpoint was a pure peer relay — messages only moved between browser clients. The HTTP endpoints (chat, combat, proposals) had no way to notify connected clients. This made real-time play impossible without constant polling. The architecture docs described these events as "planned"; they are now implemented.

## Test plan

- [x] All 92 dm-api tests pass (`pytest tests/ -q`)
- [x] All 253 game-engine tests pass
- [x] `broadcast_to_session` unit tests cover: no-op path, delivery to 1 and N clients, dead-connection pruning, empty-key cleanup, session isolation
- [x] Integration tests verify `combat_update` and `chat_message` arrive at a real WebSocket client over a threaded Starlette TestClient
- [x] Existing `test_websocket.py` tests (connect, broadcast, isolation, malformed JSON) unchanged and passing
- [x] `black`, `isort`, `autoflake` clean

body:
## Summary

- Adds `crates/solobase-core/src/blocks/vector/migrations/{001_vector_schema.sqlite.sql, 001_vector_schema.postgres.sql, mod.rs}` for the one static block-owned table (`suppers_ai__vector__registry`) and wires `migrations::apply` into the `Init` lifecycle. Same pattern as solobase #137 / #190 / #192 / #193 / #194 / #195.
- Removes the inline `ensure_registry()` + `registry_schema()` helpers that previously ran `CREATE TABLE` on every `create_index` call. The migration now runs once at boot through `apply_if_blessed` (hash-gated; `SOLOBASE_RUN_MIGRATIONS=1` for schema changes).
- Adds `idx_vector_registry_model` so future model-rollup queries are index-backed instead of full-scanning the catalog. Existing `prefixed_name` lookups stay PK-served.

## Dynamic per-index tables — decision

The vector block creates **N** runtime per-index tables per user-created index: `{prefixed}_meta`, `{prefixed}_fts`, and a `vec0` virtual table — names are `suppers_ai__vector__{user_name}…`, where `user_name` is user-supplied at `create_index` time. These are **not** materialized by solobase: the upstream `wafer-run/vector` runtime block owns their DDL via `vclient::create_index(ctx, cfg)`, dispatched from `pages.rs::create_index`. They stay on that path because:

1. Their names aren't known at compile time, so a static `.sql` file can't express them.
2. A wrapper `db::ddl` call at create-index time would just duplicate what `wafer-run/vector` already does (FTS5 setup + vec0 dimensions wiring).

Both the SQL file header and `migrations/mod.rs` document this scope split.

## Tracker

Last block on the ensure_table-removal list (`/workspace/.../ensure-table-removal-in-progress.md`). With this merged, `wafer-block-sqlite`'s `ensure_table()` shim can be retired as a follow-up once a deploy has run `--run-migrations` on every existing DB.

- [x] `cargo check -p solobase-cloudflare --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` clean

body:
## Summary
This PR introduces a new `FileSystem` class that provides a flexible asset search path system, replacing hardcoded asset directory paths throughout the codebase. Assets are now resolved through configurable search paths with priority ordering, enabling better asset organization and supporting multiple asset directories (e.g., base assets, patches, DLC).

## Key Changes

- **New FileSystem class** (`file_system.hpp/cpp`):
  - Singleton pattern for centralized asset path resolution
  - Support for multiple search paths with priority ordering
  - Methods: `resolvePath()` (returns optional), `resolvePathOrThrow()` (throws on failure)
  - Default initialization sets up search paths: `ResHR` (debug only), `ResPatch`, `Res`, `ResDLC`

- **Updated asset loading paths** across all renderers and managers:
  - Removed `assets/` prefix from all asset paths (now relative paths like `shaders/`, `textures/`, `ui/`, `fonts/`, `models/`)
  - Updated `renderer_metal.cpp`: 30+ shader and texture path references
  - Updated `renderer_vulkan.cpp`: shader and texture path references
  - Updated `asset_manager.cpp`: image, OBJ, and GLTF loading to use FileSystem
  - Updated `audio_engine.cpp`: audio file loading
  - Updated `rmlui_manager.cpp`: font and document loading
  - Updated `font_manager.cpp`: font file loading
  - Updated `helper.cpp`: generic file reading

- **Build system updates**:
  - Modified `VaporMacros.cmake`: assets now copied to `Res/` instead of `assets/`
  - Updated `Vaporware/CMakeLists.txt`: asset copy target uses `Res/` directory

- **Engine initialization**:
  - `engine_core.cpp`: FileSystem initialized early in engine startup before any asset loading
  - `asset_manager_test.cpp`: Updated test to use FileSystem

## Implementation Details

- All asset paths are now relative (e.g., `"shaders/3d_pbr_normal_mapped.metal"` instead of `"assets/shaders/3d_pbr_normal_mapped.metal"`)
- FileSystem resolves paths by checking each search path in priority order (lower priority value = searched first)
- Graceful fallback: `resolvePath()` returns `std::nullopt` if asset not found; `resolvePathOrThrow()` throws `std::runtime_error`
- Maintains backward compatibility through centralized resolution logic

## Summary

Key changes:

author: sparlane
body:
## Description

Three stages: node:26-slim builds the frontend bundle, python:3.13-slim with build-essential and libgdal-dev compiles the venv and runs collectstatic, then a clean python:3.13-slim runtime image receives only the venv, collected static files, and app source directories. The runtime stage installs libgdal36 (runtime library only, not the full -dev package) and contains no compiler toolchain, node runtime, frontend source, or build scripts. The CI workflow's separate node/frontend pre-build step is removed since Docker handles it.

## Summary by Sourcery

Switch to a multi-stage Docker build that produces a minimal Python runtime image and moves Django configuration to environment-based settings suitable for containerized deployment.

New Features:
- Add a dedicated frontend build stage using node:26-slim to produce the static bundle within the Docker build.
- Introduce a Python builder stage that creates a virtualenv, installs dependencies, and runs collectstatic before copying artifacts into the runtime image.
- Configure Django settings to be driven primarily by environment variables, including database configuration and secret key.

Enhancements:
- Refactor Dockerfile into separate frontend, app-source, Python builder, and slim runtime stages to reduce image size and remove build toolchains from the final image.
- Ensure both builder and runtime stages share a single source-of-truth file list via an intermediate app-source stage to keep container contents consistent.
- Update runtime image to use libgdal36 runtime library instead of the full libgdal-dev toolchain.
- Simplify container startup by removing in-container schema creation and migration generation from the start script and relying on pre-built artifacts.
- Pass DJANGO_SECRET_KEY via environment instead of reading from a file at runtime for better alignment with container practices.

CI:
- Remove GitHub Actions steps that separately set up Node and build the frontend, delegating the frontend build to the Docker build process.

Deployment:
- Wire docker-compose to supply DJANGO_SECRET_KEY and other Django settings via environment variables for containerized deployments.

author: kylinmountain
body:
## Summary

Adds a **Skill Factory** that distils an OpenKB wiki into a redistributable [Anthropic Skill](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/skills) — a portable directory that Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, and Cursor all install and load natively.

- New `openkb skill new <name> "<intent>"` CLI command writes `<kb>/output/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` (+ optional `references/<slug>.md` for depth-on-demand).
- New `/skill new` slash command in `openkb chat` — same generator, conversational entry point. The chat agent now has write access scoped to `<kb>/output/**` and `<kb>/wiki/explorations/**` so users can iterate via natural-language follow-ups.
- Auto-regenerated `<kb>/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` lists all compiled skills, so pushing the KB to GitHub makes `npx skills@latest add <owner>/<repo>` work end-to-end.
- Companion commands: `openkb skill validate` (structural lint), `openkb skill eval` (trigger accuracy + body coverage), `openkb skill history` / `openkb skill rollback` (iteration safety).

## Architecture

Reuses the existing `openai-agents` SDK + LiteLLM stack from `openkb.agent.query`. All skill-related code lives under `openkb/skill/`:

- `creator.py` — builds the compile agent via `build_skill_create_agent`, system prompt loaded from `openkb/prompts/skill_create.md` and interpolated with intent + skill name + wiki schema. Tools are scoped: read wiki (`list_wiki_dir`, `read_wiki_file`, `get_page_content`, `get_image`), nested semantic search (`query_wiki`, narrow follow-ups only), write within the skill root.
- `generator.py` — the shared `Generator` primitive that wraps compile → validate → marketplace-publish so both CLI and chat entry points get the same quality gate.
- `validator.py` — pure-Python structural lint (frontmatter, name kebab-case, file sizes, references resolve, **foreign-wikilink gate** preventing `[[concepts/]]` / `[[summaries/]]` / `[[sources/]]` from leaking into the shipped artifact).
- `evaluator.py` — two-pass quality measurement: a trigger grader (description-only) and a coverage grader (body + references) run concurrently via `asyncio.gather` bounded by a semaphore. Surfaces ambiguous outputs and per-task failures separately so a single bad call doesn't discard the rest.
- `workspace.py` — `save_iteration` / `restore_iteration` with reversible-rollback safety: the current state is preserved as a new iteration before any overwrite.
- `marketplace.py` — regenerates the per-KB `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`.
- `tools.py` — path-scoped IO primitives.

Shared helpers (`skill_dir`, `skills_root`, `skill_workspace_dir`, `extract_frontmatter`, `extract_body`, `extract_description`) live in `openkb/skill/__init__.py` as single sources of truth.

## Quality story

Three orthogonal gates catch different failure modes:

| Gate | Signal | When it runs |
|---|---|---|
| `validate_skill` | Structure: missing frontmatter, illegal description chars, foreign wikilinks in shipped output, oversized files | Auto, after every compile (inside `Generator.run`); also on demand via `openkb skill validate` |
| `run_eval` | **Trigger accuracy** (description-only grader fires on the right questions?) + **Body coverage** (body+references actually support what the description promises?) | On demand via `openkb skill eval` |
| `save_iteration` / `restore_iteration` | Iteration history: every overwrite preserves the prior version; rollback also saves the pre-rollback state first | Auto on `skill new -y`; on demand via `skill history` / `skill rollback` |

## Performance

- Skill compile uses `parallel_tool_calls=True` so the early read-fan-out phase batches independent reads in a single turn (~5-10 outer turns saved per compile, ~20-40s wall-clock).
- `run_eval` dispatches ~30 grader calls concurrently via `asyncio.gather` with `Semaphore(EVAL_CONCURRENCY=8)`. Empirical run on a 30-page PDF: skill compile **48s** end-to-end, eval **22s** for 20 prompts.
- Per-task failures captured with `return_exceptions=True` so one MaxTurnsExceeded doesn't discard the other 29 successful gradings.

## Test plan

- [x] `uv run pytest` — full suite green (500+ tests)
- [x] CLI: command name validation, KB detection, wiki-content gate, overwrite + iteration-save logic, marketplace.json regen, validate/eval/history/rollback flows
- [x] Chat `/skill new`: covered by dedicated tests; `write_kb_file` allow-list covered by 9 path-traversal tests
- [x] Validator: foreign-wikilink detection in body and references, frontmatter parse edge cases, file-size limits, kebab-case enforcement
- [x] Evaluator: trigger accuracy, body coverage, ambiguous grader output segregation, partial-failure isolation
- [x] Workspace: rollback preserves current state before overwrite (reversibility regression test)
- [x] **Manual acceptance**: ran `openkb skill new agent-design "Decide between workflows vs agents..."` against the Anthropic *Building Effective Agents* PDF. Result: trigger accuracy 19/20 (95%), body coverage 10/10 (100%), compile 48s, eval 22s. SKILL.md installed into Claude Code's `~/.claude/skills/` and verified to activate on composition-pattern questions.

## Known / deferred

- **Anthropic prompt caching** on the coverage grader: the openai-agents SDK takes `instructions` as a plain string with no hook for `cache_control` markers, so explicit Anthropic caching would require SDK-level work. OpenAI's automatic prefix caching already applies because the system prompt is byte-stable across the 10 coverage calls per eval.
- **Granularity**: one wiki source → one wide skill (e.g. `agent-design`) rather than fan-out to N narrow skills per source. Chosen deliberately — broad worldview skills are a valid Anthropic-Skills pattern when the description is tight and exclusionary. The validator's foreign-wikilink gate and the eval's body-coverage metric together protect against the failure modes that broad skills are prone to.

author: tamermomtaz
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes a critical data integrity issue where stair elements (objectives, key results, etc.) were being created without a `strategy_id`, causing them to leak across strategies in AI context and break tree counting. The fix includes:

1. **Backend**: Auto-migration to repair existing orphans + code changes to ensure `strategy_id` is always persisted
2. **Frontend**: Updated wizard and editor to pass `strategy_id` on creation, and AI endpoints to include it in requests
3. **Tests**: Added regression tests to prevent future orphan creation

## Key Changes

### Backend (`app/main.py`)
- Added `ensure_no_orphan_stairs()` auto-migration that runs on startup:
  - Inherits `strategy_id` from parent elements (handles multi-level wizard trees)
  - Falls back to org's single strategy if unambiguous
  - Soft-deletes unresolvable orphans to prevent AI context leakage
  - Idempotent: re-runs are no-ops after first clean pass
- Integrated migration into lifespan with error handling

### Backend (`app/routers/stairs.py`)
- Modified `create_stair()` to always persist `strategy_id`:
  - Accepts explicit `strategy_id` from request
  - Inherits from parent if not supplied (prevents wizard-created children from becoming orphans)
  - Added `strategy_id` column to INSERT statement with proper parameter binding

### Backend (`app/routers/ai.py`)
- Updated `ai_generate_strategy()` to persist `strategy_id` when creating AI-generated elements
- Added `strategy_id` parameter to INSERT statement

### Frontend (`src/StairsApp.jsx`)
- Modified strategy wizard to pass `strategy_id` in POST request (not just PUT afterward)
- Added safety check: only PUT if server didn't already persist it
- Updated manual element creation to include `strategy_id` in POST

### Frontend (`src/components/ExecutionRoom.jsx`, `StaircaseView.jsx`)
- Updated AI chat requests to include `strategy_id` from context
- Ensures AI advisor operates within correct strategy scope

### Tests (`backend/tests/test_source_isolation.py`)
- Added `TestCreateStairPersistsStrategyId` class with two regression tests:
  - Verifies explicit `strategy_id` is persisted in INSERT
  - Verifies child elements inherit parent's `strategy_id` when none supplied

### Models (`app/models/schemas.py`)
- Added optional `strategy_id` field to `AIGenerateRequest`

## Implementation Details

- **Idempotency**: The migration checks for orphans before running; after a clean pass, subsequent startups skip it entirely
- **Safety**: Soft-delete (sets `deleted_at`) rather than hard-delete, allowing recovery if needed
- **Backward compatibility**: Frontend PUT fallback handles older backends that might ignore POST `strategy_id`
- **Multi-level trees**: Migration loops up to 25 times to resolve deeply nested wizard-created elements
- **Single-strategy orgs**: Automatically assigns orphans to the only available strategy

author: ashukamar990
body:
💡 **What:** Implemented the `getRatingMap` utility to pre-calculate product ratings in $O(R)$ time and refactored core rendering and sorting logic to use this map for $O(1)$ lookups.

🎯 **Why:** The previous implementation performed $O(R)$ filtering for every product being processed. This resulted in $O(P \times R)$ complexity during rendering and $O(P \log P \times R)$ during sorting, which caused significant main-thread blocking and UI stutter as the number of products and reviews grew.

📊 **Impact:** Rendering and sorting are now significantly more efficient. 
- **Legacy Approach:** ~146ms - 292ms (for 100 products / 5000 reviews)
- **Optimized Approach:** ~2.0ms - 2.3ms
- **Improvement:** ~70x - 140x faster rendering performance.

🔬 **Measurement:** Verified using a local Node.js benchmark script comparing the legacy filtering logic against the new map-based approach. Sorting accuracy and rating values were cross-checked to ensure no regressions.

author: vampik33
body:
## Summary

Phase 0 P0.2 — defense-in-depth audit layer on top of P0.1's writer-side redactor + denylist.

`greentic-bundle doctor` now runs a leak scan as part of every workspace and artifact check. Findings surface as `secret-leak: <kind>` `DoctorCheck` entries; the CLI exits non-zero when `report.ok == false` so CI can rely on it as a gate.

## Patterns scanned (default-on)

1. **Dev-store filenames** — `.greentic/dev/`, `.greentic/state/dev/`, any `.dev.secrets.env`. Reuses `bundle_fs::dev_secret_match` so the writer denylist and reader audit stay aligned.
2. **`state/setup/*.json` with non-empty `secret_values`** — straightforward leak detection.
3. **`state/setup/*.json` `normalized_answers` parallel leak** — cross-checks `form.questions[*].secret == true` ids against `normalized_answers` keys. Codex caught this shape during P0.1 review.
4. **Raw archive bytes contain a dev-store filename substring** — catches anything that bypassed per-file enumeration (squashfs/zip metadata, symlink-target strings).

Pattern 5 (env-shape heuristic over `state/config/**`) is deferred to P0.3 / Phase C — the non-secret config channel needs to exist first, otherwise legitimate non-secret answers false-positive.

## Surface changes

- **CLI exit code flip** — `doctor` now returns non-zero when any check fails. JSON report still printed to stdout for inspection. This is the only behavior-shifting change to existing callers; the JSON schema is unchanged (new checks slot in as additional `DoctorCheck` entries).
- **`bundle_fs::dev_secret_match`** bumped to `pub(crate)` so the scanner reuses the same matcher as the writer denylist (single source of truth for what counts as a dev-store path).

## CI gate

- **In-Rust scanner** runs via `cargo test` (gates the main CI job through `pr-ci.yml`). The new unit + integration + CLI tests fail CI if any pattern regresses.
- **`ci/local_check.sh`** adds a shell-level `grep` over any `.gtbundle` in the working tree as repo-hygiene defense in depth against accidentally-committed leaky fixtures.

## Test coverage

| Layer | Count | Coverage |
|-------|-------|----------|
| Unit (`doctor_secrets::tests`) | 14 | each pattern + false-positive guards (malformed JSON, non-setup-state files, clean trees, short-haystack edge case) |
| Integration (`tests/build_artifact.rs`) | 2 | clean-bundle emits passing `secret-leak scan` check; bypass-redactor path (overwrite redacted state, rebundle via `bundle_fs::write_bundle`) is caught by `doctor_target` with both `secret_values populated` and `normalized_answers leak` findings |
| CLI (`tests/workspace_cli.rs`) | 2 | CLI exits non-zero on leak with finding in JSON; clean bundle surfaces passing `secret-leak scan` check |

Full suite: **145 tests passing** (was 127 — +18 new).

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passes
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` passes
- `GREENTIC_BUNDLE_USE_BUNDLED_CATALOG=1 cargo test --all-features` passes (101 unit + 25 build_artifact + 19 workspace_cli + others, all green)
- `python3 ci/i18n_check.py validate` passes (no new i18n strings — CLI surface unchanged)
- Shell-level grep gate passes (no committed `.gtbundle` artifacts in the tree)

## Plan refs

See `plans/next-gen-deployment.md` Phase 0 P0.2.

Related:
- P0.1 (landed 2026-05-18, #112): writer-side redactor + denylist this PR audits.
- P0.4 (next): extraction-path hardening — same TOCTOU shape as P0.1, different layer.
- Phase B B12a: runtime plaintext-reader migration — pattern 5 enablement waits on this.

## Test plan

- [x] All existing tests still pass
- [x] New unit + integration + CLI tests pass
- [x] Clippy clean with `-D warnings`
- [x] i18n validate clean
- [x] Manual smoke: `cargo run -- doctor --artifact <leaky.gtbundle>` exits 1 with JSON on stdout
- [x] Manual smoke: `cargo run -- doctor --artifact <clean.gtbundle>` exits 0

### Motivation
- Replace the old auto-download/build behavior for the 2decomp-fft dependency and require a real external installation to simplify configuration and avoid hidden build steps.
- Implement Stage‑7 and Stage‑8 IBM functionality (scalar/velocity interpolation, force spreading, boundary safety, grid adapter, RHS candidate, feedback, one-way/two-way forcing, Lagrangian state) and provide deterministic check targets to validate correctness.
- Provide runner scripts and Python assertions so CI or local smoke tests can reproducibly build and validate the new modules.

### Description
- Modified `cmake/FindDECOMP2D.cmake` to prefer an external install and use `DECOMP2D_ROOT` or `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH`, and to error out if not found instead of attempting an automatic download/build.
- Extended `src/CMakeLists.txt` to add and install numerous new check executables and to link them with the `decomp2d` target.
- Reworked and split several Fortran sources: updated `fibre_stage5_closed_loop_diagnostics_audit.f90` and `fibre_stage7_feedback_sign_audit.f90` to use dedicated IBM modules rather than ad‑hoc internal routines; added many new modules and check programs under `src/` implementing Stage‑7 and Stage‑8 functionality (e.g. `fibre_stage7_scalar_interpolation`, `fibre_stage7_velocity_interpolation`, `fibre_stage7_force_spreading`, `fibre_stage7_boundary_safety`, `fibre_stage7_channel_grid_adapter`, `fibre_stage7_power_consistency_check`, `fibre_stage8_config`, `fibre_stage8_lagrangian_state`, `fibre_stage8_runtime_grid_bridge`, `fibre_stage8_velocity_to_fibre`, `fibre_stage8_feedback_candidate`, `fibre_stage8_oneway_forcing`, `fibre_stage8_twoway_force_density`, and many check programs).
- Added/updated test harnesses and automation: numerous `stage*_checks/run_*.sh` build-and-run scripts were standardized to require `DECOMP2D_ROOT` and pass `-DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH`, and many Python assertion scripts were added/updated under `stage*_checks/` to verify the produced `.dat` outputs.
- Minor cleanup and safety checks in runner scripts: explicit detection of built executables, error messages when required artifacts are missing, and checks that output files are created.

### Testing
- New automated check targets were added for Stage‑5, Stage‑6, Stage‑7 and Stage‑8 (examples: `fibre_stage7_scalar_interpolation_check`, `fibre_stage7_force_spreading_check`, `fibre_stage7_power_consistency_check`, `fibre_stage7_boundary_safety_check`, `fibre_stage7_channel_grid_adapter_check`, `fibre_stage7_rhs_candidate_check`, `fibre_stage8_config_check`, `fibre_stage8_runtime_grid_bridge_check`, `fibre_stage8_lagrangian_state_check`, `fibre_stage8_velocity_to_fibre_check`, `fibre_stage8_feedback_candidate_check`, `fibre_stage8_oneway_forcing_check`, `fibre_stage8_twoway_force_density_check`) and corresponding runner scripts under `stage*_checks/` were added or updated to pass `-DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH`.
- Assertion scripts were added or updated to validate numeric tolerances and boolean flags written to `stage*_outputs/*.dat` for the new check programs (Python scripts under `stage*_checks/`).
- No automated CI test run is included in this PR; the changes add the check targets and runner scripts so CI can build and execute them (they will fail early with a clear message if `DECOMP2D_ROOT` is not present).

author: sriramr98
body:
resolves #1937 
[docs](https://github.com/dbt-labs/docs.getdbt.com/issues/new/choose) dbt-labs/docs.getdbt.com/#


### Problem

[#1684](https://github.com/dbt-labs/dbt-adapters/pull/1684) added `validate_doc_columns` to warn on (and skip) columns documented in `schema.yml` that don't exist in the database. Post-merge review surfaced two issues:

  1. **Quoting is ignored.** The macro unconditionally lowercases both sides before comparing, so `MyCol` documented with `quote: true` silently matches a physical `mycol` (and vice versa) — producing wrong comments or missing warnings.
  2. **Redundant metadata call on Snowflake.** `default__persist_docs` pre-fetches columns via `get_columns_in_relation`, but `snowflake__alter_column_comment` already fetches them internally. Every Snowflake model with `persist_docs: { columns: true }` now pays for two `describe table` calls instead of one. The original empty-query bug never affected Snowflake.


<!---
  Describe the problem this PR is solving. What is the application state
  before this PR is merged?
-->

### Solution


  1. `validate_doc_columns` now reads `column_dict[col_name]['quote']` and uses **case-sensitive** comparison when truthy; otherwise it falls back to the existing case-insensitive comparison.
  2. Added a `snowflake__persist_docs` override that skips the pre-fetch and delegates to `snowflake__alter_column_comment`. The `validate_doc_columns` call is moved **inside** `snowflake__alter_column_comment`, reusing the column list it already retrieves. Net: one `describe table` call, missing-column warning preserved.
  3. Other adapters (Postgres, Redshift, BigQuery, Spark, Athena) continue to use `default__persist_docs` / their existing `__persist_docs` overrides and pick up the quote-aware comparison automatically — the warning continues to fire on every adapter.

New shared tests in `dbt-tests-adapter` cover both fixes and are wired into every adapter's functional suite:
  - `BasePersistDocsQuotedColumnCaseSensitive` — quoted column with case mismatch must warn.
  - `BasePersistDocsAllColumnsMissing` — every documented column invalid must not crash and must warn for all.

  can to help reviewers understand your changes. Include any alternatives and
  tradeoffs you considered.

body:
💡 **What**: Removed `always_run = timestamp()` trigger from `null_resource.download_bank_of_anthos` in both `Bank_GKE` and `MC_Bank_GKE` modules, replacing it with `always_run = "true"`. Added a bash-level file existence idempotency check in the `local-exec` provisioner.
🎯 **Why**: The dynamic `timestamp()` trigger forced Terraform to destroy and replace the download resource on *every single* `terraform apply`. Because downstream resources depend on this download ID, this cascaded into a full wipe and redeployment of the entire Bank of Anthos application on every apply, creating a massive, recurring performance bottleneck.
📊 **Impact**: Reduces subsequent `terraform apply` time from several minutes (due to downloading and re-deploying the full app) down to mere seconds when no application version changes exist.
🔬 **Measurement**: Verified using `tofu plan` which now correctly shows 0 replacements and 0 changes to existing `null_resource` execution graphs unless the `version` variable changes.
⚠️ **Scope**: Affects the GKE foundation/app deployments for Bank of Anthos (single and multi-cluster).

author: hanfour
body:
## Summary

實作 multi-source ingest spec（#146 / `380d7d9`）的 Phase 1 第一步：**只動 DB schema + migration**，不碰 tRPC router / ingest route / web UI / evaluator cutover / GDPR cascade extension / partition roll-forward cron — 那些 Phase 1 後續 step 處理。

5 個新 table、2 個 ALTER、1 個 hand-edited migration（drizzle 沒法直接表達 PARTITION BY，所以 `client_events` 的 CREATE TABLE 部分手寫，其他靠 drizzle-kit generate）+ 9 個 integration tests。

## Schema additions

- `devices` — 物理裝置 enrollment（hostname / os / agent_version / status / revoked_at）。partial index `(user_id) WHERE revoked_at IS NULL` + 同 pattern 的 `(org_id)`，匹配 `api_keys` 既有慣例。
- `device_enrollment_tokens` — 1hr TTL 的一次性 bootstrap token，`UNIQUE token_hash`。
- `device_api_keys` — long-lived `cda_*` key，PK on `device_id` 把 1:1 寫進結構。
- `client_sessions` — per-session static metadata，`text PK`（client-supplied UUID）+ self-FK on `parent_session_id` for claude subagents。spec 解釋過為何不用 `(org_id, id)` composite PK（FK chain 複雜度太高）— tenant guard 在 ingest route 做。
- `client_events` — RANGE-partitioned by `ingested_at` MONTHLY。PK 是 `(id, ingested_at)`、dedup UNIQUE 是 `(session_id, event_id, source, ingested_at)`，因為 postgres 要求 partition key 必須出現在每個 uniqueness constraint。In-partition retry dedup 抓住常見情境（~60s daemon flush cadence）；cross-partition dedup 在 evaluator 層處理。

## Existing-table deltas

- `request_bodies`: `ADD device_id` (nullable FK) + `ADD source NOT NULL DEFAULT 'gateway'`。**`client_session_id` 沒在 ALTER 列表內** — 它早在 gateway body-capture 時就 add 過了（`packages/db/src/schema/requestBodies.ts:16`），spec O3 也確定 v1 永遠不 populate（沒有官方 CLI 送 `X-Session-Id`），保留為 Phase 5+ wrapper-script stub。
- `usage_logs`: `ADD device_id` (nullable FK)。Gateway 在解 `ak_*` token 拿到 device binding 時 populate。

## Migration mechanics

`0013_multi_source_ingest_phase1.sql` 是 drizzle-kit 產的 + 手動 patch：把 `client_events` 的 CREATE TABLE 結尾加上 `PARTITION BY RANGE (ingested_at)`，並補 4 個初始 partition（2026-05 / 06 / 07 / 08）。drizzle schema 檔留下 `// Physical table is RANGE-partitioned ...` 註解提醒未來 regenerate 不要打架。`0013_down.sql` 按依賴反序 drop 整套，partition 先個別 drop（讓 operator 想 DETACH 保留資料的話有空間）。

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm --filter @caliber/api test:integration tests/integration/migrations/0013.test.ts` — **9/9 pass** (13.49s on postgres:16-alpine testcontainer)
- [x] `pnpm --filter @caliber/db --filter @caliber/api --filter @caliber/gateway --filter @caliber/gateway-core build` — 4/4 build clean
- [x] `pnpm --filter @caliber/web typecheck` — clean
- [ ] CI: lint-type-test / integration / gateway-integration / evaluator-integration / coverage / e2e

Test 涵蓋：所有 5 個 table 存在、`client_events` 真的是 partitioned（`pg_partitioned_table.partstrat = 'r'`）、4 個 initial partition、每個 partition 繼承 PK + UNIQUE、INSERT 真的按 `ingested_at` 路由到對的 partition、parent SELECT 透明看到所有 partition、dedup UNIQUE 抓 in-partition retry、`DROP TABLE partition_2026_05` 乾淨移除一個月資料、ALTER 兩欄都有正確 nullability + default。

## Out of scope (Phase 1 後續 step)

- tRPC routers (`devices.list / create / revoke / enrollmentToken.issue`)
- fastify `POST /v1/ingest` + `cda_*` auth middleware + session tenant-guard upsert
- evaluator pipeline cutover to `evaluator_events` view
- `gdprDelete` worker extension to cascade `client_sessions` + `client_events`
- monthly partition roll-forward cron
- web `/dashboard/devices` UI

Java uses angular brackets (< and >) to provide a specific type (the "type argument") to a generic type. For instance, List is a generic type, so a list containing strings can be declared with List<String>.

author: kangzj
body:
Fixes https://linear.app/a8c/issue/SEARCH-199

## Why

When comparing the free and paid Jetpack Search plans, customers couldn't see that autocomplete — search query suggestions as they type — is part of the search experience. Autocomplete shipped recently (#48473) but was missing from the comparison grid, understating the value of both the free and paid offerings. This adds it so customers can make a more informed choice.

## Proposed changes

* Add an **Autocomplete** row to the pricing comparison grid (`NewPricingComponent`), placed after **Spelling correction**, with a tooltip describing the search-suggestions experience.
* The row is marked as included (✓) in the paid **and** free columns — a matching `<PricingTableItem>` was added to each column, keeping the `newPricingArgs.items` ↔ `PricingTableItem` mapping 1:1 (no off-by-one with the existing gated Search-blocks rows).

## Screenshots

Captured at `/wp-admin/admin.php?page=jetpack-search&new_pricing_202208=1` via local docker at 1440 wide.

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| ![before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/09bf7f52-3bae-4fd9-9f96-27a4f722ecf8) | ![after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/69473760-3057-4357-81ec-98e3cbb35a93) |

## Related product discussion/links

* https://linear.app/a8c/issue/SEARCH-199
* Follows the same pattern as #48891 (Search blocks / Embedded search page rows)

## Does this pull request change what data or activity we track or use?

No.

## Testing instructions

* Spin up a WP env with the Jetpack Search plugin active.
* Go to **Jetpack → Search**. To force the new pricing grid on a local/disconnected env, append `&new_pricing_202208=1` to the upsell page URL (`admin.php?page=jetpack-search&new_pricing_202208=1`).
* Scroll to the feature comparison grid and confirm:
  * An **Autocomplete** row renders, with a clear tooltip on its info icon.
  * It is shown as included (✓) in **both** the paid and free columns.
  * It sits directly after **Spelling correction**, and every existing feature row still aligns with the correct paid/free included state (no off-by-one in the grid).

author: weegy
body:
## Summary

Replaces Dependabot PR #83 (which CI-failed on the peer-dep cascade: `next-intl@3.26.5` declared `peer next@^10..^15`, so `next@16` install errored before tests could run) with a coordinated repo-wide bump.

| Pkg | From | To |
|---|---|---|
| `next` | ^15.5.16 | ^16.2.6 |
| `next-intl` | ^3.26.5 | ^4.0.0 (resolves the v15-pinned peer) |
| `eslint-config-next` | ^15.5.16 | ^16.2.6 |

## Migration changes

### 1. `eslint.config.mjs` rewritten for native flat-config

`eslint-config-next@16` ships flat-config arrays via `next/core-web-vitals` and `next/typescript` sub-path exports. The v15-era `FlatCompat`-wrapper bridge is no longer needed and in fact crashes at load time with "Converting circular structure to JSON" (legacy schema validator chokes on the new plugin refs). Switched to direct ES import + spread.

### 2. `tsconfig.json` auto-updated by `next dev` on first boot

- `jsx: "preserve" → "react-jsx"` (Next 16 uses automatic runtime)
- added `.next/dev/types/**/*.ts` to `include`

Reformat is cosmetic — committed as-is.

### 3. `react-hooks` v6 strict rules downgraded to `warn`

`eslint-plugin-react-hooks@v6` (bundled with `eslint-config-next@16`) added four React-19-era strict rules that flag **30+ pre-existing call sites**:

| Rule | Count | What it flags |
|---|---|---|
| `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` | 26 | cascading-render hint |
| `react-hooks/refs` | 4 | `.current` access during render |
| `react-hooks/immutability` | 2 | `ref.current = …` assignment |
| `react-hooks/error-boundaries` | 1 | JSX inside `try/catch` |

These are legitimate code-quality observations but **unrelated to the v15→v16 dep upgrade**. Set to `warn` so this PR stays a pure-dep migration; refactor tracked as follow-up.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm run typecheck` (web-ui) | 0 errors |
| `npm run lint` (web-ui) | 0 errors, 53 warnings (downgraded strict rules above) |
| `npm test` (web-ui vitest) | 18/18 files, 125/125 tests pass |
| `npm run dev` boot | "Ready in 284ms" with Turbopack (default in v16) |
| `/store/builder/<draft-id>` render | 4 panels visible (508/493/493/46px), Separators present, persisted layout intact (rrp v4 + Next 16 stack OK) |
| Browser console errors | 0 (apart from pre-existing hydration mismatch, see below) |

## Known follow-ups (separate tickets)

- **`middleware.ts` deprecated in Next 16** in favour of `proxy.ts`. Our middleware uses edge runtime which `proxy` does not yet support, so keeping `middleware.ts` (still works in v16, only deprecated) until next-intl publishes proxy/edge guidance. Will throw a soft warning in `next dev`.
- **Pre-existing hydration mismatch** in `app/page.tsx:494` (`scope={activeId}` differs SSR vs client because `useChatSessions` mints a UUID on mount). React 19 strict mode in Next 16 surfaces this as a louder console error; behavior unchanged from main.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI green
- [ ] Verify `npm run dev` boots locally and renders home page
- [ ] Verify `/store/builder/<id>` workspace still renders all 4 panels + persists layout (covers next 16 × rrp v4 interaction)

Closes #83.

author: melvincarvalho
body:
Live-fire smoke of #497 surfaced two real gotchas with the new \`write_acl\` tool. Fixing both.

## The bugs

### 1. write_acl could lock you out

Relative WebID paths in \`agents\` (e.g. \`../profile/card.jsonld#me\`) resolve against the \`.acl\` URL, not the pod root. Writing an ACL with a wrong-relative agent silently produced an ACL that didn't actually grant the caller Control — and on the next read_acl, they'd be locked out. AuthenticatedAgent Write was the only escape hatch.

### 2. No clear docs on URL resolution

The \`agents\` field accepting URIs (and the URL resolution rules) was implicit. Users had to know WAC well enough to predict resolution behavior.

## The fixes

- **Safety check**: after building the proposed ACL doc, parse it with its real URL so relative agents resolve correctly, then verify the caller's WebID still has Control. If not, refuse with an explanatory error pointing at the most common cause (relative WebIDs).
- **Footguns docs section**: concrete right/wrong examples for relative vs absolute WebIDs in \`agents\`, plus notes on the safety check and SSE keep-alive considerations.

## Legitimate ownership transfer

Still possible — just two steps:

1. \`write_acl\` granting Control to the new owner in addition to yourself
2. New owner calls \`write_acl\` removing you

## Test plan
- [x] 27/27 MCP tests pass (added test that triggers the safety)
- [x] Live-fire: tried to lock self out → safety fires with clear error

author: devemberx
body:
## Summary

Polarion's REST API silently stores unknown enum ids (`type` / `status` / `severity` / `resolution` / project-defined custom enums) verbatim on every write path — they look real on later reads but never match Lucene queries. Reproduced on `MCP_Test_Project` for both standard and custom fields, including brand-new `custom_fields` keys on a work item type that defines no customs. Only `priority` partial-validates (non-numeric strings coerce to project default; numeric ghosts still persist verbatim).

This PR documents the behavior instead of enforcing it client-side. A wrapper-thin server keeps multi-client usage (Cursor / Copilot / scripts) flexible, and the existing `list_*_enum_options` tools already give the LLM the exact lookup it needs. Docstring fidelity is now the only guard, so each write tool docstring explicitly directs the LLM to call the matching `list_*_enum_options` before writing any enum-shaped field.

## Type of Change

- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)
- [ ] Refactor (no functional changes, code quality improvement)
- [x] Documentation update
- [ ] CI / tooling / dependency update

## Changes

- `create_work_item` / `update_work_item` / `update_document` docstrings: precise ghost-write paragraph (verbatim by default; `priority` only coerces non-numeric inputs), and explicit `list_work_item_enum_options` / `list_document_enum_options` redirect with full argument hint
- `list_document_enum_options` / `list_work_item_enum_options` docstrings: align tone with write tools (`does NOT validate ... stored verbatim as ghost values`), add `priority` partial-validation note on the work-item side
- `CLAUDE.md` enum paragraph rewritten: `lenient` → `essentially absent`; clarifies that `priority` is the only partial coercion case, brand-new custom-field keys also persist as ghosts, and docstring fidelity is the only guard going forward

## Testing

- [ ] Unit tests added / updated (`tests/`)
- [ ] `dry_run=True` path verified for all write tools
- [x] `uv run pytest` passes locally
- [x] `uv run mypy src/` passes with no errors
- [x] `uv run ruff check src tests` passes with no warnings

```bash
uv run ruff check . && uv run ruff format --check . && uv run mypy src/
uv run pytest -q
```

All 501 tests pass; lint, format-check, and mypy clean.

## Golden Rule Compliance

- [x] No `print()` calls — all logging goes to `stderr` via `logging`
- [x] `from __future__ import annotations` present in every modified module
- [x] All tool inputs/outputs are Pydantic models (no raw `dict`)
- [x] All new tool functions are `async def`
- [x] Tool docstrings follow Google style with Args / Returns / Raises
- [ ] Synthesis read paths (`read_document`, `read_document_parts`) convert HTML → Markdown via `html_to_markdown()`
- [ ] Greenfield write paths (`create_work_item(description=...)`) convert Markdown → HTML via `markdown_to_html()` + `sanitize_html()`
- [ ] Round-trip pairs (`get_*(include_*_html=True)` ↔ `update_*(*_html=...)`) pass raw Polarion HTML verbatim — no Markdown conversion, no sanitization
- [ ] Any new list tool supports `page_size` and `page_number` pagination
- [x] No secrets hardcoded — env vars via `pydantic-settings` only

## Notes for Reviewers

- No code-path changes; `_build_*_payload` and `merge_custom_fields` untouched. Reviewer focus: docstring wording accuracy + CLAUDE.md correctness.
- Reproduction artifacts left on `MCP_Test_Project` (`MCPT-558` through `MCPT-561`) — please recycle manually; no `delete_work_item` tool exists.
- Considered and dropped: client-side enum guard with `getAvailableOptions` caching + `validate_enums=True` opt-out flag. Rejected because it would make `list_*_enum_options` redundant for write paths, risk false positives on fields like `asil` (returns "No enum options" but accepts values), and add API calls under the 3 req/s budget. May revisit as an opt-in flag if a concrete use case emerges.

author: martinciu
body:
## 🐛 Bug

Reproduced today on ccpulse worktree \`237-test-color\`:
\`/mc:brainstorm-issue 237\` wrote spec, plan, and review-note
correctly, but **never created the feature bead**. The user saw a
stale bead from a different feature and assumed brainstorm had
produced an empty-description record. It hadn't produced anything.

## 🔬 Root cause

In any worktree where bd uses **shared mode** (the default — bd
walks up from CWD to find \`.beads/\` in the main repo), Step 5.5's
bootstrap check is wrong:

\`\`\`sh
[ ! -d .beads ]              # true (worktree has no local .beads/)
bd init --stealth --quiet …  # → "workspace already initialized", exit 1
                             #   (bd walked up to main's .beads/)
\`\`\`

The model interpreted the init failure via the "log warning and
continue" guard as "bd op failed → beads is best-effort → skip the
rest of this step" — cascading skip that swallowed the
\`bd create --type feature\` call. Spec/plan/note landed on disk;
bd state was silently lost.

## 🔧 Fix

Two changes in \`.claude/commands/mc/brainstorm-issue.md\`:

- 🪜 **Step 5.5 step 1**: replace \`[ ! -d .beads ]\` with
  \`bd status\` (walks up). If bd is already reachable anywhere up
  the tree, skip init. The init branch fires only on the very first
  \`/mc:brainstorm-issue\` per project; subsequent runs across
  worktrees skip straight to step 2.
- 🛡️ **Failure-handling note**: rewritten to spell out that
  sub-steps are independent — a step 1 failure must not skip step
  2 (the one that creates the bead). Explicit "do not cascade"
  guard.

## ✅ Test plan

- [ ] In a worktree where bd resolves to a parent's \`.beads/\` via
  walk-up (the shared-mode topology), run \`/mc:brainstorm-issue <N>\`
  and confirm a feature bead lands in bd with \`branch:<name>\` label
  and the five pinned comments.
- [ ] In a fresh repo where no \`.beads/\` exists anywhere up the
  tree, run the same command and confirm bd gets initialized in
  CWD on first run, then feature bead created.
- [ ] In a repo without \`bd\` on PATH, the command still writes
  spec/plan/note and skips Step 5.5 cleanly.

## 🔗 Follow-up

Feature bead for ccpulse#237 will be created manually after this
fix lands, so \`/mc:execute\` can resolve the plan in the next
phase.

## Summary
Adds a Sentry integration verification page and updates routing configuration to support Sentry monitoring. This allows developers to test client-side and server-side error capture without writing custom code.

## Changes
- **New verification page** (`/sentry-example-page`): A client-side page with two buttons to trigger test errors:
  - Client-side error button that throws an error directly in the browser
  - Server-side error button that calls a companion API endpoint and captures the response error
  - Includes status feedback (sending/sent states) and user-friendly instructions in French
  
- **New API endpoint** (`/sentry-example-page/api`): A simple GET route that throws a server-side error for testing `onRequestError` instrumentation

- **Updated routing configuration** (`proxy.ts`): Added two public paths:
  - `/sentry-example-page` — the verification page itself
  - `/monitoring/tunnel` — Sentry tunnel route for CSP-friendly error proxying

## Implementation Details
- The verification page is intentionally not linked from the UI (protected by obscurity) and can be safely deleted after Sentry validation
- Server-side errors are captured via Sentry's `onRequestError` handler in instrumentation
- The page includes helpful documentation comments explaining its purpose and usage

author: tend-agent
body:
## Summary

The `nightly`, `running-in-ci`, and `review-runs` skills tell the bot to do work in a worktree under `$TMPDIR`. GitHub Actions runners leave `$TMPDIR` unset, so the recipe expands `"$TMPDIR/tend-update-workflows"` to `"/tend-update-workflows"`, which `git worktree add` rejects with `fatal: could not create leading directories of '/tend-update-workflows/.git': Permission denied`. Hard-code `/tmp` instead, with a one-line explanation in each skill so a future maintainer doesn't reintroduce `$TMPDIR`.

## Why

`cargo-affected-bot` hit this twice on consecutive nights running the bundled `nightly` skill:

- [run 26020369573](https://github.com/max-sixty/cargo-affected/actions/runs/26020369573) (2026-05-18) — `git worktree add "$TMPDIR/tend-update-workflows"` failed; the subsequent `cd` failed; `uvx tend@latest init` ran in the main checkout and wrote workflow changes that the bot then had to `git checkout -- .github/workflows` to revert.
- [run 25984436621](https://github.com/max-sixty/cargo-affected/actions/runs/25984436621) (2026-05-17) — same shape, recovered by `export TMPDIR=/tmp` and rerunning the recipe.

Both runs eventually produced the correct PR, but each one burned bash cycles and tokens on the recovery dance, and the first one polluted the main checkout in passing. The fallback "succeeded" only because nothing was committed before the revert — a slightly different recipe ordering would have shipped a broken workflows update.

The same `$TMPDIR` pattern in `running-in-ci` and `review-runs` is unexercised so far this month but would fail identically the first time a bot tries to update a `.claude/skills/` file under those recipes.

`$TMPDIR` was introduced as "the tempdir env var" in [#216](https://github.com/max-sixty/tend/pull/216), [#219](https://github.com/max-sixty/tend/pull/219), and [#328](https://github.com/max-sixty/tend/pull/328), apparently from local shells where it was set. GHA's `ubuntu-latest` does not set it.

Evidence gist: https://gist.github.com/da54a63f2b2042b0c3db2fd971a90a87

## What changes

- `plugins/tend-ci-runner/skills/nightly/SKILL.md` — workflow-regen recipe writes to `/tmp/tend-update-workflows`, `/tmp/tend-old-ver`, `/tmp/tend-update-body.md`. Updated prose links the worktree to `/tmp` and notes why `$TMPDIR` is not used.
- `plugins/tend-ci-runner/skills/running-in-ci/SKILL.md` — skill-PR recipe writes to `/tmp/skill-fix`. Same prose update.
- `plugins/tend-ci-runner/skills/review-runs/SKILL.md` — skill-edit recipe writes to `/tmp/review-runs-fix`. Same prose update.

Only the three skill recipes change. No script or workflow changes.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI on this PR passes (pre-commit, actionlint).
- [ ] Next nightly run on a consumer regenerates workflows from `/tmp/tend-update-workflows` without the `Permission denied` stumble or the `git checkout -- .github/workflows` recovery step.

Utiliza la API de Contexto de React (useData) para centralizar el estado global.
Carga un conjunto de datos inicial desde lapalma.json y persiste de forma automática cualquier cambio realizado desde el panel de control en el localStorage del navegador.

## Summary
One-line column-name fix in `coverage_tier_service.py`. The market_metrics SELECT used `ORDER BY as_of_date DESC` but the actual column is `trade_date` (see `data_pipeline/models.py:186`).

```
(psycopg2.errors.UndefinedColumn) column "as_of_date" does not exist
```

`ORDER BY as_of_date DESC` → `ORDER BY trade_date DESC`. Added a comment block referencing the canonical column source so the next agent doesn't reintroduce.

The broken path returned None silently, so cached payloads have `market_cap_cr=None` — those remain valid. Fresh computes will now populate the field correctly.

## What type of PR is this?

- [ ] API-change
- [x] BUG
- [x] Improvement

## Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

Ref https://github.com/matrixorigin/matrixone/issues/24348

## What this PR does / why we need it:

Ref https://github.com/matrixorigin/matrixone/issues/24348

The deterministic paired-range path in `getIndexForNonEquiCond` still returned before the existing non-PK range guard ran, so a large secondary-index paired range could bypass the `InFilterCardLimitNonPK` / selectivity cutoff that already protected single-range candidates. On large tables that can reopen the same expensive index-join choice the earlier guard was meant to avoid.

This change applies the same stats guard to paired-range candidates and adds a focused unit test for the large-range case. The planner behavior for small/selective paired ranges is unchanged.

To keep this follow-up low risk, it does not add new distributed BVT cases: the existing `expr_opt_test.go` coverage already checks that non-sort-key composite filters are preserved, and this PR only touches the local secondary-index candidate selection guard.

author: charlesbochet
body:
## Summary

Cross-version upgrade fails at the 2.1 `GateExportImportCommandMenuItemsByPermissionFlagCommand` stage:

```
[GateExportImportCommandMenuItemsByPermissionFlagCommand] Found 3 command menu item(s) to update for workspace ...
error: column WorkspaceEntity.isInternalMessagesImportEnabled does not exist
```

(see https://github.com/twentyhq/twenty-infra/actions/runs/25929264129/job/76219964380)

### Root cause

Same class of bug as #20581 and #20583, one layer deeper in the call graph.

1. The 2.1 workspace command emits a `commandMenuItem` migration (3 items differ from the current standard expressions).
2. After the migration commits, `WorkspaceMigrationRunnerService.invalidateCache` walks the related-for-validation metadata for `commandMenuItem`, which includes `objectMetadata`. That puts `flatObjectMetadataMaps` in the keys set.
3. `getLegacyCacheInvalidationPromises` sees `flatObjectMetadataMaps` in the keys and calls `WorkspaceMetadataVersionService.incrementMetadataVersion(workspaceId)`.
4. `incrementMetadataVersion` did a bare `findOne` on `WorkspaceEntity` with no `select` → TypeORM emits a SELECT for every column declared on the entity → hits `isInternalMessagesImportEnabled` (added by #20457), whose DB column is only created by the 2.5 fast instance command `1778525104406-add-is-internal-messages-import-enabled`, which has not run yet at the 2.1 stage. 💥

### Fix

The function only reads `workspace.metadataVersion`, so narrow the `select` to `['id', 'metadataVersion']`. No behavior change.

```diff
 async incrementMetadataVersion(workspaceId: string): Promise<void> {
   const workspace = await this.workspaceRepository.findOne({
+    select: ['id', 'metadataVersion'],
     where: { id: workspaceId },
     withDeleted: true,
   });
```

## Summary Adds a temporary, deterministic backend bridge that maps structured NRCS rundown JSON into ordered Google Sheet rows compatible with the existing vMix automation workflow. ## What’s included - **NRCS parser** (`parseNrcsRundown`) — normalizes loosely typed JSON input - **Template mapper** (`mapNrcsToSheetRows`) — generates rows in broadcast order: headlines → intro → main topics → one-sentence news → sport → weather → recommendation → outro - **Row format helpers** — `SheetRow` objects, full A–J matrix, CSV export (columns C/D/E/F/I/J) - **Google Sheets writer** (optional) — clears and writes rows via `googleapis` when env vars are set - **REST API** - `POST /api/nrcs/map-to-rows` — returns `{ rows, coreColumns, csv }` without calling Google - `POST /api/nrcs/export-to-sheet` — same output; add `?write=true` to push to Sheets when configured - **Fixture** — `backend/fixtures/nrcs-example.json` for manual testing ## Configuration See `backend/.env.example` for optional Google Sheets settings: - `GOOGLE_SHEETS_SPREADSHEET_ID` - `GOOGLE_SHEETS_SHEET_NAME` - `GOOGLE_SHEETS_DATA_START_ROW` (default `2`) - `GOOGLE_SHEETS_CREDENTIALS_JSON` or `GOOGLE_SHEETS_CREDENTIALS_PATH` ## Usage example ```bash curl -X POST http://localhost:3010/api/nrcs/map-to-rows \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "Cookie: " \ -d @backend/fixtures/nrcs-example.json ``` ## Notes - Mapping uses simple heuristics (no AI) as requested for a short-lived compatibility layer. - Main topics use `SYN TO ILU TEMA` / `Double Box`, quote rows use `ILU TO SYN`, and playout cues are derived from slug/speaker names unless overridden via `playoutCue`.
  
## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * NRCS endpoints now produce spreadsheet-ready rows, core columns and CSV previews. * Optional direct write to Google Sheets with a write flag; responses include write status when used. * Improved mapping/formatting of NRCS content into ordered sheet rows for broadcast automation. * Added example NRCS fixture for testing and demonstration. * **Chores** * Added Google API library and example environment configuration for Sheets credentials. author: tips-of-mine
body:
…invisible client

Audit complet du repo 2026-05-18 a identifié `GeometryPass.cpp:385` (frontFace=CW appliqué par PR25 3009263, 2026-05-06) comme cause probable du bug "avatar humanoïde invisible dans le client de jeu" noté 2026-05-05 (memory projet).

Conflit empirique vs théorique :
- PR25 (empirique) : passer `CCW -> CW` a rendu l'avatar visible en mode éditeur, et la PR affirmait "BONUS : corrige aussi le client".
- Audit (théorique) : analyse arithmétique de la view matrix (ee181da) + symétrie avec `ShadowMapPass.cpp:200` (CCW+BACK) et `TerrainRenderer.cpp:542` (CCW+BACK, fix PR #613) sur les mêmes meshes -> CW est probablement faux, l'avatar devrait être rendu avec CCW+BACK.

L'utilisateur confirme (2026-05-18) que l'avatar reste invisible dans le client de jeu malgré PR25 -> PR25 a fix l'éditeur mais pas le client.

Plutôt que de basculer aveuglément en CCW (risque de recasser l'éditeur), on pose un patch DIAGNOSTIC TEMPORAIRE : `cullMode = VK_CULL_MODE_NONE`.

Résultats possibles au test :
1. Avatar visible en client -> c'est bien le winding, on bascule CCW (cohérent avec ShadowMap + TerrainRenderer legacy + règle CLAUDE.md). Si CCW casse l'éditeur, c'est que client et éditeur consomment des meshes à conventions différentes -> plan dédié pour aligner.
2. Avatar toujours invisible avec NONE -> ce n'est PAS le winding, on enquête ailleurs (descriptor set, depth state, blend, texture transparente, position out of frustum).

À reverter (back en BACK_BIT + frontFace déterminé) avant merge final. Cette PR sert uniquement à produire un binaire client de diagnostic via CI.

Audit complet à venir en lots suivants : sécurité master (Mersenne session_id, absence de mutex, énumération comptes, CAPTCHA TLS sans validation cert), validation gameplay shardd vide, migrations 0023 dupliquée, sauvegardes éditeur non-atomiques, etc.

Déploiement : ✅ client uniquement, pas de redéploiement serveur.

author: famecodeteam
body:
## Summary
Two operational fixes to address the post-deploy state of brief pages.

**A) Graceful brief-link fallback on the status page.** Phase 4 hid the brief link card whenever no synced \`BriefRecord\` existed, which regressed any shoot whose Trello webhook hadn't fired since deploy: clients lost access to the brief entirely. New resolution order:
1. New \`/brief/<slug>?code=<hash>\` link if a synced \`BriefRecord\` is present (best UX, the doc-synced page).
2. Fall back to \`shoot.briefUrl\` (legacy Google Doc) if a Doc was detected but not yet synced.
3. Hide the card if neither exists.

Once a brief syncs, the card automatically upgrades to the new URL.

**B) \`/api/backfill-briefs\` endpoint.** POST, \`CRON_SECRET\`-protected. Iterates every shoot and, for those with a \`briefUrl\`, calls \`registerBrief()\` + \`syncOne()\`. Server-side mirror of the existing \`scripts/backfill-briefs.ts\` — necessary because my local Vercel CLI session can't decrypt the UPSTASH credentials, so \`scripts/backfill-briefs.ts\` writes to the local file store instead of production Upstash. The endpoint runs inside the production runtime where the env is fully resolved.

Idempotent: \`registerBrief\` no-ops when nothing changed, \`syncOne\` hashes the Doc and skips if unchanged. Safe to re-run.

## Verified locally
Seeded a shoot \`0214-tiktok-9bee2654\` with \`briefUrl\` set and no \`BriefRecord\`. Status page DOM shows:
\`\`\`
{ href: "https://docs.google.com/document/d/SOMEEXAMPLE/edit", label: "Brief", target: "_blank" }
\`\`\`
Once a \`BriefRecord\` with \`parsedJson\` lands for the same shoot, the loader's \`briefHref\` precedence kicks in and the href becomes \`/brief/0214-tiktok?code=9bee2654\`.

## Test plan
- [ ] \`pnpm typecheck\` clean (verified).
- [ ] \`pnpm build\` registers \`/api/backfill-briefs\` (verified).
- [ ] Deploy. Hit a status page whose brief hasn't synced yet — Brief link card shows pointing at the Google Doc.
- [ ] \`curl -X POST .../api/backfill-briefs -H 'Authorization: Bearer …'\` — returns \`{ ok: true, summary: { totalShoots, eligible, registered, syncs: [...] } }\`.
- [ ] After backfill, the same status page now points the Brief link at the new \`/brief/<slug>?code=<hash>\` URL.

author: edwinsteele
body:
## Summary

- **Chart labels invisible in dark mode** — the color-init script was executing *before* the `<style>` block was parsed, so `getComputedStyle` returned empty strings for the CSS vars and Chart.js fell back to black labels on the dark background. Fixed by moving `<style>` before the chart.js `<script>` imports.
- **Submit button now right-aligned** — wrapped Chart type / Time window / Group display controls in a single flex-column div; the submit button sits at the bottom with `margin-top:auto; justify-content:flex-end` so it always lands on the right regardless of screen width.
- **Reduced vertical scroll** — series selector column capped at `max-height:420px` with `overflow-y:auto`, so a large LGA or brand list scrolls internally rather than pushing the whole form taller.

## Test plan

- [ ] Open workbench in dark mode — verify line chart legend labels are readable (light text on dark bg)
- [ ] Check submit button appears at bottom-right of the controls panel on both wide and narrow viewports
- [ ] Expand "By LGA" section — confirm series list scrolls within its column rather than stretching the form
- [ ] Verify heatmap views and lead-lag page still render correctly (no regressions)

author: kekzl
body:
## What

End-to-end A/B on **Gemma-3-12B-it Q4_K_M** at pp2048 refutes the Phase 2C production deployment. IMMA path is **3.8× slower** than the default dequant→cuBLAS path. Decision: **DEFERRED**, all artifacts retained.

## Why

The Phase 2B chain (PRs #256→#267) reached a ~40 TOPS plateau in microbench at M=N=4096 K=2048 (4.3 % of the 931 TOPS raw MMA peak). The Phase 2B ceiling memo (`2026-05-18-q4k-imma-phase2b-ceiling.md`) speculated that the kernel "might already be competitive with the dequant→cuBLAS path." Phase 3 is the empirical check on the only available test model. The speculation is refuted.

## Setup

- Model: `gemma-3-12b-it-Q4_K_M.gguf` (6.8 GiB)
- Hardware: RTX 5090 (sm_120a, GB202)
- Build: this branch (PR #269 wire-up + base IMMA stack)
- Bench: `imp-cli --bench --bench-pp 2048 --bench-reps 10 --prefill-chunk-size 0 --max-tokens 64 --temperature 0`, 3 trials × 10 reps each, median reported
- Env: `CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8` for cuBLAS determinism
- IMMA opt-in: `--set gemm.q4k_imma_enabled=true`

\`--prefill-chunk-size 0\` is critical — the default chunked prefill at \`chunk_size = 512\` would never let M reach the IMMA dispatch gate (M ≥ 1024).

## Results

| Config | pp2048 (tok/s) | tg64 (tok/s) |
|---|---:|---:|
| OFF (dequant→cuBLAS, default) | **6418** | 116 |
| ON  (IMMA, opt-in)            | **1697** | 119 |
| Δ                             | **−74 %** | ±2 % (noise) |

Trial-by-trial OFF: 6319 / 6418 / 6414 (σ ≈ 1.5 %).
Trial-by-trial ON:  1698 / 1691 / 1696 (σ ≈ 0.2 %).

Decode (tg64) is unaffected because the dispatch gate is M ≥ 1024; decode runs at M=1.

## Why IMMA is empirically slower

Per-dispatch arithmetic for a Gemma-3-12B FFN tile shape (M=2048, N=K≈3840):

\`\`\`
IMMA at 40 TOPS               =  1.5 ms / dispatch
cuBLAS dequant + FP16 GEMM    =  0.26 ms (14 µs dequant + 245 µs at 244 TFLOPS)
⇒ ~6× per-call ratio
\`\`\`

Compounded across ~336 Q4_K dispatches per prefill (~48 layers × 7 weights/layer) ⇒ 3.8× e2e slowdown. Plus per-call activation-quant launch overhead (unamortised) and weight-cache cold start on first rep.

## Decision

**DEFERRED.** All artifacts retained for future researchers to re-bench when one of these conditions appears:
- Larger FFN shapes (N ≥ 8192, K ≥ 4096) widen the 40 TOPS plateau region
- A fundamental kernel restructure ships (persistent CTAs + stream-K, CUTLASS template instantiation, etc.)
- Activation-quant cost can be fused into the prior layer's epilogue
- A workload where dequant→cuBLAS isn't reachable appears (fp16_cache + dequant_scratch both unavailable)

## Files

- NEW \`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-18-q4k-imma-phase3-refuted.md\` — full findings memo with arithmetic, re-eval triggers, full PR chain
- EDIT \`docs/roadmap.md\` §\`pp=512 on large dense models\` — collapses the multi-phase entry into the final DEFERRED decision with all three phase memos cross-referenced

## Risk

None. Doc-only PR; no code touched. Independent of any in-flight PR; merge order doesn't matter.

## Recommended merge

The artifacts are useful as research baseline even with the refutation. The companion PR #269 (dispatch handler) should still merge — it's the only way the knob does anything when a future re-eval happens. The kernel stays in the codebase by way of #267 (already merged) and #268 (already merged).

## Summary
- Bump `STYLE_ITEMS_PER_TURN` from 3 to 32, effectively including all style items every turn
- Update tests to handle pool sizes smaller than the limit

## Root cause
The style rotation (introduced with scene-style conditionals) reduced style items from all 12 to 3 per turn. Critical anti-verbosity guidelines ("never explain what a moment means", "keep dialogue natural and brief", "not a romance novel narrator") were absent most turns, causing Mag-Mell to default to verbose inner monologue. Pre-rotation conversations had all items and produced significantly better output.

author: theofidry
body:
## Description

Hardens GitHub Actions checkout steps reported by `zizmor`'s [`artipacked`](https://docs.zizmor.sh/audits/#artipacked) audit.

Most workflows only need repository contents during checkout, so they now disable persisted checkout credentials. The two checkout steps that intentionally keep credentials for later repository writes are documented with explicit `zizmor` suppressions.

## Changes

- Adds `persist-credentials: false` to checkout steps.
- Keeps persisted credentials for the Private Packagist Conductor checkout because that workflow performs dependency updates and needs repository write credentials.
- Keeps persisted SSH credentials for the performance metrics repository checkout because the workflow later pushes metrics updates to `infection/infection-metrics`.
- Adds inline `zizmor: ignore[artipacked]` comments for those two intentional exceptions, with the reason documented next to each checkout.

author: hatafatif
body:
## Summary

Closes Phase 3. Wires the rest of the generation pipeline:

- **F3.6** — Webhook handlers (LP + exam) with shared-secret + idempotency.
- **F3.7** — Manual refresh endpoints (\`POST /api/v1/generated-{lps,exams}/{id}/refresh\`).
- **F3.8** — Post-generation LP tagging (calls F3.1's \`tag_lp\`).
- **F3.9** — Per-question exam sub-SLO tagging.
- **F3.10** — Revision LP path (concatenated prior-topic context, capped).
- **F3.11** — Batch generation fired from \`publish_breakdown\`; new \`GET /api/v1/breakdowns/{id}/generation-status\`.
- **F3.12** — \`GET /api/v1/orgs/me/usage\` with by-subject + by-curriculum breakdown.
- **F3.13** — \`GET /api/v1/class-lesson-slots/{id}\` surfacing \`lp_status\` / \`lp_error_message\` for the teacher app.

## Design notes

### Webhook path UUID = our row id, not the upstream job_id
At dispatch time we don't yet know LP Assistant / UG_EG's \`job_id\`, so F3.4/F3.5 set the \`callback_url\` to \`/api/v1/webhooks/lp/{generated_lps.id}\`. The webhook handler looks up our row by that path UUID and persists the upstream \`job_id\` from the body for debugging. The webhook does NOT 4xx on \`job_id\` mismatch — our path UUID is the authoritative identifier.

### Shared-secret gate is fail-closed
\`settings.lp_assistant_webhook_secret\` and \`settings.ug_eg_webhook_secret\` default to \`""\`. The handler refuses ALL traffic when the secret is unconfigured (rather than implicitly accepting unsigned requests). Operator must set the env vars before staging takes traffic.

### Batch generation runs as a BackgroundTask
Publishing a breakdown returns immediately; the cache walk + dispatch happens after the response. For a class-scope breakdown with ~60 slots and a fully-warm cache, this is ~60 SQL hits and zero LLM calls (the expected steady state). For a cold global publish, it'll fire ~30 LP requests + ~6 exam requests.

### Default FA/SA configs live in code, not DB
\`DEFAULT_FA_CONFIG[subject]\` / \`DEFAULT_SA_CONFIG[subject]\` in \`batch_service.py\`. Only \`Eng\` is populated today (matches the seed). Unknown \`(subject, slot_type)\` combos log WARNING and skip the slot, rather than 500-ing. Plan to extend per subject as we onboard them.

### Migration
\`20260518000000_generated_lp_revision_topics.sql\` adds the side table that links a revision \`generated_lps\` row to its source topic_ids. F3.8 joins through it to gather candidate sub-SLOs for revision-LP tagging. Idempotent (\`IF NOT EXISTS\`).

### Per-org usage attribution (v1)
Counts only class-scope rows (\`scope='class'\` with the org's CSTs as \`scope_ref_id\`). Global rows reused by every org don't double-count here. Documented in the route's docstring and inline in the plan; v2 will refine (D-10 follow-up).

## Test plan

- [x] 15 new pure-Python tests:
  - \`test_webhook_processor.py\` (4): wrap upstream status into webhook payload shape.
  - \`test_exam_question_walker.py\` (3): exam_json tree walker handles malformed items.
  - \`test_batch_service_units.py\` (4): default FA/SA configs + \`_config_for\` lookups.
  - \`test_lp_tagging_service.py\` (already merged in #59): tag_lp parsing + candidate filtering.
- [x] 4 DB+HTTP-gated webhook auth smoke tests (skip unless \`DATABASE_URL\` is set).
- [x] Full server suite: **124 passed, 38 skipped** — no regressions.
- [x] App imports clean; all 6 new endpoints registered:
  - \`POST /api/v1/webhooks/lp/{generated_lp_id}\`
  - \`POST /api/v1/webhooks/exam/{generated_exam_id}\`
  - \`POST /api/v1/generated-lps/{id}/refresh\`
  - \`POST /api/v1/generated-exams/{id}/refresh\`
  - \`GET  /api/v1/breakdowns/{id}/generation-status\`
  - \`GET  /api/v1/orgs/me/usage\`
  - \`GET  /api/v1/class-lesson-slots/{slot_id}\`
- [ ] **After merge:** manual end-to-end test on staging (publish breakdown → wait → all LPs READY → tagged → SLO coverage updates on mark-taught) — gated on the Railway auto-deploy issue being resolved.

## REBUILD.md

Third slice of [UNI-1994](https://linear.app/unite-group/issue/UNI-1994) — extends the consumption pattern (PRs #93, #94) to the brand **accent** colour pair on Dimitri's checkout CTA.

## What changes

\`src/app/clients/dimitri-itr/DimitriPortalClient.tsx\`:

- Two new defaults: \`DUNCAN_BRAND_ACCENT_DEFAULT = "#E62128"\`, \`DUNCAN_BRAND_ACCENT_HOVER_DEFAULT = "#c4181f"\`
- Page root \`<div>\` sets \`["--brand-accent"]\` + \`["--brand-accent-hover"]\` inline (alongside the existing \`["--brand-primary"]\`)
- 3 literal hex consumers swap to var():
  - Line 308: button background → \`var(--brand-accent)\`
  - Line 319: onMouseEnter → \`var(--brand-accent-hover)\`
  - Line 320: onMouseLeave → \`var(--brand-accent)\`

## Why two vars, not one + color-mix

The previous design specified both shades exactly (\`#E62128\`/\`#c4181f\`). Computing the hover from the active shade via \`color-mix(in srgb, ... <N>%, black)\` would change the exact rendered tone. Two named tokens keeps the operator hand-off cleaner — both shades come from \`brand_config\` directly, no computed surprise.

## Why only Dimitri

CCW and Bulcs portals don't have an accent CTA equivalent in their current shape — their pages use the primary colour throughout. If a CTA pattern lands in those files, \`--brand-accent\` will get added then.

- [x] \`npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json\` — clean
