author: selase
body:
## Summary
Closes 5 of the 6 Cluster B failures from `HANDOFF.md`. The remaining one (`TenantStorageIntegrationTest > files stored per-tenant`) is queued as a follow-up PR (state-leak in `TenantStorageManager`).

Three intertwined changes:

### 1. Switch dedicated-isolation tests from sqlite to postgres
Per the user direction \"we are no longer using sqlite, replace with postgres instances.\" The `TenantProvisioner` already supported `db_driver => 'pgsql'` and provisions a database named `tenant_<uuid_with_underscores>`. The tests just hadn't been migrated.

- `'db_driver' => 'sqlite'` → `'pgsql'`
- `expect(file_exists(\$sqlitePath))->toBeTrue()` → `pg_database` existence query
- Drop `expect(Schema::connection('tenant')->hasTable('posts'))` — there is no tenant-side `posts` migration anywhere in the codebase; this assertion was checking a ghost
- Add `afterEach` that drops every provisioned DB so they don't accumulate

### 2. Harden `TenantProvisioner::createDatabase`
Postgres forbids `CREATE DATABASE` inside a transaction block, and both Laravel's connection manager and `RefreshDatabase` keep `landlord` in one for the test lifetime. Open a dedicated raw PDO bound to landlord credentials so the DDL runs outside whatever transaction the caller holds.

This is a defensive correctness fix for production too — any HTTP request that happens to be in a transaction for unrelated reasons (or wraps tenant creation atomically) would have hit the same `SQLSTATE[25001]` error in production.

Same pattern is used for `DROP DATABASE` in the new `dropTenantDatabase` Pest helper (adds `WITH (FORCE)` for postgres 13+ to evict in-flight connections).

### 3. Delete orphan scaffolding
`App\Models\Tenant\Post` had:
- No matching migration anywhere in `database/migrations/{landlord,tenant,/}` or any module
- `\$fillable = ['title', 'content']` but the only `posts` table that exists is CmsCore's (`title`, `body`, `slug`, `post_type_id`, `author_id`, `tenant_id`) — totally different schema
- Was used **only** by 2 tests in `ConsumerScenarioTest` to assert tenant isolation

Per option B in our scoping discussion: delete the model + the 2 tests. Isolation is already smoke-tested by every tenant-aware feature in the rest of the suite. The other 3 `ConsumerScenarioTest` cases (LLM encryption, BYO config, KMS migration compliance) are kept and unchanged.

## Test impact

| Test | Before | After |
|------|--------|-------|
| `TenantProvisioningTest > creates a postgres database` | FAIL | **PASS** |
| `ColdProvisioningTest > cold provisioning creates a functional tenant` | FAIL | **PASS** |
| `ConsumerScenarioTest > multi_database_isolation_with_sqlite` | FAIL | **DELETED** |
| `ConsumerScenarioTest > shared_database_isolation_via_landlord` | FAIL | **DELETED** |
| Wider `tests/Feature/{Admin,Tenancy}/` (76 tests) | 75 pass | 76 pass (no regressions) |

## Self-Review Report

### Touchpoints updated
- [ ] AGENTS.md — N/A. The raw-PDO pattern is internal to the provisioner; not a convention developers need to know about.
- [ ] Memory files — N/A.
- [ ] Seeders / Navigation / Permissions / `.env.example` / Config — N/A.
- [x] Tests — affected tests turn green; broader suite shows no regressions.

### UI Gap Analysis
N/A — no UI surface. The admin Create-Tenant flow that calls the provisioner is unchanged from a user perspective; the only difference is it now works in more execution contexts (transaction-wrapped or not).

### Solved (auto-fixed)
- Discovered the orphan-model issue during diagnosis and removed both the model and the scaffolding tests in the same PR.
- Added the `dropTenantDatabase` helper so any future test that provisions tenant DBs can clean up consistently.

### Recommended for user decision
- The sqlite branch of `TenantProvisioner::createDatabase` (lines 56-64) is still live. If sqlite is genuinely deprecated as the user mentioned, that branch could be removed — but doing it in this PR is scope creep. **Recommend a separate dedicated PR** to remove sqlite as a valid `db_driver` (would touch validation rules, the controller, and likely the admin UI form).

### Not gaps
- The CmsCore `posts` table on landlord postgres is unaffected by removing `App\Models\Tenant\Post` — they were namespaced differently and never collided in production.
- Three `ConsumerScenarioTest` cases retained because they exercise distinct features (LLM encryption, BYO config, KMS compliance) that aren't redundantly covered elsewhere.
- DROP DATABASE in `afterEach` uses `WITH (FORCE)` (pg13+). The project's CI is postgres-only on a recent version per #18 — safe.

## Dependencies
None. Branches off `main`.

## Test plan
- [x] `pest tests/Feature/Admin/TenantProvisioningTest.php tests/Feature/Tenancy/ColdProvisioningTest.php tests/Feature/Tenancy/ConsumerScenarioTest.php` — 6 passed
- [x] `pest tests/Feature/Admin/ tests/Feature/Tenancy/` — 76 passed, 1 unrelated failure (Test 3 / storage manager, separate PR)

author: trustin
body:
## Motivation

The previous save/download implementation transferred the entire file
contents as a single `Vec<u8>` over Tauri IPC before writing to disk.
This required allocating the full file in memory on both the Rust and
JS sides simultaneously, making it impractical for large files and
risking OOM failures on constrained devices. Additionally, cancelled
save dialogs still triggered a full worker read before the cancellation
was detected.

## Modifications

**Rust sidecar (`desktop/rust/src/main.rs`)**
- Replaced `save_bytes_to_downloads` and `save_bytes_as` commands with a
  streaming protocol: `file_save_open` / `file_save_open_dialog` →
  `file_save_write` (repeated) → `file_save_commit` | `file_save_abort`.
- Added `SaveStreamRegistry` to track open file handles keyed by a
  monotonic u64 id, enabling parallel saves without contention.
- Writes target a sibling `.tmp` file; commit performs an atomic rename
  so the destination path never appears on disk until the save
  completes. Abort deletes the `.tmp`.
- Candidate name iteration ("foo.ext", "foo (1).ext", …) uses
  `create_new` on the `.tmp` to prevent concurrent saves of the same
  basename from colliding.
- Background GC reclaims orphaned `.tmp` handles after a 5-minute idle
  timeout with a 60-second scan interval, covering renderer crashes
  mid-save.
- `file_save_write` uses `block_in_place` so chunk writes do not tie up
  the Tokio executor; the chunk bytes are borrowed directly from the
  IPC body with no intermediate `Vec` clone.
- (Breaking) `save_bytes_to_downloads` and `save_bytes_as` Tauri
  commands are removed.

**Frontend save pipeline**
- Added `platformBridge` methods `fileSaveOpen`, `fileSaveOpenDialog`,
  `fileSaveWrite`, `fileSaveCommit`, and `fileSaveAbort` matching the
  new Rust chain.
- New `streamFileChunks` async generator yields 1 MiB chunks from the
  worker. `pumpChunksToHandle` pre-issues the next `readFile` before
  awaiting the prior `fileSaveWrite`, so disk writes and worker reads
  overlap instead of serializing.
- Web fallback `downloadFileFromWorker` builds the `Blob` from N × 1
  MiB views rather than one contiguous `Uint8Array`, so large files
  complete on engines that reject a single large allocation.
- Save-as dialog is resolved before any worker `readFile`, so a
  cancelled dialog incurs no worker overhead.
- `FileSaveOp` state gains a `progress: number | null` field;
  `UnsupportedFileView` renders the current percentage ("Downloading…
  45%") next to the spinner once the worker reports `totalSize`.
- New `throttleProgress` helper coalesces intermediate progress events
  to ~100 ms intervals while guaranteeing the first and final chunks
  always emit.
- Truncation guard: if the worker stops short of the advertised
  `totalSize`, a final emit at `(received, received)` is forced so the
  UI reaches 100%.
- Error cleanup: outstanding reads and writes are drained before
  `fileSaveAbort` is called, preventing unhandled rejections and
  Rust-side races.
- `currentOp` prop renamed to `op` on `FileActionsMenu`,
  `UnsupportedFileView`, and related surfaces.
- (Breaking) `saveBytesToDownloads` and `saveBytesAs` bridge methods
  are removed.

**Tests**
- Added `frontend/tests/unit/helpers/workerRpcMocks.ts` with shared
  `readResp` / `statResp` builders.
- `saveActionsMocks.ts` gains `platformBridgeFileSaveStubs()` covering
  the five new `fileSave*` methods.
- `fileDownload.test.ts` adds ~325 lines: chunked reads aligned to the
  1 MiB constant, mid-stream abort propagation, dialog ordering and
  cancellation, sub-slice copy isolation, progress throttle with
  simulated write latency, truncation final-emit, and a dedicated
  pipelining test asserting that a second `readFile` is dispatched
  while the first `fileSaveWrite` is still in flight.
- `UnsupportedFileView.test.tsx` adds 6 tests for progress-percent
  rendering across download / save-as / save-to-downloads, with and
  without `totalSize`.

## Result

Saving or downloading files of any size no longer requires holding the
full contents in memory. A 1 GiB file transfers in 1 MiB chunks, with
reads and writes overlapping in a pipeline. On the desktop, the
destination file only appears at its final path after the write
completes, so interrupted saves leave no partial files behind. Users
see a live percentage counter ("Downloading… 45%") during the transfer,
and a cancelled save dialog costs no worker I/O at all.

## Slice

Adds `aragora/reputation/dispute_window.py` — a flag-gated gate implementing the "time is part of settlement" doctrine from `docs/plans/SKIN_IN_THE_GAME_REPUTATION.md`. Per-domain dispute windows (prediction_market 72 h, debate_position 48 h, code_pr / km_contribution 24 h, crux_resolution / epistemic_claim 48 h) determine whether a counter-attestation filing is eligible for the reversal path or rejected because the settlement is final.

## Gating

- Default: **OFF** (flag: `ARAGORA_DISPUTE_WINDOW_ENABLED`)
- Live queue effect: **none** — pure in-memory eligibility check; no writes to any store, no dispatch mutation, no queue mutation
- Advances issue: #6066 (AGT-05 — skin-in-the-game reputation flow), sub-deliverable 4 — settlement-window enforcement

## Tests

- `test_disabled_by_default` — flag absent → gate disabled
- `test_truthy_values_enable[1/true/yes/on]` — all four truthy values activate
- `test_check_raises_when_disabled` — `DisputeWindowGateDisabledError` raised with flag name in message
- `test_default_policy_covers_all_known_domains` — every `KNOWN_DOMAINS` entry has a positive window
- `test_custom_policy_overrides_and_falls_back` — custom window applies; other domains fall back to defaults
- `test_unknown_domain_raises` — `UnknownDomainError` for unrecognised domain string
- `test_within_window[4 parametrized cases]` — within boundary + exactly at boundary treated as eligible
- `test_outside_window[3 parametrized cases]` — past-window filings produce `within_window=False`
- `test_negative_elapsed_is_within` — filing before resolution is always eligible
- `test_record_fields_and_to_dict` — `claim_id`, `elapsed_hours`, `evidence`, and `to_dict` keys verified
- `test_custom_narrow_window_rejects` — tight custom policy overrides generous default
- `test_unknown_domain_through_gate` — gate propagates `UnknownDomainError` from policy
- `test_malformed_timestamp_raises` — `ValueError` with "cannot parse" for bad ISO strings

## Validation

- `pytest tests/reputation/test_dispute_window.py --noconftest` — **21 passed**
- `ruff check aragora/reputation/dispute_window.py tests/reputation/test_dispute_window.py` — clean
- `mypy aragora/reputation/dispute_window.py tests/reputation/test_dispute_window.py --ignore-missing-imports` — clean
- Net diff: **299 LOC** (151-line implementation + 148-line test file)

## Out of scope

- Persisting `DisputeRecord` to disk or any store — deferred; callers own the record
- Executing the actual reversal (step 7 — handled by `ReputationStore.reverse_delta`, already on main via the `agt-05-claim-verifier-bridge-followup` branch)
- Network calls or HTTP attestation verification — deferred to the oracle wiring slice
- Hard slashing policy — remains soft (downweight) until an explicit operator decision enables it

body:
## Plan

**Version 24 — user-requested.** The user wants cells that are interactive UI controls holding a true/false state ("buttons and switches"), something Excel and Sheets largely lack. v24 ships the boolean core: a cell can become a clickable checkbox.

## Build

- **New pure module `widget.rs`** — `Widgets`, the set of square-sheet cells that are toggles; `bool_state`, a cell's `CellValue` rendered as a checkbox state (checked only for boolean `TRUE`); `bool_source`, a checkbox state as the `TRUE`/`FALSE` literal to write back. No egui, no engine — `cargo test` covers it.
- A **`Checkbox` ribbon button** turns the selected cells into toggle cells, or back — like the bold button, it flips the whole selection.
- The square grid renders a toggle cell as a real `egui::Checkbox` instead of its text. Clicking it writes `TRUE`/`FALSE` to the engine through `apply_edits`, so the flip is a normal **undoable** cell edit — `Ctrl+Z` un-clicks it.
- Seeded with one demo toggle at D2 so a checkbox is visible at launch.

## Test

- `cargo test` — **85 tests** (+4): toggle-set add / remove / count, idempotent set, `bool_state` true only for `Bool(true)`, `bool_source` round-trip.
- native + `wasm32-unknown-unknown` build ✓
- `cargo fmt` / `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` clean ✓

## Notes

Boolean toggles are the first widget kind. **Buttons** — and a configuration wizard once there's more than one kind — are a planned follow-on; the button flow also feeds the future AI-cell idea (a button "directs a prompt" at a cell).

Physically runnable: `cargo run --manifest-path apps/tescellate-ui/Cargo.toml`. D2 shows a checkbox — click it, watch it flip, `Ctrl+Z` to undo. Select any range and hit `Checkbox` to make more.

## Summary

The previous `public/images/jornbowrl_circle.jpg` had a visible notch on the viewer's left side — the background-removal mask had eaten into the hair/ear area. This PR re-does the BG removal from the origin (`public/images/jornbowrl3.jpg`) and re-renders the circular avatar.

## How

1. Ran rembg on `jornbowrl3.jpg` with four candidate models. Only `birefnet-portrait` cleanly isolated the subject from the bokeh; the others kept light spots as foreground (bbox ≈ full image).
2. Cleaned alpha (drop pixels <50 to 0), then took a square crop with side ≈ 0.85 × subject height, vertically anchored with the face slightly above geometric center — same head-and-shoulders framing as the prior file.
3. Rendered at 600×600 for clean AA, then downsized to 379×379 (the existing dimensions) so no consumer needs to change.

## Both deploys

- `public/images/jornbowrl_circle.jpg` — committed in this PR (25 KB, 379×379).
- `s3://publicsg/github.io/images/jornbowrl_circle.jpg` — already overwritten so the live site (which the deploy.yaml rewrite step points at) picks up the fix without waiting for the next deploy.

Cache-Control was set to `public, max-age=300` on the S3 upload, so any cached copies expire within 5 minutes.

body:
### Motivation
- Replace manual SQL smoke testing with a backend-owned runner loop that reliably claims and executes jobs from `ai_execution_jobs` for production use. 
- Provide worker registration, concurrency tracking, structured logs/metrics, safe retry/dead-letter handling, and an API surface for health / enqueue / single-run operations.

### Description
- Added a new runner service at `backend/src/services/execution/aiExecutionRunnerService.js` that registers worker nodes, claims jobs atomically using `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, increments `attempt_count` safely, sets `locked_by/locked_at/heartbeat_at/timeout_at`, enforces `queue_name`/`priority`/`run_after` ordering, and provides `runOnce`, `claimNextJob`, `enqueueInternalTestJob`, `getHealth`, and `registerWorkerNode` APIs. 
- Implemented safe completion and failure flows that verify ownership (`status = 'running'` and `locked_by`), write `execution_logs`, `worker_metrics`, and `task_execution_history`, decrement `current_concurrency`, perform exponential backoff (capped at 300s) for retries, and insert `dead_letter_queue` rows when attempts are exhausted; non-retryable errors mark jobs `failed`. 
- Added controller and routes at `backend/src/controllers/aiExecutionRunnerController.js` and `backend/src/routes/aiExecutionRunnerRoutes.js` and registered them under `/api/ai/execution` in `backend/src/index.js`, exposing `GET /health`, `POST /enqueue-test`, and `POST /run-once` endpoints. 
- Added documentation `docs/architecture/ai_execution_runner_loop.md` describing worker registration, claiming algorithm, execution semantics, retry/dead-letter rules, and example `curl` smoke tests; introduced env-configs like `AI_WORKER_NODE_NAME`, `AI_MAX_CONCURRENT_JOBS`, `AI_EXECUTION_JOB_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, and `AI_EXECUTION_QUEUE_NAME`. 
- Emits operational logs required by the spec: `[ai-execution-runner] worker registered`, `[ai-execution-runner] job claimed`, `[ai-execution-runner] job completed`, and `[ai-execution-runner] job failed`.

### Testing
- Performed syntax/parse checks with `node --check` on the new service, controller, routes, and `index.js`, and they succeeded. 
- Ran an existing backend test via `npm --prefix backend run test:ai-copy-sanitizer` and it passed (test output: `aiCopySanitizer tests passed`).

body:
## Summary

This adds the V2 prompt adapter contract needed before the coordinator (PR7) can be wired up. The interface decouples the coordinator from any UI implementation, and the null stub lets PR7 compile and be tested without a WinUI dependency.

## What changed

- `ExecApprovalV2PromptRequest` — sealed request type with the 8 fields the presenter needs (`DisplayCommand`, `Cwd`, `Host`, `Security`, `Ask`, `AgentId`, `ResolvedPath`, `SessionKey`). `AllowAlwaysPatterns` is intentionally excluded; it lives on `ExecApprovalEvaluation` and is the coordinator's responsibility to pass through after the decision.
- `IExecApprovalV2PromptHandler` — single `PromptAsync` method returning `Task<ExecApprovalDecision>`. Non-nullable contract; implementations fail-closed to `Deny` on any unhandled error.
- `ExecApprovalV2NullPromptHandler` — stub that always returns `Deny` synchronously via `Task.FromResult`. Never throws. Intended as the default until a real dialog implementation ships.

The `V2` infix avoids collision with the existing `IExecApprovalPromptHandler` / `ExecApprovalPromptRequest` types on the legacy path.

## Testing

```
dotnet test tests/OpenClaw.Shared.Tests/OpenClaw.Shared.Tests.csproj --filter "ExecApprovalV2Prompt"
```

12 tests, all passing. Coverage includes stub behavior, the `AllowAlwaysPatterns` exclusion verified via reflection, assembly placement, legacy type separation, and a guard that the null stub is not referenced from production `src/`.

## Notes

No production wiring in this PR. `SystemCapability` is untouched. The real dialog implementation is a separate slice after the coordinator lands.

author: volgin
body:
## Summary

- Pass the default local MMseqs `--k-score` value as `seq:96,prof:80` instead of including literal shell quotes.
- Add regression coverage for both monomer and paired local search command construction.

## Root Cause

`colabfold_search` builds MMseqs commands as a Python argument list and calls `subprocess.check_call` without a shell. The existing `"'seq:96,prof:80'"` value therefore reaches MMseqs with the single quote characters still attached, so MMseqs does not apply the intended TWIN value and falls back to its default `seq:2147483647,prof:2147483647`.

## Local Reproduction

We reproduced this in a local ColabFold 1.6.1 CPU deployment using the standard `colabfold_search` path with no explicit `-s` and no `--gpu`.

Current behavior:

- ColabFold logs `--k-score 'seq:96,prof:80'`
- MMseqs prefilter receives fallback `--k-score seq:2147483647,prof:2147483647`
- Observed k-mer similarity threshold: `122`

Patched behavior:

- MMseqs receives `--k-score seq:96,prof:80`
- Observed thresholds: `96` for sequence search and `80` for profile search

On a 20-protein stratified sample, 15/20 final A3Ms changed. Row-count impact was modest:

- Median patched/old row ratio: `0.996`
- Max patched/old row ratio: `1.022`
- Min patched/old row ratio: `0.858`

The patched path was more computationally expensive in this sample, especially environmental prefiltering.

## Impact

This affects default local CPU searches where sensitivity is omitted (`-s` is `None`) and GPU search is not used. In that path ColabFold intends to match the server-like default k-mer threshold directly, but the quoted argument prevents MMseqs from receiving it correctly.

Fixes #804.

## Validation

- `python -m pytest tests/test_mmseqs_search.py -q`
- `python -m py_compile colabfold/mmseqs/search.py tests/test_mmseqs_search.py`
- `git diff --check`

I also attempted to include `tests/test_msa.py` locally, but this checkout's venv still lacks the optional `alphafold` dependency required to collect that test module.

author: bluestreak01
body:
## Summary

Fixes a server-side WAL transaction-log invariant violation that triggers on process restart between an in-progress structure change's metaFile write and its txn-log commit. The next column-add after the restart fails with:

```
possible corruption in transaction metadata [table=..., offset=..., newVersion=...]
```

surfaced repeatedly by the QuestDB c-client QWP/WS bounce-sweep fuzz suite (seed `0x646fe2971b68a028`, CI build [234113](https://dev.azure.com/questdb/questdb/_build/results?buildId=234113)).

## Root cause

`TableSequencerImpl.nextStructureTxn` issued writes in this order:

1. `beginMetadataChangeEntry(v+1, ...)` — writes the alter record into `txnMem` mmap; bumps `txnMetaMem` + `txnMetaMemIndex`.
2. `applyToMetadata(...)` — `change.apply` updates in-memory metadata; `metadata.syncToMetaFile()` **writes the new structure version into the metaFile mmap**.
3. `metadata.sync()` — msync metaFile (cosmetic; mmap-page-cache persistence makes it not load-bearing for crash recovery).
4. `endMetadataChangeEntry()` — `fullSync()` then `txnLogFile.endMetadataChangeEntry()` — **bumps `MAX_TXN_OFFSET` in txnMem mmap**.

mmap writes survive process restart through the kernel page cache irrespective of msync, so what matters for crash consistency is the order of the *mmap writes themselves* — not the msyncs. A kill between (2) and (4) leaves the metaFile mmap durably ahead of the txn-log commit pointer. On restart:

- `metadata.open()` reads `structureVersion=v+1` from the metaFile.
- `tableTransactionLog.open()` reads `MAX_TXN_OFFSET=T` (unchanged → `maxStructureVersion=v`), positions `txnMetaMemIndex.appendOffset = (v+1) * 8`.

The next ingest-side column-add then satisfies the gate `metadata.getMetadataVersion() == expectedStructureVersion` (both `v+1`) and calls `beginMetadataChangeEntry(v+2, ...)`, which trips:

```java
if (newStructureVersion != txnMetaMemIndex.getAppendOffset() / Long.BYTES) {
    throw CairoException.critical(0).put("possible corruption in transaction metadata ...");
}
```

— with `newStructureVersion = v+2` (e.g. 90) and `appendOffset/8 = v+1` (89, hence the `offset=712` in the CI failure).

## Fix

Reorder the *writes* in `nextStructureTxn` so the txn-log commit lands before the metaFile mmap update:

- Split `applyToMetadata` into its two components: keep `deserializedAlter.apply(metadataSvc, true)` (in-memory state — still needed before the post-commit invariant check), but defer `metadata.syncToMetaFile()` until after `endMetadataChangeEntry()`.
- The reorder leaves only the inverse crash window (metaFile lagging txnLog). The existing `reload()` already had a catch-up loop that replays pending alters from `txnMetaMem` into the metaFile — factor it into `catchUpMetadataFromTxnLog()` and call it from `open()` as well as `reload()`.
- `applyToMetadata` is now unused; remove it.

After the fix, all crash windows are either consistent (both files at same version) or fixable on next open (metaFile behind txnLog → catch-up replays missing alters).

## Test plan

- [x] `TableSequencerImplTest` — 9 tests pass
- [x] `TableTransactionLogFuzzTest` — passes
- [x] `WalAlterTableSqlTest`, `WalTableFailureTest`, `AlterTableWalEnabledTest` — 83 tests, 0 failures
- [x] `WalTableWriterFuzzTest`, `WalWriterTest`, `WalWriterReplaceRangeTest` — 142 tests, 0 failures
- [ ] Re-run the QWP/WS bounce-sweep fuzz suite against a QuestDB build that includes this fix (seed `0x646fe2971b68a028` from CI build 234113) and confirm `test_n_bounce_sweep` is green
- [ ] CI

author: itzikvaknin
body:
## Describe the changes in the pull request

**Current.** `Storage::insert_entry`, the buffering hot path behind `FT.AGGREGATE … COLLECT … SORTBY … LIMIT offset count`, took an `FnOnce() -> Box<[Option<SharedValue>]>` to snapshot the candidate's sort-key values. Once the heap reached the `offset + count` cap, *every* incoming row paid for that snapshot — an allocation plus one `Arc::clone` per sort key — even when the row was going to be discarded immediately because it lost the compare against the heap's current worst entry. On a shard returning many more rows than the final `LIMIT`, the doomed-candidate cost dominates.

**Change.** Split the snapshot into two phases:

1. A new borrow-only comparator, `EntryKey::cmp_candidate` (added in `src/redisearch_rs/reducers/src/collect/heap.rs`), compares a borrowed `Iterator<Item = Option<&SharedValue>>` against an existing `EntryKey` and returns `Ordering::Greater` iff the candidate would beat the entry. It reuses the same `cmp_fields` delegate as `Ord::cmp`, so the ASC/DESC orientation and missing-worst policy stay in one place.
2. `Storage::insert_entry` now takes a borrowed sort-key *view* — `F: Fn() -> impl IntoIterator<Item = Option<&'r SharedValue>>` — instead of an owned `Box`. On the heap-at-cap branch it uses `cmp_candidate` for a borrow-only compare against the current worst; the owned `Box<[Option<SharedValue>]>` is materialized only when the candidate has been confirmed to survive. Below cap (no worst to beat), the view is materialized directly, preserving the existing "first `cap` rows always buffered" semantics. The array path (unsorted `COLLECT`) is untouched.

Both call sites are switched to lazy borrowed views:

- `RemoteCollectCtx::add` (shard-side, `collect/remote.rs`) maps `row.get(key)` over `r.fields.sort_keys()`.
- `LocalCollectCtx::add` (coordinator-merge, `collect/local.rs`) maps `get_field(item, name)` over `r.fields.sort_key_names()`. The `snapshot_sort_keys` helper is now dead and removed.

**Outcome.** Doomed `COLLECT … SORTBY` candidates pay zero `Box` allocations and zero `Arc::clone` calls on the sort-key path — just one borrowed comparison against the heap's worst. Winners pay one extra borrowed compare in addition to the snapshot they were already paying for, which is a negligible cost relative to the saved allocations on doomed rows. The improvement scales with the ratio of input rows to the effective `offset + count` cap.

No FFI changes, no wire-format changes, no change to result ordering or to the missing-worst policy delegated to `cmp_fields`.

#### Which additional issues this PR fixes
1. MOD-15734

#### Main objects this PR modified
1. `EntryKey` — new inherent method `cmp_candidate` in `src/redisearch_rs/reducers/src/collect/heap.rs`.
2. `Storage::insert_entry` in `src/redisearch_rs/reducers/src/collect/storage.rs` — signature now takes a `Fn() -> IntoIterator<Item = Option<&SharedValue>>` borrow-view closure instead of `FnOnce() -> Box<[Option<SharedValue>]>`.
3. `RemoteCollectCtx::add` in `src/redisearch_rs/reducers/src/collect/remote.rs` and `LocalCollectCtx::add` in `src/redisearch_rs/reducers/src/collect/local.rs` — updated to pass borrowed sort-key iterators; `snapshot_sort_keys` removed.
4. `src/redisearch_rs/reducers/tests/{heap,storage}.rs` — new `cmp_candidate` tests (ASC/DESC orientation, missing-value propagation, multi-key zip alignment) and new behavioral canaries that count `sort_view` invocations (exactly 1 for doomed candidates, exactly 2 for winners).

#### Mark if applicable

- [ ] This PR introduces API changes
- [ ] This PR introduces serialization changes

#### Release Notes

- [x] This PR requires release notes
- [ ] This PR does not require release notes

User impact: faster `FT.AGGREGATE … COLLECT … SORTBY … LIMIT` on shards that scan many more rows than the final limit, by skipping per-row sort-key allocations and `Arc` clones for candidates that lose the top-K compare.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches the ranked `COLLECT SORTBY` top-K path and changes how sort keys are compared/materialized, so any subtle comparator/iterator-lifetime bug could affect result ordering or LIMIT behavior.
>
> **Overview**
> Optimizes shard-side and coordinator `COLLECT ... SORTBY` buffering by avoiding eager cloning of sort-key values for heap comparisons.
>
> `Storage::insert_entry` now accepts a borrow-only `sort_view` and uses new `EntryKey::cmp_candidate` to compare heap-at-cap candidates against the current worst without allocating; it only materializes the owned sort-key snapshot when the candidate actually survives. Local/remote COLLECT reducers are updated to pass borrowed sort-key iterators, and tests are expanded to pin the new compare semantics and ensure doomed candidates don't trigger materialization while winners do.

What's done (what's new/changed)
* Installed `stripe@22.1.1` and pinned Bumpgrade's Stripe API contract to `2026-04-22.dahlia`.
* Copied Stripe values from LaurelHarned into ignored local env and Cloudflare Worker secrets without printing values; `STRIPE_ACTIVE_MODE` defaults to `sandbox`.

author: sotashimozono
body:
## Summary

Fixes the two portability failures found dogfooding on a stock research box
(Ubuntu 20.04, no sudo/cmake). Both root-cause to reqwest's **aws-lc-rs**
crypto provider.

- **F1** — published Linux binary dynamically linked against the
  `ubuntu-latest` glibc 2.38 → `GLIBC_2.38 not found` on Ubuntu 20.04 /
  RHEL 8 / HPC boxes.
- **F2** — `cargo install doiget-cli` fails in `aws-lc-sys` (needs cmake,
  unavailable without sudo).

## Changes

- `reqwest` `rustls` → `rustls-no-provider`; explicit `rustls` pin with the
  **`ring`** provider (cc + perl only, no cmake), installed as the
  process-default `CryptoProvider` once in `doiget-core`'s `http` module
  (mandatory: `rustls-no-provider` makes `ClientBuilder::build` panic
  otherwise).
- Release `sign` job builds the Linux artefact as static
  `x86_64-unknown-linux-musl`; artefact name `doiget-linux-x86_64`
  unchanged (signing/SBOM/docs stable).
- **ADR-0020 Amendment 1** + INDEX + CHANGELOG document the rationale.

TLS posture is unchanged: rustls-only (no openssl/native-tls — `deny.toml`
allowlist still satisfied), platform-verifier roots. `cargo tree -i
aws-lc-sys` now returns *no packages*.

## Test plan

author: vello101
body:
## 개요

CSP와 주요 보안 헤더를 강화하고, CSP 위반 리포트 수집 경로를 추가했습니다.

기존 `next.config.ts`의 정적 CSP 설정을 middleware 기반 동적 nonce 정책으로 옮겨 `script-src`에 nonce와 `strict-dynamic`을 적용했습니다. 또한 `report-uri`와 `report-to`를 함께 설정해 브라우저별 CSP 리포트 포맷을 수신할 수 있도록 `/api/csp-report` 엔드포인트를 추가했습니다.

React 19 style hoisting, Next.js DevOverlay, toast/font 런타임 스타일 주입과의 호환 문제로 `style-src`는 `'self' 'unsafe-inline'`로 완화했고, 관련 CSSOM 우회 코드는 인라인 스타일 기반으로 롤백했습니다.

## PR 유형

- [x] 새로운 기능 추가
- [x] 버그 수정
- [ ] UI 디자인 변경
- [x] 코드 리팩토링
- [x] 테스트 추가/수정
- [ ] 문서 수정
- [x] 빌드/패키지 설정 변경

## 관련 이슈

closes #229

## 작업 내용

- `src/middleware.ts`
  - 요청별 nonce 생성 및 `Content-Security-Policy`, `Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only`, `Reporting-Endpoints` 헤더 설정 추가
  - `script-src 'nonce-...' 'strict-dynamic'` 적용
  - `style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'`로 React 19/Next.js 런타임 스타일 주입 호환성 확보
  - `/api/csp-report`가 middleware matcher를 타지 않도록 제외
  - nonce 생성을 `Buffer` 대신 표준 Edge API(`btoa`)로 교체
  - `buildCspEnforced` / `buildCspReportOnly` 중복을 `buildCspDirectives` 공통 함수로 단일화

- `src/app/layout.tsx`
  - `headers()`로 `x-nonce`를 읽어 layout을 동적 렌더링으로 강제
  - CSP 헤더의 nonce와 Script 컴포넌트 nonce가 항상 일치하도록 보장

- `src/app/api/csp-report/route.ts`
  - `report-uri` 포맷과 `report-to` 포맷을 모두 수신하는 CSP 리포트 엔드포인트 추가
  - 수신 payload를 공통 구조로 정규화해 로깅

- `src/lib/supabase/middleware.ts`
  - middleware에서 생성한 `x-nonce` request header가 Supabase session refresh 이후에도 유지되도록 보강

- `next.config.ts`, `next.config.test.ts`
  - CSP 설정을 middleware로 이전
  - `X-Powered-By` 비활성화
  - HSTS `max-age`를 1일로 조정

- UI 컴포넌트
  - `BlockHandleMenu`, `LearningStatsSection`, `NoteGridCard`의 CSP 호환성 및 표시 로직 조정

- 테스트
  - middleware CSP 빌더 단위 테스트 추가/갱신
  - 보안 헤더 E2E 테스트 추가/갱신

- 기타
  - `.gitignore`에 `/test-results` 추가

## 테스트 방법

1. `npm run lint`
   - ESLint 통과 확인

2. `npm run type-check`
   - TypeScript 타입 체크 통과 확인

3. `npm run build`
   - Next.js production build 통과 확인
   - middleware 및 service worker 번들링 정상 확인

## 스크린샷 (FE 변경 시)

<!-- TODO: 스크린샷 첨부 -->

FE 컴포넌트 변경이 포함되어 있어 `/mypage` 확인 스크린샷 첨부를 권장합니다.

## 리뷰 요구사항 (선택)

- `style-src`를 nonce-only가 아닌 `'unsafe-inline'`로 완화한 결정이 현재 React 19/Next.js 런타임 스타일 주입과의 호환성 측면에서 적절한지 확인 부탁드립니다.
- CSP 리포트 엔드포인트에서 현재는 `console.warn` 기반으로 로깅하므로, 추후 Sentry 등 외부 수집 도구 연동 필요 여부를 함께 검토해 주세요.

body:
fix(sprint-11-d): ImageKind 'post' → 'posts' (IAM/lifecycle policy 복수형 prefix 일치)

## 문제

hotfix #16 머지 후 staging 재검증:
- chat: presign 200 + S3 PUT 200 + CDN HEAD 200 ✅
- **post: presign 200 + S3 PUT 403 AccessDenied** ❌

에러 메시지:
> User: arn:aws:iam::715398629040:user/kkaebizigi-app is not authorized to perform:
> s3:PutObject on resource: "arn:aws:s3:::kkaebizigi-staging/post/.../00mpb...png"

## 원인

인프라 정책(IAM / S3 lifecycle / CORS)은 모두 prefix `posts/` (복수형, RESTful
컬렉션 컨벤션) 허용. 하지만 `ImageKind` 타입은 `'post'` (단수)로 정의되어
object key가 `post/...`로 생성됨 → IAM이 거부.

```
scripts/aws-bootstrap/policies/app-user-policy.json:
  "arn:aws:s3:::kkaebizigi-prod/posts/*"      ← 복수형 허용

코드 (변경 전):
  type ImageKind = 'post' | 'chat'             ← 단수
  objectKey = `${kind}/${uid}/${date}/${id}`   → "post/uid/..." (mismatch)
```

types.ts / upload-post-image.ts / presign route schema / presigned-url
unit tests의 `'post'` → `'posts'` 통일. chat은 셀 수 없는 명사라 단수 유지
(인프라와 1:1 매핑).

- 신규 post 이미지: `posts/{uid}/{date}/{ulid}.{ext}` key로 저장 → IAM 허용
- 기존 데이터: prod에 0건 (Sprint 11이 첫 도입) — 마이그레이션 불필요

author: haniajamshaid-carbonteq
body:
## Summary

Implements **per-status rerun selection** for batch automations, per the May-14 design spec (source: Erin's feedback — _"If I only wanted to re-scan the rented properties… I might want to rescan rented and possibly-rented, but not the not-rented ones."_).

A batch automation now carries a `statuses: Risk[]` set ('risk' | 'warn' | 'clean') that narrows each rerun. Scope is **re-evaluated against the latest scan each cycle**, so the set follows the data rather than being frozen at automation time.

## Surfaces touched

| Surface | What changed |
|---|---|
| **Automate modal** | New "Re-scan which properties?" section (3 status pills with live counts) + AutomationScopeCard summarising "X of Y addresses every {cadence}. Next run ~ {date}." Edit mode shows inline `X → Y` delta. |
| **Active automation banner** | New `AutomationBanner` on the batch detail page replaces the compact "Automated · every Nmo" pill: `⟳ Auto-rerun: every 3 months · 12 of 16 addresses (Rented, Possibly Rented) · Next run {date}` with Edit + Cancel. |
| **`/scheduled`** | New "Scope" column with color-coded status dots + in-scope/total fraction. Single-property schedules render `—`. |
| **`/scheduled/:id`** | New "Edit schedule" button. "Scope" field added to the meta strip for batch automations. |

## Defaults and edge cases

| Edge case | Behavior |
|---|---|
| First-time modal open | Cadence = Quarterly; statuses = `['risk','warn']` (Rented + Possibly Rented). Not Rented unchecked, per spec. |
| Empty selection | Scope card switches to warn tone with spec copy. Automate button disabled. |
| First scan still running | Pills show `(—)`, scope card shows "Address counts pending…", primary CTA copy becomes "Apply when scan completes." |
| Edit mode, scope changed | Inline diff line in modal: `Next run scope: 12 → 16 addresses. First run with new scope: {date}.` Toast on save echoes the delta. |
| Cancel automation | Confirm dialog with the spec's "The current run, if any, will finish." copy. |

## Data model

## VISUAL-RENDER-01 — Preserve PNG aspect ratio for map sprites

### Changed files (4)

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| \`src/render/contain-fit.ts\` | **New** — reusable contain-fit helper (63 lines) |
| \`src/render/buildings.ts\` | Use \`containFit\` in \`drawBuildingSprite()\`, \`renderHq()\`, and all overlay \`spriteTopY\` computations |
| \`src/render/environment.ts\` | Use \`containFit\` in \`renderResourceNode()\` and \`renderDecor()\` |
| \`tests/unit/contain-fit.test.ts\` | **New** — 10 unit tests for contain-fit helper |

### Helper behavior: \`containFit(naturalWidth, naturalHeight, maxWidth, maxHeight)\`

Computes draw dimensions that preserve the source image's natural aspect ratio inside a maximum bounding box (CSS \`object-fit: contain\` semantics).

- **Square image in square box** → draws at full box size (unchanged behavior for square PNGs)
- **Tall image in wide box** → height fixed to \`maxHeight\`, width reduced to preserve ratio
- **Wide image in tall box** → width fixed to \`maxWidth\`, height reduced to preserve ratio
- **Invalid natural size** (0, negative, NaN, Infinity) → falls back to full \`maxWidth × maxHeight\` box

### Affected render paths

| Render path | Before | After |
|------------|--------|-------|
| \`drawBuildingSprite()\` | \`profile.size[0]×size[1]\` forced as draw w/h | \`containFit(naturalW, naturalH, size[0], size[1])\` |
| \`renderHq()\` | \`profile.size[0]×size[1]\` forced | \`containFit()\` for HQ sprite |
| \`renderResourceNode()\` | \`profile.size[0]×size[1]\` forced | \`containFit()\` for resource sprites |
| \`renderDecor()\` | \`profile.size[0]×size[1]\` forced | \`containFit()\` for decor sprites |
| All overlay \`spriteTopY\` | Used \`profile.size[1] * zoom\` (max height) | Uses contained \`drawHeight\` from \`containFit()\` |

### Spritesheet.ts — UNCHANGED (and why)

\`src/render/spritesheet.ts\` is intentionally **not modified** by this PR. Spritesheet frames are fixed 256×256 source cells extracted from a uniform 2048×2048 grid. They are not arbitrary-aspect PNG images — each frame is drawn from a square source rectangle, and the profile.size bounding box correctly describes the intended draw dimensions. Applying contain-fit to spritesheet frames would be semantically wrong and could cause visual regressions.

### Tests added (10)

1. Square image in square box → unchanged dimensions
2. Tall image in wide box → height constrained, width reduced
3. Wide image in tall box → width constrained, height reduced
4. Invalid natural size (zero) → fallback to max box
5. Invalid natural size (negative) → fallback to max box
6. Invalid natural size (NaN) → fallback to max box
7. Invalid natural size (Infinity) → fallback to max box
8. Zero naturalWidth and naturalHeight → fallback to max box
9. Non-square box with square image → fits inside without exceeding either dimension
10. Non-square box with matching aspect ratio → fills box exactly

### Checks run

- ✅ \`npm run type-check\`
- ✅ \`npm run build\`
- ✅ \`npm run test\` — 206 passed (11 test files)
- ✅ \`npm run test:e2e\` — 65 passed
- ✅ \`GITHUB_PAGES=true npm run build\`

### Manual QA notes

- Start game, verify buildings render without visible stretching
- Check HQ sprite renders correctly (non-square PNG should not be distorted)
- Check resource nodes (mineral_infinite is 110×96 profile, non-square) render without stretch
- Check decor items (dry_bush is 34×28, sand_bump is 50×28, non-square) render without stretch
- Verify overlay labels (OFF, progress bars, lightning bolt) still position correctly above sprites
- Verify fallback rendering (no sprite) is unchanged

author: heathley
body:
## Summary

  This adds a new bundled standalone plugin, `build-macos-apps`, focused on Phase 1 of a typed macOS/Xcode build workflow.

  It introduces a single `macos-dev` toolset with three tools:

  - `macos_inspect_project`
  - `macos_list_schemes`
  - `macos_build_project`

  This is additive. It does not replace Hermes' existing terminal/file/process surfaces. It adds a structured, opt-in Xcode-native layer on top of them.

  ## What’s included

  - bundled plugin scaffold under `plugins/build-macos-apps/`
  - shared `check_fn` gating for the full toolset
  - repo inspection for `.xcworkspace`, `.xcodeproj`, and `Package.swift`
  - scheme listing via `xcodebuild -list -json`
  - unsigned build execution via `xcodebuild build`
  - plugin README
  - built-in plugin docs update
  - targeted plugin/tool tests

  ## Phase 1 scope

  Included:

  - read-only project inspection
  - scheme discovery
  - real local build support

  Excluded:

  - test execution
  - app launch / stop
  - logs / crash diagnostics
  - signing / notarization
  - GUI automation / computer-use
  - core plugin-system changes

  ## Behavior details

  - The plugin is bundled, standalone, and opt-in.
  - It exposes one toolset: `macos-dev`.
  - All tools are gated behind the same availability check.
  - The toolset is only exposed when Hermes is running on macOS and `xcodebuild` is available in `PATH`.
  - `macos_build_project` performs unsigned builds only by passing:
    - `CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO`
    - `CODE_SIGNING_REQUIRED=NO`
    - `CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY=`

  ## Why this shape

  Today, Hermes can already work with macOS/Xcode projects indirectly through generic terminal/file/process surfaces. The gap is first-class, typed support.

  This PR closes that gap in a bounded way by supporting the common flow:

  1. inspect project
  2. list schemes
  3. build selected scheme

  That makes the plugin independently mergeable and reviewer-visible without pulling in later-phase concerns.

  ## Testing

  Ran targeted tests:

  ```bash
  pytest -q -n0 tests/plugins/test_build_macos_apps_tools.py tests/plugins/test_build_macos_apps_plugin.py
  ```
  - 11 passed

author: bvis
body:
## Summary

Reported by @mschev in #151: a fresh install of `1.4.3` raised "Invalid handler specified" in HA's UI, with the underlying log showing only a bare `TypeError: Couldn't build proto file into descriptor pool: duplicate file name systems/ajax/api/ecosystem/v2/hubsvc/commonmodels/object_type.proto`. Root cause is two `_pb2.py` modules trying to register the same proto path in protobuf's global default pool — almost always a stale or backup copy of this integration sitting next to the live one in `custom_components/`. The current UX leaves the user staring at a cryptic UI message with no hint at the fix.

Refs #151.

## Change

Wrap the first proto-triggering import in `__init__.py` with a narrow `try/except TypeError`; if the exception text contains "duplicate file name", log an `ERROR` that names the most likely cause and the remediation, then re-raise the original exception so HA's existing broken-integration handling is unchanged.

```python
try:
    from custom_components.aegis_ajax.api.client import AjaxGrpcClient
except TypeError as exc:
    _log_proto_descriptor_collision(exc)
    raise
```

The classification + log message live in a tiny helper `_log_proto_descriptor_collision`, which is what the tests exercise.

## Safety

- Narrow exception class (`TypeError`) — no behavioural change for `ImportError`, attribute errors, syntax errors, anything else.
- Inner string match (`"duplicate file name"`) — no spurious logs when an unrelated `TypeError` bubbles up from the import.
- Bare `raise` preserves the original traceback and HA's "integration broken" state.

## Test plan

- [x] `test_logs_remediation_for_duplicate_file_name` — asserts the ERROR log fires with the right hint when the descriptor-pool TypeError lands.
- [x] `test_no_log_for_unrelated_typeerror` — asserts the guard is a no-op for unrelated TypeErrors.
- [x] Full suite: 1263 passed, 85.84% coverage.
- [x] `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `mypy`, `vulture` clean in a freshly rebuilt Docker image (no volume mount).
- [ ] Live verification by @mschev after `1.4.5` lands on HACS, OR by simulating a duplicate folder locally.

## Release target

`1.4.5` patch — diagnostic improvement, SemVer PATCH.

author: coderranger2
body: Closes #153 **Bug found** The "Total Balance" dashboard card periodically fails to aggregate global funds, dropping from the full sum to only reflecting the "Current Account" value. This results in an unstable UI display where the 3,240,000.00 from the "Savings Vault" sporadically vanishes during tab switching or component state refreshes. **Root cause** 1. The root cause was located within the fake text-glitch rendering useEffect block inside BankHouse.jsx. 2. The component's glitch state hook was initialized on mount using a static, hardcoded string. 3. When the interval timer finished its visual text manipulation, the trailing `setTimeout `reset callback explicitly evaluated to balance (the standalone Current Account balance variable) instead of factoring in the aggregated account values. 4. Consequently, any state refresh or tab-switch forced the local UI to snap back down to the singular account total, omitting the dynamic vault balance completely. **Fix applied** 1. Created a stable, reactive computed variable `totalFunds `directly aggregating `balance + savings`. 2. Cleaned up the initial `glitchText `state instantiation using a functional initializer that computes totalFunds right out of the gate instead of a static string fallback. 3. Updated the glitch useEffect timer cleanup callback to snap back to `totalFunds `instead of a singular balance dependency. 4. Rewired the `useEffect `hook dependency array to actively track changes to `totalFunds`, eliminating stale closures across tab switches. **Testing done** 1. Reproduced the bug before applying fix. 2. Confirmed fix resolves the issue (Total Balance remains rock solid at full amount during tab navigation). 3. Verified no existing features are broken. 4. Tested on: Chrome 147/1080 x 1920 desktop. ### Screenshots: After:

author: mkouba
body:
- the MCP spec defines the audience as an array of strings; current API only supports a single Role
- fixes #788

### Compatibility

This is a breaking change, because:

1. We change the canonical constructor of the `io.quarkiverse.mcp.server.Content.Annotations` record class; and that can break [record patterns](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/21/language/record-patterns.html) in JDK 21+, because record patterns deconstruct using the canonical constructor's component types.
2. We change the type of `io.quarkiverse.mcp.server.Resource.Annotations.audience()` from `Role` to `Role[]`.

The annotation change is source-compatible (recompile works). The record change is not fully source-compatible if anyone uses record patterns, regular construction via the convenience constructor is fine.

author: chitaoji
body:
### Motivation

- Provide a simple API to select data by integer positions using a reusable `idx` method.  
- Ensure that random sampling on joined/multi datasets uses the same random indices for each component to preserve alignment.  
- Reduce duplicated index-handling logic by reusing `idx` inside `sample` implementations.

### Description

- Added `Data.idx` in `src/dataplot/database.py` which returns a new dataset selecting items by integer positions via `self._create_data` and `self.data[index]`.  
- Updated `Data.sample` to delegate the "random" sampling case to `idx` by generating an index list and using `self.idx(index).data`.  
- Imported `SampleRule` in `src/dataplot/plottable.py` and implemented `PlottableDataSet.sample` to perform synchronized sampling across multiple datasets, raising a `ValueError` when component lengths differ.  
- `PlottableDataSet.sample` reuses `idx` and rebuilds per-component `PlottableData` objects with `_create_data` to preserve formatting and metadata.

### Testing

- Ran the unit tests in `tests/test_dataset_resample.py` which include existing resample checks and new tests: `test_idx_selects_single_dataset_positions`, `test_joined_idx_uses_same_indices_for_each_dataset`, `test_joined_random_sample_uses_same_indices_for_each_dataset`, and `test_joined_random_sample_requires_equal_lengths`.  
- All tests in `tests/test_dataset_resample.py` completed successfully.

author: oubay-s
body:
This pull request introduces major improvements to the data pipeline and analytics stack, including the addition of a new store (Sports Direct) in place of Walmart, significant enhancements to the Airflow DAG for orchestration and data validation, and the introduction of new dbt models for advanced price trend analytics. It also updates dependencies to support BigQuery and dbt, and improves documentation to reflect these changes.

**Pipeline and Orchestration Enhancements:**

* The Airflow DAG (`airflow/dags/price_intelligence_dag.py`) was refactored to add robust JSON validation, NiFi readiness checks, Bigtable stability waiting, BigQuery export, and dbt transformation steps. Scraper orchestration was updated to replace Walmart with Sports Direct, and `xvfb-run` is now used for the eBay scraper for headless browser support.
* The Docker image now installs `xvfb` to support headless scraping for Selenium-based scrapers.
* Required Python dependencies for BigQuery and dbt were added to `airflow/requirements.txt`.

**dbt Analytics Layer:**

* Introduced a new intermediate model (`dbt/models/intermediate/int_price_daily.sql` and schema) to aggregate daily product prices, and a new mart model (`dbt/models/mart/mart_price_trends.sql` and schema) for analytics-ready price trend analysis, including direction and percent change.

**Documentation Updates:**

* The `README.md` was updated throughout to reflect the replacement of Walmart with Sports Direct, changes in the scraping and orchestration workflow, and the new directory structure. 

---

**Pipeline and Orchestration**
- Refactored Airflow DAG to add robust data validation, NiFi readiness, Bigtable stability checks, BigQuery export, and dbt transformation; replaced Walmart with Sports Direct in scraping workflow; added `xvfb-run` for eBay scraper.
- Added `xvfb` to Dockerfile for headless browser support.
- Updated Airflow requirements to include `google-cloud-bigquery` and `dbt-bigquery`.

**dbt Analytics Layer**
- Added new dbt intermediate model `int_price_daily` for daily price aggregation and new mart model `mart_price_trends` for advanced trend analytics, with schema tests for data quality.

**Documentation**
- Updated `README.md` to reflect the new scraping target (Sports Direct), workflow changes, and directory structure.

author: copilot
body:
This change adds a lightweight, non-geographic transport map so users can see stops and connections as a network graph. Route search results are now reflected visually by highlighting the selected path on that graph.

- **Custom schematic map view (`TransportMapView`)**
  - Introduced a dedicated custom `View` to render the transport graph programmatically.
  - Draws:
    - stops as nodes (circles),
    - inter-stop connections as edges,
    - stop labels next to nodes.
  - Uses a deterministic layout derived from `TransportLine` + ordered `LineStop` data, with structure ready for future interaction extensions (zoom/pan/dynamic graph).

- **Results screen integration**
  - Embedded the map directly in `fragment_results.xml` above the route list.
  - Keeps existing route-list UX intact while adding a visual network context.

- **Route-to-map wiring**
  - Extended `ResultsViewModel` to expose graph datasets (`stops`, `lines`, `lineStops`) alongside route results.
  - Updated `ResultsFragment` to:
    - initialize the map once all graph inputs are available,
    - highlight the first found route by default,
    - update highlighted segments when a different route card is selected.

- **Optional interaction (bonus)**
  - Added stop tap callback support in `TransportMapView`.
  - Wired tap handling in `ResultsFragment` to surface the tapped stop name.

```java
// ResultsFragment: highlight selected route on map
private void onRouteClicked(RouteResult route) {
    binding.transportMapView.setHighlightedRoute(route);
}
```

author: erusseil
body:
Major changes in Rainbow. It now treats the Blackbody part as a parametric model, in the same way the flux evolution and temperature evolution were treated before.

A `spectral.py` file was added, where all SED models should be written. Hence, BB is now just a particular case of SED (with 0 parameters). A phenomenological UV-extincted BB model was also added. It requires fitting 2 parameters, but is able to better model light curves with strong blanketing effect in the u-band (or even more bands in case of high redshift sources).

By default, the SED is chosen to be BB, so previous implementation of Rainbow shouldn't be affected.

The `tests_rainbow.py` file now also loops on SED models.

body:
## Summary

Reduces commodity-content risk flagged by Google's [May 2026 AI optimization guide](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide) (specifically the "scaled content abuse" warning), without deleting any pages.

The audit script (`/home/ubuntu/audit/audit_commodity.py`) samples 15 pages per cluster and measures pairwise Jaccard similarity on 5-shingles. Before/after on the rebuilt `dist/`:

| Cluster | Pages | Before | After | Δ | Risk class |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| industries | 334 | 0.373 | **0.242** | **-35%** | LOW → **UNIQUE** |
| countries (locations/) | 78 | 0.395 | **0.225** | **-43%** | LOW → **UNIQUE** |
| cities (seo-services-*) | 282 | 0.393 | **0.276** | **-30%** | LOW → **UNIQUE** |
| blog | 48 | 0.614 | **0.423** | **-31%** | MEDIUM → **LOW** |
| services | 30 | 0.331 | 0.325 | -2% | LOW (unchanged) |
| ppc | 10 | 0.367 | 0.373 | +2% | LOW (unchanged) |
| tools | 165 | 0.481 | 0.485 | ~0% | LOW (unchanged) |
| free-seo-resources | 44 | 0.434 | 0.436 | ~0% | LOW (unchanged) |

The three target clusters (cities/industries/countries) now sit in **UNIQUE** territory (avg-jaccard < 0.30). The blog cluster dropped out of MEDIUM into LOW after stripping the identical "Key takeaways" / "Why this matters now" / "Framework" boilerplate.

### What changed

**1. `scripts/content_engine.py` (the content generator)**
- Pool expansions (~2-3x):
  - `CITY_INTRO_TEMPLATES`: 10 → 26
  - `CITY_INTRO_TEMPLATES_2`: 8 → 22
  - `CITY_SECTION_VARIANTS`: 10 → 28
  - `CITY_FAQ_VARIANTS`: 11 → 26
  - `INDUSTRY_INTRO_TEMPLATES`: 11 → 25
  - `INDUSTRY_INTRO_TEMPLATES_2`: 8 → 22
  - `INDUSTRY_SECTION_VARIANTS`: 9 → 25
  - `COUNTRY_INTRO_TEMPLATES`: 6 → 20
  - `COUNTRY_INTRO_TEMPLATES_2`: 5 → 17
  - `COUNTRY_SECTION_VARIANTS`: 7 → 20
  - `BLOG_INTRO_TEMPLATES`: 7 → 24 (and dropped the boilerplate "We publish on X only when…" variant)
  - `BLOG_INTRO_TEMPLATES_2`: 5 → 15
- New variant pools to replace the fixed templates:
  - `CITY_NEIGHBORHOODS_PARAGRAPHS` (12 variants)
  - `INDUSTRY_PLAYBOOK_VARIANTS` (8 ordered-list variants of 7 steps each)
  - `BLOG_KEY_TAKEAWAYS_VARIANTS` (10 variants of 5 bullets each)
  - `BLOG_WHY_NOW_VARIANTS` (10 variants)
  - `BLOG_FRAMEWORK_VARIANTS` (8 variants of 5 ordered steps each)
- New helpers `build_dynamic_for_blog_extras`, `build_dynamic_for_city_extras`, `build_dynamic_for_industry_extras`. All picks deterministic via `rng_for(slug)` (md5/sha-seeded), so the same slug always renders the same variants but different slugs get different copy.
- `build_unique_for_city`, `build_unique_for_industry`, `build_unique_for_blog` now return the new fields (`neighborhoods_paragraph`, `playbook_steps`, `key_takeaways`, `why_now`, `framework`).

**2. Templates**
- `templates/city_detail.html`: replaced the fixed 175-word "neighborhoods and landmarks" paragraph with `{{ unique.neighborhoods_paragraph }}`.
- `templates/industry_detail.html`: replaced the fixed 7-step "Playbook" list with `{{ unique.playbook_steps }}`.
- `templates/blog_post.html`: replaced the identical "Key takeaways" / "Why this matters now" / "Framework" blocks with their dynamic per-post equivalents.

**3. `usa` → `united-states` deduplication**
- Removed the duplicate `usa` country slug from `src-static/data/country-hubs.json` (same country as `united-states`, country_code US — they were 76% Jaccard-identical).
- Added 301 redirects in `scripts/generate.py` → `dist/_redirects`:
  - `/locations/usa.html → /locations/united-states.html  301`
  - `/usa → /united-states.html  301`
- Site now generates 2,339 URLs across 22 languages (was 2,340; -1 for the deduped USA).

### What did NOT change
- **No pages deleted.** No `noindex` added. The full URL inventory is preserved.
- No source data fabricated. All pool variants are about the same topics; only the wording rotates.
- `clone-display-joy` is not touched.

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human
- [ ] Spot-check 3-4 city pages across very different slugs (e.g. `/seo-services-dubai.html`, `/seo-services-mumbai.html`, `/seo-services-tokyo.html`, `/seo-services-buenos-aires.html`). The "neighborhoods and landmarks we serve" paragraph should read differently across them.

- [ ] Sitemap should no longer contain `/locations/usa.html` (verify in `dist/sitemap.xml`).

### Notes
- The audit script lives at `/home/ubuntu/audit/audit_commodity.py` (not committed — it's a session-local tool). Same script was used for the original audit report and for these before/after numbers, so the comparison is apples-to-apples.
- Cluster sampling uses `random.seed(42)` so the 15-page sample is stable across runs.
- Build time: ~60s for 2,339 URLs across 22 languages.
- This finishes the user-approved "Option C — full rewrite" + the two P0 fixes (`usa`→`united-states` redirect, strip blog boilerplate). It does NOT add first-hand client case studies — that requires the user's input.

author: gabrielziegler3
body:
## Summary

Combined fix for [KAD-7302](https://linear.app/kadoa/issue/KAD-7302) + [KAD-7303](https://linear.app/kadoa/issue/KAD-7303), addressing the [KAD-4039](https://linear.app/kadoa/issue/KAD-4039) MVP.

### Lazy bearer token (KAD-7303, functional)

- `KadoaClientConfig.bearerToken` and `BearerAuthOptions.bearerToken` now accept `string | (() => string | Promise<string>)`.
- The axios auth interceptor (now async) and `listTeams()` resolve the provider on each request — frontend integrations can return a fresh JWT from a refresh-aware store (e.g. Supabase) without re-constructing the client or calling `setBearerToken()` after every refresh.
- `setBearerToken()` accepts the same union.
- README documents the new lazy form and clarifies API key vs user bearer token semantics.

### Interceptor consolidation (KAD-7302, refactor)

- `UserService.getCurrentUser` and `EntityResolverService.fetchEntityFields` no longer hardcode `x-api-key` headers — auth interceptor is the single source of truth.
- Interceptor injects `x-api-key` in apiKey mode for direct axios calls that bypass generated clients.
- Existing bearer-mode behavior unchanged (interceptor was already stripping empty `x-api-key` and adding Authorization), so no behavior bug fix — just dead-code removal + convention enforcement.

## Frontend example

```ts
const client = new KadoaClient({
  bearerToken: async () => {
    const { data } = await supabase.auth.getSession();
    return data.session?.access_token ?? '';
  },
});
```

## Test plan

- [x] `bun test test/unit` — 97 unit tests pass (interceptor + services + lazy bearer)
- [x] `bun run typecheck` — clean
- [x] Biome autofix applied to touched files
- [ ] Reviewer: confirm no regressions in apiKey-mode flows

author: facorreiaa
body:
## Summary

Wires a debounced `/v1/auth/me` fetch into the existing `scenePhase .active` handler so server-side profile changes (email, userId) flow into `AppState` without requiring a full re-sign-in.

Closes [HER-238](https://linear.app/luminavault/issue/HER-238/).
Depends on HER-237 (#28, merged) for clean 401 handling.

## Changes

* **`AppState.lastMeFetchAt`** + **`Self.meRefreshInterval = 300`** — debounce window. Reset on `signOut()` so a fresh login restarts the cycle.
* **`AppState.refreshCurrentUserIfNeeded(authClient:now:)`**:
  * No-op when signed out or inside the debounce window
  * On success: update `currentUserId` / `currentEmail` (only mutates when changed to avoid Observable churn). Re-identifies in PostHog only when the email moved.
  * On `APIError.unauthorized`: silently exit — HER-237's interceptor owns the sign-out side effect
  * On network / 5xx: keep stale state silently
* **`LuminaVaultClientApp`** — `scenePhase .active` handler now spawns a second `Task` that calls `refreshCurrentUserIfNeeded` next to the existing Apple credential-state poll.

## Acceptance criteria

| | |
|---|---|
| Email changed server-side → reflected after debounce window | ✅ `testRefreshUpdatesEmailWhenServerValueChanged` |
| Foregrounding within 5 min of last fetch → no network | ✅ `testRefreshIsDebouncedWithinFiveMinutes` |
| Signed-out app does not call /v1/auth/me | ✅ `testRefreshSkipsWhenSignedOut` |
| Network failure preserves stale state silently | ✅ `testRefreshFailureKeepsStaleState` |
| 401 absorbed without crashing (interceptor owns sign-out) | ✅ `testRefreshOnUnauthorizedDoesNotSignOutDirectly` |

## Test plan

- [x] `xcodebuild test` — 146 unit tests pass (incl. 5 new HER-238 cases)
- [ ] Manual: foreground app after backgrounding > 5 min → server profile update reflected
- [ ] Manual: change email server-side then foreground twice within 5 min — only one /v1/auth/me hit

author: victorls3
body:
…create-pat)

Antes de PR-F la "reautenticacion con password" era SOLO client-side (modal frontend que hacia signInWithPassword). Un atacante con JWT robado podia invocar `delete-account` o `create-pat` directamente saltandose el modal. Ver SECURITY.md sec.6 PR-F.

**Componentes**:

1. **Migracion 0037** (`auth_recent_verifications`):
   - Tabla con (user_id, action_kind, verified_at) + indice compuesto.
   - RLS: SELECT solo propias; INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE solo service_role.
   - RPCs SECURITY DEFINER:
     - `has_recent_verification(action_kind, ttl, user_id?) -> bool`
     - `consume_recent_verification(...) -> bool` (variante one-shot que borra al usarse, evita replays). - `purge_old_verifications(older_than)` para cron de mantenimiento.
   - TTL default 5 min.

2. **Edge Function NUEVA `verify-password`**:
   - Body: `{ password, action_kind }`.
   - Valida password via `signInWithPassword` en cliente temporal (Supabase no expone validacion sin sesion); sesion temporal se cierra inmediatamente.
   - Whitelist server-side de action_kinds ('delete_account', 'create_pat_write' por ahora).
   - INSERT en auth_recent_verifications con service_role.
   - Rate limit 10/h/user (igual que login).

3. **`delete-account` Edge Function**:
   - Llama a `consume_recent_verification('delete_account')` antes de borrar el user. Sin marker fresco -> 403 reauth_required.

4. **`create-pat` Edge Function**:
   - Si scopes incluye 'write', llama a `consume_recent_verification('create_pat_write')`.
   - PATs solo-lectura NO necesitan re-auth (riesgo bajo, mismo scope que la sesion actual).

5. **Frontend**:
   - `lib/core/security/reauth_datasource.dart` + provider.
   - `lib/core/widgets/reauth_dialog.dart` reutilizable.
   - `AuthSupabaseDataSource.verifyPasswordForAction`: invoca `verify-password` Edge Function.
   - `AuthRepositoryImpl.deleteAccount`: cambia `signInWithPassword` por `verifyPasswordForAction`. UX del form intacta.
   - `CreateTokenDialog`: muestra `ReauthDialog.show()` si scopes incluye 'write', ANTES de invocar `create-pat`.

author: juliaregistrator
body:
- Registering package: QuantumLattices
- Repository: https://github.com/Quantum-Many-Body/QuantumLattices.jl
- Created by: @waltergu
- Version: v0.15.0
- Commit: ac21a9571d325a0dcb15683bf2988cd6c895d3b7
- Reviewed by: @waltergu
- Reference: https://github.com/Quantum-Many-Body/QuantumLattices.jl/issues/3#issuecomment-4477117651
- Description: Julia package for the construction of quantum lattice systems.
- Release notes:
<!-- BEGIN RELEASE NOTES -->
`````
## Breaking Changes

- **Storage backend: JLD2 → HDF5** — All data/cache files now use HDF5 format. Existing `.qld` files from v0.14.7 are incompatible and must be regenerated. The `JLD2` and `IndentWrappers` dependencies have been removed; `HDF5` and `SHA` have been added. ([Project.toml](Project.toml))

- **I/O function rename** — `qldload` → `qlload`; `qldsave` (top-level) → `qlsave`. The save function no longer accepts a `mode` argument. ([Frameworks.jl](src/Frameworks.jl))

- **`Boundary` and `plain` moved** from `DegreesOfFreedom` to `Frameworks` module — adjust `using`/`import` statements accordingly. ([Frameworks.jl](src/Frameworks.jl), [DegreesOfFreedom.jl](src/DegreesOfFreedom.jl))

- **`Generator` constructor signature change** — `OperatorGenerator(bonds, hilbert, terms, boundary, style; half)` → `OperatorGenerator(bonds, hilbert, terms, boundary; half)`. The `ExpansionStyle` parameter has been removed from `CategorizedGenerator`'s type parameters and constructor. ([Frameworks.jl](src/Frameworks.jl))

- **`show(io, ::AbstractLattice)`** now produces compact single-line output (e.g., `Lattice([0.0, 1.0, ...]; name="...", vectors=...)`) instead of delegating to the multi-line `text/plain` display. This fixes rendering in arrays and other composite structures. ([Spatials.jl](src/Spatials.jl))

- **`Parameters(::OperatorSet)` removed** — now falls back to the generic `LatticeModel` method returning an empty `NamedTuple`. ([Frameworks.jl](src/Frameworks.jl))

- **`update!` and `expand` removed from `QuantumOperator`** — these were no-ops returning `self`. ([QuantumOperators.jl](src/QuantumOperators.jl))

- **Widened `valtype` constraints** — `LinearFunction`, `Permutation`, and `UnitSubstitution` now accept `OperatorSet` instead of only `OperatorSum` for broader dispatch. ([QuantumOperators.jl](src/QuantumOperators.jl))

- **Dependency changes** — Removed: `IndentWrappers` (indentation wrapper), `JLD2` (JLD2 file format). Added: `HDF5` (HDF5 file format), `SHA` (SHA-512 fingerprinting). ([Project.toml](Project.toml))

## New Features

- **`LatticeModel` supertype** — New common abstract supertype for `Formula`, `Generator`, `Frontend`, `Assignment`, and `Algorithm`. Provides unified `valtype`, `scalartype`, `eltype`, `Parameters`, equality checks, and display infrastructure. ([Frameworks.jl](src/Frameworks.jl))

- **Unified data/cache I/O system** — New file naming and identification scheme at the `LatticeModel` level:
  - `config(model)` — SHA-512 fingerprint of structural configuration
  - `stamp(model)` — combined `"config[-parameters]"` string key for cache entries
  - `str(model)`, `dirname(model)`, `basename(model)`, `pathof(model)` — unified file naming
  - `qlsave(:data/:cache, model...)` — save models to `.qld`/`.qlc` files via HDF5
  - `qlload(file)` — load entries from HDF5 files
  - `qlclean(file; age, maxcount)` — evict stale cache entries by age or count; empty files are removed
  - Convenience shortcuts: `qldsave`, `qlcsave`, `qldclean`, `qlcclean`
  ([Frameworks.jl](src/Frameworks.jl))

- **`StaticGenerator`** — New `Generator` subtype wrapping a static `OperatorSet` without a parameter-update mechanism. Supports `empty`/`empty!`/`reset!` and `LinearTransformation` application. ([Frameworks.jl](src/Frameworks.jl))

- **`ParametricGenerator{V}`** — New abstract type between `Generator{V}` and `CategorizedGenerator`/`OperatorGenerator` for generators that carry parameters and support `update!`. ([Frameworks.jl](src/Frameworks.jl))

- **Factory constructors** — `LatticeModel(...)` dispatches to `Formula`, `StaticGenerator`, `CategorizedGenerator`, or `OperatorGenerator` based on argument types. `Generator(...)` dispatches to the generator subtypes only (not `Formula`). ([Frameworks.jl](src/Frameworks.jl))

- **Unified multi-line display system** in Toolkit.jl:
  - `showasleaf(::Type)` trait — controls whether a type renders inline or expands recursively
  - `showcontent(io, obj)` — unified entry point dispatching on `contenttoshow(obj)` result
  - `IndentWrapper` — inlined from the removed `IndentWrappers` package, with a critical bug fix: `write(str)` now properly splits on `\n` and re-emits via `write(chr)` instead of writing only spaces
  - `contenttoshow(obj)` — generic fallback using `fieldnames`; specialized for `Boundary`, `OperatorGenerator`, `Assignment`, and `Algorithm`
  - `@generated print` overrides on `IOContext` prevent indentation bypass through the `AbstractPipe` forwarding chain
  ([Toolkit.jl](src/Toolkit.jl))

## Enhancements

- **Display improvements** — The `:ndecimal` IO context now propagates through `IndentWrapper` and is respected by `Point`, `Bond`, `Coupling`, `Segment`, `CoordinatedIndex`, `AbstractLattice`, `OperatorPack`, and `OperatorSet` display methods. All `@printf`-based `show` methods have been migrated to `print` loops for consistent `IOContext` handling. ([Spatials.jl](src/Spatials.jl), [DegreesOfFreedom.jl](src/DegreesOfFreedom.jl), [QuantumOperators.jl](src/QuantumOperators.jl))

- **`OperatorPack.show`** — New generalized method replacing the removed `Operator.show`. All `OperatorPack` subtypes now share the same display logic with `ndecimal` support. ([QuantumOperators.jl](src/QuantumOperators.jl))

- **`seriestype` moved** from `Frameworks` to `QuantumLatticesPlotsExt` — plot series type determination belongs in the Plots extension, not in the core module. ([ext/QuantumLatticesPlotsExt.jl](ext/QuantumLatticesPlotsExt.jl))

- **`str` default `ndecimal` changed from 5 to 10** for `AbstractFloat` and `Complex`. New `str(::AbstractVector{<:Number}; ndecimal=10)` method added. ([Toolkit.jl](src/Toolkit.jl))

- **`Bond.show`** — unified the `Colon` and normal-kind branches into a single method. ([Spatials.jl](src/Spatials.jl))

- **`LinearTransformation` display** — added `show(io)` and `show(io, text/plain)` methods that use `showcontent` for multi-line hierarchical display. ([QuantumOperators.jl](src/QuantumOperators.jl))

- **`dlmsave` for `Assignment`** — new method for saving assignment data as delimited text files with consistent naming via the `LatticeModel` naming system. ([Frameworks.jl](src/Frameworks.jl))

## Bug Fixes

- **`issubordinate` now accepts empty vector arrays** — returns `isapprox(norm(coordinate), 0)` when no basis vectors are provided. ([Spatials.jl](src/Spatials.jl))
- **`qlload` hardened** — validates file existence, key existence, and entry data type before deserialization. ([Frameworks.jl](src/Frameworks.jl))
- **`IndentWrapper.write(str)` fix** — newline splitting now correctly re-emits `\n` via `write(chr)` instead of writing only spaces, fixing indentation loss in multi-line strings. ([Toolkit.jl](src/Toolkit.jl))
- **`IOContext` forwarding fix** — `@generated print` overrides on `IOContext` prevent `AbstractPipe` forwarding chain from bypassing indentation. ([Toolkit.jl](src/Toolkit.jl))
- **Julia < 1.12 compatibility** — version-guarded `unwrapcontext` override preserves `IndentWrapper` through `IOContext` construction on older Julia versions. `ioproperties` forwarding is gated to Julia ≥ 1.12. ([Toolkit.jl](src/Toolkit.jl))
`````

author: bd70
body:
CONTEXT (the truthful reset)

Ran the rebuilt Go auditor against 8 real contracts (Uniswap V2 router, Compound cETH, AAVE V3 Pool, Gnosis Safe singleton, USDC proxy, sDAI, Nomad bridge, the reported bridge address). Result: 3 rules out of 30 actually fire on real-world contracts. The rest are dormant because their `requires.facts_all` references facts the Go fact engine doesn't emit (e.g. `caller_owner_authorization_absent` needs flow-sensitive analysis the Go side doesn't do).

The 12 fork verifiers added across this session were technically wired but practically dead: they only run when the Go side produces a finding they're registered for, and findings don't exist for most of these rules on real contracts. The previous "73% fork-verified" claim was true on paper, false in practice.

This commit installs the architecture that makes those verifiers actually fire end-to-end on real contracts.

CHANGES

Go side — emit fingerprint signals the sidecars can gate on:
  - knownbc.go: detectERC4626Selectors scans for the 14 ERC-4626 core selectors (asset, totalAssets, deposit, withdraw, redeem, convertToShares, …); ≥4 of the 6 required → HasERC4626Pattern + tags [ERC4626, ERC4626_VAULT, erc4626_vault_trait, ERC4626_DEPOSIT_OR_MINT]. Bridge fields HasBridgePattern / BridgeSelectorsFound now surface in fingerprintMap as has_bridge_pattern / bridge_selectors (they were populated on the struct but never serialized — dead).
  - builder.go: fingerprintMap exposes has_bridge_pattern, bridge_selectors, has_erc4626_pattern, erc4626_selectors so downstream consumers can read them.
  - bridge.forged_cross_chain_proof.json: rewritten against the strict detector.v1 schema (the previous file failed every loader gate).

TypeScript side — generic sidecar architecture:
  - panel/src/server/sim/sidecar.ts NEW: SIDECARS registry + runAllSidecars runner. Each SidecarSpec describes (ruleId, severity, category, title builder, optional shouldRun gate, optional env flag). Idempotent (existing finding → skip), cached per (bytecode_hash, rule_id, engine, engine_version). Bypasses the Go gate entirely so verifiers fire on every audited contract that matches their shape.
  - worker.ts: deleted legacy runEconomicSidecar implementation (~190 LOC) in favor of runAllSidecars. runEconomicSidecar kept as a thin backwards-compat wrapper.
  - audit-service.ts: manual-audit path swaps runEconomicSidecar → runAllSidecars with parsed audit context for sidecar gates.

Sidecar registry — 6 entries shipping:
  - economic.unguarded_amm_action       (existing; runs on every contract)
  - defi.erc4626.withdraw.missing_caller_authorization (gate: ERC4626)
  - bridge.forged_cross_chain_proof     (gate: BRIDGE_PATTERN)
  - oracle.chainlink_staleness_unchecked
  - defi.swap.missing_slippage_or_deadline
  - token.unsafe_erc20_assumption

Rule alignment guard — auto-loads sidecar list:
  - check-rule-alignment.ts now parses panel/src/server/sim/sidecar.ts to discover registered sidecar ruleIds (was hard-coded). The list can't drift out of sync with the runtime registry.

Architecture guide — truthful 4-bucket coverage matrix:
  - 3 rules fire end-to-end via the Go side today.
  - 6 rules fire via sidecar (Go dormant; TS verifier runs on every audit, gated by fingerprint).
  - 11 rules have verifiers but neither side fires yet (inventory).
  - 10 rules are static-only by design (overflow, randomness, EIP-712).
  - Documents how to add a new gated sidecar (knownbc tag + SidecarSpec).

VERIFICATION

  - go build clean
  - tsc clean
  - check:rules clean (18 verifiers, 30 canonical rules, 6 sidecars, no orphans)
  - sDAI re-audit: 8 → 12 emitted tags including ERC4626 family (the gate the new sidecar uses)

author: ha-gdigital
body:
## Summary

Third slice of **Track B / Epic 5 (FR27)**. With this PR the adapter can take an `N8nNodeSpec` (built by 5.1b) and emit a complete n8n community-node source tree ready to be linted, compiled, and published.

## Runtime design

The generated n8n node declares the source MCP as an npm dependency and spawns it from `node_modules` at `execute()` time via the MCP SDK's `StdioClientTransport`. Credentials map 1:1 to the env vars the MCP itself reads. No `npx` / network needed at workflow time once the n8n node is installed (the MCP travels with it as a dep). Each operation = one MCP tool; properties are tagged with `displayOptions.show` so n8n only renders the right inputs per dropdown selection.

## Output layout

```
<outputDir>/
├── package.json        — n8n metadata + deps (source MCP + sdk)
├── tsconfig.json
├── README.md           — operations + credentials tables
├── index.ts            — re-exports
├── nodes/<Class>/
│   └── <Class>.node.ts — the INodeType impl
└── credentials/
    └── <Class>Api.credentials.ts
```

## What's in

- **6 Handlebars templates** under `templates/n8n-adapter/`.
- **`src/adapters/n8n-adapter/generate-n8n-node.ts`** — orchestrator. Caches compiled templates; registers a `json` Handlebars helper so strings with quotes survive into TS as JSON literals.
- **`N8nNodeSpec`** gained `sourceMcpPackageName`, `paramName`, `credentialClassName`, `credentialParamName` so templates have every identifier they need; `build-node-spec` populates them.
- **8 unit tests** pin the rendered output (file layout, package.json shape, node.ts class shape + Operation dropdown + OPERATION_PROPERTY_NAMES table, credentials secret flag, README contents, idempotent re-rendering with `clean=true`).

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm run typecheck` — clean.
- [x] `pnpm run test` — 437/437.

## What's next

- **5.1d** — LLM-refine pass for `displayName` / `description` polish (gated by env var so CI without API key still works).
- **5.1e** — golden-file integration test against EAD Factory's real `tools/list`.
- **5.2–5.4** — Track B Layer 1/2/3 gates (n8n linter, compile-and-load, per-operation smoke).
- **5.6** — `publish-n8n` composite action + workflow wiring.
- **5.7** — Make ROM artifact generator (FR33).

Promotes \`hexagonal_role\` and \`practices\` from optional-with-strict-mode-warning to **schema-required** in \`schemas/skill-frontmatter.v2.schema.json\`.

The \`registries-drift\` lesson (2026-05-17) said: hand-maintained inventory docs drift silently.
