author: hahwul
body:
## Summary

Scanning [`discourse/discourse`](https://github.com/discourse/discourse) surfaced ~150 phantom routes whose URLs contained raw Ruby string interpolation — `/#{base_c_route}/:message_id`, `/#{root_path}/trusted-session`, etc. The line-based Rails parser kept the `#{...}` placeholder intact even when the referenced variable was a simple string literal assigned right above the route block.

Add a per-file `local_string_vars` map in `parse_routes_file`. As we walk lines:
- `^name = "literal"$` assignments are captured into the map.
- Before route-matching the line, `#{name}` references are expanded against the map. Unresolved names survive unchanged — better than producing an empty `/` placeholder.

This handles the common DRY pattern Discourse's chat plugin uses ([`plugins/chat/config/routes.rb:115`](https://github.com/discourse/discourse/blob/main/plugins/chat/config/routes.rb#L115)):

```ruby
base_c_route = "/c/:channel_title/:channel_id"
get "#{base_c_route}/:message_id" => "chat#respond"
```

Block-iteration vars (`%w[users u].each do |root_path|`) still slip through — properly resolving them would require emitting each route N times, one per array element. Left for a follow-up.

Continues the [`project_analyzer_accuracy`](https://github.com/owasp-noir/noir/tree/main) precision sweep.

Fixture extension: `spec/functional_test/fixtures/ruby/rails_advanced/config/routes.rb` now declares a `base_c_route` var and uses it in two route registrations. The tester's expected-endpoints list adds the two resolved URLs and bumps the count.

Verified on discourse/discourse: phantom `#{...}` routes drop **153 → 150** (the 3 simple-var cases in the chat plugin's `base_c_route` / `base_channel_route` blocks resolve correctly). The remaining 150 are all `#{root_path}` block-iteration vars.

## Test plan

- [x] `crystal spec spec/functional_test/testers/ruby/rails_advanced_spec.cr` — 94 examples, 0 failures (new interpolation case asserts)
- [x] `crystal spec spec/functional_test/testers/ruby/` — 569 examples, 0 failures
- [x] `./bin/noir -b /path/to/discourse-discourse -f json` — confirmed `base_c_route` interpolations resolve

body:
Este PR introduz o envio automático de notificações por e-mail para o registro de horas, garantindo que o aluno seja devidamente informado sempre que iniciar ou finalizar um período de atividade no sistema.

**O que foi feito:**

* **Expansão do `EmailService**`
* Adicionados os métodos `sendHoursStartedEmail()` e `sendHoursStoppedEmail()`.
* Conteúdo dinâmico com formatação de data e hora no padrão brasileiro (DD/MM/YYYY HH:mm:ss, UTC-3).
* O e-mail de finalização inclui o cálculo exato da duração da atividade (HH:mm:ss).


* **Integração no `HoursService**`
* Disparo de e-mails acoplado aos métodos de `startHours()` e `stopHours()`.
* **Tratamento de Erros (Resiliência):** Se o serviço de e-mail falhar, a exceção é capturada e logada, garantindo que a gravação das horas no banco de dados não seja interrompida ou bloqueada.


* **Infraestrutura e Documentação**
* Reaproveitamento seguro da configuração existente do JavaMailSender e Mailtrap, mantendo a autenticação JWT intacta.



**Como testar:**

1. Autentique-se no sistema e dispare a requisição para iniciar a contagem de horas. Verifique a caixa de entrada (ex: Mailtrap) para confirmar o e-mail com o horário de início.
2. Dispare a requisição para parar a contagem. Verifique se o e-mail de encerramento chegou contendo os horários de início, fim e a duração total correta.
3. (Opcional) Force uma falha na credencial do Mailtrap e registre uma hora para garantir que o fluxo principal não quebra (gravação no banco deve ocorrer normalmente).

author: skipi
body:
## Summary

`sem-ai deploy create` previously sent a thin body (`{project_id, name, description, url, bookmark_parameter1?}`) — missing the required `unique_token` field and all the things that turn a deployment target into a real promotion gate: `object_rules`, `subject_rules`, `env_vars`, `files`. The `--branch` flag also misused `bookmark_parameter1` (a deployment-history filter) as if it were a real branch restriction.

This PR brings `sem-ai deploy create` to full parity with the Semaphore `POST /api/v1alpha/deployment_targets` API, and adds the missing `deploy update` command.

## What changed (`cmd/deploy.go`)

- **Always send `unique_token`** — current code never sent it; the API rejects with HTTP 400.
- **`object_rules` flags** — `--tag-regex`, `--tag-exact`, `--branch-regex`, `--branch-exact`, `--allow-all-branches`, `--allow-all-tags`, `--allow-prs`. Each emits one entry with the appropriate `match_mode` (`ALL` / `EXACT` / `REGEX`). If no rule for a type is provided, that type is implicitly blocked — which is the right safe default for tag-only release targets.
- **`subject_rules` flags** — `--subject-any`, `--subject-user` (UUID auto-detected vs `git_login` string), `--subject-role` (repeatable), `--subject-auto`.
- **Secrets bound to the target** — `--env-var NAME=VALUE` (repeatable) and `--file PATH=LOCAL_SOURCE` (repeatable; reads the local file and base64-encodes the content).
- **Explicit bookmark params** — `--bookmark1/2/3`. The misleading `--branch` flag is dropped; old callers must move to `--branch-exact` (real restriction) or `--bookmark1` (history filter), depending on intent.
- **New `sem-ai deploy update <target-id>`** — PATCHes `/deployment_targets/:id` with the same flag surface as `create`. Only sent fields change; the rest is preserved server-side. `--name` renames.

## Skill update (`.agents/skills/deploy/SKILL.md`)

Updated to teach agents the new `create` / `update` surface — flag tables for object/subject rules, the implicit-block-when-no-rule semantics, the `--subject-auto` pattern for release targets, target-bound secrets vs project secrets, and the `deployment_target:` YAML reference for promotion gating.

author: ajay-blitzy
body:
## Summary

  Hides Component entities from the catalog whose linked GitHub repo has no
  pull-request history. The filter is silent and always-on — no new UI control.

  - **Backend** (`BlitzyProjectHistoryProcessor`): post-processes Component
    entities, calls `octokit pulls.list` (state=all, per_page=1) for the
    `github.com/project-slug`, and stamps `blitzy.io/has-project-history:
    'true' | 'false'`. Results cached 6h keyed by slug. On GitHub errors
    (rate limits, 5xx, network) the existing annotation is preserved so a
    transient failure can't flip entities.
  - **Frontend** (`EntityHasProjectHistoryFilter` + headless picker): hides
    entities annotated `'false'`. Missing annotation passes through so the
    catalog isn't blank during the backfill window before the processor has
    stamped every entity.
  - Also a small tag tweak on `catalog-blitzy-sandbox.yaml` (adds `design`,
    `frontend`; alphabetizes the list).

  ## Behavior notes

  - The catalog filter API is equality-based, so we can't push "annotation
    != 'false'" to the server. Filtering happens client-side after fetch,
    which means a page may render fewer-than-page-size rows until every
    entity is stamped. This converges within one processor cycle.
  - Malformed or missing `github.com/project-slug` → stamped `'false'`.

  ## Test plan

  - [ ] Unit tests pass: `EntityHasProjectHistoryFilter` (4 cases: true /
        false / missing / no-op) and `BlitzyProjectHistoryProcessor`
  - [ ] Load the catalog page in dev — Components with PR history are
        visible; Components from empty repos disappear after the processor
        runs
  - [ ] Restart backend with a populated cache — no GitHub calls made for
        slugs within the 6h TTL
  - [ ] Simulate a GitHub 5xx (or unplug network) — entities keep their
        prior annotation; no entities flip to `'false'`

body:
## Summary
Expanded the onboarding window to include a post-permission setup flow where users select their audio output device and choose a preset for their headphones before closing the window. This replaces the minimal "success" state with a more comprehensive kickstart experience.

## Key Changes

- **Renamed success mode to setup**: Changed `.success` case to `.setup` to better reflect the new interactive nature of this state
- **Added setup flow UI**: Implemented three-step setup interface:
  - Output device picker with device type detection and icons
  - Preset selector with AutoEq catalog integration and fallback search
  - "What's next" section explaining menu bar icon, A/B compare, and editor features
- **Integrated preset catalog**: Added `PresetCatalog` and `DevicePresetMemory` dependencies to enable preset browsing and application during onboarding
- **Implemented device selection**: Users can now switch between output devices, with the engine automatically restarting on the selected device
- **Added preset application logic**: Integrated preset suggestion matching, catalog search filtering, and popular headphone quick-picks (HD 600, DT 990, etc.)
- **Enhanced window layout**: Wrapped content in `ScrollView` and adjusted frame sizing (540px width, 720px max height for setup mode vs 480px for permission modes)
- **Improved onAppear logic**: Updated permission state detection to properly route authorized state to setup mode and start the engine immediately
- **Added helper subviews**: Created `OutputRow`, `PresetRow`, and `WhatsNextRow` components for the setup interface
- **Updated documentation**: Revised class-level comments to describe all three modes and their purposes

## Implementation Details

- The setup mode freezes the selected output at entry time to prevent UI thrashing during preset application
- Preset application is async and respects device selection changes (cancels if user switches outputs mid-fetch)
- Popular headphone queries use canonical AutoEq naming conventions for reliable matching
- Device icons are determined via heuristic name matching (AirPods, Bluetooth, USB DAC, built-in, etc.)
- The engine starts immediately when entering setup mode so users hear EQ applied to their chosen output in real-time

author: bobr2610
body:
This pull request introduces a new Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) system, strengthens authentication and password handling, and improves the reliability and security of the account storage mechanism. It also enhances the unit tests for authentication and encoding utilities. The most important changes are summarized below.

### RBAC System

* Added a new RBAC implementation: introduced `Permission` enum, `AccessRule` struct, and `RBACManager` class to manage user permissions at the database and table level, with JSON serialization support. (`apps/server/include/qdb/server/rbac.h`, `apps/server/src/rbac.cpp`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-c92e5863ff03a1ea6c8f4f0abfc36df4357ee3335864c602bee78e7487644599R1-R63) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-76512b828f88a299ac2848fd71ba98bee276efe69d81acc151cc82da29d0f589R1-R117)

### Account Security & Authentication

* Improved password hashing: switched to PBKDF2 with 600,000 iterations for secure password storage, replacing the previous custom iterative SHA-256 approach. (`apps/server/src/security.cpp`)
* Hardened authentication: replaced direct string comparison with `CRYPTO_memcmp` for constant-time password hash comparison to prevent timing attacks. (`apps/server/src/security.cpp`)
* Improved salt generation: made salt generation more robust by checking return values and increased default salt size to 32 bytes. (`apps/server/include/qdb/server/security.h`, `apps/server/src/security.cpp`, `apps/server/tests/auth_test.cpp`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-df1be7db73e954087200f52d6b97fa5fffac1c094b910d00f3c4acaf5dbcf040L29-R44) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-6cf95324b4284bdf9f05b881da34aa82db35105f50cf4b4b7512a1cd2d5dcadbL98-R142) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-173e5bb22feb1578fdde556cdc1d39a2ba97e6870dea56edc0617099d410a876L60-R90)

### AccountStore & JWT Handling

* Made `AccountStore` and `JwtHandler` methods `const` where appropriate and improved error handling and atomicity in file save/load operations (using temp files and permissions). (`apps/server/include/qdb/server/security.h`, `apps/server/src/security.cpp`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-df1be7db73e954087200f52d6b97fa5fffac1c094b910d00f3c4acaf5dbcf040L29-R44) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-df1be7db73e954087200f52d6b97fa5fffac1c094b910d00f3c4acaf5dbcf040L51-R54) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-6cf95324b4284bdf9f05b881da34aa82db35105f50cf4b4b7512a1cd2d5dcadbL30-R121)
* Improved JWT handling: enforced correct JWT type, checked for expiration, and handled empty secret keys gracefully. (`apps/server/src/security.cpp`)

### Base64 & Utility Improvements

* Improved Base64 URL encoding/decoding: ensured no padding or unsafe characters, and added stricter decoding checks. (`apps/server/src/security.cpp`, `apps/server/tests/auth_test.cpp`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-173e5bb22feb1578fdde556cdc1d39a2ba97e6870dea56edc0617099d410a876L60-R90) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-6cf95324b4284bdf9f05b881da34aa82db35105f50cf4b4b7512a1cd2d5dcadbL160-R237)

### Test Enhancements

* Enhanced and expanded authentication tests: added deterministic hashing, salt variation, expired JWT, and improved test isolation by using temp files for account storage. (`apps/server/tests/auth_test.cpp`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-173e5bb22feb1578fdde556cdc1d39a2ba97e6870dea56edc0617099d410a876R5-R22) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-173e5bb22feb1578fdde556cdc1d39a2ba97e6870dea56edc0617099d410a876R137-R176) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-173e5bb22feb1578fdde556cdc1d39a2ba97e6870dea56edc0617099d410a876L147-R192)

These changes collectively strengthen the security model, add flexible RBAC, and improve test coverage and reliability.

author: edward-rosado
body:
## Summary

Proposes a **fully autonomous** 7-workstream, 3-wave (plus Wave 4 hand-off) execution plan for the next round of simplification — runs end-to-end with **no human approval gates** from kickoff through codex hand-off.

- **Wave 1 (4 parallel WS):** MidiSender Protocol, PadRuntime Protocol, close shell.dispatch 8-arm tail, PassiveReportFormatter
- **Wave 2 (2 parallel WS, gated on Wave 1):** Device Protocol + registry, Generic Elektron SysEx envelope
- **Wave 3 (1 WS, gated):** CLI command registry
- **Wave 4 (autonomous final phase):** Learning extraction → saves a **complete in-repo collaborator handoff package** (skills, rules, templates, run report, architecture-diff doc, PR #21 rebase guide, autonomous-run playbook for future use); PR #21 hand-off issue auto-generated with link to the in-repo guide

## What lands in the repo (Wave 4)

The final learning PR contains everything a future collaborator (human or agent) needs out of the box — **no dependency on user-home `.claude/` or session memory**:

| Artifact | Path | For |
|---|---|---|
| Reusable agent skills | `.claude/skills/learned/<name>/SKILL.md` | Future agent runs |
| Project rules | `.claude/rules/{parity-fixture-discipline,coverage-gate-100pct,cascade-merge-pattern}.md` | Agents + humans |
| Phase templates | `.claude/templates/workstream/{planner,tdd,coverage,cascade,docs}-*.{md,ps1}` | Future autonomous runs |
| Run report | `docs/SIMPLIFICATION_RUN_REPORT.md` | Humans |
| Run log (preserved) | `docs/SIMPLIFICATION_RUN_LOG.md` | Audit / debug |
| Architecture diff | `docs/ARCHITECTURE_BEFORE_AFTER.md` | Onboarding |
| Autonomous playbook | `docs/AUTONOMOUS_RUN_PLAYBOOK.md` | Kickoff doc for future runs |
| Codex package | `docs/PR21_REBASE_GUIDE.md` + `docs/PR21_MODULE_MAPPING.md` | PR #21 reviewer |
| State schema | `docs/SIMPLIFICATION_STATE.schema.json` | Tooling |
| Forward-ported skills | `.claude/skills/learned/{python_tooling_pitfalls,github-token-no-workflow-trigger}/SKILL.md` | Repo-scoped (not user-home) |

A "fresh-clone test" validates Wave 4 by simulating a new contributor and verifying they can answer 5 onboarding questions using only in-repo files. Any gap triggers `doc-updater` and re-validates.

## Gated requirements (apply to every WS — no exceptions)

| Gate | Threshold |
|---|---|
| **Branch coverage on touched files** | **100%** via `pytest --cov-branch --cov-fail-under=100` |
| **V1.34 parity** | All 505 JSON fixtures byte-identical |
| **Lint / format / type** | `ruff` + `black` + `isort` + `pyright --strict` clean |

A WS does not reach `pr_open` until all three gates pass locally. CI failures auto-revert and re-enter the implementation phase.

## Why autonomous

The cleanup batch (PRs #22–#28) merged 6 PRs in ~3 hours using a monitor-driven cascade pattern. This plan formalizes that pattern: persistent state on disk (`SIMPLIFICATION_STATE.json` + `SIMPLIFICATION_RUN_LOG.md`), event-driven phase fanout, auto-rebase on cascade conflicts, deterministic decision rules, hard 72h time budget. Human investment: kickoff message + PR #29 merge. That's it.

## How (cooperative path)

1. Land the 7 PRs on base autonomously.
2. Learning phase extracts patterns → saves to `.claude/skills/learned/`, `.claude/rules/`, `docs/SIMPLIFICATION_RUN_REPORT.md`.
3. Auto-generate codex hand-off issue. PR #21 shrinks from ~30k LOC to ~5–8k.

## Per-WS pipeline (11 phases)

```
plan → tdd → implement → coverage_gate (100% or loop) → reviewing (×3 parallel) → docs → pr_open → ci → merge
                                                                                    ↑
                                                                          doc-updater is mandatory,
                                                                          not optional
```

## Execution model

Each workstream is an **isolated git worktree** with a dedicated agent crew using the `everything-claude-code` plugin. Wave 1 alone runs ~16 specialist agents in flight simultaneously at the review peak (4 worktrees × 4 reviewers each).

## Launch

After PR #29 merges:

```
/loop run docs/SIMPLIFICATION_PLAN.md
```

Equivalent autonomous form:

```
CronCreate: every 1h, prompt = "<<autonomous-loop>>"
```

Hard stop: send `STOP`, call `CronDelete`, or close PR #29.

## Constraints (non-negotiable)

- V1.34 byte-level behavior unchanged.
- The 11 parity-API symbols in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` section 8 untouched.
- All 505 JSON parity fixtures byte-identical.

## Out of scope

- Collapsing the four pad engines (Ambitious option declined).
- Pyright as a CI gate (separate workstream once Protocols land).

## Test plan

This PR adds documentation only — no code changes.

- [x] `pytest` 2,000+ tests still green (unchanged base)
- [x] `ruff` / `black` / `isort` clean
- [ ] Plan reviewed and merged before the autonomous orchestrator is kicked off
- [ ] Each workstream PR runs the full 3-gate pipeline (100% branch coverage + parity + lint) before opening

See `docs/SIMPLIFICATION_PLAN.md` for the full plan (439 lines).

author: lovesegfault
body:
Self-hosted runners (notably actions-runner-controller containers) don't ship `node` on `PATH` — the GHA runner bundles its own under `externals/node20/` and invokes node20 actions with that binary directly, without adding it to `PATH`.

The auth-token script is currently returned as `node <file>`, so when `niks3-hook serve` (or storescan's `niks3 push`) execs it, the lookup fails:

```
error="... resolving auth token: running auth token script: exec: \"node\": executable file not found in $PATH"
```

`process.execPath` is the absolute path to the node binary running this action, so baking it into the script command makes the exec PATH-independent. Works on GitHub-hosted (where it resolves to the same node that's on PATH anyway) and self-hosted alike.

author: neilotoole
body:
## Summary

Closes [#640](https://github.com/neilotoole/sq/issues/640). Tightens
the LIKE-family argument parsers so that single-arg function wrappers
around column / literal arguments are rejected with a clear error
rather than silently stripped to the inner leaf.

**Pre-fix surprise:**

```text
.actor | where(like(.first_name, max(.last_name)))
# rendered as `"first_name" LIKE "last_name"` — max(...) silently
# disappeared because ast.NodeUnwrap walked through the FuncNode.
```

**Post-fix:** the same input errors with
`like() second argument must be a string literal or column selector`.
Rejections now also name the offending node, so the user can see what
tripped the parser (e.g. `got *ast.FuncNode: max(.last_name)`).

Same fix applies on every argument of every like-family function:
`contains` / `startswith` / `endswith` and their `i`-variants, plus
`like` / `ilike`, both LHS and RHS — eight functions, two arguments
each, all sharing the tightened parsers via `parseLikeColArg`,
`ParseLikeArgs`, and `ParseLikePatternArgs`.

## Verify it yourself

Against any sakila source (the examples use `@sakila`):

**Valid args still work:**

```shell
sq '@sakila.actor | where(startswith(.last_name, "GU")) | .first_name, .last_name'
sq '@sakila.actor | where(ilike(.first_name, "pen%")) | .first_name'
# like/ilike accept a COLUMN as the pattern — runs, no error:
sq '@sakila.actor | where(like(.first_name, .last_name)) | .first_name, .last_name'
```

**The #640 fix — function-wrapped args are now rejected** (each was
silently stripped pre-fix):

```shell
sq '@sakila.actor | where(like(.first_name, max(.last_name)))'
# sq: like() second argument must be a string literal or column selector:
#     expected selector node type, but got *ast.FuncNode: max(.last_name)

sq '@sakila.actor | where(contains(max(.first_name), "X"))'
# sq: contains() first argument must be a column selector: ... got *ast.FuncNode: max(.first_name)

# Canonical silent-strip case: a function around a LITERAL. Pre-#640 this
# rendered as contains(.first_name, "X") and matched rows; now it errors:
sq '@sakila.actor | where(contains(.first_name, _strftime("X")))'
# sq: contains() second argument must be a string literal, got *ast.FuncNode: _strftime("X")
```

**Error detail and edge cases:**

```shell
# contains-family errors name the offending node (parity with like/ilike):
sq '@sakila.actor | where(contains(.first_name, .last_name))'
# sq: contains() second argument must be a string literal, got *ast.ColSelectorNode: .last_name

# A negative numeric literal lexes as one signed-number token, rejected as unquoted:
sq '@sakila.actor | where(like(.first_name, -42))'
# sq: like() second argument must be a quoted string literal or column selector
```

The cleanest contrast: `like(.first_name, .last_name)` **runs**, but
`like(.first_name, max(.last_name))` **errors** — that one-level-deeper
wrap is exactly what used to be silently stripped.

## Changes

- **`libsq/ast/render/function_like.go`**: new local helper
  `unwrapExpr` peels only `*ast.ExprNode` wrappers (stops at any
  non-ExprNode or at any ExprNode with `!= 1` child). Replaces
  `ast.NodeUnwrap[ast.Node]` / `ast.NodeUnwrap[*ast.LiteralNode]`
  in:
  - `parseLikeColArg` (shared LHS for all 8 functions)
  - `ParseLikeArgs` RHS (contains family)
  - `ParseLikePatternArgs` RHS (`like`/`ilike`)

  User-meaningful nodes like `*ast.FuncNode` are preserved so
  `renderSelectorNode` / the literal type assertion can reject them
  with the existing user-facing error framing, wrapped via
  `errz.Wrapf` to preserve the underlying diagnostic
  (`expected selector node type, but got *ast.FuncNode: max(.x)`).

  `ParseLikeArgs` (contains family) now appends the offending node's
  type and text to its rejection (`got %T: %s`), matching the detail
  `ParseLikePatternArgs` already surfaces for `like`/`ilike`.

  Only single-arg function wrappers were ever silently stripped. Other
  non-string arguments were always rejected: a bare numeric literal
  such as `-42` lexes as a single signed-number token
  (`NUMBER: '-'? INTF`) and is rejected via the unquoted-literal path,
  and a binary expression (e.g. `.a == .b`) stops at the multi-child
  `ExprNode`.

- **`libsq/query_string_test.go`**: 9 new sub-tests pin the rejection
  across the dispatch matrix, plus one enriched assertion:
  - `contains/function-wrapped-lhs-rejected` — `contains(max(.col), "X")`.
    Covers the shared `parseLikeColArg` LHS path for all 8 functions.
  - `contains/numeric-rhs-rejected` — `contains(.col, 42)`. Pins the
    contains-family *unquoted-literal* branch (`wasQuoted == false`),
    distinct from the non-literal branch; mirrors
    `like/numeric-rhs-rejected`.
  - `contains/function-wrapped-rhs-rejected` — `contains(.col, max(.last_name))`.
    Selector-inner RHS; same user-visible error pre/post-fix, but the
    new dispatch path is correct.
  - `contains/function-wrapped-literal-rhs-rejected` — `contains(.col, _strftime("X"))`.
    The **canonical silent-strip case**: pre-fix would have rendered as
    `... LIKE '%X%' ESCAPE '|'`. Uses SLQ's `PROPRIETARY_FUNC_NAME`
    (admitted by the grammar without arity gating) for a real
    1-arg-function-over-literal input.
  - `like/function-wrapped-rhs-rejected` + `ilike/function-wrapped-rhs-rejected`
    — selector-inner mirrors for the like/ilike family RHS.
  - `like/function-wrapped-literal-rhs-rejected` + `ilike/function-wrapped-literal-rhs-rejected`
    — literal-inner mirrors for the like/ilike family RHS.
  - `like/negative-numeric-rhs-rejected` — `like(.col, -42)`. Pins that
    `-42` is one signed-number literal (not a unary-operator
    expression), rejected via the unquoted-literal path.
  - `contains/non-literal-pattern` assertion enriched to pin the
    offending-node context (`got *ast.ColSelectorNode`).

- **`CHANGELOG.md`**: entry under `Unreleased > Changed`. User-facing
  language; describes the behavior change, names the per-family error
  messages, and accurately characterizes the `-42` / operator scope.

## Behavioral impact

Visible to users: a like-family argument wrapped in a single-arg
SLQ function (e.g. `max(.col)`, `_strftime("X")`) now errors instead
of being silently stripped to its inner leaf. Rejection messages now
include the offending node's type and text. No existing literal-only
or selector-only inputs change behavior. All 8 like-family test
functions pass against all configured drivers.

## Out of scope / follow-ups

- **RHS SQL-expression support** (e.g. `like(.col, upper(.other))`
  with the wrapper *honored* rather than rejected). This is the
  [#628](https://github.com/neilotoole/sq/issues/628) open-question-2
  future-feature direction; it needs per-driver expression-rendering
  machinery and warrants its own issue/PR.
- **`renderSelectorNode` nil-input hardening** (return an error rather
  than risk a panic on `node.Text()`). The deep review confirmed the
  LIKE-family path is nil-safe — callers guarantee a non-nil node and
  `baseNode.Text()` is nil-safe — so this is a low-priority defensive
  cleanup that matters only for other callers; a dedicated PR if
  pursued.

(The earlier "strip internal Go type names from error messages"
follow-up is intentionally **not** pursued: the deep review settled on
surfacing `got <type>: <text>` consistently across the LIKE family
because it makes rejections actionable.)

## Test plan

- [x] `make lint` clean (0 issues).
- [x] All 8 like-family tests
  (`TestQuery_string_{contains,startswith,endswith,icontains,istartswith,iendswith,like,ilike}`)
  pass against all configured drivers (sqlite3, postgres, mysql,
  sqlserver, clickhouse, oracle).
- [x] 9 new rejection sub-tests + 1 enriched assertion pass per driver.
- [x] Full CI matrix green (`Analyze (go)`, `lint`, `test-nix`
  macOS/Ubuntu, `test-windows`).
- [x] Manually verified the examples above against a sakila SQLite
  source with the branch binary.

This PR went through several iter

body:
## Summary
- Strip `$schema` and `$id` from every `components.schemas[K]` body inside `stripMarkers`. Zod v4's bulk `toJSONSchema` leaks these onto every emitted body, and the relative-URI-fragment `$id` (e.g. `#/components/schemas/SortDirection`) makes Swagger UI's strict ref resolver chase a literal `/components/schemas/<Id>` path from the leaf and fail every named-component lookup. The fields are redundant in OpenAPI — the schema's identity comes from its `components.schemas` key.
- Revert the `description`-to-parameter-object copy from PR #54. Description stays on the parameter `schema` only (where Zod emits it). The duplication was visible noise without improving Swagger-UI rendering.
- New `openapi-conformance.spec.ts` case reproduces the cvs-kalo / bff-zod-4 regression (named `SortDirection` enum referenced by a `@Query() ZodDto` property), runs `SwaggerParser.validate`, and asserts no `$id`/`$schema` on the named component and `description` only on the parameter schema.

## Context
PR #54 squashed before this commit landed, so the `$id`/`$schema` strip never reached `main`. This branch carries that one missing commit.

Closes #55

- [x] `npm run typecheck` clean

Report grows from 9 to 28 pages.

body:
**INSTRUMENTATION ONLY — no behavior change.** Probes the firstByte-after-arbitration wire-SYN case to validate Codex's recommended drain fix before shipping it in round 9.

## Why

After round 7 closed Attack 3 (inter-write empty-queue leak), residual ~5% per-active-frame echo_mismatch comes from Attack 1 (grant→first-byte window). Codex independent analysis recommended a local drain fix in `sendRawWithEcho`. Before shipping, instrument to measure:

- How frequently does the condition fire?
- Post-drain distribution: real echo / foreign initiator / other / exhausted
- Histogram of SYN burst sizes

## What

Probe inserted in `sendRawWithEcho` at the r3 guard (line 1066). When the firstByte-after-arbitration condition matches AND echo is wire SYN, drain up to 8 bytes, classify each, increment counters. **Falls through to existing ErrBusCollision emit unchanged.** The drained bytes are consumed but `sendWithRetries` re-arbitrates anyway.

6 new counters + 6 accessors + 6 unit tests.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests pass
- [ ] CI green
- [ ] 30-min live deploy: gateway counter exposure
- [ ] Analyze histogram → decide round-9 drain cap

body:
## Problem

Non-technical users often struggle to notice and understand JSON syntax errors in the request body editor. Common mistakes like leading zeros in numbers (`"customerNumber": 0000`) produce cryptic error messages ("Unexpected number in JSON") that are only visible as subtle red squiggly underlines.

## Changes

### 1. Improved error messages (json-lint-utils.js)
New utility that detects common JSON mistakes and provides clear, actionable messages:

| Mistake | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Leading zeros `0000` | "Unexpected number in JSON at position 11" | "Invalid number "0000": JSON does not allow leading zeros in numbers. Use 0 instead." |
| Trailing commas `{"a": 1,}` | "Unexpected token" | "Trailing comma: The last item must not have a comma after it." |
| Unquoted keys `{name: "x"}` | "Unexpected string" | "Unquoted key "name": JSON requires property names in double quotes." |
| Single quotes `{'key': 1}` | "Unexpected token" | "Wrong quote style: JSON uses double quotes, not single quotes." |

### 2. Auto-show tooltip (lint-errors.js)
- When the user stops typing (1.2s debounce), the first visible lint error tooltip is shown automatically
- No need to hover over line numbers to discover errors
- Tooltip auto-hides after 8 seconds
- If no error is in view, editor scrolls to the first error

## Files changed
- `packages/bruno-app/src/utils/codemirror/json-lint-utils.js` (new)
- `packages/bruno-app/src/components/CodeEditor/index.js`
- `packages/bruno-app/src/utils/codemirror/lint-errors.js`

author: railway-app[bot]
body:
## Problem

The Dockerfile contained a fallback `RUN test -f ... || echo '...' > index.html` in the nginx stage that silently swallowed a failed or empty `COPY --from=build`. When the build stage produced no output (or the copy failed), the fallback wrote the "Build Failed" error page into the image and the container started successfully — hiding the real problem and making it look like a runtime issue rather than a build issue.

## Solution

Removed the misleading fallback and replaced it with two explicit guard steps: a `RUN ls -la /app/dist && test -f /app/dist/index.html` at the end of the build stage that fails the Docker build immediately if Vite didn't produce output, and a `RUN ls -la /usr/share/nginx/html && test -f /usr/share/nginx/html/index.html` in the nginx stage that confirms the `COPY --from=build` actually landed the files. Both steps print the directory listing to the build log, making any future failure trivially diagnosable.

### Changes
- **Modified** `frontend/Dockerfile`

author: prabhat-at
body:
## Summary

Drafted as the next cache lever after PR α delivered ₹4.26 cr/month savings. Per industry research (Tensormesh on MemGPT), our 41.2% cache_read ratio is the structural ceiling of naive prefix caching on MemGPT-style architectures. The next ~15-25pp of hit rate is gated by the **multi-step rebuild cascade**.

**Gated to test user 92744418 only.** Validation period 24-48h before graduation.

## Evidence — the cascade in PR #66 logs

\`\`\`
agent 21196fa2  at 18:25:21  cache_read=23,724   <- step 1 of user turn
agent 21196fa2  at 18:25:26  cache_read=2,114    <- step 2 same turn 5s later
                              cache_creation=44,973  <- rewrites the just-cached prefix
\`\`\`

Cause: agent calls \`core_memory_append\` → next step's \`_rebuild_memory_async\` mutates the system prompt → cache invalidates → next step writes the same content again. Happens 1.7x per user turn on average (2.7 step avg agent loop).

## What this PR does

Threads \`step_index: int\` through \`_build_and_request_from_llm\` (and streaming variant) into \`_create_llm_request_data_async\`. When \`step_index > 0\` **AND** \`at_user_id == \"92744418\"\`, skip \`_rebuild_memory_async\`. Reuses the system prompt from step 0 of the same user turn.

Emits \`[REBUILD_SKIPPED_MID_TURN]\` log when the skip fires, so we can verify in production.

## Why this is behaviour-equivalent

- Memory state still persists to DB (unaffected — \`core_memory_append\` runs normally)
- The LLM that just called \`core_memory_append\` already sees the appended content in its own assistant message's \`tool_use\` content
- The system prompt block being deferred carries the SAME memory it had at step 0 — only the chars_current / memory_edit_timestamp values would change
- The next user turn (\`_step()\` re-entry) gets a fully fresh rebuild

## Diff scope

- \`letta/agents/letta_agent.py\` only
- 3 call sites pass \`step_index=i\` (loop iteration)
- 3 function signatures get \`step_index: int = 0\` keyword
- 1 conditional in \`_create_llm_request_data_async\` skips rebuild + logs

No other files touched.

## Test plan

- [ ] Merge + Jenkins deploy
- [ ] T+15 min: smoke test — system still functions for non-test users (gate ensures default behaviour preserved)
- [ ] Test user 92744418: run a 20-30 turn conversation
- [ ] Verify quality unchanged (read transcript)
- [ ] grep \`[REBUILD_SKIPPED_MID_TURN]\` — confirm it fires on intermediate steps
- [ ] grep \`[CACHE_OBS_USAGE]\` for test user — confirm cache_read does NOT collapse to ~2114 between consecutive calls in the same agent
- [ ] After 24-48h clean run: graduate via 1-line gate removal

## Risk

Low. Same risk shape as PR α before graduation. Gated, observable, one-line rollback.

## Expected impact (universal, after graduation)

- Hit rate 41.2% → 55-65%
- Cost/min ₹5.38 → ~₹4.20
- Additional savings: ~₹1.5-2 crore/month on top of PR α
- Combined PR α + β: ~₹6 crore/month vs pre-caching baseline

## Summary

- New helper `src/shared/paths.py::resolve_under_root(root, name) -> Path | None` for the `(root / name).resolve() + is_relative_to(root.resolve())` containment idiom
- 11 callsites migrated across 7 source files
- 9 characterization tests pinning the contract (incl. suffix-collision case)
- Helper returns `Path | None`; callsites preserve their original error shape (HTTPException, dict-error, silent None) — no API change at any callsite

## Migrated sites

| File | Sites | Error shape preserved |
|---|---|---|
| `src/agent/server.py` | 3 (read / ingest / delete) | HTTPException(400, "Path traversal not allowed") |
| `src/agent/workspace.py` | 2 (_read_file / update_file) | `None` and `{"error": ...}` respectively |
| `src/agent/builtins/mesh_tool.py` | 1 (save_artifact) | `{"error": f"Invalid artifact name: {name}"}` |
| `src/agent/builtins/image_gen_tool.py` | 1 (final filename check) | **see behavior-change note below** |
| `src/browser/server.py` | 1 (`/uploads/{path}`) | HTTPException(400) |
| `src/dashboard/server.py` | 1 (`_resolve_upload_path`) | HTTPException(400) |
| `src/host/server.py` | 1 function, 2 calls (`_stage_paths`) | HTTPException(400, "invalid handle") |

## :warning: One behavior change at `image_gen_tool.py:94-95`

That site previously used `str(resolved).startswith(str(_ARTIFACTS_DIR.resolve()))` which has a latent suffix-collision bug: `/x/artifacts2/foo` would false-pass against root `/x/artifacts`. `is_relative_to` correctly rejects this.

**Practical impact**: zero. Upstream sanitization at lines 86-87 (`Path(filename).name` + `_FILENAME_UNSAFE_RE`) strips directory components and unsafe chars before this final check, so no realistic input could trigger the bypass. But the guard is now correct in principle.

## Out of scope (deferred)

- `src/agent/builtins/file_tool.py:46-74` — two-stage symlink walk with intermediate target check; deeper defense, not a direct match for this helper.
- `src/dashboard/server.py:7157` — static-asset `str().startswith()` check (same latent-bug shape as image_gen_tool). Codex review flagged as "not a simple replacement" so deferred to a focused follow-up.

body:
## Summary

Register shared cross-cutting concerns through the feature composition model.

This continues the move away from layer-level `DependencyInjection` classes by activating application, API, and infrastructure cross-cutting behavior through explicit feature modules.

## Changes

- Add `CrossCuttingConcerns` as an explicit `IFeature` marker.
- Add `ApplicationCrossCuttingModule` for use case telemetry decorators.
- Add `ApiCrossCuttingServiceModule` for:
  - `ProblemDetails`
  - `GlobalExceptionHandler`
  - `HttpContextAccessor`
- Add `ApiCrossCuttingWebAppModule` for `UseExceptionHandler()`.
- Add `InfrastructureCrossCuttingModule` for `IClock -> SystemClock`.
- Remove `Application/DependencyInjection.cs`.
- Remove cross-cutting registrations from `ApiAdapterExtensions`.
- Move clock registration out of `Infrastructure/DependencyInjection.cs`.
- Update `Program.cs` to activate `CrossCuttingConcerns` through feature composition.
- Reuse a single `FeatureWebAppBuilder` for WebApplication feature activation.

## Design decisions

- `CrossCuttingConcerns` is reserved for technical concerns that cut across features.
- Security, authorization, OpenAPI, persistence, and domain event dispatching remain out of this scope.
- `HttpContextAccessor` is treated as a generic request-context concern, not as security-specific.
- `ICurrentUser`, authentication, and authorization stay in the API adapter for now and will be handled separately.
- `IClock` is treated as a cross-cutting technical service because it keeps time access testable across application workflows.
- Product use cases are registered before cross-cutting concerns so telemetry decorators can be applied afterwards.

## Testing

- `dotnet build`
- `dotnet test`
- Result: all tests passed

### Motivation
- Provide a real Content Browser in the ImGui editor that enumerates files under `Resources` so Blender outputs and converted assets are discoverable without editing code. 
- Hook the existing build scripts (`RunBuildTextures.bat`, `RunBuildMeshes.bat`, `RunBuildFonts.bat`) into the editor so users can run asset conversion from the UI. 
- Surface build and content warnings/errors in an editor-local Output Log and make the system safe for missing folders, path quirks and asynchronous execution.

### Description
- Added `EditorAssetBrowser` (`EditorAssetBrowser.h/.cpp`) that scans `Resources` recursively, supports categories (`Textures/Models/Shaders/Fonts`), `Sources/Compiled` view modes, search filter, selection, and displays relative path/extension/size/modified time and simple icons.
- Added `EditorOutputLog` (`EditorOutputLog.h/.cpp`) providing thread-safe `Info/Warning/Error` entries, `Clear()` and `GetEntries()` used by the UI with simple color coding.
- Added `EditorProcessRunner` (`EditorProcessRunner.h/.cpp`) to execute batch files on Windows via `cmd /S /C`, quote arguments, capture `stdout/stderr`, and stream lines to a callback; on non-Windows it emits a friendly message.
- Added `EditorAssetBuildService` (`EditorAssetBuildService.h/.cpp`) that runs builds asynchronously, prevents double-start, expands `All` to `Textures->Meshes->Fonts` sequence, forwards `ProjectDir` and `Configuration` to batch scripts, and routes process output into `EditorOutputLog` classifying warnings/errors.

- Project integration: added new sources/headers to `Project/Ken4lowEngine.vcxproj` and `.filters` so the files participate in the Visual Studio project.
- Safety and platform notes: missing/invalid folders are warned to `EditorOutputLog` (no crash), paths are quoted for external processes, external batch execution is implemented for Windows only, and UI disables build controls while a build is running.

- Compiled new modules individually: ran `g++ -std=c++20 -IProject/Engine/Editor -c Project/Engine/Editor/EditorOutputLog.cpp`, `EditorAssetBrowser.cpp`, `EditorProcessRunner.cpp` and `EditorAssetBuildService.cpp` and they produced object files successfully (new-file compilation checks passed).

body:
## Summary

- Adds `frontend/e2e/specs/admin-manual-distribution.spec.ts` — the longest missing path from issue #76's acceptance criteria
- Pins the invariant: `csphd0001` (phd/nstc, college C) → professor approve → cs\_college rank+finalize → admin allocate+finalize → `application.status = 'approved'`
- Uses `@nightly` tag so it runs in the nightly E2E suite without blocking PR CI

## Why this spec matters

No existing spec takes an application all the way to `approved` via the full ranking+distribution pipeline. PR #278 (`ManualDistributionService.execute_general_distribution`) modifies the finalize path — this spec provides a regression guard for that invariant.

## Key design decisions

| Decision | Rationale |
|---|---|
| `csphd0001` not `stuphd001` | `create_ranking` filters by `std_academyno` vs `college_code`; stuphd001 has `EE`, cs\_college has `C` |
| `force_new: true` on ranking creation | Avoids reusing a stale unfinalized ranking from a prior run that might not contain the current application |
| Ranking finalize **before** allocate | `finalize()` at line 701 requires `CollegeRanking.is_finalized=True`; `allocate()` does not |
| `config.semester ?? "yearly"` | `AllocateRequest.semester` is a required string; active config may have `semester: null` for yearly scholarships |
| DB assertion on ranking item | Defensive check that `std_academyno='C'` matched `cs_college.college_code='C'`; surfaces mismatch with a clear error message |
| `afterAll` cleans `college_rankings` row | `deleteApplicationCascade` removes `college_ranking_items` but not the parent `college_rankings` row |

## Test plan

author: leecgeorge
body:
Three substantive additions to the panel-review machinery, the
  project-blueprint producer, and the spec-driven-dev consumer:

  - Trajectory table elision on approval. approve_document trims the
    `### Trajectory` table to the latest 15 data rows before hashing;
    older rows collapse into a single "N earlier passes elided" summary
    row. _is_normal_pass_row skips elided rows for halt and strict-bar
    accounting so long-lived docs don't drown the rendered panel-review
    section.

  - Phase-dependent panel triggers and tag mechanism. archive_pass.py
    now requires --phase {1,2,3}. Panelists prefix every HIGH Concern
    with [contract] / [detail] (Phase 3 only) / [upstream]. [upstream]
    auto-routes to halt votes in Phases 2 and 3 regardless of disposition
    — the explicit `Halt and re-scope` disposition is rare in practice
    and an [upstream] finding silently disposed as Addressed papers
    over the gap. Phase 3's strict-bar signal switches from
    Deferred-downstream to [detail]-tag accumulation; the script stashes
    tags=dXuYcZ in Trajectory Notes so consecutive passes can compare.

  - Cross-Feature Contracts. PLAN.md gains an optional
    `## Cross-Feature Contracts` section for invariants that span
    multiple features — shared event-key registries, cross-feature
    interface contracts, enforcement artifacts one feature owns on
    behalf of others. validate_blueprint is the producer: writes
    per-CFC content hashes, scans for orphaned tag bindings, emits
    `orphaned-stale-content` WARNs when a shipped spec drifts from
    current CFC text. validate_spec is the consumer: enforces that
    each participating feature carries `[CFC-N]` on a THEN line, and
    that features named in Enforcement own a `[CFC-N]`-tagged task.
    The shared scripts/cfc_parser.py prevents producer/consumer drift
    on the file format. Synthesizer self-check gains (d) tag presence,
    (e) closed-feature-row integrity, and (f) CFC authoring fidelity.
    New documentation/CFC.md carries the design rationale.

body: ## Summary - Wraps `JSON.parse` in `parseDeckResponse` with a `jsonrepair` fallback, behind a plausibility check (at least one card with non-empty `q` and `a`) so we don't ship junk on truly truncated responses. - Adds two tests in `ClaudeService.test.ts`: the German-quote recovery case and the repair-also-fails case. - Adds a changelog entry — paying users on non-English content stop seeing silent "Failed" rows. ## Why Spotted via Hotjar (German user, Safari, 1h ago). Job `169477` (`cofi Jost.zip`, Corporate Finance) failed with `Claude returned invalid JSON` because the model emitted a raw ASCII `"` to close a German `„…"` quote, prematurely ending the JSON string. Reproduced the parse failure locally on the user's payload and confirmed the fix recovers the full 56-card deck. This is not isolated — **12 of the 13 most recent failed `claude` jobs in prod (~92%)** hit this same error class. Skew is heavy toward German/Swedish/medical-jargon decks. ## Trio PM / designer / engineer all weighed in before code was written. PM said same-day hotfix and silent repair; designer said deliver-with-warning row; engineer recommended `jsonrepair` over tool_use to avoid an SDK migration under incident pressure. Compromise: ship the parser fix today (this PR), follow up with the UX surface (failure-row copy + repair-warning row) in a separate PR. ## Risk `jsonrepair` is permissive — it'll happily close brackets on a truncated response and produce a deck with a card missing `a`. The plausibility check in `tryRepairDeckArray` guards against that: if no card with both `q` and `a` exists after repair, we fall through to the original error. ## Test plan - [x] `pnpm test src/lib/claude/ClaudeService.test.ts` — 19/19 pass, including the two new cases - [x] `pnpm test` (full server suite) — 1487 pass, 7 skipped, 8 todo - [x] `pnpm --filter notion2anki-server build` - [x] `pnpm --filter 2anki-web typecheck`, `lint`, `test:run` — all green - [ ] Sonar local run skipped — `sonar-scanner` not installed in this environment. Expect Sonar CI feedback after push; small surface (one new helper + one new dep) should be low-risk. - [ ] After merge + deploy: monitor `/api/upload/jobs` failure rate for `type='claude'` over next 24h; tail server logs for `[Claude] Recovered malformed JSON via jsonrepair` to confirm the path is firing for real users. ## Follow-ups (separate PRs) - Web: failure-row copy + suppress restart for "invalid JSON" failures + email-support CTA. - API: surface a `repaired` flag on the job response so the deck-ready row can show an amber "open them in Anki to check" note. - Long-term: migrate to Anthropic structured output / tool_use, which eliminates this class entirely. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- Need help on this PR? ## Summary

Real bug surfaced while building #130. \`getBrandConfig\` and \`getPortalContent\` both wrap their Supabase reads in a 5-min in-memory cache (UNI-1992 / UNI-1947 Pillar 2). invalidateBrandConfigCache(slug);
invalidatePortalContentCache(slug);

author: yhny1001
body:
本 PR 解决两个 agent runtime 健壮性 issue 的**后端部分**。前端 UI 闭环走单独的 PR（见 follow-up）。

## Summary

### Issue #54: workspace IO tools 把目录访问翻译成业务级错误

之前 `workspace_read_file` / `workspace_write_file` / `workspace_apply_patch` / `workspace.commit` 在 model 把目录路径（如 \`persist\` / \`output\`）当文件读写时，OS 抛 \`EISDIR\` → \`DomainError::InternalError\` → \`agent.internal_error\` + \`retryable=false\`，run 直接崩。

修复链路（严格 Clean Architecture，3 处穷尽 match 同步更新）：

- \`DomainError::Conflict(String)\` 新增 → \`ApplicationError::ValidationError\` / \`CommandError::BadRequest\` / HTTP 409。
- \`file_agent_repository::workspace_store::ensure_target_is_not_directory\` 在 \`read_text\` / \`write_text\` 前用 \`fs::symlink_metadata\` 探测，目录目标抛 \`DomainError::Conflict("workspace.path_is_directory: ...")\`。
- 共享 \`parse_workspace_conflict_message\` 放在 \`agent_tools/common.rs\`，\`pub(crate)\` 暴露，workspace 工具的 \`classify_workspace_io_error\` 和 runtime-service 的 \`perform_host_chat_commit\` 复用同一 source of truth（不重复造轮子）。
- \`workspace_read_file\` description 强化，明确禁止目录目标，提示使用 \`workspace_list_files\`。

### Issue #55: instruction drift 后端事件

当模型在 \`workspace.commit\` 后回纯文本、tool_calls 为空、tool_after_finish、max_tool_rounds_exceeded 等漂移场景，之前：committed 的 chat 消息留作孤儿，无法回滚；UI 也没拿到 retry 信号。

- \`loop_runner\` 跟踪每一次 \`AgentToolEffect::ChatCommitted\`。
- 漂移触发时 emit \`run_rollback_targets\` warn event（**在 \`run_failed\` 之前**），载荷含每条 committed message 的 \`{ path, mode, messageId, round }\`。
- \`run_failed\` payload 新增 \`userRetryable: bool\`：\`retryable=true\` 时为 true；drift codes（\`model.tool_call_required\` / \`agent.tool_after_finish\` / \`agent.max_tool_rounds_exceeded\`）即使 \`retryable=false\` 也设为 \`userRetryable=true\`。
- \`workspace.commit\` description 强化"必须 same-or-next turn 调 \`workspace.finish\`，不准回纯文本"契约。
- \`docs/Agent/RunEventJournal.md\` + \`docs/Agent/ToolSystem.md\` 同步更新。

## Commits

- \`fdeca94\` chore: ignore local .cursor/ skill workspace
- \`44997a1\` fix(agent): translate workspace directory access to recoverable tool error (#54)
- \`fb23853\` fix(agent): emit run_rollback_targets + userRetryable on instruction drift (#55)

## 改动范围

21 个文件，主要在 \`src-tauri/src/{domain,application,infrastructure,presentation}/\`，没有任何 vendor 文件改动，所有改动遵守仓库 \`.cursor/skills/tauritavern-contribution/SKILL.md\`（项目 contribution skill，本 PR 不进版本控制因为在 .gitignore）。

## 验证

\`cargo test --lib\` 589 全绿（含 11 个新增测试覆盖 \`DomainError::Conflict\` 转换、\`classify_workspace_io_error\`、\`userRetryable\` 各 drift code、以及 end-to-end \`foreground_run_emits_rollback_targets_on_tool_call_required_drift\` 集成测试）。

## 关联 PR

- 前端 UI 闭环（让 Retry 按钮 / drift 消息回滚 / send 解锁真正生效）走单独 PR，依赖本 PR 合并。

## Test plan

- [ ] 让 agent 把 \`workspace_read_file\` 的 path 设成 \`persist\`（一个 workspace root），确认返回 \`workspace.path_is_directory\` 业务错误而不是 \`agent.internal_error\`，且 run 不崩
- [ ] 触发模型在 commit 后回纯文本的 drift 场景，确认事件 journal 里能看到 \`run_rollback_targets\`，\`run_failed.userRetryable === true\`
- [ ] cargo test --lib 通过

author: zeriaxdev
body:
## Summary

`npm run production` was failing with:

```
error TS6059: File '…/test/content.test.ts' is not under 'rootDir' '…/src'.
error TS6059: File '…/test/endpoints.test.ts' is not under 'rootDir' '…/src'.
error TS6059: File '…/test/mcp.test.ts' is not under 'rootDir' '…/src'.
```

`tsconfig.production.json` excluded `src/tests` (a path that doesn't exist) instead of the real top-level `test/` directory, so the default `**/*` include glob pulled the test files in. With `rootDir: ./src`, that's a fatal config error.

Rather than just fix the exclude string, this PR makes the prod config `extend` the dev `tsconfig.json` and only override `outDir`. That eliminates the silent drift between the two — production now inherits the same `exclude: ["test"]`, `skipLibCheck`, `experimentalDecorators`, `emitDecoratorMetadata`, etc. After the rootDir fix alone, a second error surfaced (`@scalar/express-api-reference` type-resolution issue) because prod wasn't inheriting `skipLibCheck`; extending fixes both at once.

## Test plan

- [x] `rm -rf dist && npm run production` — clean, no errors
- [x] `ls dist/` shows the expected tree (handlers, parsers, models, mcp/, main.js, …)

author: me1iissa
body:
## Summary

- musl `posix_spawn(3)` parent's `read(read_end, count=4)` on the
  cancel-pipe was parking forever after the child's `execve` succeeded.
  Three independent close paths failed to decrement the pipe's
  `writers` / `readers` counts: `vfs::close`, `execve`'s `FD_CLOEXEC`
  purge, and the `dup`/`dup2` family.  `fork`/`clone3` without
  `CLONE_FILES` was also missing the symmetric *bump* — pipe ends were
  duplicated into the child fd table with no count increase, mirroring
  the W216 H_A gap for AF_UNIX sockets that PR #233 closed.
- Patch closes all three close paths and the bump path symmetrically;
  the pipe-end detection predicate (`file_type == Pipe`,
  `mount_idx == usize::MAX`, `flags & 0x8000_0000 != 0`) matches the
  shape already used by `handle_exit_or_kill_thread`.
- New `test_pipe_refcount_fork_exec_close_chain` (Test 0bc2) scripts
  the cancel-pipe lifecycle's five stages against the pipe helpers.

## Verifier-named evidence

Pre-patch (per dispatch, sid `d90fb9da005d`):

  PID 1 (musl firefox-bin parent) TID 2 wedged in
  `read(fd=11, buf=0x7ffffffec724, count=4)` at `rip=0x7f000005b5c0`
  for `STUCK_IN_NR=0@19006t` (~9 s at TICK_HZ=2000).  fd=11 was the
  read end of a `pipe2(O_CLOEXEC)` immediately preceding the vfork.
  The child explicitly `close(11)`d its copy of the read end, set
  `FD_CLOEXEC` on its write-end fd=12, then `execve(/disk/opt/firefox/glxtest)`.
  Parent then `close(12)` and `read(11, 4)` — the read parked forever.

Post-patch (sid `24e41b121df7`, KVM `firefox-test,kdb,syscall-trace`):

```
4957  [SC]     pid=1 tid=2 nr=3 a1=0xc                  # parent close(fd=12)
4958  [SC-RET] pid=1 tid=2 nr=3 ret=0x0
4959  [SC]     pid=1 tid=2 nr=0 a1=0xb a2=... a3=0x4    # parent read(fd=11, 4)
4960  [SC-RET] pid=1 tid=2 nr=0 ret=0x0                 # → 0 (EOF) immediately
4961  [SC]     pid=1 tid=2 nr=3 a1=0xb                  # parent close(fd=11)
4962  [SC-RET] pid=1 tid=2 nr=3 ret=0x0
```

  `STUCK_IN_NR` counter: 0 across the whole run.  Aggregate sc
  advanced past the prior `sc=1972` plateau; PID 2 reached
  `exit_group(0)` from inside glxtest at `nr=231`.  The next gate
  downstream is unrelated (a separate `#GP` cluster).

## In-kernel test

```
TEST: pipe refcount — fork+exec+close chain (musl posix_spawn cancel-pipe)
  created pipe id=1 ✓
  stage 0 (post-pipe2): writers=1 readers=1 ✓
  stage 1 (post-fork bump): writers=2 readers=2 ✓
  stage 2 (post-child-exec CLOEXEC purge): writers=1 (parent only) ✓
  stage 3 (post-child close(read_end)): readers=1 (parent only) ✓
  stage 4 (post-parent close(write_end)): writers=0 is_eof=true ✓
  → parent's blocked read(read_end) would now return 0 (EOF)
[PASS] pipe refcount — fork+exec+close chain (musl posix_spawn cancel-pipe)
```

## Diff size

5 files, 259 lines (≈40% test, ≈60% kernel).  Within budget given the
three independent close paths plus the symmetric fork bump.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo +nightly check --features test-mode` — pass
- [x] `cargo +nightly check --features firefox-test,kdb,syscall-trace` — pass
- [x] Test 0bc2 passes under `--features test-mode`
- [x] KVM `firefox-test` end-to-end: `read(fd=11, 4)` returns 0 (EOF)
      immediately after parent's `close(write_end)`; `STUCK_IN_NR=0` for
      the run; PID 2 reaches `exit_group(0)`.
- [ ] 3-trial KVM reproducibility soak (dispatched separately per
      coordinator note).
- [ ] Downstream regression check: existing `pipe_pollhup`,
      `clone3_wake_vfork_on_execve`, and `epoll`/`select` pipe tests
      should remain green.

## References

- POSIX.1-2017 `read(2)`  — EOF semantics when all writers close.
- POSIX.1-2017 `write(2)` — EPIPE / SIGPIPE when all readers close.
- POSIX.1-2017 `dup2(2)`  — silent close-before-overwrite of fildes2.
- POSIX.1-2017 `fork(2)`  — duplicate-open-file-description semantics.
- POSIX.1-2017 §2.14      — shared open-file-description semantics.
- IEEE Std 1003.1-2017    — `posix_spawn(3)` cancel-pipe pattern.

author: robertschaft
body:
Two cross-thread shapes for arrays, plus a refactor of section 13 around them.

**`T[].splitOff(int)`** — consumes the receiver and returns an `OwnedPair<T[], T[]>` of owning halves backed by a shared refcounted allocation. The halves can be moved into independent long-lived threads (via partial-move accessors, MOVE-07); the allocation is freed when the last half drops.

**`Arrays.stream(@bound T[])`** — exposes the array as a JDK `Stream<@bound T>`. `.parallel().forEach(...)` / `.reduce` / `.collect` cover read-only data-parallel processing via the underlying `Spliterator`; callers needing a specific executor use `ForkJoinPool.submit(...)` per standard JDK practice. In-place parallel *mutation* is **not** a stream operation — `Stream<@bound T>` doesn't write back into the source — that use case stays on the `splitOff` path.

**Generic pair records.** Replaces one-off `ArraySplit<T>` / `ConcurrentArraySplit<T>` with general-purpose `BoundPair<L, R>` and `OwnedPair<L, R>` in `laterita.lang`. Heterogeneous and unequal-sized future returns reuse the same records.

**Section 13 restructure.** Each surface now has one consolidated code block: `class T[] { ... }` lists everything laterita adds to arrays; `class Arrays { ... }` mirrors the static surface plus `stream`. Supporting records follow as ARR-03/04/05 (`MutableConsumer`, `BoundPair`, `OwnedPair`).

**Docs.** Reasoning subsection rewritten around the two shapes. Terminology gains `BoundPair` and `OwnedPair` entries with the `ArraySplit`/`ConcurrentArraySplit` entries removed; buffer-splitting entry updated. OQ-21 moved to `resolved-questions.md`; OQ-19 tombstone updated to the new numbering.

Example covers long-lived workers pre-extracting halves via `split.left()` / `split.right()` and moving them into virtual threads.

author: matze4u
body:
## Problem

`FluentDataMapper::map()` produces wrong results when a source key has a `null` value **and** the template contains any conditional expression (`??`, `?:`, ternary `? :`).

### Root cause

`isset()` returns `false` for keys whose value is `null` (PHP semantics). In `FluentDataMapper.php` line 863, the `isset()` check fails for null-valued source keys, causing the `else` branch to assign the **entire source array** as the named source alias. The `ExpressionEvaluator` then resolves this alias to the full source array instead of `null`.

This code path is only reached when `hasConditionalExpressions($template)` or `hasWildcardOperators(...)` returns `true` (lines 846–848). A template without `?`, `?:`, `??` bypasses the bug; a template with a single ternary expression triggers it for **all** null fields.

### Reproducer

```php
$template = [
    'a' => '{{ id }}',
    'b' => '{{ baubeginn }}',
    'c' => '{{ erledigt == true ? 1 : 0 }}',
];

$source = [
    'id' => 1,
    'baubeginn' => null,
    'erledigt' => true,
    'other' => 'x',
];

$result = DataMapper::template($template)
    ->source(json_encode($source))
    ->map()
    ->getTarget();

// ACTUAL: 'b' => ['id' => 1, 'baubeginn' => null, 'erledigt' => true, 'other' => 'x']
// EXPECTED: 'b' => null
```

## Fix

One-line change: `isset($this->source[$sourceName])` → `array_key_exists($sourceName, $this->source)`

`array_key_exists()` returns `true` for keys with `null` values, so `null` correctly lands in `$namedSources` and the evaluator returns `null`.

## Tests

Three new regression tests in `ConditionalExpressionsTest.php`:

- **preserves null source values** when template has conditional expression
- **does not replace null values with entire source array** (multi-field scenario)
- **handles null coalescing combined with conditional expressions**

All 38 tests pass ✅

body:
Adds a clone-first VPS quickstart and tightens docker-compose so a fresh clone fails loud instead of starting with weak default secrets.

## What changed

- **`.env.example`** (new) — operator template covering `AGENTWORKS_SESSION_SECRET`, `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`, per-service `BIND_ADDR`/`HOST_PORT` vars, data/config dirs, version pin.
- **`VPS-QUICKSTART.md`** (new) — 8-step clone → `cp .env.example .env` → `docker compose up` path, including an `ssh -L` tunnel example and Codex/Claude Code MCP wiring. Complements (does not replace) the existing `docs/vps-blank-slate-install.md` sanitized-archive flow.
- **`docker-compose.yml`** — enforce `AGENTWORKS_SESSION_SECRET` and `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` via `${VAR:?...}` (removes the weak `:-agentworks-local` default that a public install would have otherwise inherited). Make each service's host bind addr and host port configurable as `${X_BIND_ADDR:-127.0.0.1}:${X_HOST_PORT:-...}` so operators can rebind without editing the compose file. Loopback remains the default for every service.
- **`README.md`** — one-paragraph pointer from the Quick install section to `VPS-QUICKSTART.md`.

Total: 2 new files, 9 lines modified, 7 lines removed (138 insertions, 7 deletions).

## Why not the rest of the original local hardening commit

This PR is the publicly-portable subset of internal commit `17e0270 chore: harden vps clone install path`. The other changes in that commit were dropped because they would have regressed v0.1.9 audit work shipped on this repo:

- Dockerfile changes — local version switches healthchecks from `127.0.0.1` back to `localhost` (the exact bug v0.1.9 audit rounds fixed), drops `EMBEDDING_MODE=stub` and `RERANKER_MODE=stub` defaults (5-15 min HF download on first boot), drops the next/react symlink restoration in admin-ui runtime.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml` — local version drops the resolve-tag job, concurrency control, semver-shaped tag glob, cosign signing, and lowercase-owner handling. Reverts to a much earlier workflow.
- `kimi-{adapter,review-adapter,tool-adapter}.ts` — local version adds a `~/.hermes/config.yaml` fallback for the API key (more local coupling, not less).
- `agents/*/AGENTS.md` — local version adds ~280 lines of Operator UX v2 guidance with a hardcoded CEO `assigneeAgentId`.
- `docs/install-runbook.md` + `docs/mcp-integration.md` — public versions are more comprehensive and already cover VPS install.
- `config/.env.example` — wording-only churn.

## Verification

On a fresh `git clone` + this branch:

```
pnpm --filter @agentworks/agentos-d typecheck   # clean
pnpm -r run build                                # clean
pnpm --filter @agentworks/agentos-d exec vitest run
# Test Files  67 passed (67)
# Tests       628 passed (628)
docker compose config                            # fails loud: required variable POSTGRES_PASSWORD is missing a value
env AGENTWORKS_SESSION_SECRET=test POSTGRES_PASSWORD=test docker compose config   # validates
rg -n 'agentworks-os-local|/Users/2agents|Adam Brown|30184da8|1c626d50|btm-optimize|cashmoney'   # clean
```

## Security notes

- Compose still defaults every published host port to `127.0.0.1` so a fresh `docker compose up` on a VPS does **not** expose unauthenticated MCP or daemon ports to the internet.
- `VPS-QUICKSTART.md` explicitly states that MCP auth forwarding is not implemented and that operators must use SSH tunnels, a VPN, or an authenticated TLS reverse proxy for remote access. n8n and the admin UI are documented under the same constraint.
- The `${VAR:?...}` enforcement is the main correctness fix: previously, an operator who forgot to set `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` got a Postgres container running with the well-known string `agentworks-local`. That's now a hard error at compose-config time.

## Known follow-ups (not in this PR)

- n8n `WEBHOOK_URL=http://localhost:5678/` is not configurable for a reverse-proxy deployment. Same `${...}` treatment would fit.
- `docs/install-runbook.md` references the installer scripts and a sanitized-archive workflow; an explicit cross-link to `VPS-QUICKSTART.md` would help operators choose.

author: israelsegundofb
body:
**💡 What:** 
Refactored the heavy `O(N*M)` array processing loops in `App.tsx` (`handlePurchaseUpdateUpload` and `handleClientFileDirect`).
- Substituted `products.find(...)` inside the `clientPurchases.map` loop with pre-built `productSkuMap` and `productNameMap` `O(1)` lookups.
- Hoisted string normalization (`toLowerCase().trim()`) for the `users` array in `handleClientFileDirect` outside of the `rawData.forEach` loop.

**🎯 Why:**
During large dataset imports (e.g., CSV/Excel uploads), repeatedly iterating over the entire products/users lists and repeatedly allocating new string objects for comparison blocks the main thread, causing significant UI freezing and slow parsing times.

**📊 Impact:** 
Reduces the algorithmic complexity of client and purchase import parsing from `O(N * M)` down to `O(N + M)` and drops thousands of string allocations. This keeps the React UI responsive during processing and significantly speeds up parsing time.

**🔬 Measurement:** 
Import a large batch of sales and purchases via a CSV file; observe the processing completion time dropping drastically with zero UI thread freezing. Verified all existing test cases (`pnpm test run`) and linting (`pnpm run validate`) still pass locally.

body:
### Motivation

- Prevent visual jitter when swapping layered parts (blink/mouth frames) by stabilizing the RectTransform layout and anchoring layered visuals to the character bottom-center.
- Provide explicit `visualRoot` and `partsRoot` RectTransforms so layered parts can be sized and positioned consistently relative to the base sprite.

### Description

- Added `BottomCenterAnchor` constant and new `ConfigureBottomCenterRoot` helper to set anchors/pivot/position/scale to bottom-center for a `RectTransform`. 
- Added `visualRoot` and `partsRoot` fields to `VNLayeredCharacterSlot` and a new `UpdateLayeredCharacterRootLayout` method that configures both roots and sets `partsRoot.sizeDelta` to `baseSprite.rect.size` to keep parts sizing stable.
- Hooked `UpdateLayeredCharacterRootLayout` into the layered character apply path (`ApplyLayeredCharacterSlot`/where layered mapping is applied) so roots are configured whenever a layered base sprite is applied.
- Updated `P_Content_VN.prefab` to add `Left/Center/Right` `VisualRoot` and `PartsRoot` RectTransforms and wired them into the `layeredCharacterSlots` entries (fileID assignments and parent changes) to match the new slot fields.

## Summary

Workspace-side companion to **vivarium-dashboard#44**, which made `pipeline_gate.prerequisites` the canonical DAG-edge read path with `parent_studies` as a back-compat fallback. This PR adds the matching lint checks so authors get the same migration nudge at edit time that the dashboard now surfaces at render time via `DeprecationWarning`.

## New checks

| Check | Level | When it fires |
|---|---|---|
| `dag_edges_legacy_only` | warning | study uses `parent_studies` without `pipeline_gate.prerequisites` — same nudge as the runtime warning |
| `dag_edges_legacy_redundant` | warning | both fields list the same parent SLUG SET (the legacy field is dead weight; drop it) |
| `dag_edges_legacy_and_canonical_disagree` | **error** | both fields list DIFFERENT parents — the dashboard reads only the canonical one, so the legacy entries are silently ignored. Exactly the foot-gun this cleanup pass exists to prevent. Errors block `/pbg-report` unless overridden. |

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/test_report_linter.py -q` — 31/31 pass (4 new + 27 pre-existing)
- [x] `pytest tests/ -q` — 376/376 (was 372; +4 new)
- [x] Three new lint-case fixtures under `tests/fixtures/lint-cases/dag-edges-{legacy-only,both-agree,both-conflict}/`
- [ ] Manual: run `/pbg-report` against v2ecoli — every study using `parent_studies` exclusively shows the warning; nothing fails

## Order

Merges in either order — the dashboard PR doesn't depend on this lint, and this lint doesn't depend on the dashboard PR. Convention says merge dashboard first since it's the load-bearing behavior change.

🔗 **View agent run:** https://app.netlify.com/projects/storied-torrone-664cd7/agent-runs/6a0b207f3ec9331d9664c4f0

🤖 **Agent:** Claude

💬 **Prompt:** The Netlify deploy errored, with the following guidance provided:

Diagnosis

- Relevant log lines: [line 9](#L9), [line 11](#L11)-[line 13](#L13), and [line 28](#L28)-[line 31](#L31). The installer is using Python 3.14.3 ([line 9](#L9)) and pip stal...

✅ **Result:** The Netlify build was failing because the build environment was automatically selecting Python 3.14.3, which is too new for several of the project's pip dependencies (notably packages that require a build step via `pyproject.toml`, such as `pandas`). The metadata preparation stage stalled and pip exited with a non-zero code, aborting the dependency installation.

Two files were added to pin the Python runtime to the stable 3.11.6 release:

- **`.python-version`** — honored by `mise`, `pyenv`, and similar version managers used in Netlify's build image.
- **`runtime.txt`** — a Heroku-style fallback that some build toolchains also consult when selecting the Python interpreter.

With Python 3.11.6 pinned, pip will use a runtime that all listed dependencies (`Flask`, `Flask-SQLAlchemy`, `Flask-Login`, `Werkzeug`, `pandas`, `openpyxl`) are known to support, allowing metadata preparation and wheel building to complete successfully.

author: saurabh500
body:
## Summary

Upgrades `mssql-tiberius-bridge` from `preview.3` to `preview.5` and removes the `value_to_sql_param()` workaround that was added in the issue #145 composite PK implementation.

## Background

The bridge's `impl ToSql for serde_json::Value` previously called `self.to_string()` on every variant, which:
- JSON-quoted strings: `Value::String("alice")` was bound as `"\"alice\""` — matching zero DB rows
- Stringified nulls: `Value::Null` was bound as `"null"` instead of SQL NULL

A local workaround `value_to_sql_param()` dispatched by variant to fix this. The fix was filed as [bridge issue #95](https://github.com/saurabh500/mssql-tiberius-bridge/issues/95) and shipped in preview.5 ([PR #96](https://github.com/saurabh500/mssql-tiberius-bridge/pull/96)).

## Changes

- **`Cargo.toml`**: bump `mssql-tiberius-bridge = "=0.1.0-preview.5"`
- **`sqlserver/helpers.rs`**: remove `value_to_sql_param()`, its `ToSql` import, and 6 now-redundant unit tests
- **`sqlserver/mod.rs`**: simplify parameter binding — no more `Box<dyn ToSql + Send + Sync>` intermediate vec or `&**b` double-deref:
  - Delete: `pk_vals.iter().map(|v| v as &dyn ToSql)`
  - Update: `once(&new_val).chain(pk_vals.iter()).map(|v| v as &dyn ToSql)`

## Tests

All 112 SQL Server driver tests pass.

Closes #145

author: estebanzimanyi
body:
Registers the portable bare-name operator dialect in MobilitySpark.

## What this delivers

- **`PortableOperatorAliasUDFs`** registers all **29** canonical bare-name
  operator UDFs from the single source of truth —
  `MobilityDB/MEOS-API meta/portable-aliases.json` (RFC #920, discussion
  MobilityDB#861, native in MobilityDB#1075), vendored read-only at
  `meta/portable-aliases.json`.
- **Equivalence by construction.** Each alias reuses the operator's own
  existing backing UDF field verbatim — the exact `functions.*` MEOS C
  symbol the typed UDF dispatches to. No operator logic is reimplemented.
- **All six type families, no headline exclusion.** The backings are the
  MEOS superclass entrypoints (`*_temporal_temporal`,
  `*_tspatial_tspatial`, `t*_temporal_temporal`, `tdistance_tgeo_tgeo`,
  `nad_tgeo_*`), which libmeos dispatches internally for any temporal
  value in the type-erased hex-WKB string — so `cbuffer` / `npoint` /
  `pose` / `rgeo` are covered alongside `temporal` and `geo`.
  `left`/`right`/`overleft`/`overright` select between the existing
  `tnumber` and `tspatial` backings.
- The type-qualified spellings these supersede 1:1 (`temporalBefore`,
  `tnumberLeft`, `teqTemporal`, …) are **dropped** — the bare name is the
  portable contract; the distinct argument-class typed surface (e.g.
  `temporal × tstzspan`) is retained.

## Parity gate

`scripts/portable_parity.py` ports the exact prefix logic of
`MobilityDB/MEOS-API portable_parity.py`:

```
[portable-parity] 29/29 canonical bare names backed by a registered UDF (100.0%); 0 unbacked
CHECK: PASS — 29/29 bare names backed, 0 unbacked, all six families
```

Wired into Maven CI as a required step.

## Six families in scope (correction)

`scripts/parity-audit.py` no longer defers `cbuffer`/`npoint`/`pose`/`rgeo`
(`DEFERRED_FAMILIES` is empty by invariant). `docs/parity-status.md` and
`docs/parity-100.md` are regenerated/reframed so the four families are in
scope and **never excluded from any headline**: 1353/1462 = 92.5% active
addressable. The remaining ~7.5% is the typed per-family UDF surface for
those four families plus the known typed-Datum tile/split returns —
tracked as a gap with a concrete plan (same `MeosNative`/`functions.*`
reuse pattern, no new operator logic), not a stopping point.

## Dependency

Stacks on **#10 → #9 → #5** (continues on issued PRs; not blocked on
review/merge). The portable layer reuses backing fields introduced by
that stack.

## Verification

- `python3 scripts/portable_parity.py` → 29/29, 0 unbacked (exit 0).
- `python3 scripts/parity-audit.py --mdb ../MobilityDB --mspark .`
  regenerates `docs/parity-status.md` with all six families in scope.
- Full Maven unit suite runs in CI (Linux). Unit tests reference the
  backing fields, which are unchanged; only the registered names move
  from type-qualified to bare.
