author: vlobstein-vc
body:
## Summary

`golangci-lint run` goes from 63 findings to 0. No behaviour change: auto-fixes, a few one-liners, constant extractions, and a CI bump so the newer linter that ships `gomodguard_v2` actually runs. Tests and build still green.

## What changed

### Auto-fixes and small one-liners

`golangci-lint --fix` covers most of the obvious ones:

- `gci`: import grouping in seven files.
- `godot`: trailing periods on three doc comments (`encryption/des.go`, `transform/encode.go`).
- `misspell`: `recieved` → `received` in `transform/transform_test.go`.
- `nlreturn`: blank line before `continue` in `transform/transform.go`.
- `perfsprint`: three `strings.Builder` swaps replacing string concatenation in loops (`cli/commandline.go`, `payload/wrapper.go`, `protocol/dotnetremoting/dotnetremoting.go`).

Two manual touches the auto-fix did not handle:

- `govet` hostport: `fmt.Sprintf("%s:%d", host, port)` in `protocol/tcpsocket.go` was IPv6-unsafe. Now `net.JoinHostPort(host, strconv.Itoa(port))`.
- `mirror`: `(*strings.Builder).WriteString(string(buf))` in `protocol/dotnetremoting/dotnetremoting.go` was allocating an intermediate string. Now `Write(buf)` directly.

### Constant extractions for `goconst`

50 findings, all on repeated string literals in the .NET BinaryFormatter and Java gadget builders. The strings are protocol identifiers used 3 to 39 times each. Extracting them is a real readability win because a fresh contributor can now grep the identifier and land on the canonical definition instead of one of N inline literals.

- New `dotnet/constants.go` exports the type-system labels (`TypePrimitive`, `TypeSystemClass`, ...), three frequently-referenced class names (`ClassDelegateSerializationHolderEntry`, ...), member names (`MemberAssemblyName`, `MemberDollarType`, ...), and the two assembly identifiers (`AssemblyMscorlib`, `AssemblySystemData`). `BinaryTypeEnumerationMap` in `general_types.go` now references the consts as map keys so the type-name → enum-int mapping has a single source of truth.
- `java/constants.go` extends the existing constants file with JVM class descriptors (`JClassString`, `JClassArrayObject`, ...), the reflection method names (`JMethodGetMethod`, `JMethodGetRuntime`, ...), Commons Collections class names, and the eight-byte `TCBlockData` prefix used by every empty-HashMap gadget receiver.
- `payload/wrapper.go` lifts the iconv chain that the canonical `/`, the RFC 3501 `,` and the URL-safe `_` rows of `phpFilterMap` share into a single `phpFilterIconvSlash` const.
- `protocol/sip/helper.go` keeps the inline string literals in the `TransportType.String()` positional array under a `//nolint:goconst` with a one-line rationale. The array is the canonical iota → name mapping, lifting each transport letter to its own const would just add indirection.

### Config and CI

- `.golangci.yml`: `gomodguard` → `gomodguard_v2` (the v1 linter was deprecated in golangci-lint v2.12.0), plus a per-path exclusion `_test\.go` for `goconst` so test-data inlining stops tripping the rule. The redundant `//nolint:goconst` on `dotnet/viewstate_test.go::ExampleProtect` is removed since `nolintlint` started flagging it as unused.
- `.github/workflows/go.yml`: bumped golangci-lint v2.10.1 to v2.12.2. The install.sh URL is pinned to the version tag (`/v2.12.2/install.sh`) instead of `master/install.sh` because the master install script's checksum table is currently stale against the v2.12.x release binaries (SHA-256 mismatch on download). Pinning the install script to the same tag as the binary keeps the verification consistent.

After: `golangci-lint run` exits with 0 findings, `go build ./...` and `go test ./...` are green.

author: lyingbug
body:
## Summary

- Persist the input-bar state used for each QA request (agent, model, knowledge base scope, web search) on the session row, so reopening a session restores the same configuration the user had when they last sent a message.
- Store the snapshot in the existing `sessions.agent_config` JSONB column to avoid a new migration; it is written best-effort in a background goroutine on every POST to `/knowledge-chat` or `/agent-chat`.
- On the frontend, snapshot the user's global default settings when entering a session and restore them when leaving, so opening an old session does not leak its state into new-chat defaults.

## Motivation

When a user clicked into an existing session from the sidebar, the chat input always showed the global Pinia/localStorage settings instead of the settings that were actually used in that session. There was no way to tell which agent/model/KB scope a previous answer was generated with. This change records that context on the session itself and rehydrates it on reopen.

## Changes

### Backend
- `types.SessionLastRequestState` carries `agent_id`, `agent_enabled`, `model_id`, `knowledge_base_ids`, `knowledge_ids`, `web_search_enabled` with `Value`/`Scan` implementations tolerant of legacy `agent_config` payloads.
- `types.Session` exposes the new struct via `last_request_state` JSON / `agent_config` column mapping.
- `SessionRepository.UpdateLastRequestState` writes only the JSONB column and `updated_at` (no perturbation of title/description).
- `SessionService.UpdateSessionLastRequestState` wraps it with tenant/user scope checks.
- `executeQA` fires the persistence in a goroutine with `context.WithoutCancel` so SSE disconnects do not drop the write.

### Frontend
- `settings` store gains `snapshotAsDefaultsIfNeeded`, `restoreDefaultsIfSnapshotted`, and `applyLastRequestState`; the snapshot is non-persistent (page refresh re-runs the same enter flow).
- `views/chat/index.vue` calls `loadSessionAndHydrate` on mount and on cross-session route updates, and restores defaults on `onBeforeRouteLeave`.
- Embedded mode (`embeddedMode=true`) skips the hydration entirely so widget hosts keep full control over the settings store.

## Test plan

- [ ] Open an existing session that was last sent with `智能推理 + KB A + web search ON` — the input bar shows the same selections after reopen.
- [ ] Switch to another session that used `快速问答 + KB B + web search OFF` — the input bar updates accordingly.
- [ ] Click "New chat" after leaving a session — the input bar returns to the user's prior global defaults, not the just-visited session's state.
- [ ] Hard refresh while inside a session — settings are still restored from `last_request_state` (no flash of stale defaults beyond the initial getSession).
- [ ] Embedded-mode chat widgets keep using the host-provided agent/KB props unchanged.
- [ ] `go build ./...` and `go test ./internal/types/... ./internal/application/repository/... ./internal/application/service/...` pass.

author: jpelaez-23blocks
body:
## Summary

- **New command**: `aid-request` — agents can request registration without an admin token
- **New script**: `scripts/aid-request.sh` with `--poll` mode for checking approval status
- **Updated README**: documents both registration flows (admin-initiated and agent-initiated) with sequence diagram
- **Updated SKILL.md**: adds `aid-request.sh` command reference and natural language mappings
- **Updated install.sh**: includes `aid-request.sh` in installation
- **Updated lifecycle**: `pending -> active` (approve) or `pending -> rejected`

## How it works

1. Agent runs `aid-request --auth <url>` — submits public key, gets `pending` registration
2. Admin reviews and approves via dashboard or `POST /agent_registrations/:id/approve { role_id: 3 }`
3. Agent polls with `aid-request --auth <url> --poll`
4. Once approved, agent uses `aid-token` as normal

**Security**: Agents never choose their own role or permissions. The admin assigns the role during approval.

## Backend endpoints required (23blocks Auth API)

| Endpoint | Auth | Purpose |
|----------|------|---------|
| `POST /agent_registrations/request` | None (public) | Agent submits registration request |
| `POST /agent_registrations/:id/approve` | Admin JWT | Approve + assign role |
| `POST /agent_registrations/:id/reject` | Admin JWT | Reject request |
| `POST /agent_registrations/:id/status` | Fingerprint proof | Agent polls status |

## Test plan

- [ ] `aid-request --help` shows usage
- [ ] `aid-request --auth <url>` submits registration (once backend is ready)
- [ ] `aid-request --auth <url> --poll` checks status
- [ ] Duplicate request detection (existing pending/active registration)
- [ ] 404 fallback message for servers that don't support agent-initiated registration

body:
In zio_ddt_write(), have_dvas and is_ganged were computed from DVAs in DDT before dde_io_lock was taken.  Due to race conditions it was possible to produce empty/corrupted block pointers, resulting in blocks read as all zeroes instead of the actual data.  The problem exists only in ZFS 2.4.

This PR merges https://github.com/openzfs/zfs/pull/18544 from OpenZFS.

### Motivation
- Corrigir o fluxo onde o bloco de foto aparece quando `fotoDisponivel = "Sim"` mas o upload não era disparado ao salvar/finalizar triagem porque o `idCaso` definitivo não estava sendo capturado/persistido nem a rotina de upload era acionada automaticamente.
- Assegurar que o upload de imagem ocorra apenas após a persistência do caso com `idCaso` definitivo para evitar fotos órfãs ou pastas temporárias (`CV-...`).

### Description
- Adicionada a função `salvarFotoDepoisDaTriagem(idCasoRecebido)` que usa explicitamente o `idCaso` recebido, lê o arquivo via `FileReader` e chama `chamarAcaoGAS('uploadFotoCaso', payload)` com `action`, `idCaso`, `talaoPMESP`, `base64`, `mimeType` e `nomeArquivo`, além de logar a resposta com `console.log('[FOTO][UPLOAD] resposta:', ...)`.

- Se houver arquivo selecionado ou link de foto, `fotoDisponivel` é preservado/ajustado para `"Sim"` e, quando houver `arquivoFoto` e `idCaso` definitivo, o código chama automaticamente `await salvarFotoDepoisDaTriagem(idCaso)` sem alterar o fluxo principal de gravação.

author: jdavidtanner
body:
### Motivation

- Provide a clear project license and entry README so the repository is consumable and installable. 
- Make core analysis and orchestration runnable in environments without optional heavy dependencies by adding deterministic, dependency-free fallbacks. 
- Improve robustness of phase runners, curvature aggregation, model loading, and statistical utilities to handle edge cases, device availability, and missing cached artifacts.

### Description

- Add `LICENSE` (MIT) and `README.md` documenting project purpose, installation, quick checks and CLI entry points. 
- Enhance `ArtifactStore` to fallback to pickle when parquet writes/read fail and make `load_df` check for fallback files, and tighten some type annotations. 
- Improve model loading with `resolve_device` and safer device resolution and ensure the loader uses the resolved `device`. 
- Make `CurvatureAggregator` tolerant to different hidden-state shapes by normalizing 1D and >2D arrays and adjust proxy registry/order and `from_config` typing. 
- Replace external `scipy.stats` usages with dependency-free helpers in `utils/statistical_utils.py` providing `pearsonr`, `spearmanr`, partial correlation, FDR, bootstraps and effect sizes. 
- Provide deterministic lexical fallback NLI scorer in `semantics/nli_scorer.py` when sentence-transformers is unavailable, using token overlap and lexical cues. 
- Add a NumPy-based OLS fallback in `regression/ols_regression.py` so regression works without `statsmodels` (previously used a sklearn fallback). 
- Refactor Phase runners (`phase1`..`phase6`) to: use resolved model device, extract and stack hidden states across variants/examples, compute curvature across stacked states, implement deterministic probe simulation when toy models or tokenizers are missing, use parquet/pickle cache fallbacks, and skip plotting when no data is available. 
- Tidy imports, logging usage, and small API fixes (e.g., `generate`/tokenizer usage and hidden-state indexing) across modules to eliminate flaky behavior.

### Testing

- Ran unit tests with `python -m pytest tests/unit` and the suite completed successfully. 
- Performed a quick import/byte-compile check with `python -m compileall -q curvature_semantics tests` which succeeded.

Stage 2 of [\`pre-release-final-pieces.md\`](https://github.com/ingcreators/annot/blob/main/docs/plans/pre-release-final-pieces.md)
— adds the Changesets CLI + config + workflow docs to prepare
for the first npm publish (Phase 3 of [\`headless-annotator-publish.md\`](https://github.com/ingcreators/annot/blob/main/docs/plans/headless-annotator-publish.md)).

## What lands

- \`@changesets/cli\` as a root devDependency (resolved \`2.31.0\`)

- Flipping any package to \`private: false\` — Stage 2 of
  the publish plan
- Changesets GitHub Action / bot — separate decision
- Touching the root \`CHANGELOG.md\` — Changesets writes

## Summary
- Wrap chat-completion response parse in try/catch and re-throw as `UpstreamError` so the raw upstream body is logged via `error_event.upstream_body` when validation fails
- Currently a plain `ZodError` is thrown and the malformed JSON is discarded — we get 22+ daily 500s on `mistral-large` with `usage:null` and no way to see what Portkey/Azure actually returned
- Schema NOT loosened: we still reject responses without proper usage (billing depends on it); this PR just gives us debug visibility into the root cause

## Background

Investigation of Mistral errors (#11039 logging) surfaced a pattern: `mistral-large` + `response_format: json_object` + non-streaming returns ZodError "usage: expected object, received null". Direct Azure + direct Portkey replays of the failing payload both return proper usage objects. Production fails with empty `upstream_body` because the Zod error path doesn't capture it.

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` clean on gen + enter

author: ejdutton
body:
## Summary

- `vat build`, `vat verify`, and `vat skills validate` previously failed to discover skills when a `skills.include` pattern stepped out of the package via `..` (e.g. `"../../docs/skills/*/SKILL.md"` in monorepos where SKILL.md sources live alongside, not inside, the package). The shared `discoverSkillsFromConfig` helper handed every pattern to a single downward-only crawl rooted at `projectRoot`, so `..` segments could never resolve to a real file. `vat audit` accepted the same config only because it has a separate filesystem-first walker.
- Each include pattern is now split into a literal base + glob remainder via `picomatch.scan`, patterns are grouped by their resolved absolute base, and the crawler runs once per base. User-supplied excludes stay anchored to `projectRoot` so anchored patterns like `docs/private/**` keep their original meaning. A pattern resolving to a nonexistent base now silently produces zero matches (matching audit's tolerance) rather than crashing.

## Test plan

- [x] New integration test `packages/cli/test/integration/skills-include-parent-traversal.integration.test.ts` — 6 cases (inside, outside via `..`, mixed inside+outside, literal include path, user-supplied excludes, nonexistent base). All four `..`-using cases fail on `main`'s code and pass on this branch.
- [x] `bun run validate` — all phases pass (lint, typecheck, duplication check, unit, integration, system).
- [x] No back-compat shim per pre-1.0 policy; semantics for in-package include patterns (no `..`) are preserved end-to-end (covered by existing integration + system suites).

author: mathieulrl
body:
Adds `derivePRFKeyForSmartAccount` to derive a deterministic 32-byte secret from a passkey and a caller-provided salt via the WebAuthn PRF extension. Same `(passkey, salt)` always yields the same output, making it suitable for seeding external accounts (e.g. Bermuda), deriving symmetric keys for in-browser encryption, or any use case needing a stable secret tied to a passkey without exposing the underlying signing key.

Public surface:
- `derivePRFKeyForSmartAccount` (SDK)
- `useDerivePRFKey` (React hook)
- `WebAuthnExtensions`, `PRFExtensionInput`, `PRFExtensionOutput` (types)
- `PRFNotSupportedError`, `PRFDerivationFailedError` (errors)

Works without re-registration on synced passkeys (Apple Passwords, Google Password Manager, 1Password, etc.). Hardware FIDO2 keys require PRF to be requested at credential creation via
`webAuthnOptions.extensions = { prf: {} }`.

## Overview

This pull request significantly stabilizes FILEX and moves it from a largely architectural prototype toward an operationally testable endpoint monitoring platform.

The focus of this work was backend stabilization, runtime lifecycle fixes, investigation workspace integration, and enabling end-to-end demo-mode validation.

---

## What Has Been Built So Far

### Core Platform Foundation
Implemented the foundational architecture for FILEX:

- Application bootstrap and lifecycle management
- Configuration management
- Structured logging
- Dependency injection / service wiring
- SQLite persistence layer with migrations
- Repository-based data access
- Event-driven architecture using EventBus

---

### Monitoring & Detection Pipeline
Implemented the endpoint telemetry pipeline:

- Filesystem monitoring engine
- File event normalization
- Detection engine with rule-based evaluation
- Detection cooldown protection
- Async event processing
- Alert engine with correlation + suppression
- Incident generation pipeline

Pipeline architecture:

```text
Filesystem
→ MonitoringEngine
→ EventBus
→ DetectionEngine
→ AlertEngine
→ Incident Persistence
→ Investigation Workspace

### Motivation
- The CI lint run failed due to `no-undef` errors in `docs/site.js` because the file uses browser globals (`document`, `window`, `navigator`) and the file relied on an `eslint-env` comment style not recognized by the flat ESLint config.

### Description
- Add an explicit globals declaration at the top of `docs/site.js` using `/* global document, navigator, window */` so ESLint recognizes the browser globals and the file no longer triggers `no-undef` errors.

- Ran `npm run lint` and the command completed successfully with `0 errors` while existing warnings remained unchanged.

## Summary

- `calculation-verifier` エージェントの検証で、README.md / CLAUDE.md の複利計算式が実装と乖離していることが判明
- 実装は**年次複利**（年初に12ヶ月分を一括追加 → 年利を適用）だが、ドキュメントは月次複利として記載されていた

## Changes

| ファイル | 変更内容 |
|--------|--------|
| `README.md` | 複利の計算式を年次複利に修正 |
| `CLAUDE.md` | 同上 |

## Before / After

**Before（誤）**
```
月次利率 = 年利率 ÷ 12
各月末資産 = (前月末資産 + 月次積立額) × (1 + 月次利率)
```

**After（正）**
```
各年末資産 = (前年末資産 + 月次積立額 × 12) × (1 + 年利率)
```

author: coldfrenzy
body:
When using an RNN, the sequence length was directly linked to n_envs_per_worker:
```
sequence_length = -(
    -self.experiment_config.collected_frames_per_batch(self.on_policy)
    // self.experiment_config.n_envs_per_worker(self.on_policy)
)
```
For large values of collected_frames_per_batch, this requires a high number of n_envs_per_workers. This can cause problems or overhead in non-vectorized and CPU environments. 
The goal of this pull request is to remove this dependency and use fixed sized sequence length by leveraging the hidden state obtained during the collection phase.

## Summary
- Ship the v0.2 stretch bulk-curated-edge import flow so an operator can seed the consumer's prose `INVENTORY.md` cross-system graph at onboarding in one declarative pass.
- Add `meho topology bulk-import <file> [--dry-run] [--json]` reading YAML / JSON and `POST /api/v1/topology/edges/bulk` posting the whole batch in one atomic transaction; `tenant_admin`-only.
- Extract `annotate_edge_in_txn` from `annotate_edge` so the bulk service can iterate the existing per-row annotate logic inside a single shared `session.begin()` block — backwards-compat preserved (every single-edge caller sees the same audit row + broadcast event).

## Atomicity decision

The issue body offered two valid semantics (atomic OR partial-with-failure-reporting). v0.2 ships atomic-only because:

- The consumer's `INVENTORY.md` is the source of truth; a partially-applied batch leaves the operator without a clean re-run path.
- An atomic failure surfaces the bad row with the structured 422 `invalid_bulk` envelope (one fix-and-rerun pass rather than the walk-the-file-N-times loop per-row 422s would force).
- A future `--continue-on-error` mode is back-compat and can ship in a follow-up.

The chosen semantics are documented in the bulk_import.py docstring and the `docs/codebase/topology.md` "Bulk import" section.

author: keough99
body:
🚨 **Severity:** MEDIUM
💡 **Vulnerability:** The existing hide-first frame-busting logic attempted to reassign `window.top.location = window.self.location` when detecting clickjacking. If the page was embedded in an iframe with `sandbox="allow-scripts"` (missing `allow-top-navigation`), modern browsers threw an unhandled `DOMException`.
🎯 **Impact:** The unhandled exception caused stack traces and internal execution context to leak into the console, potentially aiding attackers in recon by exposing script structure, while failing to gracefully recover. 
🔧 **Fix:** Wrapped the `window.top.location` assignment in a `try...catch` block. The exception is now caught and a generic, non-sensitive warning is logged instead.
✅ **Verification:** Verified by loading the page inside a test iframe with restrictive sandbox permissions. Monitored Playwright's console events to ensure the error was correctly caught and no page exceptions leaked. Tests ran and passed. Also added the vulnerability details to Sentinel's journal.

author: sectoramen
body:
## Summary

Closes the four Major findings from the threat-model review (TM-01..TM-04), the Minor bug fixes that came with it, gosec false-positive cleanup, pre-commit noise, and a pass of OSS-readiness URL/attribution hygiene.

- **Web UI hardening** — bind to `127.0.0.1` by default with container auto-detection, Origin/Referer CSRF guard, and a CSP/X-Frame-Options/X-Content-Type-Options/Referrer-Policy middleware on every response.
- **Real bug fixes** — rune-vs-byte similarity bug in plaintext redactor telemetry; TOCTOU race in output_manager cleanup (fixed via `os.OpenRoot`).
- **Repo hygiene** — internal `code.aws.dev` clone URL replaced with `github.com/awslabs/ferret-scan`; internal Slack channel and `@amazon.com` contacts replaced with GitHub Issues links; release script repointed from GitLab pipelines to GitHub Actions; `.gitlab-ci.yml` parameterized with built-in CI vars.
- **Pre-commit** — bumped Go pin to 1.26.3, fixed PGP marker obfuscation tripping `detect-private-key`, fixed two YAML syntax errors in the example pre-commit config, bumped the ferret-scan hook from v1.5.0 to v1.5.2 (v1.5.0 had a broken bin path).
- **gosec** — went from 28 false positives to 0 by adding inline `// #nosec` annotations with bounded-input rationale on the relevant 25 sites.

Detailed breakdown is in the commit message.

## Threat model status

| ID | Title | Status |
|---|---|---|
| TM-01 | Web UI binds to all interfaces | **Mitigated** |
| TM-02 | CSRF on mutating endpoints | **Mitigated** |
| TM-03 | Missing security headers | **Mitigated (defense-in-depth)** |
| TM-04 | Suppression endpoints lack auth | **Mitigated** (closed by TM-01) |
| TM-05 | Strict CSP requires template refactor | Open (tracked) |
| TM-06 | Cloudscape stylesheet on third-party CDN | Open (tracked) |
| TM-07 | Transcribe SSRF defense-in-depth | Deferred (GenAI disabled) |

## Test plan

- [x] `make build` clean
- [x] `go vet ./...` clean
- [x] `go test -count=1 ./...` — all 23 packages pass, 30+ new unit tests in `internal/web`, `internal/redactors`, `internal/redactors/plaintext`
- [x] Manual smoke tests on the freshly-built binary:
  - default bind is `127.0.0.1` (`lsof` confirms `localhost:port`, not `*:port`)
  - `FERRET_CONTAINER_MODE=true` env auto-binds to `0.0.0.0` with stderr warning
  - `--bind 127.0.0.1` overrides the env (priority order works)
  - All four security headers present on `GET /health`
  - Cross-origin POST `Origin: http://evil.example` → 403; same-origin → 200; no-Origin (curl) → 200
  - File-mode CLI scan unchanged (regression check)
  - Stdin scan + streaming redaction unchanged (regression check)
- [x] `pre-commit run --all-files` — 15/16 hooks pass
- [ ] Reviewer to confirm the ferret-scan hook's documentation false-positives (example SSN/CC patterns in our own docs) are fine to handle as a follow-up suppression PR rather than blocking on this branch.

## Risk

The bind-default change is the highest-blast-radius edit. Bare-metal users running `ferret-scan --web` without `--bind 0.0.0.0` will lose LAN visibility — that's intentional, and the stderr warning + README hardening note explain the new default. Container users (Docker, Podman, K8s) keep working unchanged because of the `/.dockerenv` / `FERRET_CONTAINER_MODE` auto-detection.

author: elitonzky
body:
## What
Adds a new authenticated endpoint that the front-end calls when the user
clicks "Contact support" on the onboarding error screen. The endpoint
accepts a generic `data` payload built by the front-end and forwards it
to a dedicated Slack channel together with a full snapshot of the
current `ProjectOnboarding` state.
### Endpoint
- `POST /api/onboard/<vtex_account>/support-contact/`
- Auth: Keycloak OIDC (`KeycloakAPIView`) — same as `start-setup`, `status`, `install-agents`
- Body: `{"data": {...arbitrary object...}}` (optional, default `{}`)
- Response: `202 Accepted` with `{"status": "received"}`
### Architecture (Views → Use Case → Service → Slack Client)
- `OnboardingSupportContactView` (thin — only validates and delegates)
- `RequestOnboardingSupportSerializer` validates `data` as a dict
- `RequestOnboardingSupportDTO` carries `vtex_account` + `data`
- `RequestOnboardingSupportUseCase` fetches the onboarding (with `select_related("project")`), builds a snapshot dict containing every field of `ProjectOnboarding` plus the linked `Project`, and dispatches the notification
- `OnboardingSupportNotificationService` renders a Slack Block Kit message with an overview grid, UUIDs section, last recorded failure, full config JSON (truncated at 2500 chars), and the front-end payload (truncated at 2500 chars)
### Fail-safety
- Always returns 202 — Slack outages, missing onboarding records or DB
  errors do not block the support request from reaching the team
- The service catches every exception and uses `logger.exception` so the
  Sentry event includes the full traceback
## Why
When the onboarding fails the front-end already routes the user to a
"Contact support" screen. Until now there was no programmatic way for
the user to actually contact the team — the screen was a dead-end. This
PR closes that loop: the click reaches the support team in real time
with the full onboarding state, allowing investigation without polling
the database or chasing logs.

Phase **P2-G** — the last additive phase. **Stacked on #251 (P2-I)** → #249 → #245. Base is the P2-I branch (P2-G-only diff).

## What

Folds the legacy `queries.select(on=/crossing=/not_on=/not_crossing=)` + `queries.line` straddle predicate (HT9) into the unified idiom as one verb `crossing_plane(spec, *, tol=1e-6, mode)` — mirroring the legacy `_select_impl`s mode-parameterized shape (one verb, not four — CLAUDE.md §2). `spec` is the legacy `_parse_primitive` grammar (dict→axis `Plane`, **2 points→`Line`** folding in `queries.line`, 3 points→`Plane`); `tol` default byte-identical. Additive — touches only `_kernel/chain.py` + `core/_selection.py` entity hooks + tests. Legacy `queries.select`/`_select_impl`/`Plane`/`Line`/`_bb_corners` **byte-unchanged** (P3 removes them).

Base concrete verb in `_kernel/chain.py` → `_spatial_crossing` hook (a `REQUIRED_VERBS` verb, **never** a `_REQUIRED_HOOKS` entry); point-family base raises loud `TypeError` (entity-only — the `GeometryChain.in_box` `inclusive=`→`TypeError` precedent); `EntitySelection`+`GeometryChain` override via one shared `core/_selection._crossing_impl` porting `_select_impl` semantics exactly.

## STOP-1 intra-ordering held (plan §6.1)

The unsafe move was touching `REQUIRED_VERBS` before the verb is inherited-callable (would kill `import apeGmsh` for all 7 chains). Executed strictly: (1) base verb + loud-raise hook *[import OK, `REQUIRED_VERBS` untouched]* → (2) entity overrides *[import OK]* → (3) append `crossing_plane` to `REQUIRED_VERBS` **last** *[import OK; all 7 concrete chains pass `__init_subclass__`]*. Same-commit `test_selection_idiom` signature carve-out (the `in_box` template, a forward-lock for P3).

## Gate (independently verified by the lead)

- `import apeGmsh` clean; `apeGmsh.__file__` under the worktree; `crossing_plane in REQUIRED_VERBS`
- 4 proof tests + `test_import_dag_polarity` **BASELINE** + `viz/Selection.py` **byte-unchanged**

body:
## Summary

Adds a `local.iface.stable:<name>` provider for Linux hosts that need DDNS to publish a stable IPv6 address instead of temporary privacy addresses.

The provider reads `/proc/net/if_inet6`, filters to the selected interface, excludes temporary, deprecated, tentative, and DAD-failed addresses, and returns the preferred stable global IPv6 candidate. IPv4 still delegates to the existing `local.iface:<name>` behavior.

## Why

On Linux hosts with IPv6 privacy extensions enabled, `local` or `local.iface:<name>` can publish temporary IPv6 addresses. Those rotate and can leave AAAA records stale. This gives users a provider-level way to keep host privacy behavior enabled while publishing a more stable address for DNS.

## Validation

- `cargo test test_provider_parse_stable_local_iface`
- `cargo test test_parse_if_inet6_line`
- `cargo test test_stable_ipv6_addresses_from_if_inet6_filters_privacy_addresses`
- `cargo test test_provider_type_name`
- `cargo test -- --test-threads=1 --skip test_build_split_client_v4 --skip test_build_split_client_v6`
- Local dry-run confirmed `IP6_PROVIDER=local.iface.stable:<interface>` selected one stable AAAA candidate.

author: nimrod-teich
body:
## Summary

Two cleanups, both deletion-heavy, surfaced during end-to-end release-pipeline validation (the `v0.0.1-test` maiden voyage in PR #29 / #30 / #33).

### README polish

- **Build-targets list** (`README.md` → Development → Build targets) didn't list `make snapshot`, `make setup`, or `make install`. Added.
- **Quick Start** said `make install-all` — that alias is going away in the Makefile section below; switched to `make install`.
- **Buildx install hint** said `sudo apt install docker-buildx-plugin` without distinguishing `docker-ce` (Docker's apt repo) vs `docker.io` (Ubuntu's stock package). The plugin doesn't exist in `docker.io` — hit this in practice on a WSL2 / `docker.io` setup: `apt` returns "Unable to locate package". Rewrote the paragraph to be honest about both paths, with the manual CLI-plugin install command for `docker.io` users.
- **Pulling the image (private repo)** subsection added — the repo is private, so anonymous `docker pull` returns `unauthorized`. New subsection covers the PAT-with-`read:packages` auth recipe and the alternative of flipping the package (not repo) visibility to public if you want unauthenticated pulls.

### Makefile — remove redundant aliases

Inherited from upstream Lava back when there were multiple binaries:

```diff
- install-all: install
  install:
- install-smartrouter: install
  ...
- build-all: build
  build:
- BINDIR ?= $(GOPATH)/bin   # declared, never used
```

With only `smartrouter` as the binary, the `*-all` and `install-smartrouter` aliases are all dispatched to the same target — pure noise. `BINDIR` was declared but never referenced anywhere (`go install` reads `$GOBIN` / `$GOPATH/bin` directly).

After cleanup: `make install` and `make build` are the only entry points. `.PHONY` trimmed accordingly.

## Net diff

```
 Makefile  | 12 ++----------
 README.md | 23 ++++++++++++++---------
 2 files changed, 16 insertions(+), 19 deletions(-)
```

(PR previously included Build-provenance / Reproducing-locally / Verifying-a-release subsections that were over-detail for the README; trimmed those out in the second commit.)

## Test plan

- [ ] Render the README on GitHub, verify formatting.
- [ ] Build targets in README match `.PHONY` in Makefile exactly.
- [ ] `make -n install` / `make -n build` / `make -n setup` / `make -n snapshot` all expand correctly (verified locally before push).
- [ ] No external automation calls the removed targets — only known caller was the README's Quick Start, updated in this PR.

author: kvestboe
body:
This PR introduces two major features: persistent save files, a full load game screen.

Game sessions are now saved to disk as JSON files using Jackson, replacing the previous in-memory repository. Each session is serialized to a DTO and written to a saves/ directory. An in-memory cache sits in front of the file layer to preserve object identity, which is required for the observer pattern between the exchange and UI controllers.

The load game screen lets players browse all existing saves in a table, inspect details like net worth, week, and status in a detail panel, and either load or delete a save. It is wired into the main menu through AppRouter.

author: krishanraja
body:
## Summary

Replaced the scroll-driven three-act narrative in the BigProblem section with an interactive flip-card interface. Cards now toggle between "fate" and "value" faces on tap/click, with a mobile carousel for smaller screens and a desktop grid layout. Removed all Framer Motion scroll transforms and timeline orchestration in favor of simple state-driven animations.

## Key Changes

- **Removed scroll-driven animation system**: Eliminated `useScroll`, `useTransform`, and the complex three-act narrative (eyebrow fade, headline crossfades, card morphing wipe, beam sweep, CTA reveal). Removed ~200 lines of scroll-progress orchestration.

- **Introduced interactive flip-card component**: New `FlipCard` component with 3D perspective transforms. Cards flip on click/tap via `[transform:rotateY(180deg)]` with CSS `[backface-visibility:hidden]` for front/back face culling. Keyboard accessible (Enter/Space to flip).

- **Added mobile carousel**: Implemented Embla Carousel for mobile (basis-[85%] snap), with dot indicators for slide navigation. Desktop remains a 3-column grid.

- **Refactored card faces**: Split into `CardFace` (front/back wrapper with glow shadow and corner chrome) and `CardChrome` (number badge, corner ticks, radial gradient overlay). Larger icons (w-12 h-12 → w-16 h-16 on desktop), improved typography hierarchy.

- **Updated CTA interactions**: 
  - "Tap to flip" hint badge on fate face (with RotateCw icon)
  - "Build this with me" button on value face, dispatches `openConsultModal` with card index
  - Main section CTA now opens consult modal with "big-problem" preselection

- **Reduced motion support**: Respects `useReducedMotion()` from Framer Motion; when true, hides the back face and disables 3D transforms, showing both faces statically.

- **Simplified layout**: Removed ambient glow, progress rail, section break dividers, and scroll-pinning. Section now uses standard padding (py-20 md:py-32) with container-width max-w-6xl.

- **Updated imports**: Removed `motion`, `useScroll`, `useTransform` from Framer Motion. Added `Carousel` components from `@/components/ui/carousel`. Changed icon from `ArrowDown` to `ArrowRight`.

## Implementation Details

- State: `flipped` array tracks flip state per card; `api` and `activeSlide` manage carousel state.
- Accessibility: Cards are `role="button"` with `tabIndex={0}`, `aria-pressed`, and `aria-label`. Keyboard handlers for Enter/Space. Focus ring on card face.
- Styling: Uses Tailwind's `[perspective:1400px]` and `[transform-style:preserve-3d]` for 3D context. Mint glow shadow with hover intensification. Corner ticks and number badge for trading-card aesthetic.
- Modal dispatch: `openConsultModal()` helper function sends custom event with optional preselection detail.

Sitemap lastmod dates updated to 2026-05-18.

author: cyber-ayi
body:
## Summary

The `xxhash` optional extra was declared in `pyproject.toml` and the comment promised "either way we fall back to this Python implementation" — but `hash_file_local` **never imported it**. So `xxh3`/`xxh128` local hashing always shelled out to a per-file `rclone hashsum` subprocess: a process spawn per file, and (after #38) only file-granularity progress.

This wires it up.

## Changes

- **`hashing`**: soft-import `xxhash`; map `xxh3→xxh3_64`, `xxh128→xxh3_128`, `xxh64→xxh64`. New `can_stream_local(algo)` predicate.
- **`hash_file_local`**: streams xxhash exactly like hashlib (chunk loop + `progress_cb`) → a single large `xxh3` file now drives the live meter per-chunk at disk speed instead of file granularity.
- **`manifest._refresh_local`**: uses `can_stream_local()` to pick windowed-EMA vs cumulative metering.

## Correctness (critical)

xxhash digests are verified **byte-identical to rclone's** output (`rclone xxh3 == xxh3_64`, `xxh128 == xxh3_128`) — so an in-process src manifest still matches an rclone-hashed dst; no false "missing"/re-copy. Verified three ways: manual, chunked-stream vs one-shot, and a test that diffs against a live `rclone hashsum` (skipped when rclone absent).

## Tests

- New: rclone byte-parity, chunked-stream parity, `can_stream_local` truth table.
- The #38 regression test retargeted to a genuinely non-streamable algo (`crc32`) — it was a false-positive once xxhash made `xxh3` streamable.
- **198 pass.**

Version 0.2.1 → 0.3.0 (backward-compatible; same digests, faster, finer progress). Follow-up to #37/#38.

## Summary

- Adds Swiss VALOR (Valorennummer) detection to `siphon-core`
- VALOR is a Swiss securities identifier used by SIX Swiss Exchange (1–9 digit numeric, context-gated)
- Previously a false-positive side effect of Malta TIN's broad regex (addressed in #274) — this PR adds deliberate, context-gated detection
- Examples: `1213853` (Nestlé), `3190000` (Swiss Re)
- Rebased onto main — picks up Postgres phase A+B (#287, #288) and `chore(api): rustfmt db.rs` to keep `cargo fmt --check` green

body:
# Problem
---

Currently, MediScan AI requires users to manually type medicine names before retrieving information. This creates a major accessibility barrier for:

* Elderly users
* Patients with lower technical literacy
* Users unfamiliar with complex pharmaceutical terminology
* Users dealing with difficult-to-spell generic names

Medicine strips, prescription labels, and packaging already contain the required information visually, but the platform had no way to process image-based inputs directly.

---
---

# Solution
---

This PR introduces a **Multimodal OCR & Prescription Strip Scanner** that allows users to upload or capture photos of:

* Medicine strips
* Bottle labels
* Printed prescriptions

The system automatically extracts the active ingredient using a vision model and pipes the detected medicine name directly into the existing MediScan AI pipeline.

---
---

# Architecture Flow
---

1. User uploads medicine strip image
2. Client validates and compresses image
3. Base64 payload sent to `/api/scan-medicine`
4. Vision model extracts active ingredient
5. Existing medicine pipeline fetches medicine data
6. Existing UI renderer displays results seamlessly

---
---

# Acceptance Criteria
---

* [x] OCR scan button integrated into existing UI
* [x] Client-side file validation implemented
* [x] Image downscaling added before transmission
* [x] Thumbnail preview with remove/reset functionality added
* [x] OCR extracts medicine names while ignoring packaging noise
* [x] Blurry/unreadable images handled gracefully
* [x] Scanned results integrated into analytics and history
* [x] Existing actions (Copy, PDF, WhatsApp, Favorites) support scanned results
* [x] Dark/light theme compatibility verified
* [x] No new external dependencies introduced

---
---

# Testing Performed
---

* Tested clear medicine strip uploads
* Verified OCR extraction accuracy
* Tested unsupported file rejection
* Verified blurry image error handling
* Confirmed scan history integration
* Tested PDF export and sharing features on scanned results
* Verified responsive rendering across themes

---
---

- **Screenshots.** A Screenshot button next to Stop captures your screen during a meeting. Screenshots are saved with the recording and sent to Claude as visual context so summaries can reference what was on screen.

author: ficcaglia
body:
## Summary

Fixes a local privilege escalation vulnerability in the `runInit()` function where a predictable PID-based temporary filename in world-writable `/tmp` could be pre-planted with a symlink by a local attacker.

## Changes

- **Replace predictable temp file with secure directory**: Changed from using a PID-based filename (`caveman-init-{process.pid}.js`) to atomically creating a fresh temporary directory with `fs.mkdtempSync()`, which creates it with mode `0700` (owner-only access).
- **Improve cleanup**: Updated cleanup logic to use `fs.rmSync()` with `recursive: true` to remove the entire temporary directory and its contents, wrapped in a `finally` block to ensure cleanup happens regardless of success or failure.
- **Add security comment**: Documented the security rationale for using `mkdtempSync` to prevent symlink-based attacks.

## Implementation Details

The vulnerability existed because:
1. The temp filename was predictable (based on process ID)
2. It was created in a world-writable directory (`/tmp`)
3. An attacker could pre-create a symlink at that path before the script ran

The fix uses `fs.mkdtempSync()` which:
- Atomically creates a directory with secure permissions (`0700`)
- Makes symlink pre-planting impossible (the directory creation would fail if a symlink already exists)
- Provides a safe location for the downloaded script

Cleanup is now guaranteed via the `finally` block, ensuring the temporary directory is removed even if the spawned process fails.

## Summary

Two cleanups left over from Phase 2 + a full rewrite of the insight engine's output text.

### Section moves on `/monthly`

- **Monthly Flows (Equity / Debt / Liquid)** moved **up** from its old spot between SIP Trends and Section 4 into the end of **Section 2 (Industry flow)**. It's a flow chart and belongs with the AMFI Snapshot + AUM Mix, not buried after SIP.
- **Industry Folios & NFO** moved **up** from Section 5 (where it sat after Category Resilience / Heatmap) into **Section 3 (Retail pulse)**. Within this section the NFO trends are now collapsed behind a *"Show NFO launch + funds-mobilised trends"* disclosure; the **Folio Additions Trend** stays visible because it's the headline retail-pulse chart.

### Insight engine prose rewrite

Every rule output now reads like an analyst's one-liner instead of an engine emit. Comparing old vs new headlines:

| Rule | Old | New |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ATH/ATL | "X at an all-time high on the available window — Y." | "X at an all-time high — Y." |
| σ-spike | "Latest MoM change +X is +2.3σ vs the typical period change — an unusual move." | "+X MoM — biggest move in recent history (+2.3σ vs typical)." |
| Multi-period | "X at its highest in 18 periods (last matched 2023-08)." | "Highest in 18 periods — last topped 2023-08." |
| Episode | "X at its lowest since the FY23 correction." | "Lowest since the FY23 correction." |
| Run | "X has risen for 3 consecutive periods." | "Up for 3 straight periods." |
| YoY | "X +18.4% YoY · accelerating from +12.1% last period." | "+18.4% YoY — accelerating from +12.1% last period." |
| Cycle | "Latest reading sits inside a Correction cycle phase (Nifty 500 in drawdown)." | "Reading lands inside the current Correction phase." |
| Drawdown | "Coincides with Nifty 500 in a 13.4% drawdown." | "Reads against a Nifty 500 down 13.4%." |
| Fallback | "Latest reading is +X% vs the trailing 12-period average (Y)." | "+X% vs trailing 12-period average." |

The **metric name** (e.g. "SIP contribution") is dropped from most outputs because it's already in the chart title right above the headline — repeating it was noise.

## Summary

Adds `spec.auth` + `spec.exposure` to ObserveStack so internal dashboards (Prometheus, Alertmanager, OpenCost) can be reached from the public internet behind Zitadel OIDC, per `[[specs/platform-public-exposure]]`. The bridge is composed fully:

- **ExternalSecret** pulling the Zitadel iam-admin PAT from AWS Secrets Manager (matches AuthStack's `consumer-providerconfig.yaml` shape inline — no per-cluster authoring).
- **Namespaced Zitadel ProviderConfig** sourcing that Secret.
- **Zitadel OIDC Application MR** via `provider-upjet-zitadel` (declarative, per direction during planning rather than out-of-band). Provider writes `client_id` + `client_secret` into a K8s Secret oauth2-proxy mounts.
- **Single-replica Redis** StatefulSet for oauth2-proxy sessions (PVC, no TLS in v1 — ambient mTLS provides transport security between the two pods).
- **Waypoint Gateway** in the observe namespace + per-component **sister Services** labeled `istio.io/use-waypoint`.
- **HTTPRoute** per component — two-rule (`/oauth2/*` → oauth2-proxy, `/` → sister Service).
- **AuthorizationPolicy.CUSTOM** per component, `provider.name` matches the IstioStack-registered extensionProvider (consumes `[[tasks/istio-stack-extension-providers]]`).
- **Optional cert-manager Certificate** when the platform wildcard at the Gateway doesn't already cover `spec.exposure.domain`.

Grafana app-level OIDC intentionally not included — split into `[[tasks/observe-stack-grafana-oidc]]` for a smaller focused follow-up.

Operator pre-requisites:
1. Cookie-signing Secret in the observe namespace (`kubectl create secret generic <name> --from-literal=cookie_secret=$(openssl rand -hex 16)`).
2. Register matching extensionProvider entry on IstioStack.
3. Zitadel project ID provided via `spec.auth.zitadelProjectId`.

## End-to-end verification on pat-local

Composed OIDC client got `client_id=373507418958665326` in Zitadel ("platform-services" project). Curl through the live stack (from inside the cluster):

```
$ curl -D - http://exposure-prometheus.monitoring:9090/
HTTP/1.1 302 Found
location: https://auth.ops.com.ai/oauth/v2/authorize?client_id=373507418958665326&redirect_uri=...%2Foauth2%2Fcallback&...
set-cookie: _oauth2_proxy_csrf=...; Domain=ops.com.ai; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax
```

Waypoint Envoy access log: `302 UAEX ext_authz_denied - inbound-vip|9090|http|exposure-prometheus.monitoring.svc.cluster.local` — UAEX = canonical Envoy `ext_authz_denied` response flag, proving the waypoint really called the registered ext_authz upstream and acted on the response.

## Known limitations (carry into release notes)

- **Platform Gateway → Waypoint routing**: requests entering through the public ELB currently bypass the per-namespace waypoint and HBONE-tunnel direct to the destination pod, so the 302 redirect only fires for in-cluster ambient sources. Same gap surfaced in the istio sibling PR. Needs a follow-up for either ambient-aware gateway or a different routing approach.
- **Sister Service pod selectors** default to stock kube-prometheus-stack v77 conventions; clusters using different chart release names must override `spec.exposure.<comp>.{podSelector, serviceName}` (pat-local does this — release name is `observe`).
- **Cookie secret** still pre-created by operator. Future iteration could compose an ExternalSecret matching the AnalyticsStack pattern.

## Test plan

- [x] `make test` — 30/30 pass (28 existing + 2 new)
- [x] `make validate:all` — 8/8 examples validate (12–29 resources each)
- [x] Live install on pat-local: Zitadel OIDC client provisioned via provider; oauth2-proxy + Redis + Waypoint + sister Service all Ready
- [x] Full curl-through-the-chain proves OIDC flow + ext_authz path (see verification above)

## Summary

v0.1 had two critical defects that prevented documented use:
- Install instructions referenced `GenAIDataSecurity.md` / `/GenAIDataSecurity` but the actual file was `dsgai_scanner_tool.md` (so the literal install commands failed)
- 6 of the 21 promised DSGAI control scans had no pattern blocks defined (DSGAI08, 09, 10, 16, 17, 19)

This PR fixes both, hardens privacy guarantees, narrows noisy patterns, and ships CI integrations.

## Highlights

### 🛡️ Strict-by-default obfuscation
- Two modes: **STRICT** (filename + line only — default) and **INTERNAL** (`--internal` — full paths for team use)
- New **VALUE-BEARING SCAN PROTOCOL (V1–V6)** — matched secret values never enter the report, the on-disk checkpoint, or any persistent tool call
- Defense-in-depth secret sweep applied even on STRUCTURAL evidence
- `DSGAI-scan.json` schema pinned to forbid `match_text` / `content` fields

### ✅ All 21 controls now have scan blocks
Added DSGAI08 (Regulatory Compliance), 09 (Multimodal), 10 (Synthetic Data), 16 (IDE Plugin), 17 (Resilience), 19 (Data Labeling).

### 🏢 VENDOR ATTESTATION REQUIRED status
New finding status for BUY-tagged controls and BUY portions of BOTH. Each generates a callout listing specific vendor attestations to request (SOC 2, DPA, training data retention policy, abuse detection docs).

### 🔧 Pattern correctness
- Engine-neutral PCRE; documented prerequisite at top of Step 2
- Narrowed: P01.4 (dp libs — escaped dots), P02.7 (vault — was matching everywhere), P04.4 (version operators — `^=` wasn't valid), P11.1 (vector queries — was matching every `.query()`), P20.5 (inference endpoints — last branch was useless)

### 📡 CVE enrichment fixed
- NVD severity filter corrected (one value per call, not duplicate param)
- GitHub Advisory uses `affects=<pkg>` filter (was fetching unfiltered feed)
- Go ecosystem added to OSV queries
- MITRE ATLAS split from CVE sources into its own subsection (it's attack techniques, not CVEs)
- Rate-limit handling and API-key support documented

### 🚀 New distribution surfaces
- **GitHub Action** (`integrations/dsgai-scan.yml`) — PR comment with FAIL/WARN/PASS/Vendor/Exploitable CVE counts, artifact upload, optional fail-on-findings. Uses correct Claude Code CLI flags (`claude -p` + `--dangerously-skip-permissions`).
- **Pre-commit hook** (`integrations/pre-commit-hook.md` + `dsgai-secret-scan.sh`) — sub-second DSGAI02 secret block before commit. Three install paths (pre-commit framework, plain git hook, Husky) — all delegate to one shared script.
- **Plain-prompt variant** (`dsgai_scanner_prompt.md`) — tool-neutral version for Cursor, Copilot Chat, ChatGPT, Gemini.

### 🆕 New flags
- `--internal` — full paths for team-internal use
- `--no-cve` — fully offline / air-gapped mode
- `--scope <path>` — restrict to a sub-directory (monorepos)
- All combinable: `/dsgai_scanner_tool --internal --no-cve --scope services/ai-gateway/`

### 📚 Documentation
- YAML frontmatter (description, argument-hint, allowed-tools)
- TL;DR quick-reference table
- Known Limitations section (honest disclosure of what static scanning can't catch)
- Tier badges explainer (T1/T2/T3 colors and examples)
- Mermaid flow diagram in README
- Badges (OWASP, framework, version, license)
- Fixed "Based On" URL (was pointing to OWASP Top 10 for LLM, now correctly points to DSGAI 2026 resource page)

## Files changed

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `dsgai_scanner_tool/dsgai_scanner_tool.md` | Rewritten (1296 lines, 81 KB) |
| `dsgai_scanner_tool/DSGAI_README.md` | Rewritten (419 lines, 21 KB) |
| `dsgai_scanner_tool/dsgai_scanner_prompt.md` | NEW — plain-prompt variant |
| `dsgai_scanner_tool/CHANGES_v0.2.md` | NEW — release notes |
| `dsgai_scanner_tool/integrations/dsgai-scan.yml` | NEW — GitHub Action |

author: allenhaozhu
body:
Add `Mathlib/Probability/NoFreeLunch.lean`, the measure-theoretic finite-`k` version of the Devroye-Gyorfi-Lugosi No-Free-Lunch theorem. For any finite input type `K` of cardinality `k` and any deterministic learning algorithm `A : (Fin n → K × Bool) → (K → Bool)`, averaging the discrete misclassification risk over the `2^k` uniformly random boolean labelings `r : K → Bool` is at least `(1/2)(k − |range x|)/k` for any fixed sample-index pattern `x : Fin n → K` (`nfl_finite_k_adversary`), and averaging again over uniform `x : Fin n → K` recovers the classical DGL bound `(1/2)(1 − 1/k)^n` (`nfl_finite_k_dgl_average`). The proof uses a bit-flip involution on labelings together with the coordinate-wise factorization of the unsampled-point indicator.

This PR replaces #39167 (withdrawn), which provided only the algebraic core; reviewers requested the measure-theoretic version, which this PR provides via a finite-`k` measurable adversary on `Fintype K` together with the standard `(1 − 1/k)^n` average-over-`x` computation.

---

## AI-assistance disclosure

Per the Mathlib [AI-use policy](https://leanprover-community.github.io/contribute/index.html#use-of-ai):

- **Tool.** Claude Code (Anthropic) with the Claude Sonnet 4.6 model.
- **Use.** I specified the target lemma statements and the proof strategy; the assistant drafted Lean 4 tactic combinations against current Mathlib. I iterated on the proofs, verified each lemma builds under `lake build` from a clean checkout, and read the final code.
- **Vouching.** I have read every declaration in `Mathlib/Probability/NoFreeLunch.lean` and can defend the proofs without further AI assistance. I welcome reviewer feedback on naming, namespace placement, and stylistic alignment with the surrounding Mathlib modules.

author: pjdoland
body:
## Summary

A user reported that the Launcher tile's Claude Code session picker showed "No previous sessions found" while `/resume` inside the same Claude session listed previous sessions. Root cause: the backend used `~/.claude/history.jsonl` as the gating source for session listing. Recent Claude Code releases don't reliably populate that file for SDK-driven invocations, and the cwd-only fallback path only scanned the Jupyter root's transcript dir, so any session launched from a different cwd disappeared from both NBI pickers while Claude Code's own `/resume` (which walks the project dirs directly) continued to find them.

## Solution

Rebuild `list_all_sessions` on a direct walk of `~/.claude/projects/*/`, which is the durable on-disk source `/resume` consumes. The cwd for each session comes from the transcript's own `"cwd"` field (Claude Code writes it on most message envelopes) so paths with literal dashes round-trip correctly; a dash-decode of the directory name is only used as a fallback for older transcripts that lack the field.

The handler's `scope=cwd` filter switches from comparing transcript-path dirnames to a realpath compare on `session.cwd`, fixing symlink-alias mismatches common on JupyterHub user dirs (NFS / EFS), and memoizes the per-session realpath inside the request so a 1k-session filter on NFS doesn't fan out to 1k network round trips.

A mtime-keyed cache memoizes per-transcript parse results so repeated list calls don't re-open every `.jsonl` on each click (addresses D207 from the audit).

The Launcher tile's row now renders the cwd basename as the inline label with the full path duplicated on both `title` and `aria-label` so screen-reader users get the disambiguating path too.

## Testing

- `pytest tests/ --ignore=tests/test_claude_client.py -q` 882 passed (6 new TestCrossSurfaceConsistency cases, 1 new symlink-alias handler case, 1 new empty-cwd silent-drop pin, autouse fixture clears `_SESSION_INFO_CACHE` between tests).
- `jlpm tsc --noEmit` clean. `jlpm lint:check` clean. `jlpm jest` 183 passed (2 new `tests/ts/launcher-picker.test.tsx` cases).
- Playwright end-to-end from a fresh `notebook-dir=/tmp/nbitour`: `scope=all` returned 107 cross-project sessions (every project on the machine), each row labeled with its project basename and the full path on `title` + `aria-label`. `scope=cwd` returned 0 (no transcripts for `/tmp/nbitour`), confirming the realpath filter works.
- Six-agent review surfaced: realpath memoization in handler (applied), autouse cache fixture (applied), aria-label fallback on the span (applied), empty-cwd silent-drop test pin (applied), tightened class docstring (applied), corrected misleading code comment (applied).

## Risks / follow-ups

- The PR replaces the chat-sidebar Resume button's underlying data source but keeps it scoped to the current cwd. Cross-cwd resume from the sidebar (open a terminal + `cd` + `claude --resume`) is deferred to a follow-up; the Launcher tile remains the path for cross-project resumes.
- A shell-out integration test that runs `claude --resume` non-interactively and diffs session ids against ours is the right cross-binary check but is deferred (it needs the CLI on the Galata runner's PATH).
- `mtime` resolution on some filesystems (HFS+ 1s) could theoretically serve stale cache entries; the cache is a perf hint, not authoritative for correctness, and transcripts are append-only so collision odds are essentially zero in practice. Worth a note but not worth complicating the cache key.

author: bromso
body:
## Summary

Sub-project 4a delivers the foundation of an MCP server for Singularmem so MCP-compatible clients (Claude Code, Cursor, custom agents) can retrieve memories without going through the CLI. New crate \`singularmem-mcp\` produces a \`singularmem-mcp\` binary that speaks JSON-RPC over stdio (via the official \`rmcp\` SDK pinned at \`=1.7.0\`), handles the MCP initialize handshake, and exposes one read tool: \`memory_retrieve\`.

- New crate \`singularmem-mcp\` depending on \`singularmem-retrieve\` + the four adapter crates + \`rmcp = '=1.7.0'\` + \`tokio = '1'\` (new workspace dep) + clap/serde/tracing.
- \`memory_retrieve\` tool with three inputs: \`query\` (required), \`limit\` (optional, default 10, clamped to [1, 50]), \`adapter\` (optional enum of the four registered providers). Returns a single text content block with adapter-formatted memory.
- Configuration via CLI flags + env vars + built-in defaults (precedence: per-call arg > CLI flag > env var > built-in). All three flags have env-var equivalents.
- 10 unit tests + 1 black-box integration test that spawns the binary and exercises the full initialize → tools/list → tools/call flow.
- README with copy-pastable Claude Code + Cursor configs, tool reference, troubleshooting. \`docs/mcp-server.md\` with layering diagram + separate-binary rationale.
- stdio purity: all tracing to stderr; stdout reserved for JSON-RPC.
- Read-only foundation; sub-project 4b will add \`memory_ingest\` + utility tools.

**Tag on merge:** \`v0.9.0\` (additive MINOR bump per Principle V).

**Design spec:** \`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-18-mcp-server-4a-design.md\`

body:
## Summary

Standalone-witness now has a self-sufficient local-dev story. A developer with only this repo checked out can run a K=N witness fleet without a ledger checkout:

```sh
make run-local                       # 1 witness on :8081
make run-local WITNESS_COUNT=3       # K=3 on :8081..:8083
make dev-up WITNESS_COUNT=3          # same, but via Docker
```

Previously the README directed developers to ledger's `cmd/init-network` to produce the PEM key + bootstrap doc the daemon needs at boot — making local development effectively impossible without a side-by-side ledger checkout.

## What's new

| Path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `cmd/gen-fixtures/main.go` + `main_test.go` | In-module fixture generator: P-256 EC PEM keys + `BootstrapDocument` JSON with derived `did:key:z…`. Idempotent. Imports only the attesta SDK; module-boundary rule preserved. |
| `scripts/run-local.sh` | Go-native orchestrator. Generates fixtures, builds binary, spawns N daemons, polls `/healthz`, tracks PIDs, traps signals, prints `LEDGER_WITNESS_ENDPOINTS=…` for a separate ledger run. |
| `scripts/local/render-compose.sh` | Emits `.run/docker-compose.yml` parameterised by `WITNESS_COUNT`. Each service builds from the existing module-root `Dockerfile` and bind-mounts `.run/` read-only. |
| `scripts/local/README.dev.md` | Operator guide: three flows (Go-native, Docker, against-separate-ledger) + troubleshooting table. |
| `Makefile` | New targets: `gen-fixtures`, `run-local`, `run-local-down`, `clean-run`, `dev-preflight`, `dev-up`, `dev-down`, `dev-logs`, `dev-status`. Existing targets unchanged. |
| `README.md` | New "Quick local run (no ledger checkout required)" section. |
| `.github/workflows/go-test.yml` | New `local-smoke` job: `make run-local` → `curl /healthz` → `make run-local-down`. Catches script rot. |
| `.gitignore` | Now covers stray `go build ./cmd/…` binaries dropped at the module root. |
| `go.mod` / `go.sum` | Adds `mr-tron/base58` indirect dep pulled in by `attesta/did`, which `gen-fixtures` imports. |

## Module boundary preserved

The new code imports only `github.com/clearcompass-ai/attesta` (`did` + `network` packages). It never imports `github.com/clearcompass-ai/ledger` — the boundary that `internal/serve/serve.go` documents stays intact.

## Robustness — modelled on ledger's `scripts/run-local.sh`

The script lifts the patterns the ledger reference uses:
- `set -euo pipefail` + case-style arg parser
- preflight (`command -v go`, port-collision check via bash `/dev/tcp`)
- `go run ./cmd/gen-fixtures` for fixtures, then `go build` once, then spawn N copies
- per-port `/healthz` polling: 50 × 200 ms (10 s) per daemon
- signal trap (`EXIT INT TERM`) auto-kills tracked PIDs on Ctrl-C in the foreground window
- `down` subcommand reads `.run/witness-pids`, idempotent on missing file

- [x] `go build ./...` — clean
- [x] `go test -count=1 ./...` — all packages pass (4/4), including daemon e2e
- [x] `make run-local` — 1 witness, `/healthz` returns `ok`
- [x] `make run-local WITNESS_COUNT=3` — all three healthy on :8081, :8082, :8083
- [x] `make run-local-down` — all PIDs cleanly stopped
- [x] `make run-local-down` idempotent on empty `.run/`
- [x] `make dev-preflight` — fails fast when docker daemon unreachable
- [x] `WITNESS_COUNT=2 ./scripts/local/render-compose.sh` — `docker compose config` parses the result
- [ ] `make dev-up` end-to-end (couldn't smoke-test in the remote container — daemon not running here; CI runner will exercise it)
- [ ] CI `local-smoke` job — exercises the full Go-native loop on every PR going forward

author: talelburg
body:
## Summary

- First consumer of `Trigger::OnSkillTestResolution` (#112): Deduction's "if this skill test is successful while investigating a location, discover 1 additional clue at that location" maps to a Success-gated trigger wrapping `If(SkillTestKind == Investigate, DiscoverClue(TestedLocation, 1))`.
- Wires the previously-stubbed `Effect::If` evaluator + adds `Condition::SkillTestKind`. `Condition::SkillTest { outcome }` stays stubbed (preferred path at resolution time is the trigger-level outcome gate).
- Tightens CLAUDE.md PR-procedure step 7: phase-doc updates land as the single final commit before merge.

Closes #39.

## Design decisions

- **Kind narrowing via `Condition::SkillTestKind` + `Effect::If`, not on the trigger.** Settles the routing question from #112's doc: triggers stay outcome-only, composition via `If` handles the qualifier. Future cards needing "while fighting / while evading" gates reuse the same composition.
- **`Condition::SkillTest { outcome }` stays stubbed.** At resolution time, the trigger already gates outcome, so the condition would be redundant inside an `OnSkillTestResolution` effect. Outside that context (e.g. a future OnEvent reaction keying off `SkillTestSucceeded`), the engine doesn't yet snapshot past-test outcome onto state. Loud TODO points at the trigger as the preferred path; evaluator unit test pins the rejection.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI green on all five jobs (fmt, clippy, test, doc, wasm).
- [ ] `cargo test -p cards --test deduction` exercises the full path with real registry: bonus on success, no-fire on failure, no-fire on non-Investigate, no-fire when uncommitted, icon-contribution to test total.

## Description

Make ffmpeg/ffprobe optional in the bundled service image by removing the custom source-build installer and replacing the old build-time path with a runtime install flow.

The service image now keeps ffmpeg/ffprobe out by default. When audio or video extraction is needed, users can set `INSTALL_FFMPEG=true` for the service container, or set `service.installFfmpeg=true` in Helm. The service entrypoint installs the Ubuntu `ffmpeg` package at startup through narrowly scoped passwordless `sudo`, which provides both `ffmpeg` and `ffprobe`.

This PR also:

- Splits media dependency checks into distinct `ffmpeg-python`, `ffmpeg`, and `ffprobe` checks so missing dependencies produce actionable install guidance.
- Uses the granular checks where possible, so audio extraction and frame extraction only require `ffmpeg-python` plus the `ffmpeg` CLI, while media splitting/probing still requires `ffprobe`.
- Adds a Helm `service.installFfmpeg` value and a duplicate-env guard so users cannot set both `service.installFfmpeg=true` and `INSTALL_FFMPEG` manually in `service.env`.
- Updates README, Helm, troubleshooting, prerequisites, audio/video, and release-note docs for the runtime install flow and caveats.

author: igorganapolsky
body:
Four execution-discipline fixes to \`scripts/ic_simple.py\` (the active scheduled trading path).

## Fix 1 — Daily 1-IC entry limit (f72e5387e)

Docstring + controlled-experiment rule promise "1 IC per day"; \`ic_simple.py\` never enforced it. \`workflow_dispatch\` could exceed it. Guard reads \`data/system_state.json\` \`trade_history\` and blocks when today's entries \`>= MAX_DAILY_STRUCTURES\`.

## Fix 2 — Persist actual fill credit, not pre-walk estimate (44f5bc3c7)

\`place_ic()\` walks the limit price down up to \$0.20/share. \`_wait_for_fill\` was throwing away \`filled_avg_price\` and the entry record stored the pre-walk estimate. Every downstream exit decision (profit target, stop-loss, lesson reward) keyed off the inflated value. Audit shows avg loss \`-\$97.81\` vs avg win \`+\$70.50\` — consistent with stops keyed to inflated credit. Now persists \`fill_price\` from \`_wait_for_fill\` → \`tuple[bool, float | None]\`.

## Fix 3 — DTE-failsafe was suppressed by MIN_HOLD_HOURS gate (39ed0acf1)

24h hold gate short-circuited every exit reason — including the failsafe and 7DTE rule. Comment at \`:413\` promises "DTE failsafe first — always close expiring positions"; code did the opposite. Intraday entry with \`dte=1\` could ride into expiration because \`hours<24\`. Fix: compute DTE first, bypass hold gate when \`dte <= EXIT_DTE\`.

## Fix 4 — Stale entry records causing duplicate close + duplicate lessons (f7cadeb4a)

\`check_exits\` called \`_close_ic\` but never removed \`entries[entry_key]\`. Grep: zero \`del entries|entries.pop\` anywhere in the file. On the next \`check_exits\` run (before the broker actually fills the close MLEG limit order), Alpaca still reports the 4 legs and the stale entry record drives a second exit evaluation. Result: duplicate MLEG close attempts, duplicate \`_record_lesson\` (corrupts journal + RAG), \`_update_thompson\` double-counts.

Fix: track \`has_entry_record\` at lookup time, pop entry on close, gate \`_record_lesson\` + \`_update_thompson\` on \`has_entry_record\` so the estimate-path doesn't fabricate a learning signal.

## Test plan

- [x] \`_wait_for_fill\` mock: \`(True, 1.85)\` on fill, \`(False, None)\` on cancel
- [x] Daily-limit: synthetic state with 1 entry today → blocks
- [x] DTE-gate: 4 cases (forces at dte≤7, holds at dte=8+hours<24, proceeds at dte=30+hours≥24)
- [x] 66/66 tests pass in iron-condor-guardian, manage, integration (no regression)
- [x] Trunk fmt clean across all 4 commits
- [ ] CI green on this PR

## Companion to recent PRs

| PR | Status | Path | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| #3982 | merged | iron_condor_trader.py | broker GTC race → 75% <4h holds |
| #3983 | merged | sync_closed_positions.py | exit_reason derivation |
| #3984 | merged | iron_condor_trader.py + ic_simple.py | time-series concentration gate |
| **#3995** | **this PR** | **ic_simple.py** | **4 execution defects** |

Net diff: +116 / -37 lines, single file, 4 independent commits.

author: devonjones
body:
## Summary

Phase 3 of the vector-driven generator architecture (D36.1, D36.6). The hard-gate primitive: a predicate function that filters Meanings BEFORE per-axis scoring runs.

**New module: `wyrd/generators/kenning/eligibility.py`**
- `admits(meaning, gate, *, packs, tag_required, tag_excluded) -> bool`
- `filter_meanings(meanings, gate, ...) -> list[Meaning]`
- 5 cheapest-first per-gate predicates, each independently testable

## Gate predicates

| Gate | Behavior | Wraps |
|------|----------|-------|
| `passes_culture_gate` | Validates against `CULTURES`; raises `UnknownCultureError` with the available cultures listed | n/a (validation only) |
| `passes_era_gate` | Half-open `[era_min, era_max)`; "no data → pass" per D5-2 | `Meaning.attested_in_era_range` |
| `passes_stratum_gate` | "no data → pass" per wyrd-lr4 Phase 3 | `Meaning.in_stratum` |
| `passes_tag_required_gate` | AND semantics; all requested tags must appear | `meaning.tags` |
| `passes_tag_excluded_gate` | ANY match disqualifies; pairs with `--exclude-tags` / wyrd-yan | `meaning.tags` |
| `passes_pack_gate` | Stable-signature no-op stub. Will check pack admission + pack-tag filtering when scenario packs land (wyrd-v2gm) | n/a (future) |

## Per-Meaning culture filtering

The culture gate is validation-only because Meanings in the bundle's culture-specific slice already come pre-filtered by culture upstream (via `<culture>_place_names.json`). The gate's job is to fail loudly on a misconfigured request rather than silently selecting from the union of all cultures.

## Architecture split

`admits` is the cheapest-first composition. Gate predicates are checked in this order so a Meaning failing an early gate doesn't pay the cost of later ones:

1. Culture (validates, doesn't iterate)
2. Tag-required (set lookup)
3. Tag-excluded (set lookup)
4. Era (iterates attested_years dict)
5. Stratum (iterates stratum dict)
6. Pack (stub today; will be cheap when implemented)

## Tests (33, all passing)

- Culture: all 5 v1 cultures accepted; unknown raises with the valid cultures listed in the message
- Era: half-open semantics (800 inclusive, 1100 exclusive, 1099 in oe-late); both-None no-filter; no-attested-years passes
- Stratum: in-stratum passes; different stratum fails; no-stratum-data passes
- Tag-required: AND semantics for multi-tag requests
- Tag-excluded: union-exclude semantics
- Pack: stub no-op pinned (test will need updating when scenario packs land — that's the operator-visible-change signal)
- `admits`: short-circuits on first failing gate (verified by setting `attested_years` to a value that would raise if reached)
- `filter_meanings`: preserves input order; empty pool OK; integration test combining ALL gates simultaneously

## Out of scope (deferred follow-ups)

- **Pre-computed bitmap indexes** for cell-based fast filtering. That half of the wyrd-ecjp.3 ticket touches the bundle-build layer (`lexicon.py` / `export_meanings`); deferred so this PR stays scoped to runtime predicate logic and avoids conflict with the parallel **wyrd-67fv** lexicon refactor.
- **NameGenerator slot-walk integration** — Phase 5 (wyrd-ecjp.5), depends on this gate + the Phase 4 scorer both shipping first.
- **Real scenario-pack support** — the pack-gate stub returns True unconditionally; the wyrd-v2gm epic adds the per-pack metadata that the predicate will eventually check.

## Test plan

- [ ] `pytest tests/test_kenning_eligibility.py` (33)
- [ ] `pytest tests/test_kenning_vector_schemas.py tests/test_kenning_meaning.py` (adjacent suites — both modules this PR consumes)
- [ ] `ruff format --check . && ruff check .`

## Summary

The audit in #45 covered the bulk of the visibility/determinism/composability work. This PR closes the three real gaps that survived:

- **Visibility** — `/assemble-team` now has `disable-model-invocation: true`. It spawns parallel `Agent`s in worktrees that edit files; the brainstorming spec-gate only fires in `new-project` mode, leaving `existing-project` invocations exposed to model auto-fire on vague feature requests.
- **Determinism** — `/fix-issue` (Steps 4+6) and `/refactor-module` (Steps 3+6) hardcoded `python -m pytest ...`. On a TypeScript project the skill would still instruct Claude to run pytest. New shared helper `skills/references/run-tests.sh` stack-detects via `detect-stack.sh` and routes to pytest (Python) or `npm test --if-present` (Node). Exit codes: `0` pass, `1` fail, `2` unsupported stack with manual-run hint, `3` bad target.
- **Composability** — The four skill bodies above now compose `run-tests.sh` instead of duplicating runner logic.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `skills/assemble-team.md` | `+disable-model-invocation: true` in frontmatter. |
| `skills/references/run-tests.sh` | **New.** Stack-aware test runner. Filter arg translates to `-k` for pytest; warns on Node when target/filter given. |
| `skills/fix-issue.md` | Steps 4 + 6 now call `run-tests.sh` (was hardcoded pytest). |

## Deliberately out of scope

author: tanish-24-git
body:
…crawl

Per request, console capture should happen automatically as part of the crawl rather than via a separate manual button. The standalone banner on /crawler/reports was confusing — users had to remember to click it after every crawl, and a fresh crawl would always show "Console log entries: 0" until they did.

Now console capture runs as **Phase 2** of every crawl:

  Phase 1 — static crawl (fast: requests-based, ~50 pages/sec)
    - discovers URLs, records HTTP status, parses HTML, follows links
    - populates results / errors / 404s / discovered CSVs

  Phase 2 — headless Chromium pass (slow: ~3 sec/URL)
    - selects up to 200 www HTTP-200 URLs from Phase 1's results
    - launches Playwright, navigates, waits for DOM + 1.5s for JS
    - captures real console messages (error+warning levels), page errors, failed network requests
    - writes into crawl_console_log.csv

  finally — flushes streams, marks STATE.is_running=False, posts the
    "Crawl complete" log event with both phases' counts.

Phase 2 is skipped if `STATE.should_stop` was signalled OR if CRAWLER_CAPTURE_CONSOLE_AFTER_CRAWL=false in .env. Failures inside Phase 2 are logged + swallowed so they don't fail the whole crawl.

Frontend
  * CrawlerReports.tsx: drop the standalone ConsoleCaptureBanner import + render. (The component file is kept on disk in case a manual trigger is wanted later.)

Backend
  * engine/engine.py: inserted the Phase 2 block in _run_crawl_body just before the "Crawl complete" log event. Reuses csv_writer's already-open streams.

author: romarq
body:
`SubstrateConfigBuilder::set_genesis_hash` is a no-op: the value is stored on the builder but `build()` never copies it into `SubstrateConfigInner`, and `impl Config for SubstrateConfig` never overrides `genesis_hash()`, so it falls back to the trait default of `None`.

Offline workflows that rely on the configured genesis hash fail with `ExtrinsicError::GenesisHashNotProvided`:

```rust
let config = SubstrateConfig::builder()
    .set_genesis_hash(genesis_hash)
    .set_metadata_for_spec_versions(...)
    .set_spec_version_for_block_ranges(...)
    .build();
let client = OfflineClient::<SubstrateConfig>::new_with_config(config);
let at_block = client.at_block(0u64)?;
at_block.tx().create_signable_offline(&call, params)?; // GenesisHashNotProvided
```

The `OnlineClient` path is unaffected, since the hash is fetched from the network when `genesis_hash` is None.

This adds the missing `genesis_hash` field on `SubstrateConfigInner`, propagates it through `build()`, and overrides `Config::genesis_hash` for `SubstrateConfig`.

body:
## Summary

Surfaced during the v0.9.2 prod cutover: a freshly-signed-up user can't follow Eagles / Sixers / Union etc through the UI. The 4 hardcoded follows in \`seed_sports_data.rb\` were for user 1 only; new users see no scores at all on /sports.

Ships the full feature in one PR.

### Backend

- **\`Providers::ESPN.teams_for_league(sport_path:)\`** — fetches the full roster from ESPN's \`/<sport>/teams\` endpoint and normalises to the \`SportsTeamsStore.upsert\` shape. Defensive empty-on-failure pattern like the other ESPN methods.
- **\`scripts/seed_sports_data.rb\`** extended to bulk-fetch NFL / NBA / MLS rosters when \`SEED_FULL_CATALOG=1\` (default). Rugby + FIFA skipped — their \`/teams\` endpoints return tournament-roster shape that doesn't match.
- **\`SportsTeamFetchWorker\` (Sidekiq)** — pulls a single team's schedule from ESPN and upserts into \`sports_matches\`. Enqueued from the new follow route so scores appear within ~30s of clicking "+ Follow".

### UI

- **\`GET /sports/manage\`** — team grid per league with follow/unfollow pill toggle. Green accent + "✓ Following" outline pill on currently-followed teams; "+ Follow" solid pill on unfollowed.
- **\`POST /sports/teams/follow|unfollow\`** — mirror the existing player follow/unfollow routes.
- **"Sports" entry** added to the Manage ▾ dropdown alongside Feeds + Tags.

## Operator step after merge + deploy

SSH the Droplet:
\`\`\`bash
docker compose run --rm app make seed-sports-data
\`\`\`
This populates the full catalog (~30 teams per league). Existing user 1's follows survive (idempotent upsert).

## Follow-up gap (separate task)

The nightly sport-sync cron isn't scheduled on the Droplet. Eager fetch on follow covers NEW follows; EXISTING follows still need a recurring tick. Proper fix: sidekiq-cron or a recurring worker. Captured in #45's STUFF.md entry.
