Ships **Surface D – Linkable public dataset** for unlocksaas.com: the entire 157-entry pSEO catalog (33 funnel teardowns, 31 pricing teardowns, 55 head-to-head comparisons, 25 named-competitor alternatives, 13 category roundups) published as a single dataset under [CC-BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) with downloads in JSON, CSV, and Markdown.

This is the third PR in the off-page strategy after `@unlocksaas/seo` (PR #20), the Verified Builder embed (PR #19), and the MCP server (PR #22). All three of those operate on existing on-page assets; this one publishes a **permanent, citable artifact** with a license-mandated backlink mechanism: CC-BY requires attribution on derivative works, so every academic paper, blog post, newsletter, and chart that quotes a row creates a structural reason to link back to `/dataset`. Same mechanism that put Wikipedia, OpenStreetMap, and Stack Exchange data into a thousand academic citations, scaled to a single-founder indie SaaS catalog.

## Surfaces shipped

| Route | Type | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `/dataset` | Static prerender | HTML hub with schema.org/Dataset JSON-LD, counts table, downloads, license, citation snippets, sourcing methodology |
| `/dataset/indie-saas-teardowns.json` | Static (1d / 1w SWR) | Full typed shape – metadata header + all five catalog arrays |
| `/dataset/indie-saas-teardowns.csv` | Static (1d / 1w SWR) | Long-format flat table, RFC 4180 compliant, opens cleanly in Excel / pandas / R |
| `/dataset/README.md` | Static (1d / 1w SWR) | Provenance, schema, license, APA-7 citation, methodology – the file academics open first |

## Why this generates backlinks

1. **Google Dataset Search** – the hub carries a complete schema.org/Dataset JSON-LD block (license, distribution[], variableMeasured[], publisher, creator, dateModified, citation). That makes the surface eligible for the Dataset rich result and the Google Dataset Search index at [datasetsearch.research.google.com](https://datasetsearch.research.google.com).
2. **License-mandated attribution** – CC-BY 4.0 permits commercial reuse but requires attribution. Every consumer (Datawrapper chart, academic paper, blog post embedding a stat) is structurally obliged to credit `https://unlocksaas.com/dataset`.
3. **Show HN bait** – a 157-row hand-curated dataset of indie SaaS analyses with permissive license is the exact shape that hits the HN front page. Even a partial front-page session typically drops 30 to 200 organic links over six months (newsletters, blog posts, "in case you missed it" roundups).
4. **Kaggle / OpenAIRE ingestion** – both pipelines crawl Dataset-schema-tagged URLs. Listing in either is a permanent high-DA backlink with auto-discovered downloads.

## Schema (CSV columns – documented in /dataset/README.md and in the Dataset JSON-LD)

| Column | Type |
|---|---|
| `entity_type` | enum: `alternative` / `funnel-teardown` / `pricing-teardown` / `comparison` / `category` |
| `slug` | kebab-case URL slug |
| `display_name` | proper-noun display (comparisons: "A vs B") |
| `category` | catalog category bucket |
| `one_line` | single-line thesis |
| `tldr` | 40-to-60-word TL;DR (alternatives use `honestVerdict`, categories use `intent`) |
| `creator` | person or company that operates the analysed product (where known) |
| `url_canonical` | https URL of the UnlockSaaS analysis page |
| `url_target` | analysed product homepage (where the catalog carries it) |
| `last_verified` | ISO 8601 date of last manual sanity check |

## Brunson Hard-Rule reconciliation

- **Single source of truth.** Every route reads from the same catalog modules (`alternatives.ts`, `funnel-teardowns.ts`, `pricing-teardowns.ts`, `comparisons.ts`, `categories.ts`) that render the public HTML pages. Drift surface = zero.
- **Counts computed at build.** No hardcoded numbers. The README's count table, the hub's count table, the Dataset JSON-LD's `keywords`, and the JSON sibling's `metadata.counts` all derive from `.length` on the actual arrays.
- **No fabricated metrics.** No invented conversion rates, traffic figures, or revenue claims. Pure pass-through of fields already on the typed catalog entries.
- **No fabricated download counts, no fabricated citation counts.** The page does not claim adoption it does not have yet.
- **`dateModified` is honest.** Latest `lastVerified` across all four dated catalogs, computed at build. Brunson Hard-Rule: no arbitrary build-time stamp masquerading as a content date.
- **License is real.** CC-BY 4.0 is the same license that gates Wikipedia content. The URL resolves to creativecommons.org. Anyone can verify reuse permissions without contacting the founder.

## Routing decisions worth a reviewer's attention

- **Hub page lives under `(marketing)/dataset/`** (route group). Download routes live under `dataset/<filename>.<ext>/` (no group) so they share the `/dataset/...` URL prefix. Next.js App Router allows literal dots in folder names; this matches the existing `<page>.md/route.ts` and `llms-feed.json/route.ts` conventions in the repo.
- **Sitemap intentionally omits raw download URLs.** `/dataset` and `/dataset/README.md` are listed; `/dataset/indie-saas-teardowns.json` and `.csv` are not. Discovery happens via the Dataset JSON-LD `distribution[].contentUrl` fields, which is the citation-friendly path for Google Dataset Search and for any consumer scraping the hub. The raw URLs are still crawlable (no `Disallow`); they are just not advertised as primary pages.
- **`Script` with `beforeInteractive` strategy for the Dataset JSON-LD.** Matches the pattern used elsewhere in this codebase for inline schema scripts. Server-rendered, no hydration cost.
- **Latest-`lastVerified` computation runs at module scope.** Cached into the static prerender so the build cost is paid once per deploy, not per request.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` clean (verified locally, exit 0)
- [x] `next build` clean (verified locally, exit 0; all 4 dataset routes prerendered as static)
- [ ] Vercel preview build succeeds
- [ ] `curl -s https://<preview>/dataset/indie-saas-teardowns.json | jq '.metadata.counts'` returns `{alternatives: 25, funnelTeardowns: 33, pricingTeardowns: 31, comparisons: 55, categories: 13, total: 157}` (or whatever the current real counts are)
- [ ] `curl -s https://<preview>/dataset/indie-saas-teardowns.csv | head -3` shows the header row + two data rows
- [ ] `curl -s https://<preview>/dataset/README.md | head -10` returns the markdown with computed counts
- [ ] `curl -s https://<preview>/dataset | grep -oE 'application/ld\+json'` confirms the Dataset JSON-LD inlines on first paint
- [ ] Run https://validator.schema.org/ against the preview `/dataset` URL and confirm the Dataset block validates without errors
- [ ] Run Google's Rich Results Test at https://search.google.com/test/rich-results against the preview URL and confirm Dataset eligibility
- [ ] Confirm the sitemap at https://<preview>/sitemap.xml includes `/dataset` and `/dataset/README.md` but NOT the raw download URLs
- [ ] After prod deploy, submit https://unlocksaas.com/dataset to https://datasetsearch.research.google.com (operator action)

## Follow-ups (out of scope)

1. **Show HN announcement** – "Show HN: A 157-row open dataset of honest indie SaaS funnel + pricing teardowns (CC-BY 4.0)" after prod deploy stabilises.
2. **Submit to Google Dataset Search** – the JSON-LD makes it auto-discoverable, but operator can also submit via [Search Console](https://search.google.com/search-console).
3. **Submit to Kaggle Datasets and Awesome Public Datasets** – both are permanent high-DA backlinks.
4. **JSON Schema at `/dataset/schema.json`** – the JSON file already advertises `$schema` pointing at this URL. Easy follow-up: publish the schema so consumers can validate against it.
5. **Per-category sub-datasets** – `/dataset/payments.json`, `/dataset/forms.json` etc., for narrower analyses. Defer until adoption signal warrants it.

author: vandranki
body:
## Summary

`store_member_responses` defaults to `False`. At save time, `_asave_session` wipes every run's `member_responses` list without checking whether the run is paused or whether the list is non-empty. For HITL setups this causes silent data loss: the cross-process resume fails because `member_responses` is empty in the DB, but there is no indication of why.

This PR adds a `log_warning` when a non-empty `member_responses` list is cleared on a **paused** run, giving operators a clear diagnostic:

```
WARNING store_member_responses=False: wiping 3 member_responses on paused run abc123.
Set store_member_responses=True to preserve them for HITL resume.
```

## Changes

`libs/agno/agno/team/_session.py` — one guard + `log_warning` before the existing `run.member_responses = []` line.

## What this does NOT change

- The wipe still happens (behaviour is unchanged for non-paused runs and for users who don't care about HITL).
- For paused runs, the warning is emitted but the wipe still occurs — it's a diagnostic, not a behaviour change.
- A separate PR would be needed to change the default or skip the wipe for paused runs.

## Relationship to other issues

- Pairs with #7978 (persist outer team run before pause) and #7821/#7760 (resume path fixes).
- Addresses the observability gap described in #7960.

Fixes #7960 (partial — diagnostic; full fix requires `store_member_responses=True` or default change)

author: sahuagin
body:
## Summary

Three `runner_*` tests in `tools::aws_recon::tests` write shell scripts and exec them through a tempdir. They were using `std::env::temp_dir()` → `/tmp`, which is mounted `noexec` on FreeBSD (and hardened Linux configs). The tests passed on CI (Ubuntu, exec-allowed /tmp) by accident; on this FreeBSD host they fail with `runner_spawn_failed` because the kernel refuses to exec the test scripts.

`noexec` on `/tmp` is the conservative default. Tests shouldn't depend on it being relaxed.

## Change

`exec_temp_root()` in `aws_recon.rs::tests`:

1. Prefer `CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR` (cargo sets this for integration tests in `tests/`).
2. Fall back: walk up from `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR` to find the workspace `target/` directory, then use `target/test-tmp/`.
3. Last resort: `env::temp_dir()` — only reached if running tests outside cargo entirely.

`target/test-tmp/` is exec-allowed by construction (cargo builds binaries there) and `cargo clean` reclaims it.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo nextest run -p mu-coding 'tools::aws_recon::tests::runner_'` — 4/4 pass
- [x] `cargo nextest run --workspace` — **679 passing, 0 skipped, 0 failing** on this FreeBSD host (vs 675 passing, 3 failing before)
- [x] `cargo fmt --check` green
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` green
- [x] `scripts/verify-claims.sh HEAD` — Files block matches diff

## Related

PR #77 (oauth2 5 + ratatui 0.30 security bumps) documented the 3 failures as `pre-existing host-portability issue`. This PR closes that out.

author: codermisaki
body:
### 💡 What: 
The `rebuildCandidates()` function previously instantiated 81 new `Set` objects every time it was called. This has been optimized to reuse the existing `Set` instances by clearing and repopulating them, only creating new sets if they haven't been initialized yet.

### 🎯 Why: 
In a Sudoku solver, especially when using backtracking algorithms or interacting with the UI rapidly, `rebuildCandidates()` is called frequently. Allocating 81 new `Set` objects on every call creates a massive amount of garbage, forcing the Garbage Collector (GC) to run often, which causes noticeable lag and slows down the solving process.

### 📊 Impact: 
Significantly reduces memory allocations and GC pauses. This makes the UI feel more responsive during rapid inputs and speeds up any algorithm steps that depend on candidate rebuilding.

### 🔬 Measurement: 
This can be verified by profiling the memory allocations in Chrome DevTools during heavy usage (e.g., loading demo boards or using the solver) and observing a sharp decrease in the number of `Set` objects created and garbage collected. Functional correctness was verified by ensuring the board still behaves and solves correctly.

# Pull Request

## Summary & Motivation

When merged, this PR will add a `+schema: pearson` override under `models.kipppaterson.pearson` in `src/dbt/kipppaterson/dbt_project.yml` so that the Phase A `int_pearson__njsla` and `int_pearson__njsla_science` models (merged in #3958) land in the `kipppaterson_pearson` BigQuery schema instead of plain `kipppaterson`.

**Phase A bug fix.** Surfaced while preparing Phase B (kipptaf wiring + crosswalk removal) for #3882. The original Phase A added the intermediates but did not configure their schema. The imported `pearson` package sets `+schema: pearson` in its own `dbt_project.yml` — which is what makes the source-system staging models land in `kipppaterson_pearson` — but that config does not apply to `kipppaterson/models/pearson/intermediate/` because those are kipppaterson-project models, not imported-package models.

Without this fix:

- Models land in `kipppaterson` schema (verified via `dbt build --target dev`).
- Dagster derives 2-element asset keys (`kipppaterson/int_pearson__njsla`) instead of the 3-element form (`kipppaterson/pearson/int_pearson__njsla`).
- Phase B's `sources-kipppaterson.yml` declarations point at `kipppaterson_pearson.int_pearson__njsla` — which would not exist.

Phase B is blocked until this merges and Dagster materializes the intermediates into the correct schema.

## AI Assistance

AI-assisted: Claude Code identified the missing schema config during Phase B preparation, traced the convention to the pearson source-system package's `dbt_project.yml`, and applied the fix. Human-directed: scope confirmation that this is a Phase A bug worth a separate small PR.

## Self-review

Refs #3882.

body:
## Summary

Module **Modification du chantier** : après l'onboarding, l'user peut ajuster son chantier (ajouter/retirer tâches et corps de métier) avec sauvegarde auto et estimation de délai recalculée en temps réel. Pose les fondations pour le module Pricing (logique d'upgrade, modal placeholder).

Cette PR implémente le brief avec les **6 décisions de pré-revue** :
1. ✅ `status: 'todo'` corrigé (au lieu de `'a_faire'`)
2. ✅ `Toast` existant non touché ; toast queue dédiée chantier (bottom-right, 2 variantes)
3. ✅ 4 états canoniques de MetierCard
4. ✅ `addTradeAfterPayment` séparé (à créer par module Pricing) — pas de flag bypass
5. ✅ Refacto MetierCard/TacheCard touche aussi onboarding
6. ✅ `calculerEstimation` du module Estimation utilisé en client pour la sticky bar live

Et la **décision (b)** : ajouter un métier crée seulement la ligne `project_trades`, pas les tâches. L'user choisit ensuite via un browse mode toggle par métier.

## Composants livrés

**Architecture serveur** :
- `lib/pricing/types.ts` — stub minimal Palier + getPalierForCount + PALIER_PRIX_CENTS + getUpgradePrice (8 tests Vitest sur les frontières)
- `lib/chantier/actions.ts` — 4 server actions avec validations strictes :
  - `addTaskToProject` / `removeTaskFromProject`
  - `addTradeToProject` (retourne `upgrade_required` si change de palier — pas d'insert)
  - `removeTradeFromProject` (retourne `has_active_tasks` si bloquant)

**Architecture client (Page `/chantier/modifier`)** :
- Server Component charge tout en parallèle, précompute index minimal des tâches et estimation initiale (snapshot pour le diff)
- Client Component avec `useOptimistic` : updates instant, revert auto sur erreur
- Sticky bar **live** : `useMemo` réactif → `calculerEstimation` à chaque changement (<1ms)
- Badge diff vs initial si > 1 semaine : `+N semaines` jaune (rallonge) / `-N semaines` vert (raccourcit)
- Toast queue : success (2s) + error (4s), bottom-right, dismiss manuel ou auto
- Modal upgrade placeholder : esc/click outside/X pour fermer, bouton "Payer" désactivé avec message "module Pricing à venir"

**Composants atomiques** :
- `components/chantier/MetierCard.tsx` — 4 états (actif_paye_avec_taches, actif_paye_sans_taches, disponible_sans_upgrade, disponible_avec_upgrade)
- `components/chantier/TacheCard.tsx` — 4 états (selectionnee_non_commencee, en_cours, terminee, disponible)
- Refacto onboarding : `StepTrades` et `StepTasks` utilisent maintenant ces composants

**Points d'entrée** (étape 8) :
- Dashboard : bouton "Modifier mon chantier"
- Vue métier : "Modifier les tâches de ce métier" → `/chantier/modifier?metier=X` (scroll auto)
- Page Estimation : bouton "Modifier mon chantier" dans le header
- `middleware.ts` : `/chantier` ajouté aux routes protégées

## Hors scope (module Pricing à venir)

- Vraie modal Stripe + Checkout
- `addTradeAfterPayment(projectId, tradeKey, paymentId)` — exigera preuve de paiement vérifiée en base
- Webhook de confirmation paiement
- Table `payments`

Le contrat de props de `UpgradeModalPlaceholder` est conçu pour qu'on puisse le swap directement avec le vrai composant du module Pricing.

## Test plan

- [ ] Pull la branche, `npm install`, `npm run dev`
- [ ] Aller sur `/dashboard` → cliquer "Modifier mon chantier" → arrive sur `/chantier/modifier`
- [ ] **Ajout tâche** : dans un métier actif, cliquer "Ajouter une tâche" (révèle les disponibles) → cocher une tâche disponible → toast vert "Tâche ajoutée" + sticky bar se met à jour
- [ ] **Retrait tâche** : décocher une tâche non commencée → toast vert "Tâche retirée"
- [ ] **Tâche lockée** : tester avec une tâche `in_progress` ou `done` (via Supabase Studio si besoin) → UI grisée, click sans effet
- [ ] **Ajout métier sans upgrade** : cliquer "+ Ajouter" sur un métier qui reste dans la tranche actuelle → toast vert "Métier ajouté", le métier apparaît dans la section "Tâches par métier" avec 0 tâche
- [ ] **Ajout métier avec upgrade** : si tu as 3 métiers actifs (tranche 1-3), cliquer "+ Ajouter" sur un 4e → modal s'affiche avec différentiel +20€, bouton "Payer" désactivé. Cliquer "Annuler" ou X ferme la modal, ton chantier n'a pas changé.
- [ ] **Retrait métier avec tâches actives** : cliquer "Retirer" sur un métier avec tâches → toast d'erreur "Retire d'abord les N tâche(s) actives"
- [ ] **Retrait métier sans tâches** : cliquer "Retirer" sur un métier vide (après avoir décoché toutes ses tâches) → toast vert "Métier retiré"
- [ ] **Sticky bar live** : faire varier la sélection → l'estimation se met à jour avec micro-animation. Si delta > 1 semaine vs estimation initiale, badge `+N semaines` jaune (ou `-N semaines` vert) apparaît
- [ ] **URL filter** : aller sur `/metiers/electricite` → cliquer "Modifier les tâches de ce métier" → atterrit sur `/chantier/modifier?metier=electricite` avec scroll auto sur la section électricité
- [ ] **Onboarding non régressé** : signup nouveau compte (ou via alias `+test`) → parcourir l'onboarding 6 étapes → les écrans Trades et Tasks utilisent les nouveaux composants mais fonctionnent comme avant

author: emilbon99
body:
# Issue Pull Request ## Linear Issue [SY-4046](https://linear.app/synnax/issue/SY-4046) ## Description Extends the Arc LSP's Rename request so renaming a channel reference in Arc source also renames the underlying Synnax channel resource. Previously, Rename on a channel identifier returned nil (channels resolve through the global resolver and have no AST), so the operation was a no-op even though the menu item appeared enabled. The LSP now exposes a generic `OnRename` callback in its `Config`. The handler runs after a rename request resolves to a valid symbol and before source-text edits are produced, and is given the resolved `*symbol.Scope` plus the old and new names so it can decide for itself whether (and how) to propagate the change. Rename on channels is gated on this callback being wired, so a host without channel-propagation logic still gets the old "source-defined symbols only" behavior. The core arc service wires a callback that delegates to `channel.Service.Rename` for `KindChannel` symbols (the channel symbol carries the channel key in `Symbol.ID`, so no name lookup is required); the callback lives in `core/pkg/service/arc` to keep `channel` free of LSP-shaped dependencies. Out of scope for this PR: cascading the rename to other saved Arc programs that reference the channel by its old name. That can be added later in a separate change. ## Basic Readiness - [ ] I have performed a self-review of my code. - [ ] I have added relevant, automated tests to cover the changes. - [ ] I have updated documentation to reflect the changes.

Greptile Summary

This PR extends the Arc LSP rename flow to support channel symbols: a new `OnRename` callback hook in `lsp.Config` is called after reference collection and before text edits are emitted, allowing the host to propagate the rename to the backing Synnax channel resource. The `channelResolver` opts channels into the flow by setting `Renameable: !ch.Internal`, and `Service.NewLSP()` wires a `channelRename` callback that delegates to `channel.Service.Rename` using the key stored in `sym.ID`. - `arc/go/lsp/rename.go` — `isRenameable` now admits global symbols with `Symbol.Renameable = true`; `findAllReferences` is extended to match global symbols by kind + name (no AST); `OnRename` is invoked between reference collection and text-edit production to ensure the old name is still resolvable during collection. - `core/pkg/service/arc/rename.go` — new `channelRename` factory produces the `lsp.OnRename` callback; it is a no-op for non-channel kinds and uses `allowInternal: false` as a safety net. - `core/pkg/service/arc/symbol/resolver.go` — `channelToSymbol` now populates `Renameable: !ch.Internal`, correctly gating rename capability on the channel's internal flag.

Confidence Score: 4/5

The production path through `Service.NewLSP()` always wires `OnRename` and validates `Channel` non-nil, so the Synnax rename behavior is correct end-to-end. The open `OnRename == nil` gating issue from the prior review remains unaddressed: `isRenameable` admits resolver-supplied `Renameable` symbols regardless of whether `OnRename` is wired, contradicting the documented API contract that `nil` restricts rename to source-defined symbols. A library caller who provides a `GlobalResolver` with `Renameable=true` symbols but omits `OnRename` will get text edits applied while the backing resource goes unmodified, leaving the document broken. arc/go/lsp/rename.go — `isRenameable` and both `PrepareRename`/`Rename` call sites do not gate resolver-supplied renameables on `OnRename != nil`.

Important Files Changed

| Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | arc/go/lsp/rename.go | Core rename logic extended for global (resolver-supplied) symbols; `isRenameable` now allows `sym.Renameable` symbols but does not gate on `OnRename != nil`, leaving the documented API contract unenforced (flagged in prior review). | | arc/go/lsp/rename_test.go | Adds comprehensive unit tests for OnRename: invocation with correct args, multi-reference text edits, error abort, source-defined symbols, and Renameable=false rejection. Test names are consistent with assertions. | | arc/go/lsp/server.go | Adds `OnRename` type and `Config.OnRename` field; wired cleanly into `Override` with `override.Nil`. No behavioral changes to existing code. | | arc/go/symbol/symbol.go | Adds `Renameable bool` to `Symbol` with clear doc comment distinguishing it from source-defined (AST-backed) symbols. Clean, non-breaking addition. | | core/pkg/service/arc/rename.go | New `channelRename` factory wires an `lsp.OnRename` callback that delegates to `channel.Service.Rename` using the key stored in `sym.ID`; correctly ignores non-KindChannel symbols and uses `allowInternal=false` as a safety net. | | core/pkg/service/arc/rename_test.go | Integration tests validate end-to-end channel rename and rejection for internal channels, using real distributed channel service. | | core/pkg/service/arc/service.go | Wires `channelRename(s.cfg.Channel)` into `NewLSP`; `Channel` is validated non-nil in `ServiceConfig.Validate()` so the callback is always present in production. | | core/pkg/service/arc/symbol/resolver.go | Sets `Renameable: !ch.Internal` in `channelToSymbol`, correctly gating rename capability on the channel's internal flag. | | core/pkg/service/arc/symbol/resolver_test.go | Adds tests verifying that regular channels are `Renameable=true` and internal channels are `Renameable=false`. |

Sequence Diagram

```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant C as LSP Client participant S as arc LSP Server participant GR as GlobalResolver participant OR as OnRename callback participant CS as channel.Service C->>S: PrepareRename(position) S->>GR: Resolve symbol at position GR-->>S: "symbol.Scope (Renameable=true)" S-->>C: Range (rename enabled) C->>S: Rename(position, newName) S->>GR: Resolve symbol at position GR-->>S: targetSym (Scope) S->>S: findAllReferences(doc, targetSym) S->>OR: OnRename(ctx, sym, oldName, newName) OR->>CS: NewWriter(nil).Rename(ctx, Key(sym.ID), newName, false) CS-->>OR: nil / error OR-->>S: nil / error alt OnRename error S-->>C: nil, err else success S->>S: Build TextEdit list S-->>C: WorkspaceEdit end ```

Comments Outside Diff (1)

 1. `arc/go/lsp/rename.go`, line 39-53 ([link](https://github.com/synnaxlabs/synnax/blob/e042512e0ffe241de83e3606e3ab354e55ccfc47/arc/go/lsp/rename.go#L39-L53)) **`OnRename == nil` doesn't enforce the documented restriction** `Config.OnRename`'s doc says "When nil, rename is restricted to source-defined symbols." But `isRenameable` returns `sym.AST != nil || sym.Renameable`, so a global symbol with `Renameable: true` passes the check even when `OnRename` is nil. `PrepareRename` will then return a valid range (enabling the rename UI item), and `Rename` will produce text edits renaming every reference in the source — while silently skipping the out-of-band resource update. The result is that Arc source now references a name the channel resolver cannot find, breaking the document. The fix is to gate resolver-supplied renameables on `OnRename` being wired, e.g. add the check in `PrepareRename` and `Rename` right after `isRenameable`: ```go // resolver-supplied symbols require OnRename to propagate the backing-resource rename if sym != nil && sym.AST == nil && s.cfg.OnRename == nil { return nil, nil } ```
Reviews (3): Last reviewed commit: ["added rename channel via arc lsp"](https://github.com/synnaxlabs/synnax/commit/4f939e7c6e2e26aee0a096a26d6b10065af3966d) | [Re-trigger Greptile]

body:
## Summary

- Wire `SystemNative_LowLevelMonitor_TimedWait` to record an optional deadline on `BlockedOnMonitorWait`, add `LowLevelMonitor.fireTimeout` (mirrors `spuriousWake` plus the `Int32 1 → Int32 0` eval-stack rewrite), and dispatch through the existing per-tick `fireExpiredDeadlines` + jump-to-deadline machinery. PR 2c will extend the same mechanism to `Monitor.Wait`.
- Preserve FIFO when multiple monitor timeouts expire in the same tick: `fireExpiredDeadlines` now sorts monitor fires by `WaitQueue` position so the head receives ownership when the monitor is unowned at fire time. ThreadId-order iteration would otherwise let a later-parked waiter with a smaller id steal the monitor.
- Loop the jump-to-deadline fallback until either a Runnable thread appears or no finite deadline remains. A single monitor-timeout fire against a held monitor produces `BlockedOnMonitorAcquire`, not `Runnable`; without the loop, a guest with the owner parked on a *later* finite wait would be misreported as deadlocked.

## Summary

- Adiciona `groupProgressByUserModule` (O(N) one-pass) + `computeModuleAvgCompletion` em `lib/lms/progress-aggregation.ts`
- Substitui loop `O(users × lessons × progress)` em `app/api/admin/lms/analytics/route.ts` por agregação linear
- 6 testes vitest cobrindo: vazio, single user, multi user ortogonal, órfãos, cálculo + módulo sem users

## Por quê

`progress.filter(p => p.userId === userId && lessonIds.includes(p.lessonId))` é O(progress × lessons), executado dentro de `for (userId of enrolledUserIds)`. Total: O(users × lessons × progress).

Com 100 users / 50 lessons / 2500 progress rows isso é 125M operações filter. Hoje, com 78 rows, é imperceptível (<1ms). O refactor remove a armadilha antes do crescimento.

- 1467 tests passing (6 novos em `progress-aggregation.test.ts`)

- Contract JSON do `moduleProgress` inalterado (`{ moduleId, title, avgCompletion, totalLessons }`)
- Edge cases preservados: módulo sem lessons → 0; módulo sem progresso → 0; módulo 100% completo → 100

## Fecha Onda 4.6

Esta PR fecha a campanha 4.6 (3 PRs sequenciais: 4.6.0 #82 instrumentação, 4.6.1 #83 N+1 + paralelização, 4.6.1b loop quadrático). Próximos passos:

- Raw SQL aggregation (`getModuleAvgCompletionSQL`, etc): adiar até `LessonProgress > 10k` rows OU `QuizAttempt > 5k` rows

These plugins already declare the right `lspServers` config at the marketplace level — that's where Claude Code actually loads LSP configs from (the user-settings schema does not include `lspServers`).

If your default is `system` node, run `nodenv shell system` (or `nodenv global system`) before `juliet-bootstrap`, or swap to `pipx install pyright` for the Python side.
- The previous iteration of this PR added a top-level `lspServers` block to settings.json directly. That block was dead config — confirmed by reading `~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/claude-plugins-official/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`, which shows the LSP config lives on plugin entries, not user settings. author: ish-dev-piqc
body:
## Summary

- Two bugs in `piqc-discipline.yml` caught when PR #85 re-ran CI after #87. Both surgical fixes.

## Plan MD

Implements: [`plans/ishika/discipline-workflow-hardening.md`](plans/ishika/discipline-workflow-hardening.md)

## Bug 1 — Shell injection in plan-MD-reference check (security)

The "Plan MD referenced in PR body" step inlines `${{ github.event.pull_request.body }}` directly into bash. GitHub substitutes the body as literal text before bash parses, so markdown backticks in a PR body become command substitutions. Observed cascade on PR #85's CI re-run:

```
supabase: command not found
Protocol: command not found
UPDATE: command not found
syntax error near unexpected token 'protocol'
```

Fixed by switching to the `env: PR_BODY:` pattern that the sibling "DB schema → type mirror" check already uses correctly.

## Bug 2 — `: any` regex matches English prose

The `(:\s*any\b|\bas\s+any\b)` regex matches comments like:

```ts
// Defensive design: any sessionStorage read failure...
```

Fixed by piping through `grep -vE ':[0-9]+:\s*(//|\*)'` to skip lines whose content starts with a comment marker. Lines from `grep -rn` are formatted `path:line:content` so anchoring `:[0-9]+:` then a comment prefix is reliable.

## Verification (local)

```
✅ Comment-prose case: '// Defensive design: any sessionStorage' — no false positive
✅ Real violation: 'const x: any = 5;' — still flagged
✅ PR body with backticks + $(): no shell execution, plan ref still found
```

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] `/piqc-review` clean — 2 files in scope, no application code changes
- [x] **No type impact** — CI-only
- [x] No new mocks
- [x] Both fixes verified locally with positive + negative cases

## Test plan

- [ ] CI green on this PR
- [ ] After merge: merge main into PR #85's branch; CI re-runs and `: any` check + plan-MD check both pass without false positives / injection chatter
- [ ] Smoke-test on a throwaway PR with a body that intentionally contains backticks and `$(date)` — confirm the shell injection is closed

## Post-merge

- [ ] `/archive-plan` moves the plan to `_archive/`
- [ ] Merge main into PR #85's branch and re-run its CI

author: agiantwhale
body:
## Summary

Detects build drift on DO rehydration and pushes the spec-compliant `notifications/tools/list_changed` to the client so it refetches `tools/list`. Silent auto-refresh — no user action required, no LLM mediation. Independent of (and parallel to) PR #48's `SERVER_INSTRUCTIONS` work, so no shared diff surface.

## Mechanism

```
Worker deploy at T0  (build:  abc1234)
  user opens chat → DO instance created → init() registers tools per abc1234
  DO storage: lastServedBuild = abc1234
  client cache: tool list @ abc1234

Worker redeploy at T1 (build: def5678)
  DO hibernates / is rehydrated on new code
  init() runs on def5678 → reads storage: lastServedBuild = abc1234
  abc1234 != def5678 → set _toolListChangedPending flag
  storage updated: lastServedBuild = def5678

onStart() (which awaits init(), then transport.connect()):
  super.onStart() returns → transport is up
  pending flag is set → call server.sendToolListChanged()
  client receives notifications/tools/list_changed
  client issues tools/list
  server responds with the def5678 tool set
  LLM's next turn sees the updated tools
```

## Why a deferred fire instead of inside init()

`McpAgent.onStart` runs `await this.init()` *before* `await server.connect(transport)`. If we call `sendToolListChanged()` inside `init()`, there's no transport — the notification is a no-op or buffered weirdly. Overriding `onStart` lets us land the notification immediately after the transport connects.

## What's NOT in this PR

- **No `_meta.serverBuild` injection on every tool response.** That was the alternative path I scoped. Skipped here because the requirement is silent auto-refresh, not user-facing warning. If we later find clients that ignore `tools/list_changed`, the `_meta` path is a natural follow-up — minimal code, would land in `src/util.ts`'s `ok()` helper.
- **No DO storage migration.** First-ever DO starts read `undefined` and don't trigger the notification — by design, since a first-ever start has nothing stale to refresh.

## Files changed

- `src/index.ts` only. +45 lines: import GIT_COMMIT_SHORT, add `_toolListChangedPending` private field, drift check at the end of `init()`, `onStart()` override that fires the notification post-transport-connect.

## Test plan

- [ ] `npm run typecheck` clean (verified locally).
- [ ] After merge to staging, connect Claude.ai (or another MCP client) to `staging.workoutcontext.fit/mcp`. Note the tool list it shows.
- [ ] Push a trivial commit to `staging` (e.g., another README tweak) — worker redeploys.
- [ ] Make a tool call from the existing session. Within a few seconds Claude.ai should silently refresh its tool list; the LLM's next turn sees any new/changed tools.
- [ ] `wrangler tail --env staging` should show no `[tools/list_changed] notification failed` error.
- [ ] Trigger a SECOND redeploy while still in the same session. The notification fires again. (Storage is updated on each init.)

## Limitations

- **Spec-compliance from clients is required.** Claude.ai honors `tools/list_changed`. Other clients vary — those that don't honor it stay on the stale list until the user reconnects. Combine with the `_meta`/server-instructions path from PR #48 if broader coverage is needed.
- **No cross-user broadcast.** Each user's DO independently detects drift on their own next start. A user who never reconnects after a deploy never gets the notification — but they also never see the staleness because tool calls just use the current build's implementations. Stale tool *descriptions* in their LLM context, sure; not stale *behavior*.

author: an-altosian
body:
## Motivation

Previously `validateXeniumBundle` ran inside `PIPELINE_INITIALISATION` and was gated by:

\`\`\`groovy
if (!workflow.profile.contains('test')) {
    validateXeniumBundle(ch_samplesheet)
}
\`\`\`

The skip-in-test guard existed because:

- The test samplesheet entry is a `.tar.gz` URL, not a directory. The validation iterates required files like `cell_boundaries.csv.gz` over that path and always fails in test mode.
- Cloud-storage inputs (`s3://`, `gs://`, `az://`) also had an early-return because `file().exists()` is unreliable before Nextflow stages the input.

Both reasons describe the **same root cause**: validation was running BEFORE staging, so it had to handle multiple un-staged input shapes (directory, tarball, remote URL).

## Change

Move the file-presence validation to **AFTER** the existing `UNTAR` staging step, where the bundle is unconditionally a resolved local directory regardless of input form.

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| [`subworkflows/local/utils_nfcore_spatialxe_pipeline/main.nf`](https://github.com/nf-core/spatialxe/blob/dev/subworkflows/local/utils_nfcore_spatialxe_pipeline/main.nf) | Delete the `validateXeniumBundle(ch_samplesheet)` call + its `!workflow.profile.contains('test')` guard. Delete the `def validateXeniumBundle` function (it was tightly coupled to the channel + un-staged-path shape). |
| [`workflows/spatialxe.nf`](https://github.com/nf-core/spatialxe/blob/dev/workflows/spatialxe.nf) | Inline file-presence checks into the existing `ch_bundle_path` `.map` block — required-file list errors, optional-file list warns. Same logic, runs once per sample after `UNTAR` (test mode) or directly against the user-provided directory (production). |

The s3/gs/az special-case is no longer needed: by the time `ch_bundle_path` runs its map, Nextflow has staged the input as a local path, so `file().exists()` works.

## Side effect: nf-core/untar stub fix

Running the validation post-staging exposed a latent bug in `nf-core/untar`'s stub.

**Real script** (when the archive has a single top-level dir): `tar -xavf --strip-components 1` — places extracted files inside `${prefix}/`.

**Stub script** (same condition): iterates `tar -tf` output and `touch \${i}` — but `\${i}` includes the top-level dir prefix (e.g. `xenium_bundle/cells.csv.gz`), so the files land at `./xenium_bundle/...` **outside** `${prefix}/`. The captured Nextflow output is only `${prefix}/`, so most of the iterated touches are lost.

The previous local patch in this repo papered over this with 4 hardcoded `touch ${prefix}/morphology.ome.tif` etc. lines — enough for the test fixture's first-stage consumers, but the test_run/ directory was still missing 12 of the 16 files defined by 10x's bundle spec, which is what made the skip-validation guard necessary.

This PR replaces the band-aid with a proper fix: in the single-top-level-dir branch, strip the leading directory from each tar entry so the stubbed file layout matches the real script. The 4 hardcoded touches are removed since the loop now creates them naturally.

\`\`\`bash
# new stub logic for the single-top-level-dir branch
for i in \`tar -tf \${archive}\`; do
    stripped=\${i#*/}
    [ -z \"\$stripped\" ] && continue
    if [[ ! \"\${i}\" =~ /\$ ]]; then
        mkdir -p \${prefix}/\$(dirname \"\$stripped\")
        touch \${prefix}/\$stripped
    else
        mkdir -p \${prefix}/\$stripped
    fi
done
\`\`\`

`modules/nf-core/untar/untar.diff` regenerated to reflect the cleaner change (still a local patch on the nf-core module; upstreaming a separate PR to `nf-core/modules` would let us drop this patch entirely, but that's a separate effort).

## Snapshot updates

Five mode-test snapshots regenerated to reflect the **now-complete** extracted-bundle file listing:

- `tests/coordinate_mode.nf.test.snap`
- `tests/default.nf.test.snap`
- `tests/image_mode.nf.test.snap`
- `tests/preview_mode.nf.test.snap`
- `tests/segfree_mode.nf.test.snap`

Each gained ~15 new entries under `coordinate/untar/test_run/`, `image/untar/test_run/`, etc. — the files that the UNTAR stub now correctly creates inside the prefix (cell_boundaries.*, cell_feature_matrix.*, cells.*, metrics_summary.csv, morphology_focus/, nucleus_boundaries.*, transcripts.zarr.zip, analysis.tar.gz, analysis.zarr.zip, analysis_summary.html, aux_outputs.tar.gz, .end-of-run).

These weren't appearing in the previous snapshots because the broken stub never placed them inside the output directory.

## Test plan

- [x] `nf-test test tests/{default,coordinate_mode,image_mode,preview_mode,segfree_mode}.nf.test --profile=+docker --ci` → **5/5 PASS** in 448s after snapshot regen.
- [x] `nextflow config -profile docker .` parses clean.
- [x] `nextflow inspect main.nf -profile test,docker` — process graph intact.

## Related

This is the architectural follow-up @awgymer and I discussed on nf-core/spatialxe#158 — moving validation to post-staging so the skip-in-test escape hatch can go away. PR #158 is independent (params-in-modules cleanup) and not blocking this.

body:
## Summary
The daily attendance letter to **الدكتور حسام فقيها** rendered only the fully-absent employees. Extended it to **three sections** in one report:

| # | Section | Source status |
|---|---------|---------------|
| أولاً | الموظفون الغائبون كلياً | \`absent\` |
| ثانياً | الدوام الجزئي (أقل من 8 ساعات) | \`incomplete_hours\` |
| ثالثاً | البصمة الناقصة (دخول بدون خروج) | \`check_in_only\` |

Empty sections show **"لا يوجد"**. On-call employees stay naturally excluded — they live under separate \`on_call_*\` enum values and the query only selects the three regular statuses.

## Design notes
- **Classification reuses the analyzer's existing statuses** — we don't reclassify, just read what's already in \`PdfDailyAttendanceSummary\`. The "<8h" rule and the on-call exemption are exactly the analyzer's existing semantics.
- **Hours format**: stored \`totalHours\` is rendered in Arabic-Indic digits (`٦.٥`) with one-decimal precision and proper plural rules (\`<2\` → ساعة, \`=2\` → ساعتان, \`>2\` → ساعات). Tiny Float noise (\`6.499999\` → \`6.5\`) is rounded out at the formatter.
- **Backward compatibility**: the range letter (\`/letters/range\`) and any legacy caller that passes only \`absences\` keeps the original single-section layout — \`buildLetter\` switches into v2 only when \`partial\` or \`missingCheckout\` is explicitly provided. The response shape stays \`{text, html, metadata}\`; \`metadata.categoryCounts\` is the only new (optional) field.
- **Range letter unchanged** by design — extending it was out of scope.

## Test plan
- [x] 11 new spec tests (Arabic-Indic numerals, hours pluralization, all six \`formatHoursWorked\` edge cases, every v2 section's empty-state, mixed-fill, metadata counts, v1 backward-compat)

author: conejogordo2013-arch
body:
### Motivation
- Prevent memory wrapping above 1MiB by enabling A20 early in the boot process to allow heap/page structures to be used safely.
- Improve boot reliability by adjusting the stack location and ensuring BIOS services are called with interrupts enabled when appropriate.
- Make the image build more robust by adding explicit sector/size constants and overlap/size validation to avoid accidental LBA collisions.
- Reduce early-boot instability by deferring optional hardware driver probing and making exception handling non-returning to avoid recursive faults.

### Description
- In `boot/LABootL.asm` the initial `sp` was moved to `0xF000`, a call to `enable_a20` was added before disk loads, and a new `enable_a20` routine was implemented that toggles the A20 gate via port `0x92`.
- The build script `build.sh` was refactored to introduce `SECTOR_SIZE` and `DISK_SECTORS`, add `sectors_for_file()` helper, validate that `boot.bin` is exactly one sector, compute `max_kernel_size` using `SECTOR_SIZE`, verify app LBAs do not overlap reserved regions, and use the variables when creating the disk image with `dd`.
- Kernel startup in `kernel/LAoskrnl.asm` was changed to defer optional drivers: network and audio driver availability flags are set to `0` and an informational message `msg_optional_deferred` is printed instead of probing/initializing optional devices during early boot.
- Interrupt handling in `kernel/interrupts.lasys` now masks all PIC IRQs early (`0xFF`), leaves interrupts disabled after `lidt` (`cli`), replaces `iretd` in exception stubs with a jump to a `fatal_exception_halt` routine, and adds an infinite `hlt` loop to avoid returning to a faulting instruction.

### Testing
- Executed the build flow by running `./build.sh`, which runs `nasm` to assemble boot/kernel/apps and writes `LuisAlbertoOS.img`, and the script completed successfully with all validation checks (boot size, kernel size limit, and app LBA overlap) passing.
- Assembler invocations in the build (`nasm -f bin ...`) completed without errors for the modified files.

body:
💡 **What:** Refactored `normalizeExerciseDetails` in `server/services/aiModificationGuard.ts` to use a Schwartzian transform (decorate-sort-undecorate) for sorting exercise details, pre-computing the `JSON.stringify` keys. Replaced `.localeCompare()` with explicit standard string comparison.
🎯 **Why:** Calling `JSON.stringify()` inside a `.sort()` comparator executes the expensive serialization operation $O(N \log N)$ times. `localeCompare` is also notoriously slow and can introduce environment-dependent behavior. This caused an unnecessary bottleneck when normalizing workout payloads.
📊 **Impact:** Reduces the number of `JSON.stringify` calls from $O(N \log N)$ to $O(N)$. Simple string comparisons are significantly faster and more deterministic than `.localeCompare()`. In local benchmarks of 100 items over 1000 iterations, execution time dropped from ~504ms to ~114ms (a ~4.4x speedup).
🔬 **Measurement:** Run `pnpm test` to verify the normalization logic still passes all correctness checks. The performance improvement is structural and applies to all environments.

author: copilot
body:
The public AI paths were still failing after the guest-auth switch because the committed `amplify_outputs.json` advertised stale API-key-only metadata, and the frontend had no fallback when `identityPool` auth was unavailable or still propagating. This updates the bundled auth metadata, adds an auth-only retry path, and fixes the user-facing guidance to reflect the actual architecture.

- **Bundled Amplify metadata**
  - Updated `amplify/amplify_outputs.json` to match the current public auth model:
    - `default_authorization_type: "AWS_IAM"`
    - `authorization_types` now includes both `AWS_IAM` and `API_KEY`
    - `Todo` model introspection now declares both `iam` and `apiKey` public rules
  - Kept `api_key` in place so static builds still have a controlled fallback path during rollout / propagation windows.

- **Public AI client fallback**
  - `PublicChatWidget.tsx` and `AiInsightsPanel.tsx` now:
    - try `identityPool` first
    - retry with `apiKey` only for auth / unauthorized / missing-credentials failures
    - preserve existing throttle / Bedrock / resolver error handling
  - Added explicit console diagnostics with component-prefixed logs for the fallback path.

- **Shared auth-error detection**
  - Extracted shared helpers in `src/utils/amplifyErrors.ts` so both components use the same auth-error classification logic instead of duplicating regex checks inline.
  - Expanded detection to cover auth-shaped thrown errors as well as GraphQL `errors[]` responses.

- **User-facing messaging**
  - Replaced the stale “current API key” authorization message in both error-formatting paths.
  - New copy reflects the real flow: Cognito guest credentials first, API key fallback second, with guidance oriented around backend deploy / unauth-role propagation / stale bundle scenarios.

- **Docs**
  - Updated the README troubleshooting table and guest-auth guidance to match the new behavior, including the automatic `identityPool` → `apiKey` fallback.

```ts
const guestClient = generateClient<Schema>({ authMode: "identityPool" });
const apiKeyClient = generateClient<Schema>({ authMode: "apiKey" });

async function generateRecipeWithFallback(description: string) {
  const result = await guestClient.generations.generateRecipe({ description });

  if (!hasAmplifyAuthError(result.errors)) {
    return result;
  }

  console.warn("[PublicChatWidget] Guest auth failed, retrying with apiKey.", result.errors);
  return apiKeyClient.generations.generateRecipe({ description });
}
```

- [x] `amplify/amplify_outputs.json` now declares `iam` as a valid provider for `Todo` and has `default_authorization_type: "AWS_IAM"`.
- [x] `PublicChatWidget.tsx` and `AiInsightsPanel.tsx` both attempt `identityPool` first and fall back to `apiKey` on auth errors only.
- [x] The fallback path is unit-testable / observable in console logs (`[PublicChatWidget] Guest auth failed, retrying with apiKey ...`).
- [x] The "Authorization error" user-facing string no longer says "with the current API key".
- [x] README troubleshooting table updated to match.
- [x] `npm run build` succeeds locally (no new TS errors).
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` in `amplify/` succeeds (PR #62 added `cd amplify && npx tsc && cd ..` to `amplify.yml` — don't break that).

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

## Problem

The AI Chat tab on the production website is still surfacing:

> Authorization error — the AI service is not accessible with the current API key. If a new deployment has just completed, refresh the page to pick up updated credentials.

even after PR #62 (https://github.com/chasepayscash-27/cpc-aws-v2/pull/62) merged ~10 minutes ago and switched the public routes (`Todo`, `generateRecipe`) to `identityPool` / `allow.guest()` auth.

The user has now had ~25+ PRs trying to fix this same error message (most recently #43, #45, #47, #50, #54, #56, #57, #58, #59, #60, #61, #62). This PR needs to land a defensive, "once-and-for-all" fix.

## Root causes still present after PR #62

### 1. Committed `amplify/amplify_outputs.json` is stale and inconsistent with the new auth model

Current contents of `amplify/amplify_outputs.json` on `main` (after PR #62):

```json
"data": {
  "url": "https://rf24g25v65cttol22ex5pp4t2q.appsync-api.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/graphql",
  "aws_region": "us-east-1",
  "api_key": "da2-fa5s7jmdvzhqrnjaop6j75oaeu",
  "default_authorization_type": "API_KEY",
  "authorization_types": [
    "AMAZON_COGNITO_USER_POOLS",
    "AWS_IAM"
  ],
  "model_introspection": {
    "models": {
      "Todo": {
        ...
        "attributes": [
          { "type": "auth", "properties": { "rules": [
            { "allow": "public", "provider": "apiKey", "operations": ["create","update","delete","read"] }
          ]}}
        ]
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Notice:
- `default_authorization_type` is still `API_KEY` (PR #62 set `defaultAuthorizationMode: "identityPool"` in `amplify/data/resource.ts` but the committed outputs file was never regenerated).
- `model_introspection` for `Todo` lists only `provider: apiKey` — there is no `iam` / guest rule. The Amplify Data client uses this introspection to validate the requested `authMode`. With this file, `generateClient({ authMode: "identityPool" })` will fail to produce a signed IAM request for these routes, AppSync returns `UnauthorizedException`, and `src/utils/amplifyErrors.ts` maps it to the "Authorization error" string above.
- `generateRecipe` under `generations` likewise has no auth-rule metadata after the change.

Even though `amplify.yml` runs `cp -f amplify_outputs.json amplify/amplify_outputs.json` after `npx ampx pipeline-deploy`, the committed file is what every developer (and every preview/sandbox build) sees. And because `src/main.tsx` and `src/components/PublicChatWidget.tsx` import `../../amplify/amplify_outputs.json` as a **static ES module**, Vite bundles whatever is in git at build time. If the pipeline-deploy step ever fails partway, or if a developer builds without running `ampx pipeline-deploy` first, the bundle ships with a stale outputs file that doesn't advertise guest auth.

### 2. No fallback when IAM/guest auth fails

PR #62 hard-switched the public clients to `identityPool` only:

```tsx
// src/components/PublicChatWidget.tsx (line 13)
const client = generateClient<Schema>({ authMode: "identityPool" });
```
```tsx
// src/components/AiInsightsPanel.tsx (similar)
```

If guest credentials aren't yet usable (Identity Pool unauth role policy still propagating, CDN serving a previous bundle, stale outputs file as in #1), there is no automatic retry with `apiKey`. The user gets stuck on the auth error and clicking "Refresh page" doesn't help if the bundle itself is the issue.

### 3. User-facing error copy still blames "API key"

`src/utils/amplifyErrors.ts` (lines ~178-195 and ~270-285) still returns:

> "Authorization error — the AI service is not accessible with the current API key. If a new deployment has just completed, refresh the page to pick up updated credentials."

We're no longer supposed to be using API key on the public path, so this message is both misleading and a duplicate of the issue we just fixed structurally. It needs to be updated to reflect the new auth model and give actionable next steps.

## Required changes

Please make ALL of the following in a single PR.

### A. Regenerate / fix `amplify/amplify_outputs.json` to reflect PR #62's auth model

Update the committed `amplify/amplify_outputs.json` so it accurately represents the new schema:

1. Change `data.default_authorization_type` from `"API_KEY"` to `"AWS_IAM"`.
2. Ensure `data.authorization_types` includes `"AWS_IAM"` and `"API_KEY"` (it already lists `AWS_IAM` and `AMAZON_COGNITO_USER_POOLS`, but `API_KEY` is missing despite `api_key` being present).
3. In `data.model_introspection.models.Todo.attributes`, add an auth rule for `provider: iam` alongside the existing `apiKey` rule, e.g.:

   ```json
author: pyup-bot
body:
This PR pins [lxml](https://pypi.org/project/lxml) to the latest release **6.1.1**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 6.1.1
   ```
   ==================

Bugs fixed
----------

* The known link attributes in ``lxml.html.defs.link_attrs`` were missing ``xlink:href``,
  which can be used for URL bypass attacks in embedded SVG/MathML/etc. content.
  https://github.com/fedora-python/lxml_html_clean/security/advisories/GHSA-4jhm-jv67-739f

* The Linux wheels use a patched libxslt 1.1.43, fixing CVE-2025-7424 and CVE-2025-11731.

* The Windows wheels use libxslt 1.1.45, fixing CVE-2025-7424 and CVE-2025-11731.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 6.1.0
   ```
   ==================

This release fixes a possible external entity injection (XXE) vulnerability in
``iterparse()`` and the ``ETCompatXMLParser``.

Features added
--------------

* GH486: The HTML ARIA accessibility attributes were added to the set of safe attributes
  in ``lxml.html.defs``.  This allows ``lxml_html_clean`` to pass them through.
  Patch by oomsveta.

* The default chunk size for reading from file-likes in ``iterparse()`` is now configurable
  with a new ``chunk_size`` argument.

Bugs fixed
----------

* LP2146291: The ``resolve_entities`` option was still set to ``True`` for
  ``iterparse`` and ``ETCompatXMLParser``, allowing for external entity injection (XXE)
  when using these parsers without setting this option explicitly.
  The default was now changed to ``'internal'`` only (as for the normal XML and HTML parsers
  since lxml 5.0).
  Issue found by Sihao Qiu as CVE-2026-41066.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 6.0.4
   ```
   ==================

Bugs fixed
----------

* LP2148019: Spurious MemoryError during namespace cleanup.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 6.0.3
   ```
   ==================

Bugs fixed
----------

* Several out of memory error cases now raise ``MemoryError`` that were not handled before.

* Slicing with large step values (outside of ``+/- sys.maxsize``) could trigger undefined C behaviour.

* LP2125399: Some failing tests were fixed or disabled in PyPy.

* LP2138421: Memory leak in error cases when setting the ``public_id`` or ``system_url`` of a document.

* Memory leak in case of a memory allocation failure when copying document subtrees.

* When mapping an XPath result to Python failed, the result memory could leak.

* When preparing an XSLT transform failed, the XSLT parameter memory could leak.

Other changes
-------------

* Built using Cython 3.2.4.

* Binary wheels use zlib 1.3.2.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 6.0.2
   ```
   ==================

Bugs fixed
----------

* LP2125278: Compilation with libxml2 2.15.0 failed.
  Original patch by Xi Ruoyao.

* Setting ``decompress=True`` in the parser had no effect in libxml2 2.15.

* Binary wheels on Linux and macOS use the library version libxml2 2.14.6.
  See https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libxml2/-/releases/v2.14.6

* Test failures in libxml2 2.15.0 were fixed.

Other changes
-------------

* Binary wheels for Py3.9-3.11 on the ``riscv64`` architecture were added.

* Error constants were updated to match libxml2 2.15.0.

* Built using Cython 3.1.4.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 6.0.1
   ```
   ==================

Bugs fixed
----------

* LP2116333: ``lxml.sax._getNsTag()`` could fail with an exception on malformed input.

* GH467: Some test adaptations were made for libxml2 2.15.
  Patch by Nick Wellnhofer.

* LP2119510, GH473: A Python compatibility test was fixed for Python 3.14+.
  Patch by Lumír Balhar.

* GH471: Wheels for "riscv64" on recent Python versions were added.
  Patch by ffgan.

* GH469: The wheel build no longer requires the ``wheel`` package unconditionally.
  Patch by Miro Hrončok.

* Binary wheels use the library version libxml2 2.14.5.
  See https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libxml2/-/releases/v2.14.5

* Windows binary wheels continue to use a security patched library version libxml2 2.11.9.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 6.0.0
   ```
   ==================

Features added
--------------

* GH463: ``lxml.html.diff`` is faster and provides structurally better diffs.
  Original patch by Steven Fernandez.

* GH405: The factories ``Element`` and ``ElementTree`` can now be used in type hints.

* GH448: Parsing from ``memoryview`` and other buffers is supported to allow zero-copy parsing.

* GH437: ``lxml.html.builder`` was missing several HTML5 tag names.
  Patch by Nick Tarleton.

* GH458: ``CDATA`` can now be written into the incremental ``xmlfile()`` writer.
  Original patch by Lane Shaw.

* A new parser option ``decompress=False`` was added that controls the automatic
  input decompression when using libxml2 2.15.0 or later.  Disabling this option
  by default will effectively prevent decompression bombs when handling untrusted
  input.  Code that depends on automatic decompression must enable this option.
  Note that libxml2 2.15.0 was not released yet, so this option currently has no
  effect but can already be used.

* The set of compile time / runtime supported libxml2 feature names is available as
  ``etree.LIBXML_COMPILED_FEATURES`` and ``etree.LIBXML_FEATURES``.
  This currently includes
  ``catalog``, ``ftp``, ``html``, ``http``, ``iconv``, ``icu``,
  ``lzma``, ``regexp``, ``schematron``, ``xmlschema``, ``xpath``, ``zlib``.

Bugs fixed
----------

* GH353: Predicates in ``.find*()`` could mishandle tag indices if a default namespace is provided.
  Original patch by Luise K.

* GH272: The ``head`` and ``body`` properties of ``lxml.html`` elements failed if no such element
  was found.  They now return ``None`` instead.
  Original patch by FVolral.

* Tag names provided by code (API, not data) that are longer than ``INT_MAX``
  could be truncated or mishandled in other ways.

* ``.text_content()`` on ``lxml.html`` elements accidentally returned a "smart string"
  without additional information.  It now returns a plain string.

* LP2109931: When building lxml with coverage reporting, it now disables the ``sys.monitoring``
  support due to the lack of support in https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1790

Other changes
-------------

* Support for Python < 3.8 was removed.

* Parsing directly from zlib (or lzma) compressed data is now considered an optional
  feature in lxml.  It may get removed from libxml2 at some point for security reasons
  (compression bombs) and is therefore no longer guaranteed to be available in lxml.

  As of this release, zlib support is still normally available in the binary wheels
  but may get disabled or removed in later (x.y.0) releases.  To test the availability,
  use ``"zlib" in etree.LIBXML_FEATURES``.

* The ``Schematron`` class is deprecated and will become non-functional in a future lxml version.
  The feature will soon be removed from libxml2 and stop being available.

* GH438: Wheels include the ``arm7l`` target.

* GH465: Windows wheels include the ``arm64`` target.
  Patch by Finn Womack.

* Binary wheels use the library versions libxml2 2.14.4 and libxslt 1.1.43.
  Note that this disables direct HTTP and FTP support for parsing from URLs.
  Use Python URL request tools instead (which usually also support HTTPS).
  To test the availability, use ``"http" in etree.LIBXML_FEATURES``.

* Windows binary wheels use the library versions libxml2 2.11.9, libxslt 1.1.39 and libiconv 1.17.
  They are now based on VS-2022.

* Built using Cython 3.1.2.

* The debug methods ``MemDebug.dump()`` and ``MemDebug.show()`` were removed completely.
  libxml2 2.13.0 discarded this feature.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 5.4.0
   ```
   ==================

Bugs fixed
----------

* LP2107279: Binary wheels use libxml2 2.13.8 and libxslt 1.1.43 to resolve several CVEs.
  (Binary wheels for Windows continue to use a patched libxml2 2.11.9 and libxslt 1.1.39.)
  Issue found by Anatoly Katyushin.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 5.3.2
   ```
   ==================

This release resolves CVE-2025-24928 as described in
https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libxm

body:
## Summary

User-facing docs (README, docs/EMBEDDED.md + .ja.md, docs/ROADMAP.md, docs/MANUAL_M5STICKS3.md), `mfsk-core/Cargo.toml`'s `[features].fixed-point` block, `mfsk-core/src/lib.rs` rustdoc, and two rustdoc comments in `mfsk-core/src/ft8/{llr.rs, decode_block/process_candidates.rs}` had several claims frozen mid-narrative — talking about a past decision-point or intermediate state as if it were still current. Each one is rewritten to be either correct-current or completed as a historical chapter. **No source behaviour change** (pure docs + rustdoc).

### The big one: `LlrT` round trip

`type LlrT = Q11i16` at `mfsk-core/src/ft8/decode_block/process_candidates.rs:976` since the 2026-05-02 `LlrScalar` trait unification (`a6425ee`, shipped 0.6.2). A brief 2026-05-04 cleanup (`195284d`) recorded a host-only Phase 1 reading that Q3i8 was recall-equivalent and wrote "Q11i16 reverted" into the Cargo.toml + lib.rs comments. 0.6.3's wider LX7 sweep (per `process_candidates.rs:967-974` rustdoc) showed Q3i8's quantization step actually was the recall ceiling on Xtensa (host f32 16/18 vs Q3i8 9/18 on `qso3_busy.wav`), so the active scalar moved back to Q11i16. The 2026-05-04 stale comments survived through 0.6.5.

This PR realigns Cargo.toml + lib.rs + the affected rustdoc + all user-facing docs on **Q11i16 = current (since 0.6.2)**, with the Q3i8 → Q11i16 → Q3i8 → Q11i16 history preserved as a completed chapter.

### Other frozen-mid-narrative drains in the same pass

- **Host AP-off / AP-on JTDX recall**: 16/18 → 13/18, 5/6 → 4/6 — reflects the 0.6.3 OSD `npre1`/`npre2` precoding + `OSD_HARDERRORS_MAX = 22` ceiling that dropped 3 CRC-luck phantoms (CHANGELOG 0.6.3 entry). README + ROADMAP now read as the full 1/6 → 5/6 → 4/6 arc.
- **Embedded `6/18 + 1 bonus = 7 total` + `~1.19 s post-SlotEnd`**: kept as the last formal 0.6.2 → 0.6.3 Q11i16 ship sweep measurement, but with a "needs `wav_sim` re-run on 0.6.5 firmware to confirm" caveat — 0.6.3's host-side OSD tightening was not re-measured on embedded (no post-0.6.3 log captured in `embedded-poc/m5stack-s3/logs/`).
- **CoreS3 row** in EMBEDDED.md + .ja.md "What we test" now reflects the 2026-05-17 pivot: StickS3 → demo / acoustic-fallback, CoreS3 → main UAC controller target (Phase B-Core, hardware bring-up in progress).
- **`embedded-poc/m5stack-core2/` standalone bench retirement** (#61 Phase 3 in 0.6.3) framed as completed history, not active.
- **MANUAL_M5STICKS3.md Uac mode** reference to CoreS3 successor now anchored with date + status (was unanchored "successor path").
- **ROADMAP.md header**: post-0.6.4 → post-0.6.5 + "What landed in 0.6.5" section (matches 0.6.5 CHANGELOG).
- **README `0.5.x` version qualifiers** on FST4-15/W + MSK144 reworded so the judgment carries forward, not just a 0.5.x-era limitation.
- **Stale log reference** `embedded-poc/m5stack-s3/logs/s3_063_q11i16_v2_2026-05-09.log` (doesn't exist in repo, never committed) rewritten as "raw log not preserved; phase logs remain under `s3_phaseA..C_q3i8_2026-05-04.log`".
- **CHANGELOG.md 0.5.4 entry**: in-place annotation that the "Phase 1 confirmed Q3i8 recall-equivalent" claim was superseded in 0.6.2 / 0.6.3, including the role swap of "lives in `core::scalar` only" between Q3i8 and Q11i16.

### Out of scope (CoreS3 firmware bring-up gate)

- Re-measuring the embedded `6/18+1=7 total` and `~1.19 s` numbers on 0.6.5 firmware (no embedded log captured post-0.6.3).
- Re-measuring `+0.16..+0.63 dB SNR improvement` from 0.6.4 (CHANGELOG canonical, original log not in repo).
- Per-protocol (WSPR / FT4 / JT9 etc.) recall numbers, which may have a similar "measured at some point" freeze pattern.

## Test plan

- [x] `RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings cargo doc -p mfsk-core --features full --no-deps` — clean.
- [x] `cargo clippy -p mfsk-core --features full --no-deps` — clean.
- [ ] CI pre-commit fence (fmt + clippy + rustdoc).
- [ ] CI full sweep matrix.
- [ ] Spot-check rendered docs.rs preview for the README table + `fixed-point` block.

body:
## Summary

- Drizzle's `sql` template interpolates a JS array as `($1, $2, …)`, which postgres reads as a record literal. `name = ANY((…))` then fails with SQLSTATE 42809 ("op ANY/ALL (array) requires array on right side"), so the daily missed-schedules check in the morning health email was stuck in `warn` since the cron migrated to a pg-boss DB lookup on 2026-05-17.
- Render `ARRAY[$1, $2, …]` via `sql.join` so each queue name binds as its own text param. Verified the new query runs against prod's pgboss tables and returns the 5 expected schedules.
- Added a regression test that compiles the captured SQL through `PgDialect` and asserts the shape (`ARRAY[$n, …]`, no `ANY(($`).

The Jetson sends all data — audio and DOA — over a single WebSocket connection. Previously `/ws/audio` only handled binary PCM frames and would fail on text frames. This extends it to handle both.

```
WS /ws/audio
  binary → raw int16 mono PCM at 16kHz (or WAV with RIFF header)
  text   → {"type": "doa", "angle": <0–359>}
```

## Summary

`pnpm setup:asc-key` worked end-to-end on first use (run [26064787366](https://github.com/joshlebed/workshop/actions/runs/26064787366) is currently building on EAS, past the credentials step), but the output had ugly inline escape codes:

```
Step 4 — Push secrets to joshlebed/workshop
^[]11;rgb:2727/2828/2222^[\^[[56;1R^[[56;36R^[]11;rgb:2727/2828/2222^[\^[[56;36R✓ Set Actions secret ASC_API_KEY_CONTENT for joshlebed/workshop
```

Those are responses to OSC 11 (background color) and CPR (cursor position) queries that gh's TUI rendering sends to the terminal. Warp / recent iTerm leaks the responses back onto stdout instead of consuming them. The commands still succeed, but it's visual noise.

Fix: capture each gh call into a shell variable. Command substitution makes gh's stdout a pipe, gh's `isatty()` check fails, the TUI mode is skipped, and the queries are never sent in the first place. The script prints its own clean `✓ <secret name>` line per call; on failure it dumps the captured output so the error message survives.

Refactored the three `gh secret set` calls and the `gh workflow run` call through a small `run_gh` helper. The `--body`-less stdin-redirect case (`gh secret set ... < $P8_PATH`) stays inline because it doesn't compose cleanly through a function — that's the only one that's still explicit.

body:
## Summary
Closes the mobile attribution gap on landing-page download buttons. Two related fixes:
### Path B — `/thanks/`-bound CTAs (nav, pre-footer, etc.)
Today, mobile users clicking these buttons land on `/thanks/`, which auto-redirects to a **bare** Play Store / App Store URL with no `install_referrer` / `pt`+`ct` params for the originating page's campaign. The install reaches the store but the page-campaign is lost.

A new client-side module (`media/js/base/mobile-attribution.js`):
- Resolves the page's campaign via the same cascade `stub-attribution.js` uses: `force > override > URL utm_campaign > default`.
- On mobile UAs, rewrites matching button HREFs to attributed `play_store_url()` / `app_store_url()`-shaped URLs.
- Attaches a click handler that fires `Mozilla.TrackProductDownload.sendEventFromURL` with the captured `https://` URL (mirroring `thanks-init.js`) and navigates via `window.location.href` so the rewrite works in any browser despite `mozilla-utils.js`'s `market://` scheme mutation.

### Path A — CMS `download_firefox_button` Play/App Store badges

These already have attributed URLs server-side and have always fired the `firefox_mobile_download` GA4 event correctly **on iOS** — the existing [`datalayer-productdownload-init.es6.js`](media/js/base/datalayer-productdownload-init.es6.js) attaches `handleLink` to every `.ga-product-download` element.

But on Android the event has been silently dropping. `mozilla-utils.js` mutates `https://play.google.com/...` to `market://details?...` on DOM ready, and the tracker's `marketURL` regex (`/^market:\/\/play.google.com/`) doesn't match that shape — so `isValidDownloadURL` returns false and the event never fires.

We supplement Android Path A buttons (`.fl-store-button-android`) with a click handler that uses the captured `https://` URL. iOS Path A is untouched (existing handler still works there) — adding ours would double-fire the event.

## Analytics changes — for Martech review
> ⚠️ **Two analytics deltas in this PR.** Both should net to *more* accurate signal in dashboards that use the `firefox_mobile_download` / `product_download` events.

Scenario Before this PR After this PR
---------

Mobile click on **nav / pre-footer** download CTA (Android or iOS), page has a campaign Click → `/thanks/` → auto-redirect to **bare** store URL (with hardcoded `utm_campaign=download` for Android, or no `pt`/`ct` for iOS). `firefox_mobile_download` event fires correctly from `/thanks/` (it captures the URL synchronously), but the install itself reaches the store with no page-campaign attribution. Click → directly to **attributed** store URL with the page's campaign. `firefox_mobile_download` event fires from the landing page (not `/thanks/`) with the same payload. Same total event volume; campaign now reaches Play Console / App Store Connect.

Mobile click on **nav / pre-footer** CTA, no campaign anywhere on page Same as today (bare store URL via `/thanks/` auto-redirect, event fires from `/thanks/`). Strict no-op (JS exits early). Identical to today.

Click on **CMS `download_firefox_button` Play Store badge (Android)** Event silently dropped on click. The existing `datalayer-productdownload-init.es6.js` handler reads `event.target.href` at click time, which `mozilla-utils.js` has already mutated to `market://details?...`; the tracker's `marketURL` regex (`/^market:\/\/play.google.com/`) doesn't match that shape. No `firefox_mobile_download` event fires. Event now fires correctly with the campaign in the URL. **Expect previously-zero volume on Android Path A clicks to appear in dashboards.**

Click on **CMS `download_firefox_button` App Store badge (iOS)** Event fires correctly (existing handler works — `mozilla-utils.js` doesn't mutate iOS URLs). Unchanged — we deliberately don't double-attach. `/thanks/` page itself (mobile user lands there directly, e.g. from a hand-rolled link or in the absence of a campaign) `thanks-init.js` auto-redirects after 1s and fires the event correctly (captures URL synchronously before mutation). **Unchanged.** Our JS doesn't touch the auto-redirect path. `/thanks/` GTM pageview for mobile users transiting `/thanks/` Fires Skipped for users who would have transited `/thanks/` (because they now go directly to the store). Mobile users who land on `/thanks/` directly still fire it.
**No GTM dashboard changes needed.** The canonical signal for mobile downloads is the `firefox_mobile_download` event itself, which fires under both Path A and Path B. If a dashboard estimates mobile downloads by counting `/thanks/` pageviews specifically, it should switch to the event count.

**Existing latent bug worth a follow-up (separate PR)**: the `marketURL` regex in [`datalayer-productdownload.es6.js:15`](media/js/base/datalayer-productdownload.es6.js) is `/^market:\/\/play.google.com/`, but `mozilla-utils.js`'s `initMobileDownloadLinks` produces `market://details?...` (no `play.google.com` in the path). This affects any click-time-URL-read handler on a `.ga-product-download` Android button. `/thanks/`'s auto-redirect is unaffected because `thanks-init.js` captures the URL synchronously before the mutation. This PR works around the regex bug for our specific buttons via the same synchronous-capture pattern. A separate PR could broaden the regex to `/^market:\/\//` to fix the root cause for any other Path A buttons across the site (e.g. release-notes, landing/gaming, landing/ios-summarizer).

## Files
- `media/js/base/mobile-attribution.js` (new)
- `tests/unit/spec/base/mobile-attribution/mobile-attribution.js` (new)
- `media/static-bundles.json` — new `mobile-attribution` bundle
- `webpack.test.config.js` — `datalayer-productdownload-init.es6.js` and `mobile-attribution.js` added to `test-deps`
- `springfield/base/templates/base-protocol.html`, `springfield/cms/templates/cms/base-flare26.html`, `springfield/cms/templates/cms/base-flare.html` — load the new bundle alongside the existing `stub-attribution` bundle

- [x] **Desktop (no UA spoof), `stub_attr_utm_campaign_value="test-19"` set**: nav button HREF stays `/thanks/`. Click → stub installer flow, `moz-stub-attribution-code` cookie carries `test-19`.
- [x] **Page with no `stub_attr` and no URL `utm_campaign`, mobile UA**: nav HREF stays `/thanks/`. JS exits early. Identical to today.
- [x] **Hand-rolled footer "Download Firefox" link** still routes to `/thanks/` on any UA (intentional — no wrapper class).
- [x] **Mobile user lands directly on `/thanks/`** (e.g. from a hand-rolled link or no-campaign nav): auto-redirect to store fires after 1s with the existing event. Unchanged.
### New behavior
- [x] **Mobile UA Chrome devtools (Android UA), page with `test-19`**: nav and pre-footer button HREFs rewrite to `play.google.com/...&utm_campaign=test-19`. `mozilla-utils.js` further converts to `market://...` on real Android. Click → store install attributed.
- [x] **Mobile UA Chrome devtools (iOS UA), same page**: nav and pre-footer button HREFs rewrite to `apps.apple.com/...&ct=test-19`. Click → App
Store.
- [x] **URL-param attribution**: any page (CMS or not) with `?utm_campaign=test-19`, mobile UA → nav HREF rewrites.
- [x] **Cascade precedence**: `stub_attr_utm_campaign_mode="force"` value `force-val` + URL `?utm_campaign=url-val` → mobile HREF reflects `force-val`. Switch mode to `default` → URL value wins.
- [x] **Path A Android button**: CMS `download_firefox_button` block on a page, Android UA, click the green Play Store badge. In DevTools
Console: `dataLayer.filter(e => e.event === 'firefox_mobile_download')` returns an entry with `platform: 'android'`, `method: 'store'`, `release_channel: 'release'`. (Previously this would have been empty due to the regex mismatch.)

author: zixi-qi
body:
## Problem

`CuMemAllocator` (sleep-mode allocator, `vllm/device_allocator/cumem.py`) uses a CUDA *pluggable* allocator. When a pool-backed tensor's refcount hits zero, `_python_free_callback` returns the allocation handle, and the C extension (`csrc/cumem_allocator.cpp:unmap_and_release`) immediately calls `cuMemUnmap` + `cuMemRelease` *synchronously from the host*. Which can trigger IMA in the case where the memory is released before all kernels on the cuda stream have completed. 

This has showed up when running deepseek v4 with sleep mode turned on. 

## Test plan
- Before the fix, running this code triggers IMA:
```
from vllm.device_allocator.cumem import CuMemAllocator

with CuMemAllocator.get_instance().use_memory_pool(tag="weights"):
    for _ in range(200):
        torch.randn(2048, 7168, device="cuda")

torch.cuda.synchronize()
print("OK")

Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/home/zixi/repos/vllm/repro_cumem_race.py", line 15, in <module>
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
  File "/home/zixi/repos/vllm/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/torch/cuda/__init__.py", line 1162, in synchronize
    return torch._C._cuda_synchronize()
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered
Search for `cudaErrorIllegalAddress' in https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html for more information.
CUDA kernel errors might be asynchronously reported at some other API call, so the stacktrace below might be incorrect.
For debugging consider passing CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1
Compile with `TORCH_USE_CUDA_DSA` to enable device-side assertions.
```
- After the fix, no IMA

---

🤖 This PR was prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code). The diagnosis, repro, fix, and PR text were AI-drafted; I reviewed every changed line, ran the repro on a B300 cluster against this patch, and own the change end-to-end.

author: adamessenmacher
body:
### Description of Change

Fixes iOS and MacCatalyst `ProgressBar` sizing so the native `UIProgressView` visually honors the MAUI-arranged height.

Previously, `ProgressBar` could be arranged with an explicit height, but `UIProgressView` kept its native intrinsic visual height. This meant requested heights like `1`, `100`, and `1000` still produced a native progress view around its default thin height.

This change wraps the iOS/MacCatalyst `UIProgressView` in a handler container that owns the MAUI layout bounds. The native progress view remains the public `PlatformView`, is centered inside the container, and is vertically scaled from its measured natural height to the arranged container height during layout.

The change also re-enables the shared native bounding-box assertion for `IProgress` and adds a focused iOS/MacCatalyst test that verifies `handler.PlatformView` itself honors explicit sizes.

Validation:
- MacCatalyst `Category=ProgressBar`: 66 run, 60 passed, 6 ignored
- MacCatalyst `Category=Label`: 109 run, 103 passed, 6 ignored
- iOS simulator `Category=ProgressBar`: 66 run, 65 passed, 1 ignored
- iOS simulator `Category=Label`: 109 run, 108 passed, 1 ignored

### Issues Fixed

Fixes #7935
